# boat

> This file is very large and may be truncated. For an index of this content, please refer to https://docs.boat.dev/llms.txt instead.

# Accounts and sign-in
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/account

Sign-in methods, reinstalling or using a second computer, and which surface (CLI, API, SDKs, dashboard) does what.

## Sign-in methods

There are four ways to sign in, on the CLI and on the [dashboard](https://boat.dev/dashboard):

* GitHub
* Google
* A 6-digit code sent by email
* [AgentID](https://agentid.com), for an AI agent that has its own AgentMail inbox. See [Sign up from an agent](/agent-auth#sign-in-with-agentid).

No method is more correct than the others. Use the one you like. You can add the others later.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat login                          # asks: github, google, email, or agentid
boat login --google
boat login --email you@example.com
boat login --agentid
```

Each method that you use is a **connection** on your account. [Dashboard > Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) lists them.

* All connections open the same account, with the same sandboxes, settings and billing.
* You can add or remove connections at any time. One connection must remain.
* The **primary** connection sets the address that gets account notifications. To change that address, make a different connection primary.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A sign-in with a method that is not connected yet makes a **separate** account. This is true also when the email address is the same. To add a second method to your account, do these steps:
>
> 1. Sign in with your usual method.
> 2. Add the connection from the Account tab.
>
> To move a connection between two existing accounts, you must merge the accounts. Only support can do a merge.

A sign-in with Google, email or AgentID does not give boat access to your code. To clone [repositories](/environments/repositories), you need a GitHub connection. You can add it when you first need it.

## Reinstalling, or a second computer

Your plan, environment, sandboxes and settings are on your account, not on your computer. To reinstall boat, or to install it on a new computer, sign in on that computer:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat onboard   # or: boat login
```

Sign in with the same method as the first time. `boat onboard` then finds your account:

* It skips each step that your account has already done.
* It does **not** open Stripe Checkout when your plan is active.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Use the same sign-in method as before. A method that was never connected to your account opens a **separate** account, with its own empty plan. This is the usual cause when a reinstall asks you to subscribe again.

## What the sandboxes are for

Onboarding asks what the sandboxes are for. There are two answers:

* Your own work.
* A platform of yours, used by third-party users. This is the default.

The second answer marks your environment [safe for third parties](/environments#safe-for-third-parties). Then none of your credentials go to those sandboxes.

You can change this at any time in [Dashboard > Environment](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=environment).

## Four ways to drive boat

The four ways use the same platform. The code examples in these docs have **CLI**, **curl**, **TypeScript** and **Python** tabs. Select a tab one time, and the rest of the page uses it.

| | Use it for | Auth |
| - | - | - |
| **CLI** (`boat`) | your terminal, CI jobs, shell scripts, and from inside a sandbox | browser sign-in or `BOAT_API_KEY` |
| **REST API** | any language, webhooks, anything the SDKs do not cover yet | `BOAT_API_KEY` |
| **SDKs** ([Python](/sdks/python), [TypeScript](/sdks/typescript)) | typed calls from your own service | `BOAT_API_KEY` |
| **[Dashboard](https://boat.dev/dashboard)** | one-off work, and the things that must not be automatable | browser sign-in |

The four ways are not identical. The differences are intentional:

| Only in the dashboard | Only in the CLI | Only in the API and SDKs |
| - | - | - |
| [Webhook delivery history](/webhooks), removing [organization members](/organizations#members-and-invites), member roles and per-member caps, sign-in connections, per-sandbox metrics, [closing your account](/data-retention/close-account) | interactive SSH, SCP, port forwarding, `boat snapshot pull` | editing a webhook in place (`PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}`), reading and writing files in a sandbox without SSH |

Invites work from the CLI too: `boat org invite`. Read [Organizations](/organizations#members-and-invites).

Some actions need a browser sign-in, on the CLI or on the dashboard. boat refuses them to an API key on purpose:

* Rotate and revoke [API keys](/api-keys).
* Turn on [zero data retention](/data-retention).

To create an API key, use a browser sign-in, or an API key with the `admin` preset. A new key never gets more rights than the key that creates it.

An agent can also sign itself in and claim a human. See [Sign up from an agent](/agent-auth).


# Sign up from an agent
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/agent-auth

Let an AI agent register itself with boat, get a human to claim it, and start the free trial, without a pasted API key.

An AI agent can sign up for boat without a human who pastes an API key. boat implements [auth.md](https://workos.com/blog/agent-registration-with-auth-md), the WorkOS agentic registration protocol.

This page is about an agent that makes a boat account. For the agents that run inside a sandbox, read [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents). For an agent that uses boat every day from your computer, read [Use boat from your coding agent](/ai-tools).

The contract is a machine-readable file at [boat.dev/auth.md](https://boat.dev/auth.md). This page is a human-readable copy of it.

> [!NOTE]
>
> If you are an agent, fetch that file and follow it. Do not work from this page. Do not answer from search results about it.

## Start

Give the agent this instruction:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
Follow https://boat.dev/auth.md and start a sandbox free trial for me.
```

The agent then does these steps:

1. It finds the endpoints from `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.
2. It registers.
3. Only after that, it calls the boat API.

## What the agent does

```mermaid theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
%%{init: {"theme": "base", "fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "themeVariables": {"fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "fontSize": "14px", "primaryColor": "#F1F3F9", "primaryBorderColor": "#263FA9", "primaryTextColor": "#060606", "secondaryColor": "#E0E3F2", "tertiaryColor": "#FEFEFE", "lineColor": "#060606", "textColor": "#060606", "mainBkg": "#F1F3F9", "nodeBorder": "#263FA9", "clusterBkg": "#FEFEFE", "clusterBorder": "#C4C4C4", "edgeLabelBackground": "#FEFEFE", "actorBkg": "#F1F3F9", "actorBorder": "#263FA9", "actorTextColor": "#060606", "actorLineColor": "#9E9E9E", "signalColor": "#060606", "signalTextColor": "#060606", "labelBoxBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "labelBoxBorderColor": "#263FA9", "noteBkgColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteBorderColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteTextColor": "#060606", "sectionBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "altSectionBkgColor": "#FEFEFE", "taskBkgColor": "#263FA9", "taskBorderColor": "#263FA9", "taskTextColor": "#FEFEFE", "gridColor": "#E0E0E0"}, "flowchart": {"padding": 16, "nodeSpacing": 48, "rankSpacing": 48, "curve": "linear"}, "sequence": {"boxMargin": 16, "actorMargin": 48, "noteMargin": 16, "messageMargin": 32, "mirrorActors": false}, "state": {"padding": 16}, "gantt": {"barHeight": 24, "barGap": 8, "fontSize": 14, "sectionFontSize": 14}}}%%
sequenceDiagram
  participant Agent
  participant boat
  participant Human
  Agent->>boat: GET /auth.md and well-known metadata
  Agent->>boat: POST /agent/identity (anonymous or email)
  alt anonymous
    boat-->>Agent: identity assertion (read-only)
  else email
    boat-->>Agent: user_code + verification URL
  end
  Agent->>Human: Open this link and type this 6-digit code
  Human->>boat: Sign in, enter the code
  boat-->>Agent: access_token (boat API key)
  Agent->>boat: POST /api/boat/billing/checkout
  Agent->>Human: Open Stripe Checkout to start the free trial
  Human->>boat: Card + trial
  Agent->>boat: POST /api/v1/sandboxes
```

There are two ways to register.

| Method | Token | What the agent can do |
| - | - | - |
| **Anonymous** | Immediately | Only `GET /me` and `GET /limits`. A sandbox create returns `claim_required` until a human claims the agent. |
| **Email (`service_auth`)** | After the person signs in and types the code | The agent must already know the user's email. |

boat does not accept ID-JAG identity assertions. The agent must not send `identity_assertion` registration bodies. An agent that has its own AgentMail inbox can [sign in with AgentID](#sign-in-with-agentid) instead.

## Sign in with AgentID

[AgentID](https://agentid.com) gives an AI agent its own identity: its AgentMail inbox. An agent with AgentID signs in to boat as itself. No human claims it, and no email code is necessary.

* The boat account belongs to the agent's inbox address.
* The agent's AgentMail organization must be verified by its human.
* The free trial still needs a human to enter a card in Stripe Checkout.

The agent does these steps:

1. It runs `boat login --agentid --json` and reads the `url` field.

2. It opens that URL in a browser. AgentID shows a waiting page with an `auth_token`.

3. It approves the sign-in with its AgentMail API key:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   curl -X POST "https://api.agentmail.to/v0/inboxes/$AGENTMAIL_INBOX_ID/authorize" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $AGENTMAIL_API_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{"auth_token":"<auth_token>","accept_disclosure":true}'
   ```

4. The browser returns to boat and shows "Login Complete".

5. It runs `boat onboard --wait --json` to finish the CLI login.

The [dashboard](https://boat.dev/dashboard) also has a **Continue with AgentID** button.

## Expect approval prompts

Almost every step sends a credential or an email address to a new host. Agent harnesses ask for approval before these actions. So the agent stops for approval more than once. This is correct behavior, not a failure.

You can retry each step by itself. When an approval stops the agent, it does these steps:

1. It says what it is about to send.
2. It waits for approval.
3. It continues from the step where it stopped.

## Trial

The trial uses the same Stripe Checkout that a human uses from the dashboard.

1. The agent calls `POST /api/boat/billing/checkout` with the claimed token.
2. The agent shows the URL that boat returns.
3. The human enters a card and starts the trial.

These rules still apply:

* A card is necessary.
* boat runs trial-abuse checks.
* There is one trial per identity.
* An anonymous token cannot start a trial.

For what the trial includes and its limits, read [Free trial](/free-trial).

## Prices

An agent must never give a price from memory or from a web search.

* `GET /api/v1/limits` returns the live plans, trial inclusions and caps. Read them there when necessary.
* To estimate usage cost, send the human to [boat.dev](https://boat.dev). It has the calculator.
* Search results and cached marketing pages are not a price source. Some of them describe other products.

## Endpoints

The endpoints are on `https://boat.dev`. They are also under `/api/boat/...`, so they work behind the existing `/api` proxy.

| Path | Purpose |
| - | - |
| `/auth.md` | Agent-readable walkthrough |
| `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | RFC 9728 discovery |
| `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | RFC 8414 + `agent_auth` block |
| `POST /agent/identity` | Register |
| `POST /agent/identity/claim` | Start or refresh the claim ceremony |
| `GET /agent/identity/claim` | Human claim page |
| `POST /oauth2/token` | Exchange assertion or poll claim |
| `POST /oauth2/revoke` | Revoke one access token |

A 401 from the boat API includes this header. An agent that only calls the API can use it to find the other endpoints.

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://boat.dev/api/boat/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"
```


# AI credentials and proxy
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/ai-credentials

Credential profiles, a second Claude or ChatGPT account when one runs out of credits, custom APIs, AI usage, and the proxy that keeps real keys out of your sandboxes.

Your sandboxes get the AI credentials of a **credential profile**: Claude and ChatGPT sign-ins, API keys, and custom APIs. With the **AI credentials proxy** on, a sandbox gets placeholder keys, and the real keys stay with boat.

| You want | Page |
| - | - |
| Connect your first key or subscription, or pass the keys of your users with `-e` | [Keys and subscriptions](/integrated-agents/keys) |
| Share keys with a team, switch accounts, keep keys out of sandboxes, see AI usage | This page |

| | CLI | API | SDKs |
| - | - | - | - |
| List profiles | `boat ai profiles` | `GET /credential-profiles` | `listCredentialProfiles` |
| Create a profile | `boat ai profile new <name>` | `POST /credential-profiles` | `createCredentialProfile` |
| Rename, make default | `boat ai profile rename` / `default` | `PUT /credential-profiles/{profile}` | `updateCredentialProfile` |
| Delete a profile | `boat ai profile rm <name>` | `DELETE /credential-profiles/{profile}` | `deleteCredentialProfile` |
| Set, remove an API key | `boat ai profile set-key` / `rm-key` | `PUT`, `DELETE /credential-profiles/{profile}/keys/{credential}` | `setCredentialProfileKey`, `deleteCredentialProfileKey` |
| Switch a credential to another account | `boat ai accounts` / `switch` | `GET /credential-profiles/{profile}/accounts/{credential}`, `PUT …/{account}/active` | `listCredentialAccounts`, `switchCredentialAccount` |
| Add, forget an account | `boat ai add-account` / `forget-account` | `POST /credential-profiles/{profile}/accounts/{credential}`, `DELETE …/{account}` | `addCredentialAccount`, `deleteCredentialAccount` |
| Set, remove a custom API | `boat ai profile set-api` / `rm-api` | `PUT`, `DELETE /credential-profiles/{profile}/custom-apis/{name}` | `setCredentialProfileCustomApi`, `deleteCredentialProfileCustomApi` |
| Proxy on or off | `boat ai proxy [on\|off]` | `GET`, `PUT /ai-proxy` | `getAiProxy`, `updateAiProxy` |
| Usage | `boat ai usage [id]` | `GET /ai-usage`, `GET /sandboxes/{id}/ai-usage` | `getAiUsage`, `getSandboxAiUsage` |
| Block, unblock a sandbox | `boat ai block` / `unblock` | `PUT /sandboxes/{id}/ai-access` | `setSandboxAiAccess` |

The profile and proxy calls need an API key with `account.admin`. Account usage needs `account.read`. Sandbox usage needs `sandbox.read` on that sandbox.

## Credential profiles

A credential profile is a named set of AI credentials. boat encrypts it at rest. The API never returns a secret value: it lists which credentials a profile holds (`connected`) and the names of its custom APIs.

Each account has one **default** profile. A sandbox gets the default profile of its owner, unless its environment names another profile. The credentials you had before profiles existed are now the profile named `default`. On the dashboard **Agents & Proxying** page, pick a profile at the top. Both tabs then show and edit only that profile: its sign-ins and keys, its proxy switch, its custom APIs and its usage.

| Credential | Kind | Set it with |
| - | - | - |
| `anthropic-api-key`, `openai-api-key`, `openrouter-api-key`, `llmgateway-api-key`, `deepseek-api-key`, `moonshot-api-key`, `mistral-api-key`, `xai-api-key`, `opencode-api-key` | API key | `set-key`, or the Agents & Proxying page |
| `claude-subscription`, `chatgpt-subscription`, `kimi-subscription`, `mistral-vibe-subscription`, `grok-subscription` | Sign-in | The Agents & Proxying page |
| `claude-bedrock`, `codex-bedrock` | AWS Bedrock | The Agents & Proxying page |

You can remove any credential with `rm-key`. A sign-in sent to `set-key` returns `400 not_an_api_key`.

### Out of credits? Switch to another account

A credential can hold several accounts: two ChatGPT sign-ins, two Claude sign-ins, two OpenAI keys. One account is in use. When it runs out of credits, switch the credential to another account. Every sandbox that uses the profile gets the other account at once, running sandboxes included. Nothing restarts, and the other credentials do not change.

On the dashboard **Agents & Proxying** page, the account in use shows next to each credential. Click it to:

* **switch** to another account,
* **add another account**: sign in again, or paste another key. The current account stays, ready to switch back to,
* **forget** an account. Forgetting the one in use switches to another account first.

Sign-ins renew only while in use. An account set aside keeps its sign-in as it was, and renews when you switch back to it.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ai accounts chatgpt-subscription
#  #  ACCOUNT          
#  1  you@work.dev     in use
#  2  you@home.dev
boat ai switch chatgpt-subscription 2

# API keys: add a second key, then switch by number, or by its last characters
echo "$OPENAI_API_KEY_2" | boat ai add-account openai-api-key
boat ai switch openai-api-key …7f3a

boat ai forget-account openai-api-key 2
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/default/accounts/chatgpt-subscription" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

# use the id of the account to switch to, from the list
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/default/accounts/chatgpt-subscription/$ACCOUNT_ID/active" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/default/accounts/openai-api-key" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value":"'"$OPENAI_API_KEY_2"'"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { accounts } = await sandbox.listCredentialAccounts({ profile: "default", credential: "chatgpt-subscription" });
const other = accounts.find((a) => !a.active)!;
await sandbox.switchCredentialAccount({ profile: "default", credential: "chatgpt-subscription", account: other.id });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
accounts = sandbox.list_credential_accounts("default", "chatgpt-subscription").accounts
other = next(a for a in accounts if not a.active)
sandbox.switch_credential_account("default", "chatgpt-subscription", other.id)
```

`--profile` picks another profile; the default is your default profile. The account list never shows a secret: a sign-in shows its email when the provider gives it, a key shows its last characters.

To give different sandboxes different accounts at the same time, use one profile per account and name the profile on an environment (see [Environments](#environments)).

### Set and remove API keys

`--copy-from` starts a new profile with a copy of the API keys and custom APIs of a profile you manage. Sign-ins are not copied: one sign-in in two profiles would sign itself out at the first renewal. Sign in again on the new profile. The CLI reads a key from stdin when you omit the value, so the key stays out of your shell history. A key is one token of up to 8192 printable characters, without spaces or line breaks; anything else returns `400`.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ai profile new ci --copy-from default
echo "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | boat ai profile set-key ci anthropic-api-key
boat ai profile rm-key ci claude-subscription
boat ai profile rename ci ci-bots
boat ai profile rm ci-bots
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"ci","copyFrom":"default"}'

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/ci/keys/anthropic-api-key" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value":"'"$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"'"}'

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/ci/keys/claude-subscription" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/ci" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.createCredentialProfile({ name: "ci", copyFrom: "default" });
await sandbox.setCredentialProfileKey({
  profile: "ci",
  credential: "anthropic-api-key",
  value: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY!,
});
await sandbox.deleteCredentialProfileKey({ profile: "ci", credential: "claude-subscription" });
await sandbox.deleteCredentialProfile({ profile: "ci" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os
from boat_sdk.models.create_credential_profile_request import CreateCredentialProfileRequest
from boat_sdk.models.set_credential_key_request import SetCredentialKeyRequest

sandbox.create_credential_profile(CreateCredentialProfileRequest(name="ci", copy_from="default"))
sandbox.set_credential_profile_key("ci", "anthropic-api-key", SetCredentialKeyRequest(value=os.environ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]))
sandbox.delete_credential_profile_key("ci", "claude-subscription")
sandbox.delete_credential_profile("ci")
```

Running sandboxes that use the profile get a changed key. You cannot delete a default profile (`409 is_default`) or a profile that an environment names (`409 in_use`).

### Organization profiles

An organization can own profiles too. By default, every active member can use them. An owner can limit a profile to a list of members with `boat ai profile access`. Read [Limit who can use an environment or profile](/organizations#limit-who-can-use-an-environment-or-profile). Only organization owners create and change them, and only they see the account list. In a profile list, `owner.kind` is `org` and `canManage` tells you if you can change it.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat --org acme ai profile new team-claude
echo "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | boat ai profile set-key team-claude anthropic-api-key
boat ai profiles --org-only
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"team-claude","org":"acme"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.createCredentialProfile({ name: "team-claude", org: "acme" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.create_credential_profile(CreateCredentialProfileRequest(name="team-claude", org="acme"))
```

To give the sandboxes of an organization the organization profile, name it on an organization environment. See [Shared sandboxes](/organizations/shared-sandboxes#shared-environments-and-ai-credentials).

### Your own Claude sign-in in a sandbox

The Claude Code credential you select in your profile sets variables in the sandbox's shells. Only the selected one does. A connected Anthropic API key that you did not select is not in the sandbox, so it is never billed:

| Selected credential | Variables |
| - | - |
| Claude subscription | `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` |
| Anthropic API key | `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` |
| OpenRouter or DeepSeek key for Claude Code | `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` |

When you select another credential, running sandboxes drop the variables of the previous one.

Claude Code prefers these variables to a sign-in. Remote Control needs a full claude.ai sign-in. To use it, run `claude` in the sandbox and sign in with `/login`. From the next shell, boat removes `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, and `claude` uses your sign-in. boat never removes that sign-in: it stays across stops, resumes and cold resumes. The agent that `boat prompt` runs still uses the profile.

## Custom APIs

A custom API is a secret for any HTTPS API, such as Stripe or your own service. You give it a name, a value and a base URL. The sandbox gets two variables:

| Variable | Value |
| - | - |
| `<NAME>` | The secret. A placeholder when the proxy is on |
| `<NAME>_BASE_URL` | The base URL. The proxy URL when the proxy is on |

The name is an environment variable name: `A-Z`, `0-9` and `_`, up to 64 characters. Provider names (`ANTHROPIC_*`, `OPENAI_*`, `AWS_*`, and so on) and names that end in `_BASE_URL` are reserved. The base URL must use HTTPS on the default port, with a public DNS name.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
echo "$STRIPE_KEY" | boat ai profile set-api default STRIPE_KEY --base-url https://api.stripe.com/v1
boat ai profile rm-api default STRIPE_KEY
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/default/custom-apis/STRIPE_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value":"'"$STRIPE_KEY"'","baseUrl":"https://api.stripe.com/v1"}'

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/default/custom-apis/STRIPE_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.setCredentialProfileCustomApi({
  profile: "default",
  name: "STRIPE_KEY",
  value: process.env.STRIPE_KEY!,
  baseUrl: "https://api.stripe.com/v1",
});
await sandbox.deleteCredentialProfileCustomApi({ profile: "default", name: "STRIPE_KEY" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.set_custom_api_request import SetCustomApiRequest

sandbox.set_credential_profile_custom_api("default", "STRIPE_KEY", SetCustomApiRequest(
    value=os.environ["STRIPE_KEY"],
    base_url="https://api.stripe.com/v1",
))
sandbox.delete_credential_profile_custom_api("default", "STRIPE_KEY")
```

Code in the sandbox must send its requests to `$<NAME>_BASE_URL`. With the proxy on, a request sent straight to the API with the placeholder fails.

## The AI credentials proxy

Without the proxy, a sandbox holds your real keys and sign-ins. Anyone with a shell in it can copy them. With the proxy on, the real keys never enter the sandbox.

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
 sandbox                              Boat                              provider
 ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<placeholder>
 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<Boat proxy>
 agent ── request + placeholder ──▶  proxy: placeholder valid?
                                       sandbox blocked?
                                       swap in the real key  ── request + real key ──▶  api.anthropic.com
       ◀──────── reply ─────────────  count tokens  ◀─────────── reply ──────────────
```

| | The sandbox holds | boat holds |
| - | - | - |
| Proxy off | The real keys and sign-ins | The real keys and sign-ins |
| Proxy on | Placeholders and the proxy URL | The real keys and sign-ins, and renews the sign-ins |

* A placeholder is worthless outside boat. It does not contain the real key.
* A copied placeholder stops working when the sandbox stops. Each start gives the sandbox new placeholders.
* The proxy sends each credential only to its own provider. An Anthropic key never goes to another host.
* The proxy puts a provider key only in the `Authorization` or `x-api-key` header. A placeholder in another header or in the URL stays a placeholder, so a provider that echoes it cannot return the real key.
* A custom API gets its secret in any request header and in the query string, never in the path. Pick a base URL you trust: a host that echoes requests shows the secret to the sandbox.
* boat renews Claude, ChatGPT and Grok sign-ins behind the proxy. The sandbox never sees a renew token.

### What the proxy covers

| Proxied | Not proxied |
| - | - |
| Claude sign-in and Anthropic API key (Claude Code) | AWS Bedrock (`claude-bedrock`, `codex-bedrock`) |
| ChatGPT sign-in and OpenAI API key (Codex) | Kimi Code sign-in (`kimi-subscription`) |
| OpenRouter, LLM Gateway, DeepSeek, Moonshot API keys | |
| Mistral API key and Mistral Vibe sign-in | |
| Grok sign-in and xAI API key | |
| OpenCode key (Go and pay-as-you-go) | |
| Custom APIs | |

Bedrock signs each request with AWS keys, so there is nothing to swap. The Kimi Code CLI renews its sign-in itself. While the proxy is on, boat withholds these credentials from sandboxes. Use a Moonshot API key in place of the Kimi sign-in.

### Turn it on

The switch is per account: one for you, one for each organization. Only an organization owner can change the organization switch. On the dashboard, open **Agents & Proxying**, then the **Proxying** tab. It holds the switch, the custom APIs and the AI usage, for the account in view: you, or the organization you selected.

A sandbox goes through the proxy when either switch is on:

* the switch of the account that owns its credential profile, or
* the switch of the organization that pays for the sandbox. An organization can make sure that no real key enters its sandboxes, whoever's profile they use.

Running sandboxes switch at their next start. Stop and resume a sandbox to switch it now.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ai proxy               # state and price
boat ai proxy on
boat --org acme ai proxy on
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/ai-proxy" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/ai-proxy" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled":true}'

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/ai-proxy?org=acme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled":true}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const proxy = await sandbox.getAiProxy();
console.log(proxy.enabled, proxy.pricing);

await sandbox.updateAiProxy({ enabled: true });
await sandbox.updateAiProxy({ org: "acme", enabled: true });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.update_ai_proxy_request import UpdateAiProxyRequest

proxy = sandbox.get_ai_proxy()
print(proxy.enabled, proxy.pricing)

sandbox.update_ai_proxy(UpdateAiProxyRequest(enabled=True))
sandbox.update_ai_proxy(UpdateAiProxyRequest(enabled=True), org="acme")
```

The proxy applies to sandboxes that use a profile of an account with the switch on. A sandbox that uses an organization profile follows the organization switch.

## Safe for third parties, with AI credentials

An environment marked [safe for third parties](/environments#safe-for-third-parties) passes nothing of yours. Turn on `proxyAiCredentials` on that environment to still pass AI credentials, as placeholders. The sandbox user can run the agents, but cannot take your keys. You can block the sandbox at any time.

`proxyAiCredentials` needs the proxy on for the account that owns the profile. If it is off, the call returns `400 ai_proxy_off`.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ai proxy on
boat env set customers --safe-for-third-parties true --proxy-ai-credentials true --credential-profile ci
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"safeForThirdParties":true,"proxyAiCredentials":true,"credentialProfileId":"ci"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.updateEnvironment({
  environmentId: envId,
  safeForThirdParties: true,
  proxyAiCredentials: true,
  credentialProfileId: "ci",
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.update_sandbox_environment_request import UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest

sandbox.update_environment(env_id, UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(
    safe_for_third_parties=True,
    proxy_ai_credentials=True,
    credential_profile_id="ci",
))
```

## Environments

An environment can name the profile its sandboxes get, with `credentialProfileId` (an id or a name). `null`, or `--credential-profile default` in the CLI, means the default profile of the sandbox owner. Like every environment change, this makes a new version. Running sandboxes move at `boat env upgrade`. See [Environments](/environments/access#ai-credentials).

## Usage

For each proxied sandbox, boat counts requests and errors, and the tokens per UTC day, credential and model. The token counts are the numbers the provider reports in its replies: input, output, cache read and cache write. A sandbox that holds real keys has no usage here, because its requests do not go through boat.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ai usage                       # every sandbox of the account in scope
boat ai usage bx_23456789 --days 7  # one sandbox, per day and model
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/ai-usage?days=30" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_23456789/ai-usage?days=7" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const account = await sandbox.getAiUsage({ days: 30 });
for (const s of account.sandboxes) console.log(s.sandboxId, s.totals.requests, s.dollars);

const one = await sandbox.getSandboxAiUsage({ sandboxId: "bx_23456789", days: 7 });
console.log(one.blocked, one.totals.inputTokens, one.totals.outputTokens);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
account = sandbox.get_ai_usage(days=30)
for s in account.sandboxes:
    print(s.sandbox_id, s.totals.requests, s.dollars)

one = sandbox.get_sandbox_ai_usage("bx_23456789", days=7)
print(one.blocked, one.totals.input_tokens, one.totals.output_tokens)
```

The account view covers the wallet in scope: your own, or an organization with `--org`, `org` or `X-Boat-Org`. In the dashboard, open the **⋯** menu of a sandbox and select **AI usage**.

`dollars` in these responses is the boat proxy charge: \$1 per 1,000 requests. It is not your provider bill. The provider bills your tokens on your own provider account.

### Cap AI spend

boat has no automatic AI spend cap. The member spend cap of an organization limits sandbox time, not provider tokens. To cap AI spend yourself:

1. Read the usage of each sandbox with `GET /sandboxes/{id}/ai-usage` on a schedule.
2. When the tokens pass your limit, [block the sandbox](#block-a-sandbox).

This works only for proxied sandboxes. Also set a spend limit in the console of your provider.

### Block a sandbox

Block a sandbox to stop its AI requests at once, running or stopped. The proxy refuses its placeholders with `403`. Unblock it to accept them again. Blocking has no effect on a sandbox that holds real keys (proxy off). The sandbox creator and the managers of its profile can block it.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ai block bx_23456789
boat ai unblock bx_23456789
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_23456789/ai-access" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"blocked":true}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.setSandboxAiAccess({ sandboxId: "bx_23456789", blocked: true });
await sandbox.setSandboxAiAccess({ sandboxId: "bx_23456789", blocked: false });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.set_sandbox_ai_access_request import SetSandboxAiAccessRequest

sandbox.set_sandbox_ai_access("bx_23456789", SetSandboxAiAccessRequest(blocked=True))
sandbox.set_sandbox_ai_access("bx_23456789", SetSandboxAiAccessRequest(blocked=False))
```

## Pricing

Profiles, custom APIs and usage tracking are free. The proxy costs money. The [wallet](/billing#wallet) pays it, not the plan's included time:

| Charge | Price | Paid by |
| - | - | - |
| Each UTC day the proxy is on | \$1 | The wallet of the account with the switch on |
| Proxied requests | \$1 per 1,000 | The wallet each sandbox bills |

`dollars` in the usage responses is the request charge for the period. It does not include the daily charge. The provider bills your tokens as usual, on your own provider account.

# Use boat from your coding agent
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/ai-tools

Let Claude Code, Codex or Cursor on your computer start and drive boat sandboxes: the boat CLI, the docs MCP server, llms.txt, skills, and an AGENTS.md snippet.

Your coding agent drives boat with the `boat` CLI, the same as you. Give it three things:

1. The CLI, signed in.
2. The boat docs, through the MCP server or `llms.txt`.
3. A short rule in `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` that says when to use a sandbox.

This page is about an agent on your computer. For the agents inside a sandbox, read [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

## 1. Install the CLI and sign in

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -fsSL https://boat.dev/install | sh
```

On Windows, run `irm https://boat.dev/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell. Open a new terminal after the install.

An agent runs commands without a browser. Sign it in with an [API key](/api-keys):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
echo "$BOAT_API_KEY" | boat login --key-stdin
```

No account yet? The agent can make one itself. Read [Sign up from an agent](/agent-auth).

## 2. Give the agent the docs

| Source | URL | Use it when |
| - | - | - |
| MCP server | `https://docs.boat.dev/mcp` | The agent supports MCP. It can search the docs and read pages. |
| Index | `https://docs.boat.dev/llms.txt` | The agent can only fetch URLs. Every page, with a one-line summary. |
| Full text | `https://docs.boat.dev/llms-full.txt` | You want all the docs in one file. It is large: about 135,000 tokens. |
| One page as Markdown | Add `.md` to any page URL, for example `https://docs.boat.dev/quickstart.md` | The agent needs one page. |

Add the MCP server:

```bash Claude Code theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
claude mcp add --transport http boat-docs --scope user https://docs.boat.dev/mcp
```

```bash Codex theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
codex mcp add boat-docs --url https://docs.boat.dev/mcp
```

```json Cursor theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "boat-docs": { "url": "https://docs.boat.dev/mcp" }
  }
}
```

For Cursor, put the JSON in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or in `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project. The **⋯** menu on every docs page also has one-click entries for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and VS Code.

## 3. Add a rule to AGENTS.md

Put this in `AGENTS.md` (Codex, Cursor and most agents) or `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code) in your project:

```markdown AGENTS.md theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
## Cloud sandboxes (Boat)

Use a Boat sandbox for builds, tests, untrusted code, Docker, and long jobs. Never run them on this computer.
Docs: https://docs.boat.dev/llms.txt. Prices and limits: run `boat limits`; never quote prices from memory.

- Create: `id=$(boat new --json | jq -r 'select(.event=="ready") | .id')`
- One-shot job: `boat run --push . -- npm test` (new sandbox, run, cost, delete; exits with the test exit code)
- Run: `boat exec "$id" --cwd my-app "npm test"` (30 s timeout; `--timeout 0` = no limit)
- Server: `boat exec "$id" --detach "npm run dev"`, then `boat exec "$id" --status <pid>`
- Copy files: `boat push "$id" ./my-app` (git-tracked files, to /home/user/my-app) or clone the repo inside the sandbox
- Public URL for a port: `boat ssh "$id" "host 3000 --private"`
- Always pass the sandbox id. `current` does not work in a non-interactive shell.
- When done: `boat stop "$id"` (keeps the disk for at least 14 days) or `boat delete "$id" --yes` (erases it)
```

The `--json` output of `boat new` is one JSON object per line. The `ready` line holds the `id`.

## Skills

The open skill pack installs boat skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other agents:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
npx skills add ariana-dot-dev/cloud-sandbox-vm-skills
```

It has 13 skills, for example `cloud-sandbox`, `parallel-agents`, `background-worker` and `public-url-hosting`. Each skill tells the agent when to use boat and which commands to run.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Some skills in the pack still show older values: the `on.ascii.dev` domain, an 80 GB disk and a fixed cap of 100 sandboxes. These docs are correct. Public URLs use `on.boat.dev`. For sizes and limits, read [Pricing](/pricing).

Inside a sandbox, every integrated agent already has a `boat` skill. You do not install it.

## Related

* [CLI reference](/cli-reference)
* [Run a coding agent on your repo](/recipes/agent-on-repo)
* [Run many agents in parallel](/recipes/parallel-agents)
* [API keys](/api-keys)


# API keys and tokens
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys

Create scoped, expiring boat API keys, use them as bearer tokens, and revoke a leaked key.

Create a key for CI or a server:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat api-key create ci --preset ci --ttl 90d
```

Store the secret as `BOAT_API_KEY`. Send it as a bearer token:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS https://boat.dev/api/v1/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

* A new key starts with `boat_`. Older keys start with `box_` and still work.
* Every new key expires. The maximum is 365 days.
* Every new key has a scope. boat checks it on each request.
* A key acts as you. It is either an **organization key** or an **account key**.

| Key | Made from | Bills and sees | Account settings |
| - | - | - | - |
| Organization key | The dashboard with that organization selected, `boat --org <org> api-key create`, `boat api-key create` while that organization is active, or `"org": "<org>"` (or `X-Boat-Org: <org>`) on `POST /api-keys/scoped` | That organization only. A request that names another organization or Personal gets `403 api_key_org_mismatch`. | Refused (`403 api_key_org_forbidden`): webhooks, AI credentials, billing, keys, members. |
| Account key | The dashboard with Personal selected, `boat --org personal api-key create`, or a request that names no organization | The organization a request names with `X-Boat-Org: <org>`, else your active wallet. Read [Active wallet](/organizations/active-wallet). | Allowed, if the scope allows it. |

The dashboard lists the keys of the selected organization. Personal lists the account keys.

> [!WARNING]
>
> A key leaked? Revoke it now. Read [Key leaked](/api-keys/store-rotate-revoke#key-leaked).

> [!WARNING]
>
> Treat API keys as secrets. Do not commit them, print them in logs or put them into images.

## Main task

1. [Create a key](/api-keys/create-and-list#create-a-key) with the smallest scope that does the job.
2. [Store it](/api-keys/store-rotate-revoke#store-a-key) as `BOAT_API_KEY` in your platform secret manager.
3. [Use it](/api-keys/create-and-list#use-the-key) from the CLI, the API or an SDK.
4. [Rotate or revoke it](/api-keys/store-rotate-revoke) when you need to.

## Production guidance

* Use one key per job.
* Use the shortest TTL that works for you.
* Use `read-only` or `ci`. Full account access requires an explicit `--preset admin`.
* Pass at least one of `--preset`, `--actions`, `--sandbox` or `--env`.
* Limit a key to sandboxes or environments with `--sandbox` or `--env` when you can.
* For keys inside your end users' sandboxes, read [Security for platforms](/security).

## Learn more

> [card] [Scopes](/api-keys/scopes)
>
> Actions, presets, the in-sandbox API key and scope errors.

> [card] [Create and list keys](/api-keys/create-and-list)
>
> Create a key, use it, list your keys and see the usage of one key.

> [card] [Store, rotate and revoke](/api-keys/store-rotate-revoke)
>
> Revoke a leaked key, store a key and replace its secret.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Keys created before scoped keys existed have no expiry and full access. Replace them with new scoped keys. `boat api-key list` shows them with no expiry.


# Create and list keys
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys/create-and-list

Create a scoped boat API key, use it, list your keys and see the usage of one key.

## Create a key

To create a key, you need one of these:

* A browser session: `boat login` with no key, or the dashboard.
* A key with the `account.admin` action, or an `admin` key. The new key cannot have more actions, more sandboxes or a later expiry than this key.

The create endpoint is `POST https://boat.dev/api/v1/api-keys/scoped`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> During a credential rollout, boat can turn off key creation for a short time. `GET /api/v1/api-keys` reports this in `catalog.scopedCreationEnabled`. While creation is off, the create endpoint returns a typed 503.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat api-key create my-project --ttl 90d --preset ci --sandbox bx_123
boat api-key create readonly --ttl 30d --preset read-only
boat api-key create admin --ttl 7d --preset admin
boat api-key create custom --ttl 24h --actions sandbox.read,exec,file.read
```

| Flag | Rule |
| - | - |
| `--ttl` | The maximum is 365 days. `--ttl never` makes a key that works until you revoke it. A key that expires cannot create one that never expires. |
| `--sandbox`, `--env` | You can give each one more than one time. |
| `--actions`, `--preset` | Use one or the other, not both. |
| No `--ttl` | The key expires after 90 days. |
| No scope flags | The command fails. Pass at least one of `--actions`, `--preset`, `--sandbox` or `--env`. |

> [!WARNING]
>
> Full account access requires an explicit `--preset admin`. An admin key can also create more keys.

A key that never expires is still a scoped key. If it leaks, it works until you revoke or rotate it. Read [Store, rotate and revoke](/api-keys/store-rotate-revoke).

For the actions and presets, read [Scopes](/api-keys/scopes).

With the API:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST https://boat.dev/api/v1/api-keys/scoped \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_ADMIN_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"tenant-42","ttl":"30d","preset":"full-sandbox","sandboxIds":["bx_123"]}'
```

The body takes `name`, `ttl`, `preset` or `actions`, `sandboxIds` and `environmentIds`.
Pass at least one non-empty scope field. Full account access requires `"preset":"admin"`.

boat shows the secret one time only. In scripts, capture it like this:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
BOAT_API_KEY="$(boat api-key create my-project --preset ci --ttl 90d --json | jq -r '.secret')"
```

You can also use the **API Keys** tab in the dashboard. It has expiry presets, action presets, a raw action picker, and sandbox and environment selectors.

## Use the key

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat login --key-stdin --json <<< "$BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/me" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { BoatApi, Configuration } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const sandbox = new BoatApi(new Configuration({
  basePath: "https://boat.dev/api/v1",
  accessToken: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY!,
}));

const me = await sandbox.me();
console.log(me.user.login);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os
from boat_sdk import ApiClient, Configuration
from boat_sdk.api.boat_api import BoatApi

config = Configuration(host="https://boat.dev/api/v1", access_token=os.environ["BOAT_API_KEY"])
with ApiClient(config) as client:
    sandbox = BoatApi(client)
    me = sandbox.me()
    print(me.user.login)
```

## What a key cannot do

* Create needs a browser session or an admin-scoped token. A credential that can make more credentials defeats least privilege.
* Rotate and revoke need a browser session or a key that can create keys. Such a key can rotate or revoke itself and any key that it could create.
* To approve an agent claim, you need a browser session. API keys cannot approve agent claims. This includes admin keys and legacy keys.

Use `boat api-key create|rotate|revoke`, or use the [API Keys](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=api-keys) tab.

## List

The CLI, the API, the SDKs and the dashboard can list keys. boat never returns the secrets.

Each row shows:

* The id, the name, the prefix and the last four characters
* The scope and the expiry
* The last use
* The request total for the last 30 days
* How many sandboxes and Agents the key created that still exist

boat labels expired keys and keys that expire soon.

A key limited with `--sandbox` or `--env` gets an empty `apiKeys` list. A browser session, a CLI session or a key with no such limit gets the full list.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat api-key list
boat api-key list --all    # include per-sandbox machine keys
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const keys = await sandbox.apiKeys();
for (const key of keys.apiKeys) {
  console.log(key.id, key.name, key.usage.requests, key.resources.total);
}
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
keys = sandbox.api_keys()
for key in keys.api_keys:
    print(key.id, key.name, key.usage.requests, key.resources.total)
```

## See usage for one key

`boat api-key usage <id>` prints the 30-day request total and the count of live resources. These are the same numbers as in the list.

* Add `--verbose` to see the split between sandboxes and Agents, and the list of created resources.
* The matching API is `GET /api-keys/{id}/usage`.
* Usage still works after you revoke the key, if you still have the id.

Revoke stops the secret. It does not delete the sandboxes or Agents that the key created.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat api-key usage sak_123
boat api-key usage sak_123 --verbose
```


# Scopes
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys/scopes

What a scoped boat API key can do: actions, presets, the in-sandbox API key and scope errors.

This page covers what each API key can do. For the full security picture, read [Security and isolation](/security).

## How boat checks a request

boat grants a request only when **both** of these are true:

1. The action is in the action set of the key.
2. The target sandbox is in the sandbox set of the key, or in one of its environments.

The default is deny. boat refuses unknown routes for scoped keys.

## Snapshots and environments

| You want to | The key needs |
| - | - |
| Create a sandbox from a saved snapshot | `sandbox.create` for the destination, and `snapshot.read` access to the source |
| Replace a saved snapshot | Access to its existing source, and access to the sandbox that you save |

A destination environment does not give access to snapshots from other environments.

## Actions

| Action | What it unlocks |
| - | - |
| `sandbox.create` | Create a sandbox |
| `sandbox.read` | List and inspect sandboxes |
| `sandbox.update` | Rename, recover, and other sandbox writes |
| `sandbox.stop` | Stop |
| `sandbox.resume` | Resume |
| `sandbox.fork` | Fork |
| `sandbox.delete` | Delete |
| `sandbox.delete-own` | Delete only the sandboxes this key created |
| `agent.prompt` | Prompt the sandbox agent |
| `exec` | Run a command |
| `file.read` / `file.write` | Read or write files |
| `ssh` | SSH, scp, and port forward |
| `desktop` | Desktop stream |
| `host` | Host a port |
| `snapshot.read` / `snapshot.write` | Snapshots |
| `environment.read` / `environment.write` | Environments |
| `account.read` | `/me`, limits, organization discovery, list keys (a key limited to sandboxes or environments sees an empty list) |
| `account.admin` | Billing, teams, webhooks, identities, account writes |
| `*` | Admin wildcard |

## Presets

| Preset | Use |
| - | - |
| `read-only` | Inspect sandboxes, files, snapshots, environments |
| `full-sandbox` | Operate a sandbox without create / resume / fork / delete / account writes |
| `ci` | Everything in `full-sandbox`, plus create, resume, fork, and delete the sandboxes this key created. No account admin |
| `admin` | `*` |

A key keeps the actions that it had when you created it. Resume, SSH and `sandbox.delete-own` joined the `ci` preset later. An older `ci` key does not get them. To get them, create a new `ci` key.

## In-sandbox API key

boat writes an API key into each sandbox for the boat CLI there. The file is `~/.config/ascii/boat/config.json`. The key works on **that sandbox** only. It is not listed by `boat api-key list` unless you add `--all`.

| It can, on its own sandbox | It cannot |
| - | - |
| Read, rename and stop the sandbox | Create, resume, fork or delete sandboxes |
| Prompt, exec, read and write files | Reach any other sandbox |
| SSH, desktop, host a port | Write environments |
| Read and save snapshots | Administer the account, billing, webhooks or keys |

* *Safe for third parties*, `--no-env` and the **boat credentials** toggle set to off remove this key.
* A separate token, `ASCII_TOKEN`, always stays. It can only host ports of its own sandbox.

Read [Security for platforms](/security) before you give end users shell access.

## Errors

Scoped keys return typed 403 errors:

| `error` | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `api_key_expired` | The TTL elapsed |
| `api_key_action_forbidden` | The action is not on the key |
| `api_key_sandbox_forbidden` | The sandbox or the environment is not on the key |

The bearer header and the SDK configuration do not change.


# Store, rotate and revoke
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api-keys/store-rotate-revoke

Revoke a leaked boat API key, store a key safely, and replace its secret with or without downtime.

## Key leaked

Do these steps now, in this order.

1. Sign in with a browser session. Revoke needs a session or a key that can create keys. A key with less access cannot revoke.
   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat login
   ```
2. Find the key and revoke it. Find the id by its name, prefix or last four characters.
   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat api-key list
   boat api-key revoke <id>
   ```
3. See what the key created. Delete the sandboxes that you do not know.
   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat api-key usage <id> --verbose
   ```
4. Look for new keys that you did not create. An `admin` key or a key with `account.admin` can create keys. Revoke them too.
5. Create a replacement with the smallest scope. Update your secret manager. Read [Create a key](/api-keys/create-and-list#create-a-key).

You can also click **Revoke** in the [API Keys](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=api-keys) tab of the dashboard.

## Store a key

| Platform | Store as |
| - | - |
| Railway | Variable named `BOAT_API_KEY` |
| GitHub Actions | Repository or environment secret named `BOAT_API_KEY` |
| Docker Compose | Environment variable or secret named `BOAT_API_KEY` |
| Kubernetes | Secret mounted or exposed as `BOAT_API_KEY` |

Do not put API keys in:

* Dockerfiles
* Images
* Source code
* Shell history
* Public CI logs

## Rotate a key

Rotate does these things:

* It revokes the old secret immediately.
* It keeps the id, the scope and the expiry date of the key.
* It replaces the secret and shows the new secret one time only.

Rotate does not extend the lifetime of the key. It does not change a legacy key into a scoped key.

You cannot rotate an expired scoped key. The API returns `409 api_key_expired`. Create a replacement key instead.

Rotate needs a browser session. Read [What a key cannot do](/api-keys/create-and-list#what-a-key-cannot-do).

### Rotate with downtime

Use **Rotate** only when you can update the deployed secret immediately.

1. Rotate the key. Run `boat api-key rotate <id>`, or use the dashboard. To find the id, run `boat api-key list`.
2. Copy the new secret.
3. Update `BOAT_API_KEY` in your platform secret manager.
4. Redeploy or restart the workers that use the key.

### Replace without downtime

1. Create a new key.
2. Update the platform secret to the new key.
3. Redeploy or restart the workers.
4. When the new deployment is live, revoke the old key.

## Revoke a key

Run `boat api-key revoke <id>`, or click **Revoke** in the dashboard. Revoke needs a browser session. The command does not take `--yes`.

* Revoke turns off the key immediately.
* The next boat API request with that secret fails with an auth error. This includes existing CLI configs and running processes.
* The sandboxes and Agents that the key created stay.
* `boat api-key usage <id>` still shows their totals.

Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/create-scoped-api-key

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /api-keys/scoped
Create an API key limited to some actions, sandboxes or environments, with an expiry. Same as boat api-key create.

# Get account limits
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/get-boat-limits

Check remaining machine starts, included VM time, the wallet, overage prices, access readiness, and concurrent-sandbox capacity for the wallet a create would bill: the `org` / `X-Boat-Org` you pass (id or name), else the account's active wallet, else personal. The response carries `teamId` when an organization wallet was read.

# List API keys
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/list-api-keys

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /api-keys
Lists API key metadata only. Raw key secrets are not returned after creation/rotation. Results include expiry and scope. A restricted API-key caller receives `apiKeys: []`; only an unrestricted account key or browser/CLI session receives the account inventory. Bearer header is unchanged; scope lives on the key.

# List GitHub repositories
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/list-github-repositories-available-to-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /repos
Returns GitHub repositories grouped by installation plus the current selected repositories for new Sandboxes.

# List organizations
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/list-organizations

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /orgs
The wallets this account can bill: your personal account first, then every organization you belong to, each with its id and name. Either spelling works wherever an org is passed (`org`, `X-Boat-Org`, `teamId`). `active` marks the wallet new sandboxes bill when a request names none; change it with `PATCH /orgs/active`.

# List webhooks
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/list-webhooks

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /webhooks
List account-wide sandbox lifecycle webhook endpoints.

Turn off an API key at once. Sandboxes that the key created keep running. Same as boat api-key revoke.

# Select a repository
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/select-repository-for-sandboxes

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /repos
Idempotently selects one repository for the sandbox environment. Use `databaseId` from `GET /repos` as `repositoryId`; selecting an already-selected repository updates its `baseBranch`.

# Set the active organization
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/set-active-organization

openapi/boat-v1.yaml PATCH /orgs/active
Set the wallet new sandboxes bill when a request names none, for this account on every client: the API, the CLI (`boat org switch` sets the same value) and the dashboard. Pass an organization id or name you belong to, or `personal` (or `null`) for your own account. `GET /limits` follows it. Sandboxes already running keep the wallet they were created with; leaving or deleting the organization resets the account to personal.

# Set OpenTelemetry export
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/set-opentelemetry-export

openapi/boat-v1.yaml PUT /telemetry
Set or replace the account's OTLP endpoint and send a test export.

# Update account data-retention policy
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/update-account-data-retention-policy

Enable or disable account zero data retention using a sandbox session.

# Update account secrets (legacy)
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/update-boat-secrets-setup

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /secrets
Save a new version of your account's sandbox environment variables and secret files. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Send an empty value to clear one. Running sandboxes keep their current version until you upgrade them.

# Update organization settings
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/update-organization

openapi/boat-v1.yaml PATCH /orgs/{org}
The owner renames the organization with `name`. Requests that name the organization by its old name fail after the rename; its id does not change. The billing name on new invoices follows when it is still the organization name. If Stripe does not answer, the request fails with 502 and nothing changes. Owners and admins set whether new sandboxes of the organization start private (only their creator can use them) or shared (every member can use those that hold none of their creator's logins). The default is shared. Existing sandboxes keep their setting; their creators change it with `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/share` and `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/unshare`. A fork of a private sandbox is private.

# Update webhook
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/account/update-webhook

openapi/boat-v1.yaml PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}
Update a sandbox lifecycle webhook endpoint.

# Attach to a detached command
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/attach-command

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}/stream
Stream the output of a command started with detached: true as it writes it, until it ends. Reconnect with the offsets every 10 minutes to follow it with no time limit.

# Add an SSH key
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/configure-sandbox-ssh-key

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/sshkey
Adds an OpenSSH public key to the running sandbox so the caller can SSH as user `user`. The response carries `machineIp`, which is the host to connect to on port 22.

This is also how you reach your own machine from inside a sandbox without the CLI: authorize the key, then open a reverse tunnel with stock OpenSSH, and a port on your machine answers at `127.0.0.1:<port>` inside the sandbox for as long as the ssh process runs.

```bash
ssh -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -N -R 7777:127.0.0.1:7777 user@<machineIp>
```

`boat forward <id> --reverse --local 7777` is the same tunnel with the key handling and redial done for you.

Create or fetch a secret-bearing desktop/noVNC URL for live computer-use visibility. Use `?vnc=1` for noVNC; a `provisioning: true` response means poll again.

# Interrupt running work
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/interrupt-running-agent-work

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/interrupt
Interrupt running agent work. By default this stops **every** conversation on the sandbox. Pass `conversation` to stop just one, leaving the others running. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

# List the command history
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/list-command-history

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/command-history
List the commands run in a sandbox in the last 7 days, newest first. Works while the sandbox is stopped.

# List conversations
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/list-sandbox-conversations

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/conversations
Every conversation on the sandbox, most recently prompted first, with what you need to pick one: how many prompts it holds, whether a turn is running in it right now, the last harness and model it ran on, a preview of its last prompt, and `current`, the one a `POST /prompt` without `new` or `conversationId` would continue. Pass an `id` back as `conversationId` on `POST /prompt` to resume that thread, or as `conversation` on `POST /steer`, `POST /interrupt` and `GET /events` to scope those. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

# List sandbox events
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/list-sandbox-events

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/events
Return Sandbox work, lifecycle, and progress events so product UIs can show what the sandbox is doing. A Sandbox runs many conversations in parallel; this streams **all** of them by default and every event carries a `conversationId`. Filter to one or more with `conversation`. Event payloads are extensible. Clients can long-poll this endpoint with `sort=asc` and a cursor to stream responses. Response events expose agent text, streaming partials via `data.is_streaming`, and tool calls/results via `data.tools`. When you poll, send the last `ETag` back in `If-None-Match`. An unchanged page answers `304 Not Modified` with no body.

# List a directory
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/list-sandbox-files

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/list
List the files and directories in one sandbox directory, with size, permissions and modification time.

# List sandbox processes
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/list-sandbox-processes

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/processes
List the processes in a running sandbox, or the last stored sample of a stopped one.

Move or rename a sandbox file or directory, also between /home/user and /tmp.

# Prompt the agent
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/prompt-sandbox-agent

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/prompt
Queue a natural-language work item for an agent harness (Codex, Claude Code, pi, OpenCode, or Prime Agent) inside the sandbox. Observe progress with `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/events`.

A Sandbox runs many conversations in parallel. Set `new: true` to start a fresh one, `conversationId` to continue a specific one, or omit both to continue the most-recently-active conversation; the response returns the `conversationId`. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

Read the stored stdout or stderr of a command from a byte offset. Works while the sandbox is stopped.

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files
Read a file from a sandbox by its path, as UTF-8 text by default or base64 for binary content.

# Replace text in files

Replace every occurrence of a text in a list of sandbox files, with one result per file.

Find the sandbox files and directories whose names match a glob pattern such as *.py.

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/permissions
Set the permission bits of a sandbox file or directory.

# Steer a running turn (API)
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/steer-a-running-turn

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/steer
Send a new message to a turn that is already running, without losing what the agent is doing. This is what typing into a coding agent while it works does: the instruction is taken into account and the work continues.

Where the harness has a native mid-turn primitive (Claude Code, Codex, pi, Prime Agent) nothing is interrupted and the response has `native: true`. Where it does not (OpenCode), Boat interrupts that turn and immediately continues the SAME conversation with the instruction, keeping the session and its memory, and the response has `native: false`.

Refused with **409 `no_running_turn`** when the conversation has nothing in flight; queue work with `POST /prompt` instead. `error.details.reason` says why: `turn_ended` (with `error.details.lastTurn.status` and `.error` of the newest turn), `turn_not_started` (the turn is starting; retry in a moment), `no_turn`, `not_running` (the sandbox is not running) or `delivery_failed` (the sandbox did not accept the steer; check the turn before sending more work). The steer shows up in `GET /events` as a `steer` event. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

# Stop a detached command
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/agent/stop-command

openapi/boat-v1.yaml DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}
Stop a command started with detached: true, and every process it started. The response holds its final history record.

# Write a file

openapi/boat-v1.yaml PUT /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files
Write or overwrite a file in a sandbox at a given path, as UTF-8 text or base64-encoded binary content.

Every account of one credential, the one in use first.

# List credential profiles

Soft-deletes an environment. The default environment cannot be deleted, and at least one environment is always kept.

Returns every non-deleted sandbox environment with its latest-version flags, contents, and per-version sandbox usage. A default environment named `base` is created on first access if none exists.

# Update an environment

openapi/boat-v1.yaml PUT /environments/{environmentId}
Rename, set as default, and/or edit flags and contents. Any flag or content change mints a new immutable version; existing sandboxes stay on their pinned version until you call upgrade.
