openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /environments/{environmentId}/upgrade
Repoints the caller's active sandboxes from an older version of this environment to its latest version, scrubbing any owner secrets the new version drops and hot-pushing the new config.

# Create sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/create-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes
Provision a new cloud computer. Store the returned `sandbox.id` with your product job/session record. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make this call safe to retry after a lost response without creating a second billable sandbox.

# Fork sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/fork-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/fork
Provision a new sandbox from an existing one. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make this call safe to retry after a lost response without creating a second billable fork.

# Get sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}
Poll this endpoint after create, stop, resume, or fork operations.

# Get sandbox usage
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox-usage

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/usage
Machine time one sandbox consumed and its cost, over its life or a billing window, for per-sandbox billing of your own users.

# Get a stop
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/get-stop

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stops/{stopId}
Returns one stop of this sandbox by the id that `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stop` returned. Old stops stay readable after a resume or a later stop. Returns 404 when the id is unknown or belongs to another sandbox.

# List sandboxes
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/list-sandboxes

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes
Your sandboxes. In an organization's scope (the active wallet, `org`, or `X-Boat-Org`) the list also holds every sandbox that organization pays for, whoever created it; `createdBy` and `access` say whose it is and what you may do with it. An unknown query parameter is refused with `400 invalid_query`, which names it.

# Delete sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/permanently-delete-sandbox-data

openapi/boat-v1.yaml DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}
Confirm and accept irreversible background deletion of a sandbox.

# Recover sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/recover-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/recover
Deprecated. Power-cycle the machine of a sandbox that stopped responding, without touching its disk.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Deprecated. boat removes this endpoint soon. After a kernel crash, the machine restarts by itself in about 15 seconds. If a sandbox still does not answer, stop it with `force`, then resume it. You lose what was written after the last good snapshot. Read [A sandbox does not answer](/troubleshooting#a-sandbox-does-not-answer).


# Resume sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/resume-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/resume
Resume a stopped sandbox from its snapshot, optionally with a different environment or time-to-live.

# Share sandbox with the organization
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/share-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/share
Let every member of the organization that pays for this sandbox use it.

A sandbox that holds none of your personal logins is shared at once.

A sandbox that holds them: your personal logins (GitHub token, Claude and Codex logins,
environment secrets, the sandbox's own CLI key) are never pushed to it again and are
wiped off its disk at its next start, so a teammate never acts as you. Files you wrote
stay. The wipe is one-way: the sandbox stays like a `noEnv` sandbox from then on. A
running sandbox stays `view` for the organization until you stop and resume it
(`restartRequired`): its running programs hold your logins in memory.

Teammates never read history recorded before the share.

Only the person who created the sandbox can share it, and only a sandbox billed to
an organization. Sharing an already shared sandbox is a no-op. Undo with
`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/unshare`.


# Stop sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/stop-and-archive-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stop
Stop active work and archive/snapshot the sandbox for later resume or fork.

A stop always saves the sandbox's disk first. If that save is failing, the stop is
refused and the sandbox keeps running so your work is not discarded, we retry
automatically and email you. You are not billed for time spent in that state.

The stop is an operation: the response and the sandbox carry it as `stop`, with an
`id` and a `status`. Poll `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` until `stop.status` is
`completed`. A failed attempt shows `failing` with its `error` and is retried
until the sandbox archives; commands and prompts you send meanwhile do not cancel
it. Only a resume ends it early (`superseded`). Calling stop again while one is
pending returns the same `id`.

Set `force: true` to stop anyway, keeping the last successful snapshot and
losing everything written since then. This is irreversible; only reach for it
after a stop has already failed. A force on a stop that is already pending
escalates that stop.

A stop never fails because the sandbox is already stopping or stopped: you get `202`
with the stop in progress, or `200` with the last stop once the sandbox is stopped.
`statusUrl` is the path that reads the stop.


# Make an organization sandbox private
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/unshare-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/unshare
Make a shared organization sandbox private again, at once. Only you can then use it.
Teammates still see it in their list and can stop it. Their SSH keys are removed from
the running machine.

Nothing on the sandbox changes: files, installs and its environment stay. Undo with
`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/share`.

Only the person who created the sandbox can make it private, and only a sandbox billed
to an organization. Making a private sandbox private is a no-op.


# Update sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/sandboxes/update-sandbox

openapi/boat-v1.yaml PATCH /sandboxes/{sandboxId}
Update a sandbox's name, time-to-live, or the subdomain it is hosted on.

# Share a saved snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/create-snapshot-share

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /saved-snapshots/{name}/shares
Make a secret code that lets any Boat account create a sandbox from this saved snapshot (`boat snapshot share <name>` in the CLI). The response shows the code once; Boat stores only a hash. Re-saving the name changes what the code deploys. Removing the name removes its codes. Everything on the disk is shared, so do not keep secrets in files on it. Needs `snapshot.write`.

# Delete all snapshots of a sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/delete-sandbox-snapshots

openapi/boat-v1.yaml DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots
Delete every ordinary snapshot of one sandbox and keep the sandbox and its saved snapshots. Same as boat snapshot delete --all.

# Delete a saved snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/delete-saved-snapshot

openapi/boat-v1.yaml DELETE /saved-snapshots/{name}
Remove a saved snapshot and release its storage (`boat snapshot rm <name>` in the CLI). Sandboxes already deployed from it are unaffected.

# Get the latest snapshot of a sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/get-latest-sandbox-snapshot

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots/latest
Return the most recent completed snapshot for this sandbox, or `null` if it has none.

# Get a saved snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/get-saved-snapshot

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /saved-snapshots/{name}
Get a saved snapshot and its status. Poll this after saving one until the status settles at ready or failed.

# Get snapshot download
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/get-snapshot-download

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/download
Return time-limited signed URLs for every chunk needed to reconstruct the sandbox filesystem at this snapshot (the full chain, base through this generation), plus the inventory. Download the chunks and reassemble them as described by `reconstruct`. The `boat snapshot pull` CLI command does this for you. A snapshot whose older layers were cleaned up answers 409 `snapshot_compacted`: read its files from `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/files` instead, which `boat snapshot pull` does for you too.


# Download a file or folder from a snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/get-snapshot-file

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/files
Stream a single file's bytes, or a folder subtree as a tar archive, directly out of a snapshot, the sandbox can be stopped or archived; the machine is never contacted. Use `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/tree` to list paths, then pass one here. Paths are relative to the snapshot root (same space as `tree` entries; docker volumes under `__dockervol__/`). An empty or `/` path downloads the whole snapshot as a tar. Folder responses set `X-Snapshot-File-Count`, `X-Snapshot-Total-Size-Bytes` and `X-Snapshot-Skipped-Base-Image-Files` headers; both response shapes set `X-Snapshot-Entry-Kind` (`file` or `dir`). File responses accept a single `Range: bytes=` header and answer 206 with `Content-Range`, so large files can be downloaded in parts and resumed.

# Get snapshot file tree
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/get-snapshot-tree

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/tree
List the files and folders captured in a snapshot, with sizes. Returns a flat list of entries you can render as a tree.

# List snapshots of a sandbox
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/list-sandbox-snapshots

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots
List visible completed snapshots for one sandbox with uncapped cursor pagination.

# List saved snapshots
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/list-saved-snapshots

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /saved-snapshots
List your saved snapshots, newest first. An unknown query parameter is refused with `400 invalid_query`, which names it.

# List share codes of a saved snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/list-snapshot-shares

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /saved-snapshots/{name}/shares
List the share codes of a saved snapshot, active and revoked (`boat snapshot shares <name>` in the CLI). The full codes are not returned. Needs `snapshot.read`.

# List snapshots
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/list-snapshots

openapi/boat-v1.yaml GET /snapshots
List visible completed snapshots across all of your sandboxes using immutable ownership attribution. Pinned, deletion-scheduled, and privacy-fenced sandbox snapshots are omitted. Follow `nextCursor` through the complete history; there is no hidden 500-snapshot cap. An unknown query parameter is refused with `400 invalid_query`, which names it.

# Delete snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/permanently-delete-snapshot-data

openapi/boat-v1.yaml DELETE /snapshots/{snapshotId}
Confirm and accept irreversible background deletion of a snapshot.

# Revoke a share code
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/revoke-snapshot-share

openapi/boat-v1.yaml DELETE /saved-snapshots/{name}/shares/{shareId}
Revoke a share code (`boat snapshot unshare <name> <share-id>` in the CLI). The code stops creating new sandboxes. Sandboxes already created from it keep their own copy. Needs `snapshot.write`.

# Save a saved snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/reference/snapshots/save-saved-snapshot

openapi/boat-v1.yaml POST /saved-snapshots
Freeze a sandbox's current state under a name (`boat snapshot <id> <name>` in the CLI). Answers `202` immediately with the snapshot in `saving`; a running sandbox takes a fresh capture first, which can run minutes. Poll `GET /saved-snapshots/{name}` until the status settles at `ready` or `failed`. Reusing one of your existing names replaces that snapshot's artifact once the new save is ready.

# API overview
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/api/v1

The boat HTTP API: base URL, bearer authentication, a create-run-stop example, errors, limits and retries, pagination, idempotency, and every endpoint by group.

The base URL is `https://boat.dev/api/v1`. Send your API key as a bearer token. For typed clients, use the [Python SDK](/sdks/python) or the [TypeScript SDK](/sdks/typescript).

> [!NOTE]
>
> Used the `box` API before? Read [Migrating from Box](/migrating-from-box).

## Quick path: create, run, stop

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
export BOAT_API_BASE="https://boat.dev/api/v1"
export BOAT_API_KEY="boat_..."   # from `boat api-key create` or the dashboard

# 1. Create a sandbox (auto-stop after 1 hour)
SANDBOX_ID=$(curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":3600}' | jq -r '.sandbox.id')

# 2. Run a command. It waits up to 60 s while the sandbox starts.
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"echo hi && uname -a"}' | jq '{exitCode, stdout}'

# 3. Stop it. Boat saves the disk and stops billing.
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/stop" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

## Recommended flow

1. Create a boat API key with `boat api-key create <name> --preset ci` or in the dashboard.
2. Create a sandbox with `POST /sandboxes`. To continue earlier work, resume or fork a sandbox instead.
3. Poll `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` until the state is `ready`, `idle` or `running`.
4. Run code with `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands`. Send `stream: true` for live output, or `detached: true` for a long job.
5. To give work to an integrated agent, send `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/prompt`. Read `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/events` while it runs.
6. To expose a port, send `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/host`. To watch the screen, send `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/desktop`.
7. Stop, resume, fork or delete the sandbox as your retention policy requires.

The API does all that the boat CLI does, except billing, the wallet, seats and plans. For those, use `boat billing`, `boat wallet` or the dashboard. To run a high-frequency control loop, run your own daemon in the sandbox. See [the daemon pattern](/platform-guide/agents#bring-your-own-harness-the-daemon-pattern).

## Authentication

Send a boat API key as a bearer token on each request:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "https://boat.dev/api/v1/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

* New keys start with `boat_`. Keys that start with `box_` still work.
* Create, rotate and revoke keys with `boat api-key`, the dashboard, or the [API key endpoints](#account-and-api-keys). See [API keys](/api-keys).
* A per-sandbox key works only on its sandbox. For reads across the account, use an account key.
* `PATCH /account/data-retention` refuses API keys. It needs a browser sign-in session.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Keep API keys and desktop URLs secret. Desktop and VNC URLs can contain access tokens. Redact them before you log or store them.

## Try it (playground)

Each reference page has a **Try it** panel.

* It sends real requests to production.
* Paste a `boat_...` key. Use a [scoped key](/api-keys/scopes) with a short expiry.
* A create, fork or resume starts a sandbox that bills your account. Stop or delete it when you are done.

## Response envelope

Each JSON response has `ok` and `type`:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
{
  "ok": true,
  "type": "sandbox.list",
  "sandboxes": []
}
```

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| `ok` | `true` for success, `false` for failure. |
| `type` | Stable response discriminator, such as `sandbox.list`, `sandbox.created`, `sandbox.stopping` or `prompt.queued`. An error has `type: "sandbox.error"`. This is not the `sandbox.error` [webhook event](/webhooks). |

## Error model

The HTTP status is the primary signal. The body has a structured envelope:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
{
  "ok": false,
  "type": "sandbox.error",
  "status": 409,
  "code": "provider_not_configured",
  "message": "Prompting is locked until Codex is configured on the Agents page.",
  "error": {
    "code": "provider_not_configured",
    "message": "Prompting is locked until Codex is configured on the Agents page.",
    "status": 409,
    "details": {
      "provider": "codex",
      "setupUrl": "https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=agents"
    }
  },
  "requestId": "req_..."
}
```

| Status | Typical codes | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| `400` | `invalid_json`, `prompt_required`, `provider_required`, `invalid_name`, `no_changes`, `invalid_path`, `invalid_timeout`, `invalid_env`, `unknown_environment`, `trial_auto_stop_required`, `fast_mode_not_supported` | Fix the request. |
| `400` | `invalid_query` | A list call got a query parameter that it does not know. Remove it. |
| `400` | `machine_not_running` (desktop, browser, port hosting, SSH key) | The sandbox has no running machine. Resume it, then retry. |
| `401` | `unauthorized` | Send a valid bearer token. |
| `402` | `billing_required`, `team_member_cap_reached` | Send the user to the returned billing URL. Or ask the organization owner to raise the member's usage cap. |
| `403` | `trial_machine_class_not_allowed`, `org_suspended` | The size needs a paid plan, or the organization wallet is suspended. See [Free trial](/free-trial). |
| `404` | `not_found`, `snapshot_not_found` | The sandbox, key or saved snapshot does not exist. Refresh your local state. |
| `413` | `file_too_large` | A file read is above 5 MiB. Get a link with `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/download-url`. |
| `409` | `account_not_ready`, `provider_not_configured`, `sandbox_not_promptable`, `resume_failed`, `fork_failed`, `sandbox_resuming`, `sandbox_stopping`, `sandbox_securing`, `snapshots_disabled`, `idempotency_in_progress`, `idempotency_key_reused` | Resolve the prerequisite or the state conflict. |
| `409` | `sandbox_running_stop_first` | You asked a running sandbox to resume with a new size, environment or `noEnv`. Stop it, then resume with the change. |
| `409` | `machine_not_running`, `sandbox_starting`, `sandbox_not_ready` (commands, files, processes) | See [Commands, files and processes](#commands-files-and-processes). |
| `429` | `rate_limited`, `limit_reached`, `member_limit_reached`, `trial_compute_limit_reached`, `IP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | A limit is full. See [Limits and retries](#limits-and-retries). |
| `500` | `http_500` and other `*_failed` codes | Retry idempotent calls with jitter. Give the `requestId` when you contact support. |
| `502` | `sandbox_direct_failed` | See [Commands, files and processes](#commands-files-and-processes). |
| `503` | `no_ready_machine`, `service_unavailable`, `browser_not_ready`, `ssh_host_key_unavailable` | Retry after the `retryAfterSeconds` in the body, or after a few seconds. |

### Commands, files and processes

These calls go to the machine of the sandbox:

* `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands`
* `GET` and `PUT /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files`
* The process calls

A command sent while the sandbox starts (for example right after a resume) waits up to 60 seconds. It fails only if the sandbox is still not ready after that.

| Status | Code | Retryable | Meaning |
| - | - | - | - |
| `409` | `machine_not_running` | No | The sandbox has no machine. It is stopped, or it never started. Resume it, wait until `GET` reports `ready`, `idle` or `running`, then retry. |
| `409` | `sandbox_starting` | Yes | The sandbox was still starting after 60 seconds. Retry every few seconds. |
| `409` | `sandbox_not_ready` | No | The sandbox is in a state that cannot run commands, such as `error` or `archived`. Resume it first. |
| `502` | `sandbox_direct_failed` | See `error.details.retryable` | The machine did not complete the call. When `retryable` is `true`, send the call again. A file read or write gives the same result again. A command with message `sandbox_restoring` did not run. A command with a different message possibly ran: check its effect before you send it again. When `retryable` is `false`, the command can still be running. Do not run it again without a check. |
| `502` | `sandbox_direct_failed` with message `sandbox_restoring` | Yes | The sandbox mounts its files in the first seconds of a resume or fork. Retry after 1-3 seconds. |

The body has the flag in `error.details.retryable`:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
{
  "ok": false,
  "type": "sandbox.error",
  "status": 502,
  "code": "sandbox_direct_failed",
  "message": "sandbox_restoring",
  "error": {
    "code": "sandbox_direct_failed",
    "status": 502,
    "details": { "retryable": true, "message": "sandbox_restoring" }
  }
}
```

A synchronous command times out after 30 seconds by default. Set `timeoutSeconds` up to 600. For a server or a longer job, send `"detached": true`, then [attach](/long-running-tasks/background-commands#attach-to-a-background-process) to its output. A detached command has no time limit. The SDK helper `run_command` / `runCommand` does both steps.

## Limits and retries

The full list of limits per plan is on [Limits](/limits). The ones that a program hits:

| Plan | Starts (create, fork, resume) per minute / hour / day | Sandboxes at once |
| - | - | - |
| \$20 | 12 / 60 / 200 | 100 |
| \$100 | 30 / 210 / 840 | 300 |
| \$500 | 65 / 420 / 1,680 | 1,000 |
| \$2000 | 90 / 600 / 2,400 | 2,000 |
| [Free trial](/free-trial) | 5 / 25 / 75 | 2 |

| Limit hit | Error |
| - | - |
| Starts | `429 rate_limited` |
| Sandboxes at once | `429 limit_reached` |
| More than 10,000 HTTP requests in 60 seconds from one IP address (an open stream counts once) | `429` with `code: IP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` |

Organization limits grow with the seats. Read [Seats](/organizations/seats-and-limits#seats).

* Every `429` sends a `Retry-After` header in seconds. The body also carries the wait.
* Every answer carries the IP limit: `RateLimit-Policy: "ip";q=10000;w=60` and `RateLimit: "ip";r=<left>;t=60`.
* Create, resume and fork answers also carry your start limits: policies `starts-minute`, `starts-hour` and `starts-day`. Read [Limits and errors](/limits#retry-rules).
* `rate_limited` names the `window` (`minute`, `hour` or `day`) and the `limit`. The `starts` object shows what remains in each window.
* `IP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` carries `retryAfter` in seconds.
* A `503` carries `retryAfterSeconds`.
* A refused start does not count against your start limits.
* Check before a batch: `GET /limits` returns `canStart` and `starts.minute.remaining`.

Pace a batch of starts to the minute limit. A retry loop does not help against an hour or day limit:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import time

from boat_sdk.exceptions import ApiException

def create_with_backoff(boat, request, attempts=6):
    for attempt in range(attempts):
        try:
            return boat.create(create_sandbox_request=request)
        except ApiException as exc:
            if exc.status not in (429, 503):
                raise
            time.sleep(min(60, 2 ** attempt))
    raise RuntimeError("start limit still full")
```

## Pagination

List endpoints (`GET /sandboxes`, `GET /snapshots`, `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/events`, `GET /repos` and others) use a cursor.

* `limit`: 1 to 200 items. The default is 100.
* `sort`: `desc` (newest first, the default) or `asc`.
* The response has `pageInfo`: `nextCursor`, `hasMore` and `limit`.
* To read the next page, send `cursor=<pageInfo.nextCursor>`. Stop when `hasMore` is `false`.
* `GET /sandboxes` also filters by `namePrefix`, `name` (exact match), `label=key=value` and `state`.
* `GET /saved-snapshots` also filters by `namePrefix` and `name`.
* A query parameter that the list does not know returns `400 invalid_query`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
cursor=""
while :; do
  page=$(curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes?limit=200${cursor:+&cursor=$cursor}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY")
  echo "$page" | jq -r '.sandboxes[].id'
  [ "$(echo "$page" | jq -r '.pageInfo.hasMore')" = "true" ] || break
  cursor=$(echo "$page" | jq -r '.pageInfo.nextCursor')
done
```

## Idempotent sandbox creation

`POST /sandboxes` and `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/fork` each make a new sandbox that bills when it succeeds. A response can get lost, for example on a timeout or a `5xx` after boat accepted the sandbox. Then you do not know if you can retry.

To make create and fork safe to retry, send an `Idempotency-Key` header. Use your own value that is unique in your account, for example a UUID.

1. The first request creates the sandbox and links it to the key.
2. Each retry with the **same account, key and request body** returns that same sandbox. It does not create a second sandbox that bills.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 6f9619ff-8b86-d011-b42d-00cf4fc964ff" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"from":"web-stack","noEnv":true,"ttlSeconds":1800}'
```

| Situation | Result |
| - | - |
| Retry after a lost `202` or a `5xx` | The same key returns the original sandbox. |
| Retry while the first sandbox is still being created | `409 idempotency_in_progress`. Retry shortly with the same key. |
| Same key, different request body | `409 idempotency_key_reused`. |
| Create that failed before the sandbox existed | The key releases within about 2 minutes, so a retry can create the sandbox. |

boat keeps keys for 24 hours. A key belongs to your account, so two accounts can use the same value. Without the header, create and fork are not idempotent. In the SDKs, pass `idempotency_key=` (Python) or `idempotencyKey` (TypeScript) to `create` and `fork`.

## Sandbox lifecycle

The API reports a stopped sandbox as `archived`. The CLI shows the same state as `stopped`.

| State | Meaning | Client behavior |
| - | - | - |
| `provisioning`, `provisioned`, `cloning` | The sandbox is being created or prepared. | Poll `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}`. A command sent now waits up to 60 seconds. |
| `ready`, `idle` | The sandbox accepts commands, prompts and access. | Run commands, prompt, open the desktop, SSH. |
| `running` | An integrated agent is working. | Read events. Commands also work. |
| `archiving` | The stop is in progress: boat saves the disk. | Poll until `archived`. |
| `archived` | The sandbox is stopped. Its disk is in a snapshot. | Resume or fork. |
| `error` | Start or runtime failed. | Resume or fork it, or delete it. See [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting). |

> [!NOTE]
>
> `idle` and `running` show only work queued with `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/prompt`. Processes that you start yourself do not change the state. A sandbox can show `idle` while your own program works inside it.

## Providers, models and reasoning

`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/prompt` runs work through one of 7 agent harnesses (providers):

| Provider | Aliases | Notes |
| - | - | - |
| `codex` | | OpenAI Codex models |
| `claude-code` | `claude` | Claude Code models |
| `pi` | | Multi-model: Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenRouter or llmgateway models |
| `opencode` | | Multi-model |
| `prime-agent` | `prime` | Multi-model |
| `kimi` | `kimi-code` | Kimi Code CLI: Kimi models (subscription or Moonshot API key) |
| `mistral` | | Mistral Vibe: Mistral models (subscription or Mistral API key) |

`provider` is optional. Without it, boat uses the harness saved on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying).

**Models and reasoning efforts change over time.** Get them from the live catalog. Do not hardcode lists.

* `GET /provider-models` returns each model of each provider and the `reasoningEffort` levels that it accepts: `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Some models accept none.
* `boat prompt --help` prints the same catalog.
* `pi`, `opencode` and `prime-agent` also accept routed model ids like `openrouter:anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`.
* Without `model`, boat uses the default saved on the dashboard for that harness.

To run a prompt in fast mode, set `fast: true`. The model stays the same and answers faster. The provider bills it at its higher fast rate. Only models with `"fastMode": true` in `GET /provider-models` accept it. Other models return `400 fast_mode_not_supported`.

Before the first prompt, connect a key or a subscription on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying). Without it, the API returns `409 provider_not_configured` with a setup URL.

> [!NOTE]
>
> A sandbox runs **many conversations in parallel**. `POST /prompt` takes `new` or `conversationId` and returns the `conversationId`. `GET /events` and `POST /interrupt` take a `conversation` filter. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

## Request examples

These examples are raw HTTP. Each feature page has the CLI, TypeScript and Python form: [Snapshots](/snapshots), [Environments](/environments), [Webhooks](/webhooks), [Data retention](/data-retention), [Desktop](/desktop-streaming), [Public URLs](/hosting). The examples use the variables from [Quick path](#quick-path-create-run-stop).

Create a sandbox without auto-stop:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":null}'
```

Read the state:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" | jq -r '.sandbox.state'
```

Stream the output of a command as it runs (newline-delimited JSON):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -N -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"npm test","timeoutSeconds":600,"stream":true}'
```

Start a server in the background, then expose its port:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"python3 -m http.server 8000","detached":true}'

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/host" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"port":8000,"public":true}' | jq -r '.url'
```

Prompt the agent to work in a repository:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/prompt" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "provider": "codex",
    "prompt": "Run the tests, fix the failures, and commit the result."
  }'
```

Read the work events of the agent:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

Get a VNC desktop URL that needs no access token:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID/desktop?vnc=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"publicAccess":true}'
```

Delete a sandbox and its snapshots. The confirmation header must hold the exact sandbox id. The header name keeps the old brand. The call returns `202`, and you cannot cancel it:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$SANDBOX_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Ascii-Confirm-Delete: $SANDBOX_ID"
```

Poll `GET /deletion-operations/{operationId}` until `status` is `completed`. See [Data retention and deletion](/data-retention).

| `PUT /ai-proxy` | [Turn the AI credentials proxy on or off](/api/reference/ai-credentials/turn-the-ai-credentials-proxy-on-or-off) | `boat ai proxy on` |
| `GET /ai-usage` | [Get AI usage](/api/reference/ai-credentials/get-ai-usage) | `boat ai usage` |
| `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/ai-usage` | [Get sandbox AI usage](/api/reference/ai-credentials/get-sandbox-ai-usage) | `boat ai usage <id>` |
| `PUT /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/ai-access` | [Block or unblock sandbox AI access](/api/reference/ai-credentials/block-or-unblock-sandbox-ai-access) | `boat ai block` |

### Account and API keys

| Endpoint | Reference | CLI |
| - | - | - |
| `GET /me` | [Get current user](/api/reference/account/get-current-boat-user) | `boat status` |
| `GET /limits` | [Get account limits](/api/reference/account/get-boat-limits) | `boat limits` |

# Plan, wallet and running out
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/billing

What your plan includes and what the wallet pays for overage. Pay and auto top-up, the bonus table, billing commands, per-sandbox cost, how to control spend, and what happens when the wallet is empty.

[Pricing](/pricing) gives prices and sizes. This page tells what your plan includes and what your wallet pays. For the card, invoices, cancel and refunds, read [Card, invoices and plan changes](/billing/plan-changes).

## Plans

Your money goes to two places:

| | Plan | Wallet |
| - | - | - |
| What it is | A monthly price that your card pays | One balance in US dollars, per account or organization |
| It pays for | Your limits, and the VM time and saved snapshots that the plan includes | Overage: use past the plan |
| At the end of the billing period | Included amounts reset. Unused VM time expires. | Nothing changes. The money stays until you spend it. |
| You add to it | `boat billing plan 100` | `boat wallet pay 50`, or auto top-up |

The wallet never pays the plan. Stripe always charges the plan to your card.

For every amount, read [Plans](/pricing#plans).

Example: a \$20 plan. You use \$25 of VM time in one month. The plan pays the first \$20 (555 h of `default`). The wallet pays \$5.

## Wallet

Each account and each organization has one wallet, in US dollars.

* It pays only for what you use above your plan.
* It can go below zero during the [grace period](#running-out). The dashboard then shows what you owe, for example `-$3.20`.
* Money in your personal wallet stays personal. It does not move to an organization.
* For an organization, only the owner can add money or change auto top-up.

### Pay

Pay adds money to the wallet one time. You need a plan first.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat wallet pay 50
```

On the dashboard, open the [Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) tab, enter an amount and click **Pay**. Stripe Checkout opens.

* Whole dollars, from \$15 to \$100,000.
* The dashboard and the CLI show the bonus before you pay.

### Bonus

A payment of \$200 or more gets a bonus. Pay and auto top-up get the same bonus. The bonus grows evenly on a log scale, from 2% at \$200 to 25% at \$10,000.

| You pay | Bonus | The wallet gets |
| - | - | - |
| \$15 to \$199 | none | the same amount |
| \$200 | +2% | \$204 |
| \$500 | +7.4% | \$537 |
| \$1,000 | +11.5% | \$1,115 |
| \$2,000 | +15.5% | \$2,310 |
| \$5,000 | +20.9% | \$6,045 |
| \$10,000 | +25% | \$12,500 |
| \$100,000 | +25% | \$125,000 |

### Auto top-up

Auto top-up adds money when the wallet runs low, so your sandboxes do not stop.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat wallet card               # add a card (Stripe)
boat wallet auto-top-up 500    # add $500 each time the wallet runs low
boat wallet auto-top-up off
```

On the dashboard, open the [Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) tab, choose an amount and turn on **Auto top-up**.

* Choose an amount from \$15 to \$100,000. Each top-up gets the bonus.
* boat charges your card when the wallet drops below 10% of the amount, and never below \$5. Example: with \$500, the charge comes when the wallet drops below \$50.
* It needs a saved card and a paid plan. It does not work during the free trial.
* With more than one card, boat tries them in order.
* After 3 declined charges in a row, auto top-up turns itself off. The owner gets an email. Fix the card, then turn auto top-up on again.

## From the CLI

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat billing                   # plan, renewal date, included time left
boat billing plan 100          # start or change the plan
boat billing portal            # card and invoices (Stripe)
boat wallet                    # wallet balance, auto top-up, cards
boat wallet pay 50             # add $50 to the wallet
boat wallet auto-top-up 500    # turn on auto top-up with $500
boat wallet auto-top-up off
boat wallet card               # add a card
boat billing extra-starts fail   # starts above your plan's limits always fail, see Limits
boat billing extra-starts wallet # the wallet pays for them (default)
boat billing extra-starts on     # the wallet pays, then the next invoice
boat billing extra-starts off
boat limits                    # included time left, starts left, sandboxes at once
```

Add `--org <org>` to run them on an organization: `boat --org acme wallet pay 50`.

### From code

The wallet routes are part of the account API that the dashboard uses. Its base is `https://boat.dev/api/boat`, not `$BOAT_API_BASE`. These routes are not in the [v1 API reference](/api/v1) and can change. The API key needs `account.admin`.

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
API=https://boat.dev/api/boat
curl -sS "$API/billing/wallet" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# -> { balanceDollars, autoTopUp: { enabled, amountDollars, triggerBelowDollars, quote }, graceUntil, cards, trialWallet, trialNote? }

curl -sS "$API/billing/wallet/quote?dollars=1000" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# -> { dollars: 1000, bonusPercent: 11.5, bonusDollars: 115, creditedDollars: 1115 }

curl -sS -X POST "$API/billing/wallet/pay" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"dollars": 1000}'
# -> { url, quote }   open url to pay in Stripe Checkout

curl -sS -X POST "$API/billing/wallet/auto-top-up" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"enabled": true, "amountDollars": 500}'

curl -sS -X POST "$API/billing/wallet/cards" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# -> { url }   open url to add a card
```

* For an organization wallet, add `teamId` (the id or the name): in the query on `GET`, in the body on `POST`. Only the owner can call them.
* `pay` answers `402 subscription_required` without a plan.
* During the free trial, the wallet pays only the [AI credentials proxy](/ai-credentials#pricing). `pay` answers `409 requires_active_plan` when the proxy is off, your sandboxes did not use it in the last 7 days, and the wallet is not in debt. When it accepts, the answer has a `trialNote`. `GET` shows the case in `trialWallet`: `ai_proxy`, `end_trial` or `null` outside the trial.
* `auto-top-up` answers `409 requires_active_plan` during the trial. It answers `409 card_required` with an `addCardUrl` when no card is saved. boat keeps the amount. Open `addCardUrl`, then turn auto top-up on again.
* An amount out of range gives `400 invalid_amount`.

## Control your spend

A personal account has no dollar cap. Use these controls:

| Control | Effect |
| - | - |
| Leave auto top-up off | Spend stops at your plan and your wallet. Then the [running-out rules](#running-out) apply. |
| [Auto-stop](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop) | Each sandbox stops after its time, 1 hour by default. |
| `boat usage <id>`, the **Cost** column | Shows what one sandbox cost. Read [Per-sandbox usage](#per-sandbox-usage). |
| Per-member caps on an [organization](/organizations/seats-and-limits#per-member-caps) | Cap the time and the sandboxes of each member. |

A stopped sandbox costs nothing in VM time. Two charges continue while sandboxes are stopped:

* [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates) above your plan's included count: \$0.056 a day each, from the wallet.
* The [AI credentials proxy](/ai-credentials#pricing), while it is on: \$1 a day, from the wallet.

A stopped sandbox keeps its disk for free for at least 14 days. After that, automated retention cleanup can delete it once enabled. The job currently reports candidates without deleting them in production. Read [Keep a stopped sandbox longer than 14 days](/snapshots/stop#keep-a-stopped-sandbox-longer-than-14-days).

## Check your balance

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat wallet
boat limits
boat limits --json
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/limits" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const limits = await boat.limits();
console.log(limits.canStart, limits.starts?.day?.remaining, limits.wallet?.balanceDollars, limits.planIncluded?.vmHoursRemaining);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
limits = boat.limits()
day = getattr(limits.starts, "day", None)
print(limits.can_start, getattr(day, "remaining", None), getattr(limits.wallet, "balance_dollars", None), getattr(limits.plan_included, "vm_hours_remaining", None))
```

`BOAT_API_BASE` is `https://boat.dev/api/v1`. `boat` is the SDK client from the [Quickstart](/quickstart#from-code). For every field, read [Get limits](/api/reference/account/get-boat-limits).

## Per-sandbox usage

Every sandbox meters its own machine time. A platform can bill its own users from the same numbers that your plan and your wallet pay.

In the dashboard:

* The **Sandboxes** page has a **Cost** column: what each sandbox cost this calendar month (UTC). Sort by it to find the most expensive one.
* The **Billing** page lists **Cost by sandbox this month**, most expensive first, with the total. For an organization, it lists every sandbox the organization pays for. One **Deleted sandboxes** line holds the machine time of sandboxes you deleted this month.

For all sandboxes in one call, add `include=cost` to the list. Deleted sandboxes are not in the list but still billed — add `include=deletedCost` (comma-separated with `cost` if you want both) for their total:

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes?include=cost,deletedCost" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# -> sandboxes: [{ id, name, type, ..., cost: { since, seconds, dollars } }]
#    deletedCost: { since, seconds, dollars }   (sandboxes deleted this month)
```

Read one sandbox over any window, while it runs or after it stops:

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat usage bx_23456789
boat usage bx_23456789 --since 2026-09-01 --until 2026-10-01
boat usage bx_23456789 --json
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_23456789/usage?since=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z&until=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const usage = await boat.usage({ sandboxId: "bx_23456789", since: "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z", until: "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z" });
console.log(usage.seconds, usage.dollars, usage.running);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
usage = boat.usage("bx_23456789", since="2026-09-01T00:00:00Z", until="2026-10-01T00:00:00Z")
print(usage.seconds, usage.dollars, usage.running)
```

| Field | Means |
| - | - |
| `seconds` | Billable machine time, with the size already applied. A `large` sandbox that ran ten minutes reads 1200. |
| `dollars` | `seconds` at list price. |
| `running` | `true` while the sandbox runs and the number grows. `false` after it stops, and while a refused stop keeps the meter paused. |

* boat never counts stopped time.
* boat does not count time after a [refused stop](/snapshots/stop#when-a-stop-is-refused).
* Omit `since` and `until` to get the full life of the sandbox.
* If a billing month ends while a sandbox runs, boat splits that stretch between the two months.

For every field, read [Get sandbox usage](/api/reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox-usage).

## AI credentials proxy

The [AI credentials proxy](/ai-credentials#the-ai-credentials-proxy) is paid from the wallet:

| Charge | Price | Paid by |
| - | - | - |
| Each UTC day the proxy is on | \$1 | The wallet of the account with the switch on |
| Proxied requests | \$1 per 1,000 | The wallet each sandbox bills |

`boat ai usage` and `GET /ai-usage` show the requests per sandbox, and `dollars` is their charge.

## Organizations

A team shares one plan and one wallet through an organization. Everything on this page applies to an organization in the same way. Read [Organizations](/organizations).

## Running out

When the wallet is empty:

* [Extra starts](/limits#extra-starts) fail with `rate_limited`, unless they are on your invoice.
* Saved snapshots above the included count get 7 days. Then boat deletes them. Read [When your wallet is empty](/snapshots/templates#when-your-wallet-is-empty).

When the wallet is empty and the plan's included time is used:

1. You get a **24-hour grace period**.
2. Your sandboxes keep running. boat sends you an email. Add money before anything stops.
3. If you do not pay in that window, boat stops your running sandboxes. Each stop takes a snapshot. boat stops them earlier if the grace period adds more new debt than 25% of the plan price, or \$50 on smaller plans.
4. Nothing is lost. Resume the sandboxes after you add money.

During the grace period, the wallet goes below zero:

* The wallet shows what you owe, for example `-$3.20`.
* Your next payment pays that amount first.
* You pay for exactly the seconds that you used.

If your plan ends and the wallet has money, running sandboxes keep running on the wallet. An organization drops to the limits of one seat.

## Related

* [Pricing](/pricing)
* [Card, invoices and plan changes](/billing/plan-changes)
* [Limits and errors](/limits)
* [Free trial](/free-trial)

* [FAQ](/faq)


# Card, invoices and plan changes
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/billing/plan-changes

Change your card, get invoices and receipts, add a VAT ID, upgrade or downgrade, cancel the plan, refunds, and move a plan between a personal account and an organization.

boat bills through Stripe. Open the Stripe billing portal for your card and your invoices:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat billing portal
```

On the dashboard: [Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) > **Manage billing**.

## Card, invoices and receipts

| You want to | Do this |
| - | - |
| Change the card | Open the portal. Add the new card and make it the default. |
| Pay an invoice that failed | Open the portal. Pay the open invoice there. This never charges twice. |
| Get invoices and receipts | Open the portal. Every invoice and receipt is there. |
| Add a VAT or tax ID | Enter it at checkout. It goes on every invoice. To add it later, [contact support](/support). |
| Know the charge on your bank statement | Statements show **DEDALE AI**, the company behind boat. |

* Checkout does not add VAT or sales tax on top of the plan price.
* For an organization, add `--org <org>`: `boat --org acme billing portal`. Only the owner can open it.

## Upgrade or downgrade

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat billing plan          # list the plans
boat billing plan 100      # move to the $100 plan
```

On the dashboard, click **Upgrade to …** or **Downgrade to …** on the Billing tab. The confirm dialog shows the exact charge.

A change applies at once, up or down:

1. A new billing month starts that day.
2. Stripe credits the unused part of the old plan: the smaller of the unused days and the unused included time.
3. Stripe charges the full price of the new plan, minus that credit.
4. The new plan's limits and included time apply at once. The time that you used so far counts against the old plan.

* Example: on day 10 of the \$500 plan, you used all the included time. No included time is unused, so the credit is zero. The invoice shows the credit for the unused days and a line for the included time used, and they cancel out.
* When the credit is larger than the new price, Stripe charges nothing. The rest stays as credit for your next invoices.
* If the card fails, the plan does not change. Your sandboxes keep running on the old plan.
* A plan change during the [free trial](/free-trial) ends the trial.

## Cancel the plan

Run `boat billing cancel`. Or open [Dashboard > Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) and click **Cancel plan**.

To pause, take the offer in that step, or run `boat billing cancel --keep-disks`. The plan stops, you pay nothing more, and boat keeps the disks of your stopped sandboxes for 90 days after the paid month, not 14. To resume them, subscribe again.

| When | What happens |
| - | - |
| Until the end of the paid month | Nothing changes. The plan does not renew. Click **Keep plan active** to undo the cancel. |
| At the end of the paid month, with money in the wallet | Running sandboxes keep running on the wallet. An organization drops to the limits of one seat. |
| At the end of the paid month, with an empty wallet | boat stops your running sandboxes. Their disks stay. Resume them after you subscribe again. |

* boat does not refund the rest of the month after a cancel.
* The money in your wallet stays on your account.
* Saved snapshots stay. Your included count follows the new plan. Each one above it costs \$0.056 a day from the wallet.
* To subscribe again, pick a plan on the Billing tab. You get no second trial.
* An organization owner cancels the organization plan in the Stripe portal: `boat --org acme billing portal`.

To cancel a trial, read [Free trial](/free-trial#cancel-the-trial). To close the account and delete your data, read [Close your account](/data-retention/close-account). A close cancels the plan at once.

## Refunds

boat does not refund unused time in general. boat refunds by itself in these cases:

| Case | Refund |
| - | - |
| You [move a personal plan to an organization](/organizations/move-personal-plan) | The unused share of the month, to your card |
| Stripe takes a payment after the plan was cancelled | The full payment |
| A stop is refused because a snapshot failed | No charge for that time. You do not need to ask. |

For any other case, [contact support](/support) with the invoice number.

## Move a plan between personal and organization

| From | To | How |
| - | - | - |
| Personal | Organization | `boat --org acme org migrate`. Read [Move a personal plan in](/organizations/move-personal-plan). |
| Organization | Personal | No single command. See the steps below. |

To move from an organization back to a personal plan:

1. Make your personal account the active wallet: `boat org switch personal`.
2. Start a personal plan: `boat billing plan 20`.
3. Optional: delete the organization with `boat org delete`. You must be the owner and the last member.

When you delete the organization:

* Its plan ends at once. boat does not refund the rest of the month.
* Each sandbox goes back to the personal billing of the person who created it.

## Seats

An organization pays one plan price per seat. Seat changes are prorated. Read [Seats, limits and caps](/organizations/seats-and-limits).


# CI with boat
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/ci

Run GitHub Actions jobs on boat sandboxes with runs-on: boat, or drive boat from any CI with the CLI.

Two ways to run CI on boat:

| Way | Setup | Use it when |
| - | - | - |
| [GitHub Actions runners](#github-actions-runners-runs-on-boat) | Install the boat CI GitHub App, change `runs-on` | Your CI is GitHub Actions |
| [The CLI from any CI](#the-cli-from-any-ci) | An API key and a few `boat` commands | GitLab CI, CircleCI, Buildkite, or one step of a GitHub job |

## GitHub Actions runners: `runs-on: boat`

Each job gets a fresh sandbox, billed per second, deleted when the job ends.

CI needs the \$20/month plan or higher. On the free trial, or without a plan, boat refuses each job once and says why in `boat ci` and on the dashboard. Start a plan, then re-run the job.

### Set up in 2 steps

1. Install the boat CI GitHub App on your GitHub organization or account. Pick the repositories:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ci connect            # jobs bill the wallet in scope (see `boat org`)
boat ci connect --org acme # jobs bill the acme organization
```

The command opens GitHub in your browser. GitHub asks you to authorize the app: boat uses that to check that you can manage the installation.

GitHub lets an app add runners to one repository only with the repository permission **Administration: write**. If your organization cannot grant it, install **Boat CI for orgs** instead: on the CI tab, click **Connect an organization without repo admin**. It needs only the organization permission **Self-hosted runners: write**. Boat makes one runner group per repository, named `boat <repository>`, so a runner only takes jobs of its own repository. It works on GitHub organizations only.

If the app is already installed, an owner of the GitHub organization can link it without reinstalling:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ci connect --org acme --account acme-github
```

Use the GitHub account name after `--account`, not the repository name. The owner can open a link generated by a boat organization admin. After authorizing on GitHub, boat shows which boat account will own the jobs, and nothing is linked until the owner confirms. Only open a link from someone you trust: that account can read the jobs' logs and sandboxes. The CI tab also has **Already installed on GitHub? Link it here**.

2. In your workflow, change `runs-on`:

```yaml theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: boat          # was: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci && npm test
```

GitHub Actions secrets, `services:`, `container:`, `actions/cache` and `actions/upload-artifact` work as on GitHub-hosted runners. Boat does not pass your own environment to the job: no saved variables, secret files, GitHub token or model provider keys. Use GitHub Actions secrets for anything the job needs. Run `boat ci` to see the last jobs.

### Sizes and options

| Label | Sandbox |
| - | - |
| `boat-small` | `small`: 2 vCPU, 4 GB |
| `boat` | `default`: 4 vCPU, 8 GB |
| `boat-large` | `large`: 8 vCPU, 16 GB |
| `boat-xlarge` | `xlarge`: 16 vCPU, 32 GB |

A job can use the RAM of its size plus all the swap on the sandbox: 4 GB from boat, plus any swapfile a step adds. When a process needs more, the kernel kills it, and boat adds an "Out of memory on Boat" warning to the run. Then use a larger size. The job runs in `$HOME/actions-runner/_work`, under `$HOME` as on GitHub-hosted runners.

Add options after the size with `/`, for example `runs-on: boat-large/from=ci-base/debug`:

| Option | Effect |
| - | - |
| `from=<name>` | Start from a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates), with your toolchain and dependencies in place. Boat keeps the disk and removes the owner secrets before the job starts. Prepare it as in [step 2 below](#2-prepare-a-saved-snapshot-one-time). |
| `debug` | When the job fails, boat keeps the sandbox for 30 minutes. Run `boat ssh <id>` to look around. |
| Every sandbox has `/dev/kvm`, so virtual machines need no option. An old `/kvm` option still works and changes nothing. |

A label with an unknown option never runs: boat refuses the job and `boat ci` shows the reason.

### Docker, containers and virtual machines

Each job runs on a full Linux virtual machine with Docker, not in a container:

* `docker build`, `docker run` and `docker compose` work in steps.
* `services:` containers (Postgres, Redis) start next to the job, on `localhost`.
* `container:` runs the steps inside the image that you name.
* The job can start its own virtual machines: QEMU, Firecracker, the Android emulator. Every sandbox has `/dev/kvm`.

Each job starts from a clean sandbox, so Docker pulls its images again. A `from=` snapshot does not remove the pulls: boat pulls registry images again at each start. See [What a snapshot saves](/snapshots/whats-saved#docker).

### Android emulator tests

The emulator is hardware-accelerated on every sandbox. Nothing is boat-specific: the job installs the Android SDK and accepts its license, as on any runner:

```yaml theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
jobs:
  android:
    runs-on: boat-large
    steps:
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v5
        with: { distribution: temurin, java-version: 17 }
      - uses: android-actions/setup-android@v4
      - uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          script: ./gradlew connectedCheck
```

An Android 14 emulator boots in about 25 seconds. Use `setup-android@v4`: `@v3` asks the SDK for the `tools` package, which Google removed, so it fails on every runner that does not ship an Android SDK.

### Windows programs with Wine

boat has no Windows runners. To build Windows executables and test them, cross-compile on Linux and run the `.exe` with [Wine](https://www.winehq.org/):

```yaml theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
jobs:
  windows:
    runs-on: boat
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends wine64 mingw-w64
      - run: x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc main.c -o app.exe && /usr/lib/wine/wine64 app.exe
```

The install takes about 17 seconds. On Ubuntu 24.04 the `wine64` package puts its program at `/usr/lib/wine/wine64`, not on the `PATH`. For Rust MSVC targets, [cargo-xwin](https://github.com/rust-cross/cargo-xwin) builds on Linux and `cargo xwin test` runs the tests with Wine. Wine runs most console programs and tests. It is not Windows: GUI, driver and installer tests need a real Windows machine.

### See and debug jobs

The **CI on Boat VMs** tab of the dashboard shows your setup steps, the repositories the app can see, every job with its wait, run time, cost and log, and why a job did not run. The CLI and the API show the same data:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ci                                   # setup steps, problems, 7-day stats, last jobs
boat ci --repo acme/api --state failed    # filter: --account, --repo, --state all|active|failed, --limit
boat ci repos                             # repositories the app can see, and their status
boat ci job <job id>                      # wait, run time, cost, sandbox, error
boat ci logs <job id> --follow            # the GitHub log, live while the job runs
```

Add `--json` for the full data. In the [API](/api/v1) and the [SDKs](/sdks/overview):

| API | TypeScript | Python |
| - | - | - |
| [`GET /ci`](/api/reference/ci/get-ci-overview) | `getCiOverview({ repo, state })` | `get_ci_overview(repo=, state=)` |
| [`POST /ci/connect`](/api/reference/ci/connect-ci-github) | `connectCiGithub({})` | `connect_ci_github(...)` |
| [`POST /ci/public`](/api/reference/ci/set-ci-public-repos) | `setCiPublicRepos({ account, allow, users })` | `set_ci_public_repos(...)` |
| [`GET /ci/jobs/{jobId}`](/api/reference/ci/get-ci-job) | `getCiJob({ jobId })` | `get_ci_job(job_id)` |
| [`GET /ci/jobs/{jobId}/logs`](/api/reference/ci/get-ci-job-log) | `getCiJobLog({ jobId })` | `get_ci_job_log(job_id)` |

Reading needs an API key with `account.read`; connecting GitHub and public repositories need `account.admin`.

Each job shows its true state and its reason: what it waits for, or why it did not run. When boat refuses a job, it says why: no paid plan, an unknown label such as `boat-huge`, a public repository, a GitHub account not linked to boat, or a sandbox boat cannot create (for example a `from=` snapshot that does not exist). The job then shows as refused, with the reason, in all three places. A full minute start limit or too many running sandboxes do not refuse the job: boat retries every 15 seconds. For the hour and day start limits, read [What happens at a limit](#what-happens-at-a-limit).

Each job is a normal sandbox named `ci-<repo>-<job id>`. It shows in the dashboard and in `boat list` while it runs. Run `boat ssh <id>` on a running job, or on a failed `/debug` job.

### Public repositories

Jobs from public repositories do not run on boat by default. Anyone can open a pull request on a public repository, and its jobs would run on your bill.

Turn them on per GitHub account, and list the GitHub users whose runs may use boat:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ci public my-account on --users "me, @a-teammate"
boat ci public my-account            # show the setting
boat ci public my-account off
```

The CI tab in the dashboard has the same switch. It checks each name on GitHub as you type.

* A run uses boat only when both its author and the user who started it (for example a re-run) are on the list. A pull request from someone else is refused with the reason, even when you re-run it.
* `--anyone` clears the list: every run uses boat, pull requests from forks too. To keep that safe, set "Require approval for all outside collaborators" in the repository's Actions settings on GitHub.
* Only the person who linked the account, or an owner or admin of its org, can change this.

### Safety

* Jobs from public repositories do not run on boat unless you [turn them on](#public-repositories).
* Each job starts with your Boat [environment](/environments) off. The job gets no Boat environment variables, secret files, GitHub token or model provider keys. A `/from=` snapshot keeps its disk, but Boat removes the owner secrets before the job starts.
* Use GitHub Actions secrets for job secrets. `runs-on: boat` jobs do not read a Boat environment, so values set with `boat env set-var` are not present.
* A job runs for at most 6 hours, the GitHub limit. boat deletes any CI sandbox that outlives its job.
* A job past your [start limits](#what-happens-at-a-limit) waits or fails. It depends on the limit.

## The CLI from any CI

Each CI job creates one sandbox, runs the tests in it, and deletes it. `boat exec` exits with the exit code of the tests, so the job fails when the tests fail.

### 1. Create a CI key and a secret

Create a key with the `ci` preset. It can create, use and delete sandboxes. Then store it as a repository secret:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat api-key create github-ci --preset ci --ttl 90d
gh secret set BOAT_API_KEY      # paste the boat_... secret that the command printed once
```

The key expires after 90 days. Rotate it with `boat api-key rotate <id>`. See [API keys](/api-keys).

### 2. Prepare a saved snapshot (one time)

Install your toolchain and dependencies once. Save the result as a saved snapshot. Each CI sandbox then starts with them in place:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
id=$(boat new --json | jq -r 'select(.event == "ready") | .id')
boat exec "$id" --timeout 600 -- bash -lc 'sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-client'
boat exec "$id" --timeout 600 -- bash -lc 'docker pull postgres:16 && docker create --name keep-postgres postgres:16'
boat snapshot "$id" ci-base
boat delete "$id" --yes
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> **A saved snapshot keeps only the Docker images that a container uses.** A plain `docker pull` is lost. Create a container from each image that you need, as above: `docker create --name keep-<x> <image>`. The container does not need to run. boat pulls registry images again at each start, so a large image adds start time. See [What a snapshot saves](/snapshots/whats-saved#docker).

10 saved snapshots are free. Run the same steps again to update `ci-base`: a save with the same name replaces it. See [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

### 3. The workflow

```yaml .github/workflows/boat-tests.yml theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
name: Tests on Boat

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      BOAT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.BOAT_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install the Boat CLI
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
          curl -fsSL "https://boat.dev/api/boat/cli/download?platform=linux-x64&channel=prod" \
            -o "$HOME/.local/bin/boat"
          chmod +x "$HOME/.local/bin/boat"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Sign in
        run: printf '%s' "$BOAT_API_KEY" | boat login --key-stdin --json

      - name: Create a sandbox from the saved snapshot
        id: sandbox
        run: |
          id=$(boat new --from ci-base --type small --ttl 1800 --json | jq -r 'select(.event == "ready") | .id')
          test -n "$id"
          echo "id=$id" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Copy the code
        run: |
          git archive --format=tar.gz -o /tmp/src.tgz HEAD
          boat scp /tmp/src.tgz "${{ steps.sandbox.outputs.id }}:/home/user/src.tgz"
          boat exec "${{ steps.sandbox.outputs.id }}" "mkdir -p repo && tar xzf src.tgz -C repo"

      - name: Run the tests
        run: |
          set +e
          boat exec "${{ steps.sandbox.outputs.id }}" --cwd repo --timeout 600 --stream -- bash -lc 'npm ci && npm test'
          code=$?
          boat scp "${{ steps.sandbox.outputs.id }}:/home/user/repo/junit.xml" ./junit.xml || true
          exit $code

      - name: Delete the sandbox
        if: always() && steps.sandbox.outputs.id != ''
        run: boat delete "${{ steps.sandbox.outputs.id }}" --yes --json
```

What each part does:

| Part | Why |
| - | - |
| Static binary download | The install script opens a browser sign-in. The binary needs none. Use `platform=linux-arm64` on an ARM runner. |
| `boat login --key-stdin` | Keeps the key out of the process list. |
| `--from ci-base` | Starts with the toolchain and dependencies in place. |
| `--ttl 1800` | Auto-stop after 30 minutes, if the delete step never runs. |
| `--timeout 600 --stream` | Stops the tests after 600 seconds. `--stream` prints the output live. `--timeout 0` = no limit. |
| `set +e` and `exit $code` | Copies the test report out, then fails the job with the exit code of the tests. |
| `if: always()` | Deletes the sandbox also when a step failed or the job was cancelled. Billing stops at the delete. |

Use the sandbox ID in every command. The `current` alias does not work in CI: each step runs in a new shell.

### Tests that run longer than 10 minutes

Give a longer `--timeout`, or `--timeout 0` for no limit. The CLI prints the output live until the command ends, and exits with its exit code:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec "$id" --cwd repo --timeout 0 -- bash -lc 'npm run test:e2e'
```

See [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands).

### One command instead of the steps above

`boat run` creates the sandbox, copies the checkout in, runs the tests, prints the cost and deletes the sandbox. It exits with the exit code of the tests:

```yaml theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
      - name: Run the tests
        run: boat run --from ci-base --type small --push . -- bash -lc 'npm ci && npm test'
```

The copy holds the files that git tracks and the new files that `.gitignore` does not exclude. A cancelled job deletes the sandbox too. If the runner dies, the sandbox stops by itself within 15 minutes. See [`boat run`](/cli-reference#boat-run-command).

### Fast apt-get: use the French Ubuntu mirror

GitHub Actions scripts often set `azure.archive.ubuntu.com`. From a sandbox, that mirror is slow. Use `fr.archive.ubuntu.com`:

| Mirror | Speed from a sandbox |
| - | - |
| `fr.archive.ubuntu.com` | about 95 MB/s |
| `archive.ubuntu.com` (sandbox default) | 23 to 105 MB/s |
| `azure.archive.ubuntu.com` | 3 to 87 MB/s |

Run this before `apt-get install`, or put it in the saved snapshot:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sudo sed -i 's#http://[a-z.]*archive.ubuntu.com#http://fr.archive.ubuntu.com#g' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources
sudo apt-get update
```

## Many jobs at once: start limits

Each job starts one sandbox. Your plan includes a number of starts. Create, fork and resume each count as a start.

| Plan | Starts included per minute / hour / day | Sandboxes at once |
| - | - | - |
| \$20 | 12 / 60 / 200 | 100 |
| \$100 | 30 / 210 / 840 | 300 |
| \$500 | 65 / 420 / 1,680 | 1,000 |
| \$2000 | 90 / 600 / 2,400 | 2,000 |
| [Free trial](/free-trial) | 5 / 25 / 75 | 2 |

* Above the included number, a job uses an [extra start](/limits#extra-starts).
* A matrix of 30 jobs on the \$20 plan: 12 start free. With money in the wallet, the other 18 cost \$0.90 and start in the same minute. Without extra starts, all 30 need about 3 minutes to start. To stay free, cap it with `strategy.max-parallel: 12`.
* To fail at once when no machine is free, add `--fail-fast` to `boat new`. Retry the job later.

### What happens at a limit

This applies when no extra start can run.

| Limit | `runs-on: boat` job | `boat new` in your own CI |
| - | - | - |
| Minute | Waits. boat retries every 15 seconds | Fails with `rate_limited` and `window: minute` |
| Hour | Waits when a start frees within 15 minutes of the job's arrival. If not, fails with the reason | Fails with `rate_limited` and `window: hour` |
| Day | Fails at once, with the reason | Fails with `rate_limited` and `window: day` |

A refused start does not count as a start. All limits and how to raise them: [Limits](/limits).

A job that a limit stopped shows as **paused** in `boat ci` and the CI tab, not as failed. On GitHub it shows the title "Paused by plan limit" and what you can do. It does not restart by itself, and turning on extra starts does not restart it. A full limit shows above the job list in the CI tab and first in `boat ci`. `boat ci` prints the command, and the CI tab links to the run. `boat ci --all` shows every job and every limit:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
gh run rerun <run-id> --failed --repo <owner>/<repo>
```

Run it after the job fails on GitHub, or use **Re-run failed jobs** on the GitHub run page.

## Cost

A job costs VM time, and an extra start when it falls above the included starts.

* boat bills each second that the sandbox runs. A `small` sandbox costs \$0.018 an hour. A 6-minute run costs about \$0.002. A deleted sandbox costs nothing more.
* The plan price comes back as VM time. A team pays the higher of the plan price and its VM time, plus its extra starts.

### Worked examples

These examples use today's prices. They assume 32 jobs per developer per workday, 22 workdays a month, 6 minutes per job on `default`, and 16% of the day's jobs in the busiest hour.

| Developers | Jobs a day | Busiest hour | VM time a month | Plan | Extra starts a month | Total a month | Per job |
| - | - | - | - | - | - | - | - |
| 5 | 160 | 26 | \$13 | \$20 | \$0 | \$20 | \$0.006 |
| 20 | 640 | 102 | \$51 | \$100 | \$0 | \$100 | \$0.007 |
| 100 | 3,200 | 512 | \$253 | \$500 | \$1,302 | \$1,802 | \$0.026 |

* At 100 developers, the day goes above 1,680 included starts. 840 starts cost \$0.03 and 680 cost \$0.05, which is \$59.20 a day.
* The same team on the \$2000 plan pays \$2,528.
* The busiest hour (512) is above the 420 included starts of the \$500 plan. Starts in that hour that are still inside the day limit add up to \$61 a month.
* At this volume, extra starts set the bill, not the job length. 2-minute `small` jobs still cost \$1,802 a month. A runner that bills per minute can cost less for short jobs at this volume.

See [Pricing](/pricing).

## Private repositories and secrets

A `runs-on: boat` job uses GitHub Actions secrets. It does not read a Boat environment.

The CLI workflow above copies the checked-out code, so its sandbox needs no GitHub access. To give those tests secrets, set them on a Boat [environment](/environments) and start with `--environment <name>`, or pass one value with `-e KEY=VALUE`. Check that a value arrived:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec "$id" 'echo ${DATABASE_URL:+set}'
```

An environment that is safe for third parties withholds all your secrets. See [Secrets](/environments/secrets).

## Other CI systems

The steps are the same in GitLab CI, CircleCI or Buildkite: download the binary, sign in with `--key-stdin`, `boat new --json`, `boat exec`, and `boat delete --yes` in a step that always runs. In code, use the [Python](/sdks/python#run-one-job-and-delete-the-sandbox) or [TypeScript](/sdks/typescript#run-one-job-and-delete-the-sandbox) SDK instead. Each page has the same job as `boat run`: create, copy the code in, run with no time limit, print the cost, delete.


# CLI reference
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/cli-reference

Every boat CLI command and flag: install, sign in, create, run, stop, resume, fork, snapshots, public URLs, environments, prompts, billing. JSON output for scripts and CI.

## Install the CLI

```bash macOS theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -fsSL https://boat.dev/install | sh
```

```bash Linux theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -fsSL https://boat.dev/install | sh
```

```powershell Windows theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
irm https://boat.dev/install.ps1 | iex
```

The installer signs you in and adds a shell function. **Open a new terminal** after the install. See [Quickstart](/quickstart).

On macOS and Linux, the installer also links the binary into `~/.local/bin`. Agents and CI jobs run shells that read no startup file, and these shells find `boat` there when `~/.local/bin` is on their `PATH`. Ubuntu and Debian add it at login.

To update, run `boat self-update`. The CLI also updates itself, at most every 6 hours, after a command ends. It never asks a question and never changes a command that runs. To keep one version for a whole script or benchmark, set `BOAT_NO_UPDATE=1` or pass `--no-update`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Used the `box` CLI before? Read [Migrating from Box](/migrating-from-box).

***

## Global flags

These flags work with all commands:

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--api-url <URL>` | Use a different API endpoint (env: `BOAT_API_URL`) |
| `--org <ID_OR_NAME>` | Run this command against an organization wallet (env: `BOAT_ORG`). The scope that you set with `boat org switch` does not change. |
| `--json` | Print JSON for machines instead of text for people |
| `--no-update` | Skip the automatic update (env: `BOAT_NO_UPDATE=1`) |

When you pipe or redirect the output, `--json` turns on automatically. Scripts get JSON without the flag, not the tables that this page shows. Some examples pipe the JSON into `jq`. Install `jq` if you do not have it.

A command that takes a sandbox ID also accepts two aliases:

| Alias | Sandbox |
| - | - |
| `current` | The last sandbox that you created or forked in this shell. `boat resume` does not change it. It needs the shell function that the installer adds. Without an ID, `boat ssh`, `boat exec` and `boat prompt` use it too. |
| `self` | The sandbox that the CLI runs inside, when you use the CLI in a sandbox |

In a script or a CI job, `current` does not work: each command runs in a new process without the shell function. Pass the sandbox ID.

***

## In scripts and CI

In an application, use the [Python or TypeScript SDK](/sdks/overview) or the [HTTP API](/api/v1) with a `BOAT_API_KEY`. You do not install a binary, and the responses have types. Use the CLI in shell scripts and CI jobs.

Sign in without the key in the process arguments. Then read JSON from stdout:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat login --key-stdin --json <<< "$BOAT_API_KEY"
sandbox_id="$(boat new --json | jq -r 'select(.event == "ready") | .id')"
trap 'boat delete "$sandbox_id" --yes --json' EXIT
boat exec "$sandbox_id" --timeout 600 "npm test"   # exits with the exit code of npm test
```

For a full GitHub Actions workflow, see [CI with boat](/ci). The [endpoint tables](/api/v1#endpoint-reference) give the API call of each command.

Most commands print one JSON object. These commands print JSON Lines, one object per line:

* `boat new`
* `boat prompt`
* `boat events`, with or without `--follow`
* `boat conversations`

Parse JSON Lines one line at a time.

When a command fails in `--json` mode, it prints a last line and exits with a non-zero code:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
{"event":"error","error":"...","code":"...","status":...}
```

The line has `code` and `status` when the boat API refused the request. Errors in the arguments go to stderr, and they are possibly not JSON.

To use the CLI in a Docker image, do these steps:

1. Download the static binary for the architecture of the image.
2. Sign in when the container starts.

```dockerfile theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
FROM debian:bookworm-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl openssh-client \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN set -eu; \
    case "$(uname -m)" in \
        x86_64|amd64) arch=x64 ;; \
        arm64|aarch64) arch=arm64 ;; \
        *) echo "unsupported arch: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    curl -fsSL "https://boat.dev/api/boat/cli/download?platform=linux-${arch}&channel=prod" -o /usr/local/bin/boat; \
    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/boat
```

```sh theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
#!/bin/sh
# entrypoint
set -eu
printf '%s' "$BOAT_API_KEY" | boat login --key-stdin --json
exec node server.js
```

***

## Shell completion
