`boat completions <shell>` prints a completion script for bash, zsh, fish, or PowerShell. The script completes these values:

* Subcommands.
* The IDs of your live sandboxes, and `current` and `self`.

The script keeps the results for 15 seconds, so the next tabs are instant.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
# bash: add to ~/.bashrc
eval "$(boat completions bash)"

# zsh: add to ~/.zshrc, after compinit
eval "$(boat completions zsh)"

# fish
boat completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/boat.fish

# PowerShell: add to $PROFILE
boat completions powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
```

***

## Authentication

### `boat onboard`

Set up this computer. The command does these steps:

1. It signs you in through the browser.
2. It saves your token.
3. It asks only for what your account still needs: the third-party safety answer and the plan checkout.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat onboard
boat onboard --google
boat onboard --email you@example.com
```

It asks which sign-in method to use: GitHub, Google, a 6-digit code that it sends to your email, or AgentID. `--google`, `--email` and `--agentid` give that answer in advance. See [Quickstart](/account#sign-in-methods).

You can run it again safely. If this computer is already signed in, it keeps that session and does not start a new sign-in. A method flag (`--google`, `--email`, `--agentid`) signs in again. On a new install or a second computer, it finds the account that you already have. It skips each step that this account has done:

| Your account already has | What `boat onboard` does |
| - | - |
| An active plan | Prints your plan and usage. **No Stripe Checkout**, no second subscription. |
| A plan with depleted usage | Points you at the billing dashboard to add money to the wallet or change tier, instead of starting another plan. |
| Answered what your sandboxes are for | Does not ask that question again, whichever way you answered. |
| A past subscription | Offers checkout without promising a 7-day trial, which Stripe grants once per customer. |

boat records your answer on the environment when you give it. boat keeps both answers, not only "a platform of mine". A plan never counts as an answer, because the dashboard checkout does not ask the question.

See [Reinstalling, or a second machine](/account#reinstalling-or-a-second-machine).

### `boat login [key]`

Sign in with an API token that you already have. Without a key, the command starts a sign-in in the browser. GitHub is the default. Google, email and AgentID also work.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat login
boat login --google
boat login --email you@example.com
boat login --agentid
boat login --key-stdin <<< "$BOAT_API_KEY"
boat login boat_abc123...
```

`--key-stdin` reads the token from standard input, not from the command line. Other users on the host can read the process arguments, so the token stays out of them. Use `--key-stdin` when you sign in without a person present. You can also give the token as an argument. You cannot use both.

Without a key, the CLI prints a URL and a code, and opens the URL. In a terminal, it waits until you finish in the browser or the link expires after 15 minutes. `--email` sends a code to that address. If you omit the address, the browser page asks for it. boat refuses disposable email domains.

Without a terminal (an AI agent, a script), sign-in takes two commands:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat login --json            # prints the URL, the code and expiresAt, then exits
boat onboard --wait --json   # waits for the browser step, saves the session, prints the links
```

Run the first command again and it shows the same link and code. It never replaces a pending link, because the code that the user already has then reaches nobody. `boat login --new` starts a new link on purpose and prints a `login_replaced` event. `boat login --wait` also waits, like `boat onboard --wait`.

All methods sign in to the same account only if they are already **connected** to it. A method that you never used before starts a new account, even when the email is the same. Add connections in [Dashboard > Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) instead. See [Quickstart](/account#sign-in-methods).

To create production API keys, run `boat api-key create` or use the API Keys page of the dashboard. For key management, see [API Keys](/api-keys). For Docker and CI setup, see [In scripts and CI](#in-scripts-and-ci).

### `boat api-key`

Create and manage API keys for SDKs, CI, and other projects.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat api-key create my-project --ttl 90d --preset ci
boat api-key create my-project --ttl 7d --sandbox bx_123 --actions sandbox.read,exec
boat api-key list                # scope, expiry, last used
boat api-key list --all          # also platform-managed per-sandbox machine keys
boat api-key usage <id>          # 30-day requests and live resource count
boat api-key usage <id> --verbose  # plus sandboxes/Agents split and created list
boat api-key rotate <id>         # old secret stops working, new one shown once
boat api-key revoke <id>
```

| Flag | Rule |
| - | - |
| `--ttl` | Default 90d. Maximum 365d, or `never` for a key that works until you revoke it. |
| `--sandbox`, `--env` | You can repeat them. |
| `--preset` | `read-only`, `full-sandbox`, `ci`, or `admin`. |
| `--actions` | You cannot use it with `--preset`. |

`create` and `rotate` show the secret one time. You cannot get it again later. `list` shows the prefix, the last four characters, the scope, the expiry, the 30-day request total, and the live resource count. `usage` still works after you revoke a key. Revoke does not delete sandboxes or Agents.

| Command | Who can run it |
| - | - |
| `create` | A browser sign-in (`boat login` without a key), or a key made with `--preset admin` |
| `rotate`, `revoke` | A browser sign-in only |
| `list`, `usage` | Any key of the account |

For a CI key, run `boat api-key create <name> --preset ci`. The same actions exist in the API: [Create a scoped API key](/api/reference/account/create-scoped-api-key), [Rotate](/api/reference/account/rotate-api-key) and [Revoke](/api/reference/account/revoke-api-key). See [API keys](/api-keys).

### `boat webhook`

Register lifecycle webhooks for all sandboxes of your account.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat webhook create https://example.com/hooks/boat --name prod --event ready --event error
boat webhook list
boat webhook rotate <id>
boat webhook remove <id>
```

`--event` takes one of 6 events: `ready`, `error`, `archived` (the sandbox stopped), `hydrated`, `degraded` and `recovered`. The deliveries name them `sandbox.ready`, `sandbox.error` and so on. Repeat `--event` or separate the names with commas. To get all 6, omit `--event`. `--name` sets a display name. You see the signing secret only when you create or rotate the webhook. See [Webhooks](/webhooks).

### `boat telemetry`

Send sandbox and account metrics, and lifecycle events, to an OTLP/HTTP endpoint.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat telemetry                                                    # show the export and its last result
boat telemetry set https://otlp.datadoghq.com -H dd-api-key=$DD_API_KEY
boat telemetry unset
```

`set` replaces the current export and sends a test export immediately. For more headers, repeat `-H key=value` (long form `--header`). boat encrypts the header values and never shows them. See [OpenTelemetry](/opentelemetry).

### `boat logout`

Sign out and clear the local token.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat logout
```

### `boat feedback`

Send feedback to the boat team by email. Replies go to your account email. You can send 5 per minute and 30 per day.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat feedback "fork is slow on large disks"
cat notes.txt | boat feedback
```

### `boat status`

Show the API health, the account that is signed in, its plan, the path of the local configuration and the path of the CLI binary.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat status
boat status --check   # exits 1 when this computer is not signed in
```

With `--json`, `account.signedIn` is `true` or `false`.

***

## Sandbox lifecycle

### `boat new`

Create a new sandbox.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new [--ttl SECONDS]
boat new --type small
boat new --type xlarge
boat new --no-auto-stop
boat new --env KEY=VALUE --env OTHER=VALUE
boat new --no-env
boat new --no-snapshots
boat new --no-monitoring
boat new --fail-fast
boat new --setup-file ./setup.sh
boat new --environment users
boat new --from web-stack
boat new --from web-stack --count 50
boat new --count 20
boat --org acme new
boat org switch acme
boat new
boat new --personal
boat new --name "api worker"
boat new --from web-stack --visibility private --host 3000 --host 8080:public --file workspace/.env=./session.env
```

| Flag | Default | Maximum |
| - | - | - |
| `--type` | `default` (the medium size) | `small`, `default`, `large` or `xlarge` (`xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher) |
| `--ttl` | `3600` (1 hour): seconds until auto-stop, counted from start or resume. It is not an idle timeout: only a running Boat agent prompt pushes it back, not `boat exec` or SSH. | `2592000` (30 days) |
| `--no-auto-stop` | off | no automatic stop |
| `--env`, `-e` | none | 100 variables, 64KB total |
| `--environment` | your default (`base`) | the name of one environment |
| `--no-env` | off | none |
| `--no-snapshots` | off | none |
| `--no-monitoring` | off | none |
| `--fail-fast` | off | none |
| `--setup-file` | none | 64KB script file |
| `--from` | none | one saved snapshot or share code |
| `--count` | `1` | `1000` sandboxes, fresh or with `--from` |
| `--personal` | off | bills you, not the active org |
| `--name` | `Box <date>`, or the snapshot name with `--from` | 120 characters |
| `--visibility` | the org's default (`boat org default-visibility`) | `private` or `shared`, org sandboxes only |
| `--host` | none | 50 ports, not with `--count` or `--fail-fast` |
| `--file` | none | 32 text files, 256KB total |

`--type` sets the machine size. A fork gets the size of its source sandbox, unless you pass `--type`. `boat resume --type` moves a sandbox to a different size. For the specifications and the hourly price of each size, see [Pricing](/pricing).

> [!NOTE]
>
> On the [free trial](/free-trial), `--no-auto-stop`, a `--ttl` above 2 hours, `large` and `xlarge` are refused.

`--env` sets environment variables on this sandbox only, on top of your dashboard secrets. When two variables have the same name, the value for this sandbox wins. See [Environments](/environments).

`--environment <name>` sets the environment that the sandbox starts from: its repositories, secrets, and credentials. If you omit it, the sandbox uses your default. boat refuses an unknown name before it creates the sandbox, so a typo costs you nothing. `--environment` and `--env` are not related. The first selects an environment. The second sets a variable on this one sandbox. See [Environments](/environments).

`--no-env` creates a sandbox that gets none of the secrets of your account. The sandbox also cannot act on your account or on other sandboxes. Use it for sandboxes that you give to your own users. SSH, SCP, desktop, snapshots, and public URLs still work. See [Environments](/environments). If you make many such sandboxes, use an environment marked safe for third parties instead. It applies the same protection to each sandbox that uses it, and the protection stays after forks and resumes.

`--no-snapshots` creates a sandbox that boat never snapshots. When you stop it, boat erases it. See [Snapshots off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#snapshots-off).

`--no-monitoring` creates a sandbox for which boat keeps none of these: command output, process output, the process list, CPU and RAM samples. You still see the live output of a running command. See [Monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#monitoring-off).

`--fail-fast` creates the sandbox only if a machine of its type is ready now. It answers in about 1.5 seconds. If no machine is ready, it fails with `no_ready_machine`. boat then creates nothing, bills nothing, and counts nothing against your start limits. It works with `--from`. `boat fork` and `boat resume` also accept it. See [Fail fast](/machines/fail-fast).

`--setup-file` reads a local shell script (UTF-8, up to 64KB). boat runs the script on the sandbox in the background after the sandbox is ready. The script never delays `ready`. To see the result, read `setupStatus` (`pending`, `running`, `done`, `failed`) and `setupError` in `boat info`. You can use it with `--from`. The script runs one time, as the user `user`, not as root. A resume does not run it again, and a fork does not copy it. Setup scripts of repositories are different: they run at every start. See [Setup scripts](/setup).

`--personal` bills you, also when an org wallet is active. For daily use, run `boat org switch` one time. All later `boat new` commands use that wallet. To change the wallet for one create, run `boat --org <org> new` or `boat --org personal new`. See [`boat org`](#boat-org).

`--from <name>` starts the sandbox from a saved snapshot that you saved with `boat snapshot <id> <name>`, or from a saved snapshot of your org. The stack is then already installed. The sandbox does not get the environment of the source sandbox. Pass `--environment`, or the sandbox uses your default. This flag is not related to `boat env set-file --from`, which reads a local file. See [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

A saved snapshot of a `--no-env` sandbox stays `--no-env`: every sandbox from it gets none of your environment secrets, even with `--environment`. `--env KEY=VALUE` still applies. To make a template that gets secrets, save it from a sandbox created without `--no-env`.

`--name` sets the name that `boat list` and the dashboard show. To change it later, run `boat rename ID NAME`.

`--visibility private` or `--visibility shared` sets who in the org can use the sandbox, before the sandbox gets a machine. Without it, the org's default applies. A personal sandbox is always private. To change it later, run [`boat share` or `boat unshare`](#boat-share-id-and-boat-unshare-id).

`--host PORT` hosts a port on an HTTPS URL as part of the create, exactly like [`boat host`](#boat-host-id-port). The URL is private (it carries a token) unless you write `PORT:public`. Repeat the flag for more ports. boat prints each URL with the sandbox id. The ports are routed before the sandbox is ready, so a service that starts later answers as soon as it listens.

`--file SANDBOX_PATH=LOCAL_FILE` writes a local text file on the sandbox. boat writes it after the disk of the sandbox is in place and before the sandbox reports `ready`, so `--setup-file` and your first command find it. A relative `SANDBOX_PATH` starts in `/home/user`. boat writes the files one time, at the first start. If a write fails, `setupStatus` is `failed` and `setupError` names the file.

In the API, these flags are the `visibility`, `hostedPorts` and `files` fields of `POST /sandboxes`, and the create answers the URLs in `hostedPorts`. One request replaces the create, the unshare, one host call per port and one write per file.

`--count <n>` with `--from` creates `n` sandboxes from the saved snapshot in one request. boat creates them together, which is faster than `n` separate `boat new` commands when you need many sandboxes at once. The command prints every sandbox id and returns. It does not wait until each sandbox is ready: watch them with `boat list`. Your start limits and your limit of active sandboxes count every sandbox of the batch. If the batch does not fit, boat creates none of it. `--count` does not work with `--fail-fast`. In the API, send `"count": n` in the body of `POST /sandboxes`. The answer lists the sandboxes in `sandboxes`.

`--from bsh_...` uses a share code that another account gave you. The new sandbox is yours and bills your account. It does not get the per-sandbox variables of the owner. See [Share a snapshot with another account](/snapshots/templates#share-a-template-with-another-account).

The command returns the sandbox ID, the IP, and the first state.

For a long workflow without interruptions, disable auto-stop:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --no-auto-stop
```

See [Keep a sandbox running](/long-running-tasks).

### `boat list`

List your sandboxes that are up or running, with their current state and ID. `boat list` without flags is the same as `boat list --filter r`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat list
boat list --filter s
boat list --filter sr
boat list --all
```

Give `--filter` one or more state group letters:

| Filter | Includes |
| - | - |
| `r` | Up/running sandboxes: `ready`, `cloning`, `idle`, `running` |
| `s` | Stopped sandboxes: `stopped` |
| `p` | Pending sandboxes: `init`, `provisioning` |
| `t` | Stopping sandboxes: `stopping` |
| `e` | Error sandboxes: `error` |

You can combine letters. For example, `boat list --filter sr` lists stopped sandboxes and sandboxes that are up or running. To include all states, use `--all`.

### `boat rename ID NAME`

Change the name of a sandbox. Only its creator can rename it.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat rename bx_f7k2q9hd "api worker"
```

### `boat extend ID`

Set the auto-stop timer of a running sandbox.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --hours 12
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --ttl 2592000
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --no-auto-stop
```

`--hours` and `--ttl` **set** the remaining time, counted from now. They do not add to the current timer. For example, `--hours 2` on a sandbox with 5 hours left leaves 2 hours. `--no-auto-stop` keeps the sandbox running until you stop it. The maximum is 30 days, or 2 hours on the [free trial](/free-trial).

### `boat info ID`

Show the details of one sandbox: state, IP, desktop availability, and remaining TTL.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat info bx_f7k2q9hd
```

When the sandbox's kernel restarted on its machine, `boat info` shows a `rebooted:` line. Every process that ran at that time ended. `crash` means the system log ended with no shutdown, for example after a kernel panic. The API returns the same data as `lastReboot`.

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
rebooted:  2026-10-21T18:54:25.000Z (crash: journal ended without shutdown)
```

### `boat stop ID`

Stop a running sandbox. boat makes a snapshot of the disk, then stops billing. The CLI shows the state `stopping`, then `stopped`. The API reports the same states as `archiving` and `archived`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd
```

`boat stop` never asks for confirmation. It accepts `--yes` (`-y`), so scripts can pass the same flag as for `boat delete`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `boat stop` returns while the sandbox is `stopping`. The snapshot takes a moment. Before you resume or fork it, poll `boat info` until the state is `stopped`.

The stop prints its id (`operation.id`, for example `stop_3f9a1c2e7b4d5a60`). To read that stop later, pass the id to `--status`. The status is `pending`, `failing`, `completed` or `superseded`. `superseded` means that a resume ended the stop. You can still read old stops after a resume or a later stop.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd --status stop_3f9a1c2e7b4d5a60
```

**If boat refuses a stop.** A stop saves the disk first. If that save fails, boat does these things:

1. It refuses the stop and keeps the sandbox running, so your work is not lost.
2. It tries the save again automatically.
3. It sends you an email.

**boat does not bill you for the time that your sandbox spends in that state.** The meter pauses automatically from the first failed attempt. See [When a stop is refused](/snapshots/stop#when-a-stop-is-refused).

A refused stop stays pending until a save succeeds. Then the sandbox stops automatically.

`--force` stops the sandbox now and keeps its last successful snapshot. All data written after that snapshot is lost permanently. Use it only after a stop failed.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd --force
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> `--force` discards unsaved work. First, read the time of the last snapshot in `boat info`. Then you know exactly what you lose.

### `boat delete ID`

Permanently delete a sandbox **and its snapshots**. boat force-stops the sandbox without a last snapshot. Then boat deletes from storage each snapshot chain that only this sandbox owns.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat delete bx_f7k2q9hd
boat delete bx_f7k2q9hd --yes
boat delete self --yes              # from inside a sandbox
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> `boat delete` destroys data. You cannot resume, fork or recover a deleted sandbox. No list of deleted sandboxes exists to restore from.
>
> **If you want to use the data later, run `boat stop` instead.** A stopped sandbox is free and keeps its disk for 14 days. `boat resume` brings it back in the same condition. To keep it longer, save a saved snapshot with `boat snapshot <id> <name>`.

The command asks you to confirm. To skip the question, pass `--yes`. In scripts (`--json`, or no terminal attached), `--yes` is necessary. Without it, the command refuses and does not wait.

Deletion is not instant. boat must remove the machine before it can remove the data. The command does these steps:

1. It removes the sandbox from `boat list` immediately.
2. It prints the deletion operation id (`bdop_…`).
3. It follows that operation until it finishes.

**What boat keeps.** boat keeps snapshot data that something else also uses. If boat deleted it, the other user of the data would break:

* A sandbox that you **forked** from this one, or a **resume** of it, restores from the same physical snapshot objects.
* A **saved snapshot** saved from this sandbox (`boat snapshot <id> <name>`) keeps its data. To remove those bytes too, run `boat snapshot rm <name>`.

boat releases the storage when the last sandbox or saved snapshot that uses a chain is gone.

### `boat deletion status OPERATION_ID`

Read the status of a deletion that you started earlier, here or through the API. The status is `pending`, `processing`, `blocked` or `completed`. `blocked` is not a final state. It means that an attempt found something that it cannot finish yet. Usually, another sandbox still reads a snapshot. boat tries again automatically, with backoff.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat deletion status bdop_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
```

See [Data retention and deletion](/data-retention).

### `boat resume ID`

Resume a stopped sandbox from its last snapshot. Before the CLI prints its last `ready` event, it waits for two things:

1. A ready state.
2. A test command that does nothing and succeeds.

This shows that the sandbox can run commands. The CLI does not wait for background hydration or setup scripts. The wait stops after 30 minutes. It fails on a final sandbox state or on an API error that cannot be retried. See [Snapshots](/snapshots).

A resume always uses the newest snapshot. You cannot resume from an older snapshot. To keep a state that you can go back to, save a [saved snapshot](#boat-snapshot-id-name).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat resume bx_f7k2q9hd
boat resume --no-wait bx_f7k2q9hd && boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd "npm test"
boat resume --fail-fast bx_f7k2q9hd
boat resume --no-env bx_f7k2q9hd
boat resume --type large bx_f7k2q9hd
boat resume -e KEY=VALUE bx_f7k2q9hd
boat resume --ttl 7200 bx_f7k2q9hd
boat resume --no-auto-stop bx_f7k2q9hd
```

The sandbox must have a completed snapshot. This means that you stopped it correctly with `boat stop`.

| Flag | What it does |
| - | - |
| `-e`, `--env` | Sets per-sandbox environment variables. It works the same as `boat new -e`. Repeat it for more values. A per-sandbox value replaces a dashboard variable with the same name. The set you pass **replaces** the current per-sandbox variables of the sandbox. |
| `--environment <name>` | Moves the sandbox to a different environment when it resumes. |
| `--no-env` | Removes your account secrets, and removes owner secrets that came from the snapshot. You cannot undo this. The sandbox stays no-env. |
| `--type` | Resumes on a different machine size: `small`, `default`, `large` or `xlarge` (`xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher). |
| `--ttl <seconds>` | Sets the lifetime of the resumed sandbox. |
| `--no-auto-stop` | Turns auto-stop off. |
| `--no-wait` | Returns when boat accepts the resume. It does not wait for `ready`. A `boat exec` sent right after waits up to 60 seconds for the sandbox by itself. This is the fastest way to run a command after a resume. |
| `--fail-fast` | Resumes only if a machine is ready now. It answers in about 1.5 seconds. If no machine is ready, it fails with `no_ready_machine`, the sandbox stays stopped, and nothing counts against your start limits. |

`--type`, `--environment` and `--no-env` change a stopped sandbox. On a running sandbox, boat refuses them with `sandbox_running_stop_first`. Run `boat stop`, wait for `stopped`, then resume with the change.

Without `--environment`, the sandbox keeps the environment version that it had. A resume never moves a sandbox to a newer version without your command. boat refuses an unknown name before it changes anything. The new environment can withhold a secret that the sandbox has now. boat then removes that secret from the disk during the resume, and it does not come back. See [Environments](/environments).

Without `--type`, the sandbox keeps its current size. boat refuses to shrink a sandbox that has more data than the smaller machine can hold. The sandbox then stays as it was. See [Sandbox sizes](/machines).

Without `--ttl` and `--no-auto-stop`, the sandbox keeps its current setting. A resume never makes the lifetime shorter or longer without your command.

A resume is like a server reboot. The systemd services that you enabled start again automatically. Processes that you started by hand do not come back: dev servers, background jobs, tunnels, desktop sessions. Start them again, or make them systemd services.

### `boat recover ID`

> [!WARNING]
>
> Deprecated. boat removes this command soon. After a kernel crash, the machine restarts by itself in about 15 seconds. If a sandbox still does not answer, run `boat stop --force ID`, then `boat resume ID`. You lose what was written after the last good snapshot. Read [A sandbox does not answer](/troubleshooting#a-sandbox-does-not-answer).

Power-cycle the machine of a sandbox that does not respond. boat does not touch the disk. Usually the sandbox answers again in 1-2 minutes.

boat refuses a recover in these cases. Resume the sandbox instead.

* The sandbox answers normally.
* A recover started less than 10 minutes ago.
* boat cannot power-cycle its machine.

This command does the same as `POST /sandboxes/{id}/recover` and Recover in the dashboard.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat recover bx_f7k2q9hd
```

### `boat fork ID`

Copy a sandbox from its latest snapshot into a new, independent sandbox.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat fork bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork --no-env bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork --type small bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork -e TENANT_ID=acme bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork --ttl 600 bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork --no-auto-stop bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork --fail-fast bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork --no-snapshots --no-monitoring bx_f7k2q9hd
```

The command returns the new sandbox ID asynchronously (HTTP 202). The source sandbox must have a completed snapshot.

A fork copies the newest snapshot of the source into a new sandbox. A fork of a running sandbox uses its last background snapshot, so files written after that snapshot can be missing. To fork an exact state, stop the source first, or save a [saved snapshot](#boat-snapshot-id-name) and run `boat new --from <name>`. The systemd services that you enabled start automatically, as on a resume. Processes that the source sandbox started by hand are not in the fork. Start them again in the fork if necessary.

boat never changes the source sandbox.

| Flag | What it does |
| - | - |
| `--type` | Gives the fork a machine size that is different from its source. |
| `--ttl <seconds>`, `--no-auto-stop` | Set the lifetime of the fork. |
| `--environment <name>` | Puts the fork on a different environment. |
| `--no-env` | Makes the fork a no-env sandbox. |
| `--no-snapshots` | boat never snapshots the fork. Stopping the fork erases it. Same as `boat new --no-snapshots`. |
| `--no-monitoring` | boat keeps no command output, process list or CPU and RAM samples for the fork. Same as `boat new --no-monitoring`. A fork of a sandbox with monitoring off keeps it off. |
| `-e`, `--env` | Sets per-sandbox environment variables on the fork. It works the same as `boat new -e`. |
| `--fail-fast` | Forks only if a machine is ready now. If none is ready, it fails with `no_ready_machine` and creates nothing. See [Fail fast](/machines/fail-fast). |
| `--wait` | Waits until the fork is ready, like `boat new`. With `--json`, it prints the same event lines as `boat new` (`created`, `state`, `ready`). |

A fork does **not** get the lifetime of its source. The default is 1 hour. So a fork of a sandbox with auto-stop off does not make another sandbox that nothing stops.

Without `--environment`, the fork gets exactly the environment version of its source. A fork never gets configuration that its source did not have. See [Environments](/environments).

A fork of a no-env source is always no-env.

The variables that you pass with `--env` **replace** the per-sandbox variables that the fork gets from the source sandbox. Without `--env`, the fork gets them unchanged.

### `boat events ID`

Read the work of the agent on a sandbox: prompts and responses. By default, the command streams **all conversations** on the sandbox. Each event has a `conversationId`, which you see with `--json`. To keep polling for new events, add `--follow`. To watch one conversation, add `--convo`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> These events are the conversations of the agent, not the lifecycle of the sandbox. A sandbox that never got a prompt returns an empty list, also after it started, stopped and resumed. For the lifecycle state, use `boat info`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat events bx_f7k2q9hd
boat events bx_f7k2q9hd --follow
boat events bx_f7k2q9hd --convo <conversationId>          # just one conversation
boat events bx_f7k2q9hd --convo current                    # this shell's current conversation
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `-f`, `--follow` | Continue polling and printing new events until interrupted |
| `--convo <id>` | Only stream this conversation (or `current`). Repeat for several. Omit to stream all conversations. Alias `--conversation` |

### `boat conversations [id]`

List the conversations of a sandbox. The conversation with the most recent prompt comes first. Each row shows these values:

* The id.
* The last activity.
* The number of prompts.
* If a turn is running.
* The last harness and model.
* A preview of the last prompt.

Alias: `boat convos`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat conversations
boat convos bx_f7k2q9hd
boat conversations bx_f7k2q9hd --json      # one JSON line per conversation
```

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
ID                                    When         Prompts  Running  Harness/model      Last prompt
8f1c2b7a-3d4e-4f5a-9b0c-1d2e3f4a5b6c  just now     1        yes      pi/claude-sonnet-5 Investigate the flaky CI job  [sandbox current, this shell]
2c0d9e4b-7a1f-4c3e-8b5d-6e7f8a9b0c1d  4 mins ago   2        no       claude             Now add tests
```

Two markers can come after the last prompt:

| Marker | Conversation |
| - | - |
| `sandbox current` | The one that `boat prompt` without flags continues from any shell. This is the conversation of the sandbox with the most recent prompt. |
| `this shell` | The one that `boat prompt` without flags continues from this shell. |

Copy an id into one of these commands:

* `boat prompt --resume <id>`
* `boat steer --convo <id>`
* `boat events --convo <id>`
* `boat interrupt --convo <id>`

### `boat steer ID MESSAGE`

Send a message to a turn that is **already running**, and do not stop it. The agent uses the message and continues its work. There are three options:

| Command | What happens to the running turn |
| - | - |
| `boat prompt` | Waits for the turn to end. |
| `boat steer` | Adds your message to the turn. |
| `boat interrupt` | Discards the turn. |

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat steer "Skip the integration tests, the unit tests are enough"
boat steer bx_f7k2q9hd "Also update the changelog when you are done"
boat steer bx_f7k2q9hd --convo <conversationId> "Focus on the auth module first"
boat steer --convo current "Stop after the first failure"
```

Without `--convo`, the command steers the conversation that this shell prompted last. This is the same conversation that `boat prompt` without flags continues. If the conversation has no running turn, boat refuses the steer with `no_running_turn`. Use `boat prompt` in that case.

How each harness handles a steer:

| Harness | What happens |
| - | - |
| Claude Code, Codex, pi, Prime Agent | The harness adds the message to the running turn natively. Nothing is interrupted. If the harness accepts the message but the turn ends before it uses the message, boat immediately continues with a new turn on the same session. So the agent always acts on a steer. |
| OpenCode | OpenCode cannot take a message during a turn. boat stops that turn and immediately continues the same conversation with your instruction. The conversation keeps all of its memory. |

The `native` field of the JSON output tells which path ran. The steer shows in `boat events` as a `steer` event with the final `mode`: `native`, `native-continued`, `fallback` or `late`. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--convo <id>` | Steer this conversation (or `current`). Omit to steer the one this shell last prompted. Alias `--conversation` |

### `boat interrupt ID`

Interrupt the running agent work in a sandbox. By default, the command stops **all conversations** on the sandbox. To stop only one, use `--convo`. The other conversations keep running.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat interrupt bx_f7k2q9hd
boat interrupt bx_f7k2q9hd --convo <conversationId>       # stop just one conversation
boat interrupt bx_f7k2q9hd --convo current
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--convo <id>` | Interrupt only this conversation (or `current`). Omit to interrupt the whole sandbox. Alias `--conversation` |

***

## Access

### `boat ssh ID [command]`

Open an SSH session in a sandbox, or run one command without a session. The CLI manages the key at `~/.ssh/ascii_box_ed25519` automatically. The file name is old, but it is the current key. For one command, `boat exec` is faster than `boat ssh`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd
boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd "cd /home/user/my-repo && npm test"
boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd -- bash -lc "cd /home/user/my-repo && npm test"
boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd -- bash -s < ./setup.sh
boat ssh -t bx_f7k2q9hd -- tmux attach
```

A command runs without a terminal. Pass `-t` (`--tty`) before the ID to give it one: `tmux attach`, `read -s` prompts and full-screen tools need it.

### `boat exec ID [command...]`

Run a command in a sandbox through the boat API. You do not need an SSH session or a key. `boat exec` exits with the exit code of the remote command, so you can use it directly in scripts and CI.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd "npm test"
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --cwd my-repo --timeout 120 -- npm run build
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd bash -lc 'echo "$HOME" && ls'
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --stream --timeout 600 "npm test"
```

One argument runs as a shell command line. More than one argument runs as argv. Each argument keeps its quoting, as with `boat ssh`.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--cwd <dir>` | sandbox work directory | Working directory, relative to the sandbox work directory (`/home/user`) |
| `--timeout <secs>` | `30` | Stop the command after this many seconds and exit `124`. `0` = no limit. Above `600`, or `0`, the output streams live |
| `--stream` | off | Print stdout and stderr as the command writes them, not when it ends. Same exit code. With `--json`, one JSON frame per line |
| `--detach` | off | Run in the background and print the process id |
| `--status <pid>` | none | Show status and logs of a process started with `--detach` |
| `--kill <pid>` | none | Stop a process started with `--detach`, and every process it started |
| `--attach <pid>` | none | Print the output of a process started with `--detach` as it writes it, from its start, until it ends. Exits with its exit code. Reconnects every 10 minutes with no gap |

A command sent while the sandbox starts (for example right after `boat resume --no-wait`) waits up to 60 seconds for the sandbox. If the sandbox is still not ready, boat returns `sandbox_starting`. Retry it.

The default timeout is 30 seconds. For a long job, give a longer timeout, or `0` for no limit:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --timeout 0 -- make -j16 test     # runs until it ends
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --timeout 7200 -- ./train.sh      # stops after 2 hours, exit 124
```

Above 600 seconds, or with `0`, the CLI starts the command in the background and prints its output live until it ends. The command keeps running through network cuts, and the CLI reconnects with no gap. It exits with the exit code of the command. Ctrl-C stops the command.

A job that a shell script starts with `&` ignores SIGINT. This is the standard rule when a shell has no job control ([bash manual](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html#Signals)). `kill -INT <pid>` then has no effect on that job. Stop it with `kill -TERM <pid>`, or run `set -m` in the script before you start the job.

A server or a job that must outlive the CLI needs `--detach`. To start it now and read it later:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
pid="$(boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --detach "npm run build" | jq -r .processId)"
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --status "$pid"
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --attach "$pid"   # follow the output live until it ends
```

`--detach` starts the command in the background and returns a JSON object. Take `processId` from it, as in the example. When you pipe or capture the output, `--json` turns on automatically. So in a script you always get JSON here, also without the flag.

The output goes to `~/.ascii/processes/<pid>.log` on the sandbox. `--status <pid>` prints these values:

* If the process still runs.
* The exit code, after the process ends.
* The last lines of stdout and stderr.

If the agent of the sandbox restarts (stop and resume), the status changes to `lost`. The log files stay on the disk. See [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands).

### `boat run [command...]`

Run one command in a new sandbox, then delete the sandbox. `boat run` creates the sandbox, copies your directory in, runs the command, prints its output live, prints the time and the cost, and deletes the sandbox. It exits with the exit code of the command. Use it as a CI step for an agent.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat run -- npm test
boat run --from ci-base --type xlarge --push . -- make -j16 test
boat run --push ./api --timeout 1800 -e NODE_ENV=test -- bun test
```

The last line goes to stderr:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
exit 0 · 4m 12s · xlarge · $0.0140 · bx_f7k2q9hd deleted
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--from <name\|code>` | none | Start from a saved snapshot or a share code |
| `--type <type>` | `default` | `small`, `default`, `large` or `xlarge` |
| `--push <dir>` | none | Copy this local directory to `/home/user/<dir name>` first, and run the command there. See `boat push` |
| `--cwd <dir>` | the pushed directory, else `/home/user` | Working directory, relative to `/home/user` |
| `--timeout <secs>` | no limit | Stop the command after this many seconds and exit `124` |
| `-e`, `--env KEY=VALUE` | none | A variable for the sandbox. Repeat it for more |
| `--environment <name>` | your default | The environment the sandbox starts from |
| `--keep` | off | Keep the sandbox after the command ends. It stops 15 minutes later. Run `boat extend` to keep it longer |
| `--personal` | off | Bill your personal account when an organization wallet is active |
| `--no-env` | off | The sandbox gets none of your account's stored secrets. Same as `boat new --no-env` |

An option that `boat run` does not have is an error, and no sandbox is created. To run a command that starts with `-`, put `--` before it. `boat exec` and `boat ssh` follow the same rule.

The command output passes through as is, also when you pipe it. `--json` prints one JSON frame for each output chunk, then a `summary` line with `exitCode`, `elapsedSeconds`, `dollars`, `sandboxType` and `deleted`.

The sandbox has auto-stop 15 minutes ahead, and `boat run` moves it forward while the command runs. If the CLI dies, the sandbox stops by itself. Without `--keep`, the sandbox has no snapshots, so a stop erases it. Ctrl-C deletes the sandbox.

### `boat push ID DIR`

Copy a local directory into a sandbox, as one archive over SSH. In a git repository, the CLI sends the files that git tracks and the new files that `.gitignore` does not exclude. So `node_modules`, build output and `.git` stay on your computer. Outside a git repository, it sends every file except `.git`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat push bx_f7k2q9hd .
boat push bx_f7k2q9hd ./api --to /srv/api
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--to <path>` | `/home/user/<dir name>` | The directory on the sandbox. boat creates it if it does not exist |

Files that exist on the sandbox are replaced. Files that you deleted on your computer stay on the sandbox. Executable bits and symbolic links stay. On Windows, the executable bit comes from git.

### `boat history ID [command-id]`

List the commands that ran in a sandbox, newest first. With a command id, print the stored output of that command. This works while the sandbox is stopped.

| What | boat keeps it for |
| - | - |
| Commands run through `boat exec` or the API | 7 days |
| The output of all other processes in the sandbox | 72 hours |

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd --mode commands
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw --stderr
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw --follow
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--limit <n>` | `20` | How many commands to list, at most 100 |
| `--mode <modes>` | all | Only these, comma-separated: `commands` (what you ran), `process` (every other process), or `sync`, `stream`, `detached` |
| `--stderr` | off | Print stderr instead of stdout |
| `-f`, `--follow` | off | Keep printing new output until the command ends |

See [Command history and logs](/long-running-tasks/command-history).

### `boat ps ID`

List the processes in a sandbox, busiest first: pid, CPU, memory, user, history record and command line. To read the output of a process, pass its HISTORY id to `boat history`. For a stopped sandbox, the command shows the last sample that boat kept, with its time.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ps bx_f7k2q9hd
boat ps bx_f7k2q9hd --json
```

### `boat env`

Manage the environments that new sandboxes start from: repositories, secrets, and the credentials that a sandbox can use. Each change makes a new version that you cannot change. Running sandboxes stay on their start version until you run `boat env upgrade`. See [Environments](/environments).

> [!WARNING]
>
> `--environment` and `--env` are different. `boat new --environment staging` sets the environment that the sandbox uses. `boat new --env KEY=value` sets one variable on that one sandbox, on top of what the environment gives it.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env list
boat env info base
boat env new staging
boat env rename staging prod
boat env default prod
boat env rm staging
```

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `boat env list` | Your environments, with the default marker, latest version, and live sandboxes per version |
| `boat env info <name>` | One environment in full: toggles, variables, secret files, repos, versions |
| `boat env new <name>` | Create an environment. Starts with everything injected |
| `boat env rename <name> <new-name>` | Rename. Sandboxes stay pinned to their versions |
| `boat env default <name>` | Make it the environment new sandboxes use when none is named |
| `boat env rm <name>` | Soft delete. Pinned sandboxes keep running. New sandboxes cannot use it |

#### `boat env set NAME`

Change what the environment injects.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set base --safe-for-third-parties true
boat env set base --github true --secrets false
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--safe-for-third-parties <true\|false>` | Master switch. `true` withholds all of your secrets: variables, secret files, GitHub, AI credentials, and the setup scripts of repositories. It overrides every flag below |
| `--github <true\|false>` | Your GitHub access: token and repository clones |
| `--secrets <true\|false>` | Your environment variables and secret files |
| `--boat-credentials <true\|false>` | The in-sandbox boat CLI credentials, so the sandbox can manage its own lifecycle |
| `--agents-credentials <true\|false>` | Your agent provider logins (Claude, Codex, and so on) |
| `--credential-profile <name\|id\|default>` | The [credential profile](/ai-credentials#credential-profiles) the sandboxes get. `default` = the sandbox owner's default profile |
| `--proxy-ai-credentials <true\|false>` | With `--safe-for-third-parties true`: still pass AI credentials, as proxy placeholders. Needs `boat ai proxy on` for the profile owner |

#### Organization environments

Add `--org <org>` to any `boat env` command to work on the organization's shared environments. Members read and use them. Owners and admins change them. Without `--org`, `boat env` works on your own environments. See [Environments](/environments/manage#organization-environments).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env list --org acme
boat env set agents --org acme --credential-profile team-claude
boat env access agents --org acme --only a@x.com,b@y.com
```

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `boat env access <env> [--org <org>]` | Show who can use the environment |
| `boat env access <env> --everyone` | Every member can use it. This is the default |
| `boat env access <env> --only <emails>` | Only owners, admins and these members. Comma-separated emails. Replaces the list |
| `boat env access <env> --add <email>` / `--remove <email>` | Add or remove one member |

Owners and admins only. See [Limit who can use an environment or profile](/organizations#limit-who-can-use-an-environment-or-profile).

#### Contents

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set-var base STRIPE_KEY=sk_live_123
printf %s "$STRIPE_KEY" | boat env set-var base STRIPE_KEY   # value from stdin, not on the command line
boat env rm-var base STRIPE_KEY
boat env set-file base backend/.env --from ./local.env
cat ./local.env | boat env set-file base backend/.env
boat env rm-file base backend/.env
boat env add-repo base octocat/hello-world --branch develop
boat env rm-repo base octocat/hello-world
```

On an environment that is safe for third parties, `set-var` and `set-file` save the value and print a `warning:` line on stderr: boat does not inject the value into sandboxes. `boat env info` then shows `no (withheld: safe for third parties)` for that toggle. To check what a sandbox really gets, run:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec <id> 'echo $STRIPE_KEY'
```

`set-file` reads the contents from `--from <local-file>`. Without `--from`, it reads from stdin. Paths are relative to the sandbox work directory (`/home/user`).

#### `boat env upgrade NAME`

Move the sandboxes of this environment to its latest version.

* Live sandboxes get the new configuration immediately. First, boat removes from the machine each secret that the new version withholds.
* Stopped sandboxes get it when they resume.
* Nothing upgrades without this command.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env upgrade base
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> boat deletes a withheld secret from the disk of the sandbox. It does not hide it. If you pin the sandbox to the older version again, the secret does not come back.

### `boat host ID PORT`

Expose a service that runs in a sandbox on a stable HTTPS URL. You do not open an SSH session.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 3000
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 3000 --title "Login preview"
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 3000 --public
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 5173 --localhost
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 3000 --json
```

The command opens the sandbox firewall, registers the HTTPS subdomain, and prints the URL: `https://<sandbox>-<port>.on.boat.dev`. If you run it again for the same sandbox and port, you get the same URL. Start the service first, with `boat exec <id> --detach "<command>"`.

A private URL carries `?_token=`. Anyone who has the full URL can open it. The token URL answers with a redirect and a cookie, so use `curl -L -c jar -b jar '<url>'`. See [Public URLs](/hosting).

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--title <title>` | none | Set the display title for the hosted port. |
| `--private` | on | Require the generated `_token` query parameter to access the URL. |
| `--public` | off | Clear any saved access token and return a URL that does not require `_token`. |
| `--localhost` | off | The service listens on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1` only. The sandbox relays the URL to it. Leave it off for a service on `0.0.0.0`. See [Services that listen on localhost](/hosting/how-it-works#services-that-listen-on-localhost). |

### `boat scp`

Copy files to or from a sandbox. Use `bx_<id>:/path` as the remote address.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
# Download a file
boat scp bx_f7k2q9hd:/home/user/output.zip ./output.zip

# Upload a file
boat scp ./local-file.txt bx_f7k2q9hd:/home/user/

# Copy a directory recursively
boat scp --recursive ./my-project bx_f7k2q9hd:/home/user/
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--recursive` | Copy directories recursively |

On macOS and Linux, a recursive copy to a new directory can send one archive over SSH. This needs `tar` on both ends. It removes one network round trip for each file. You see the new directory only after the full transfer. These copies use the installed OpenSSH `scp`:

* Single files.
* Merges into a directory that exists.
* Trees that the archive mode does not support.

### `boat forward ID`

Forward one TCP port from a sandbox to your computer.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat forward bx_f7k2q9hd --remote 8080
boat forward bx_f7k2q9hd --remote 3000 --bind 0.0.0.0
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--remote <port>` | required | Remote port on the sandbox |
| `--local <port>` | same as remote | Local port to bind |
| `--bind <addr>` | `127.0.0.1` | Local bind address |

#### `--reverse`: reach your machine from the sandbox

`--reverse` sends the tunnel in the other direction. A port on your computer
becomes available inside the sandbox at `127.0.0.1:<remote>`. An agent in the
sandbox can then call an MCP server, a local model, or a webhook receiver that
stays on your laptop.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
# your app on localhost:7777 answers at 127.0.0.1:7777 inside the sandbox
boat forward bx_f7k2q9hd --reverse --local 7777

# a local model on 11434 shows up inside the sandbox on 11500
boat forward bx_f7k2q9hd --reverse --local 11434 --remote 11500
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--local <port>` | required | Port on your computer to expose |
| `--remote <port>` | same as local | Port the sandbox listens on |
| `--bind <addr>` | `127.0.0.1` | Bind address **inside the sandbox**. Anything other than loopback needs `GatewayPorts` enabled on the sandbox's sshd |

Both directions run in the foreground until you press Ctrl+C. The tunnel can
stop because the sandbox moved. For example, `boat stop` then `boat resume`
brings the sandbox back on a new IP. The CLI then gets the connection again and
tries up to five times before it stops. A failure at startup, for example a
port that is already in use on the other side, shows immediately. The CLI does
not try again.

Neither direction makes anything public. The tunnel uses the same SSH session
as `boat ssh`, and the sandbox side listens on loopback only. For a public HTTPS
URL for a port inside the sandbox, use [`boat host`](#boat-host-id-port).

### `boat desktop ID`

Open the desktop streaming URL of the sandbox in your browser.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat desktop bx_f7k2q9hd
```

The desktop streams over Moonlight (60fps WebRTC).

The JSON output has `viewerUrl`. It carries the desktop token in its query string. Treat it as a secret.

### `boat browser ID`

Get a stream that shows only the browser of the running sandbox.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat browser bx_f7k2q9hd
boat browser bx_f7k2q9hd --profile /data/chrome-profile
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--profile <path>` | a managed dir on the sandbox | Absolute path on the sandbox used as the Chrome user data dir (the Chrome profile). |

With `--profile`, you can keep more than one signed-in Chrome profile on one
sandbox. You select one profile for each stream. boat creates the directory and
gives it to the browser user. The path must be absolute and outside system
directories. It must not be under `/home/user`, because the browser sandbox
hides that path with an empty directory. The profile is on the sandbox
filesystem, so snapshots and forks keep it. When you change the profile, Chrome
restarts and the stream stays up. Sandboxes created before this feature return
`chrome_profile_unsupported`. To use the flag, create the sandbox again on a
current image.

The stream has these properties:

* 1920x1080 at 60 fps.
* It shows Chrome with tabs and an address bar.
* It uses a separate streaming process and identity.
* It does not give access to the desktop clipboard bridge.
* It does not create a separate sandbox.
* It cannot fall back to the desktop.
* The window-close controls are hidden. Mute, reconnect, and fullscreen stay on the viewer.

Behavior:

* When you close the last tab, Chrome opens a new tab and the stream stays up.
* When you run the command again, the live stream stays up.
* When you open the new URL in a second tab, it replaces the first tab and keeps the same Chrome session.
* New sandboxes get the browser-view files when boat provisions them.

Keep the URL secret.

This feature limits the display and the input. It does not isolate the browser from the sandbox. Code that already runs in the sandbox can read or change the browser process and its data. This is especially true for code with root access.

***

## Snapshots

### `boat snapshots [id]`

List the snapshots of all your sandboxes, or of one sandbox.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat snapshots
boat snapshots bx_f7k2q9hd
boat snapshots bx_f7k2q9hd --limit 50
boat snapshots --all
```

| Flag | Description |
| - | - |
| `--limit <n>` | How many snapshots to read per page |
| `--all` | Read every page, not only the first |

Resume and fork always use the newest snapshot. Older snapshots expire after about one day, and you cannot restore them. To keep a state, save a saved snapshot.

### `boat snapshot ID NAME`

Save the disk of a sandbox under a name. `boat new --from <name>` can then deploy it as many times as you want. To replace a saved snapshot, use its name again.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat snapshot bx_f7k2q9hd web-stack
boat snapshot self web-stack        # from inside a sandbox
boat snapshot rm web-stack          # remove it and release its storage
```

A save from a running sandbox first makes a new capture, so it can take minutes. The CLI polls until the snapshot is `ready`. 10 saved snapshots are free. Each one more costs \$0.056 a day from the wallet. See [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

### `boat snapshot share|shares|unshare`

Give another boat account a secret code that deploys one of your saved snapshots.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat snapshot share web-stack              # make a code; it shows once
boat snapshot shares web-stack             # list codes, use counts, status
boat snapshot unshare web-stack shr_...    # revoke one code
boat new --from bsh_...                    # the other account deploys it
```

`share` prints the full code one time only. Save it immediately. boat removes these items from the sandbox of the other account: your logins, API keys, secret files, repository clones and SSH keys. The other account gets all other data on the disk. See [Share a snapshot with another account](/snapshots/templates#share-a-template-with-another-account).

### `boat snapshot latest|tree|pull`

Look inside a snapshot or download it. This works while the sandbox is stopped.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat snapshot latest bx_f7k2q9hd
boat snapshot tree <snapshotId>              # files and sizes
boat snapshot pull <snapshotId> -o ./restore # download and reassemble (long form --out)
boat snapshot pull <snapshotId> -o ./restore --path /home/user/project/report # extract one file or folder; repeat --path for more
```

`pull` writes `home_user/` (your `/home/user`) and `docker/` (named volumes). See [Snapshots](/snapshots).
`pull` recreates symlinks that stay inside `home_user/` and `docker/`. On every platform it skips a link that points outside that tree, such as `/etc`, or one that resolves through another symlink. On Windows it also skips links unless Developer Mode is on or the shell runs as administrator. It prints how many entries it skipped.

### `boat snapshot delete SNAPSHOTID...`

Permanently delete ordinary filesystem snapshots. The command accepts all snapshots, and the snapshot disappears immediately. boat erases its stored data in the background when nothing reads it. A newer snapshot that you keep can be built on it. Then its data stays until that newer snapshot is deleted too. `--all <sandboxId>` deletes all ordinary snapshots of a sandbox and keeps the sandbox. To remove a saved snapshot, use `boat snapshot rm <name>` instead.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat snapshot delete <snapshotId>
boat snapshot delete <snapshotId> <snapshotId> --yes
boat snapshot delete --all bx_f7k2q9hd
```

See [Data retention and deletion](/data-retention).

***

## AI agents

### `boat prompt [id]`

Send a prompt in natural language to an AI agent in the sandbox.

* Without an ID, the prompt goes to the current sandbox of your shell (the last `boat new` or `boat fork` there). If you run the CLI inside a sandbox, it goes to that sandbox.
* Without `--provider`, the prompt uses the default harness and model from the dashboard (Agents & Proxying).
* Before the first prompt, connect a key or a subscription on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying). Without it, the prompt fails and the CLI exits with code 1. See [Keys and subscriptions](/integrated-agents/keys).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat prompt "Fix the failing tests in this repo"
boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd --provider claude "Fix the failing tests in this repo"
boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd --provider codex --model gpt-5.4-mini --reasoning-effort xhigh "Refactor auth module"
boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd --provider codex --model gpt-6.1-sol --fast "Refactor auth module"
boat prompt --attach ./error.png --attach ./trace.log "Why does this crash?"
```

| Flag | Required | Values |
| - | - | - |
| `--provider` | no | One of the 7 harnesses: `claude`, `codex`, `pi`, `opencode`, `prime`, `kimi`, `mistral`. Default: the default harness on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying) |
| `--model` | no | Provider-specific model name. Default: the model selected for that harness on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying) |
| `--reasoning-effort` | no | Provider/model-specific thinking level such as `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`. The accepted levels differ for each model. Some models have none |
| `--fast` | no | No value. Run this prompt in fast mode: same model, faster output, billed by the provider at its higher fast rate. Only fast-capable models accept it. Default: the choice saved on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying) for that model |
| `--new` | no | Start a new conversation instead of continuing this shell's current one |
| `--resume <id>` | no | Continue a specific conversation by id (or `current` for this shell's) |
| `--attach <path>` | no | Attach a file (image, PDF, any file). Repeat for multiple. Alias `--image`. Saved on the sandbox under `~/attachments`. Images are also sent to vision-capable models |
| To get the current list of providers, models, and reasoning efforts from the boat API, run `boat prompt --help`. It lists the models that support fast mode under "Fast mode (--fast):". |

#### Conversations (running agents in parallel)

A sandbox runs **many conversations at the same time**. Each conversation has its own history. So one sandbox can run more than one independent agent task in parallel, for example different features, different users, or a demo. The tasks do not wait in a queue.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat prompt --new "Start on the billing refactor"     # conversation A
boat prompt --new "Investigate the flaky test"        # conversation B, runs alongside A
boat prompt --resume <A> "Now add tests"              # continue a specific conversation
boat prompt "quick follow-up"                          # continues THIS shell's current conversation
boat conversations                                     # list them all, with ids to resume
```

* **`--new`** starts a new conversation and makes it the current conversation of this shell. Each prompt prints its conversation id directly under `queued:` (`conversation: <id>`, with `(new)` when `--new` created it). In `--json`, the id is in `conversationId`.
* **`--resume <id>`** continues a specific conversation. `--resume current` continues the current conversation of this shell.
* **No flag** continues the current conversation of this shell. The "current conversation" belongs to your shell, the same as the `current` sandbox id. Two shells (or two people) can prompt the same sandbox. Each one keeps its own conversation, and they do not interfere.
* **[`boat conversations`](#boat-conversations-id)** lists all conversations on the sandbox with the id, the number of prompts, the running state and the last prompt. You can then resume a conversation from another shell or another day by its id.
* Conversations run in parallel up to a limit for each sandbox. The limit increases with the memory of the sandbox. Above the limit, new prompts wait in a queue and start when turns finish.
* You can continue a conversation with a different `--provider`. The history stays after the change.

For how harnesses, conversations, the agent lifecycle, and parallel runs work together, with diagrams, see [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).

### `boat ai`

Manage AI credentials: credential profiles, API keys, custom APIs, the AI credentials proxy, usage, and blocking. `--org <org>` selects an organization for `proxy`, `usage` and `profile new`. See [AI credentials](/ai-credentials).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ai accounts chatgpt-subscription        # out of credits on this account?
boat ai switch chatgpt-subscription 2        # every sandbox on the profile uses account 2 now
boat ai proxy on
boat ai profiles
boat ai profile new work --copy-from default
boat ai profile default work
echo "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | boat ai profile set-key work anthropic-api-key
echo "$STRIPE_KEY" | boat ai profile set-api work STRIPE_KEY --base-url https://api.stripe.com/v1
boat ai usage bx_23456789 --days 7
boat ai block bx_23456789
```

| Command | Description |
| - | - |
| `boat ai accounts <credential> [--profile <p>]` | The accounts of one credential, numbered, the one in use marked |
| `boat ai switch <credential> <account> [--profile <p>]` | Switch the credential to another account: its number, email or last key characters. Every sandbox on the profile uses it at once, running ones included |
| `boat ai add-account <credential> [value] [--profile <p>]` | Add another API key, ready to switch to. Reads stdin when the value is omitted or `-`. For another sign-in, use "Add another account" on the dashboard |
| `boat ai forget-account <credential> <account> [--profile <p>]` | Delete an account. Forgetting the one in use switches to another account, or removes the credential if it was the last |
| `boat ai proxy [on\|off]` | Show the proxy state and price, or turn it on or off. Running sandboxes switch at their next start |
| `boat ai profiles [--org-only]` | The profiles you can use, yours and your organizations' |
| `boat ai profile new <name> [--copy-from <profile>]` | Create a profile. With `--org`, the organization owns it |
| `boat ai profile default <profile>` | Make the profile its owner's default. Sandboxes get it at their next start |
| `boat ai profile rename <profile> <new-name>` | Rename a profile |
| `boat ai profile access <profile> [--everyone\|--only <emails>\|--add <email>\|--remove <email>]` | Organization profiles: show or set which members can use it. Owner only. See [Limit who can use an environment or profile](/organizations#limit-who-can-use-an-environment-or-profile) |
| `boat ai profile rm <profile>` | Delete a profile. Not the default, and not one an environment names |
| `boat ai profile set-key <profile> <credential> [value]` | Set an API key, for example `anthropic-api-key`. Reads stdin when the value is omitted or `-` |
| `boat ai profile rm-key <profile> <credential>` | Remove an API key or a sign-in, for example `claude-subscription` |
| `boat ai profile set-api <profile> <NAME> --base-url <url> [--value <v>]` | Set a custom API. The sandbox gets `NAME` and `NAME_BASE_URL`. Reads stdin without `--value` |
| `boat ai profile rm-api <profile> <NAME>` | Remove a custom API |
| `boat ai usage [id] [--days N]` | Proxied usage: per sandbox for the account in scope, or per day and model for one sandbox. Default 30 days |
| `boat ai block <id>` | Refuse the sandbox's AI placeholders, running or stopped. No effect on a sandbox with real keys |
| `boat ai unblock <id>` | Accept them again |

***

## Account

### `boat limits`

Show the start limit closest to full, the plan and the wallet in one line. When a limit is full, it shows what happened and the next command. A create, a fork, and a resume each count as one start.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat limits
boat limits --all      # every limit and every way past a full limit (--details is the same)
boat limits --json
```

The `--all` output shows these values:

* Remaining starts for each minute, hour and day.
* The plan money left to run sandboxes, in dollars.
* The wallet balance, in dollars.
* The sandbox types that you can create now, and why each other type is blocked.

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
types: small, default
  large: not during the free trial; the first payment unlocks it
  xlarge: needs the $100/month plan or higher
```

`--json` prints the same payload as the API, with `starts.minute.remaining`, `wallet.balanceDollars`, `planIncluded.vmHoursRemaining`, `startLimitsWithWallet` and `machineTypes`.

### `boat usage ID`

Show the machine time that one sandbox used and its cost, for its full life or for a time window. This works on running and stopped sandboxes. The value for a running sandbox increases until the sandbox stops. `running` in the JSON tells if the sandbox still runs. It is false after a stop, and also while a refused stop keeps the meter paused.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat usage bx_f7k2q9hd
boat usage bx_f7k2q9hd --since 2026-09-01 --until 2026-10-01
boat usage bx_f7k2q9hd --json
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--since <time>` | sandbox creation | Count from this time, ISO 8601 or Unix seconds |
| `--until <time>` | now | Count up to this time, ISO 8601 or Unix seconds |

The text output shows the billable machine time (with the multiplier of the sandbox type), the cost at list price, and the window. `--json` prints the API payload: `seconds`, `dollars`, `secondsPerDollar`, `sandboxType`, `billingMultiplier`, `since`, `until` and `running`. See [Per-sandbox usage](/billing#per-sandbox-usage).

### `boat dashboard`

Open your web dashboard in the browser, already signed in. The link has a code that you can use one time. The code expires in 15 minutes and cannot call the API. It is never your sandbox token. So the link is safe in a terminal, a log, or a message. If you signed in with a service API key, the link opens the dashboard signed out. To create, rotate, or revoke API keys, you must sign in through the browser.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat dashboard
```

### `boat org`

Show, switch, create, transfer, or delete the **organization wallet** that new sandboxes bill to. An organization has one shared plan and one shared wallet.

* `boat org switch` sets the active wallet of the account (`PATCH /orgs/active`). An account API key without `--org` bills the same wallet. The dashboard bills the organization selected in its sidebar.
* `--org` (or `BOAT_ORG`) uses a different wallet for one command.
* Name an organization by its id or its name, as `boat org list` shows them.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat org                     # show the active wallet (same as boat org status)
boat org list                # organizations you belong to, ids and names
boat org switch acme         # bill new sandboxes to acme, from the CLI, the dashboard and the API
boat org switch personal     # back to your own account
boat --org acme new          # bill one create to acme without switching
boat --org personal new      # bill one create to your account while an org is sticky
boat org create "Acme"
boat --org acme org transfer alice
boat --org acme org delete --yes
boat --org acme org migrate      # move your personal plan and sandboxes into acme
boat org members                 # members and pending invites of the org in scope
boat org invite dana@example.com # owner only
```

For what members can do with the sandboxes of the organization, see [Organizations](/organizations).

`boat org transfer`, `boat org delete` and `boat org migrate` act on the scope of the command. This is `--org` or `BOAT_ORG` if set. If not, it is the wallet from `boat org switch`. If you delete an org with `--org`, a different wallet from `boat org switch` stays active.

`boat org migrate` is for an owner who paid personally before the organization existed. It does these things:

* From that moment, each sandbox billed to your personal account bills the organization.
* Your personal plan ends the same day. boat refunds the unused part of the month to your card.
* The money in your personal wallet stays on your personal account.

The organization must already have a plan. `boat --org acme billing plan 20 --move-personal` starts a plan and does the move in one step.

### `boat share ID` and `boat unshare ID`

Make one of your organization sandboxes shared (every member can use it) or private (only you can use it). Members always see it and can stop it.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat share bx_f7k2q9hd      # every member can use it
boat unshare bx_f7k2q9hd    # only you can use it, at once
```

* A sandbox that holds none of your personal logins changes at once, both ways.
* A sandbox that holds your logins (GitHub token, model keys, secrets): `boat share` removes them at its next start, so members never act as you. If the sandbox runs, members can use it after you stop and resume it. Its running programs hold your logins in memory. The removal cannot be undone; `boat unshare` still makes the sandbox private again.
* `boat unshare` removes members' SSH keys from the running sandbox.

`boat list` shows `shared` or `private` next to your organization sandboxes. `boat info` shows it on the `org:` line.

This is not `boat snapshot share`, which gives a saved snapshot to another account. The API calls are [Share sandbox with the organization](/api/reference/sandboxes/share-sandbox) and [Make an organization sandbox private](/api/reference/sandboxes/unshare-sandbox).

### `boat org default-visibility`

Show or set whether new sandboxes of the organization start shared or private. Owners and admins set it. The default is `shared`. Existing sandboxes keep their setting.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat org default-visibility            # shows the current value
boat org default-visibility private    # new sandboxes start private
```

### `boat billing`

Manage the plan of the wallet in scope. This is your personal account, or the organization from `boat org switch` or `--org`. A step that needs a card opens Stripe Checkout in your browser. The command waits until the payment is complete.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat billing                       # plan, renewal date, the fullest start limit, wallet, extra starts
boat billing --all                 # also limits, prices, auto top-up and cards (--details is the same)
boat billing plan                  # the tiers, with the current one marked
boat billing plan 100              # switch to the $100/mo tier (prorated) or start it
boat billing status                # same as boat billing
boat billing extra-starts fail     # starts above your plan's limits always fail, even with money in the wallet
boat billing extra-starts wallet   # the wallet pays for them, an empty wallet fails them (default)
boat billing extra-starts invoice  # the wallet pays, then the next invoice (shows a summary, t shows the full terms; --yes accepts them)
boat billing extra-starts on       # same as invoice
boat billing extra-starts off      # turns the invoice off: the wallet pays again (does not change fail)
boat billing portal                # Stripe portal: card, invoices, VAT details, cancel
boat billing cancel                # cancel at the end of the paid month; offers to keep your disks 90 days
boat billing cancel --keep-disks --yes   # the same, without prompts
boat --org acme billing plan 20 --move-personal   # first org plan + bring your personal plan and sandboxes
```

The plan of an organization is per seat. `boat --org acme billing plan 100` bills \$100 × seats. The seats are the members. There are more seats if the owner bought extra seats on the dashboard. See [Organizations](/organizations/seats-and-limits#seats).

Credit packs, prepaid balance and auto-refill are gone. `boat wallet` replaces them.

### `boat wallet`

Show and fill the dollar wallet in scope. The wallet pays overage only: VM time past the plan, extra saved snapshots, extra starts and the AI proxy. It never pays the plan. See [Plan, wallet and running out](/billing#wallet).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat wallet                        # balance, auto top-up, cards
boat wallet pay 50                 # add $50 once, in Stripe Checkout ($15 to $100,000)
boat wallet auto-top-up 500        # add $500 each time the wallet runs low ($15 to $100,000)
boat wallet auto-top-up off
boat wallet card                   # add a card, in Stripe
boat --org acme wallet pay 500     # the organization's wallet (owner only)
```

* A payment of \$200 or more gets a bonus of 2% to 25%. `boat wallet pay` shows it before you pay.
* Auto top-up charges the card when the wallet drops below 10% of the amount, and never below \$5. It needs a saved card and a paid plan.

### `boat data-retention`

Show or enable zero data retention (ZDR). With zero data retention, boat deletes each sandbox permanently when it stops.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat data-retention status
boat data-retention enable
boat data-retention enable --yes
```

To enable it, you need a browser sign-in session (`boat login` without a key). An API key does not work. See [Data retention and deletion](/data-retention).

### `boat self-update`

Find and install the latest CLI release on your current channel.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat self-update
```

The local configuration is at `~/.config/ascii/boat/config.json`. `boat status` prints its path, the API URL in use, the account and the plan.


# Compliance and uptime
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/compliance
