SOC 2 status, platform uptime and the live status page, where data is stored, GDPR erasure, and how to report a security issue.

| Topic | Answer |
| - | - |
| SOC 2 | In progress |
| Sandbox uptime | 99.95%, measured over the history of all sandboxes |
| Platform status | Live on [status.ascii.dev](https://status.ascii.dev) |
| Where data is stored | Machines in Germany, Finland and France. Snapshot copies can be stored outside the EU. |
| Erase your data (GDPR) | [Close your account](/data-retention/close-account) |
| Report a security issue | [Support](/support) |

## Uptime

Sandboxes have an uptime of 99.95%. boat measures this over the history of all sandboxes.

* For the platform (the API, the dashboard, starts and stops), see the live status and its history at [status.ascii.dev](https://status.ascii.dev).
* A sandbox that stops answering has its own recovery steps. Read [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting#a-sandbox-does-not-answer).
* For a production workload, write to [support](/support) before you launch. Tell us your expected starts per minute and sandboxes at once.

## Data location

* Sandboxes run on machines in Germany, Finland and France.
* Snapshot copies can be stored outside the EU.

How long boat keeps each kind of data is on [Data retention](/data-retention#how-long-boat-keeps-data).

## Erase data

| Need | Page |
| - | - |
| Erase one sandbox or snapshot | [Delete](/data-retention/delete) |
| Keep nothing after a stop | [Zero data retention](/data-retention/zero-data-retention) |
| Erase your whole account (GDPR right to erasure) | [Close your account](/data-retention/close-account) |

## Report a security issue

Write to [support](/support). Put "security" in the subject. Do not post details in public channels such as Discord.

For how boat isolates sandboxes and protects credentials, read [Security and isolation](/security).


# Concepts
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/concepts

Every boat word defined once: sandbox, snapshot, saved snapshot, stop, resume, fork, delete, environment. The sandbox states, and the matching words at E2B, Daytona and Modal.

boat gives you sandboxes. A sandbox is a full Linux virtual machine with its own disk. You stop it to stop paying. You can resume it with the same disk for at least 14 days.

## Lifecycle

```mermaid theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
%%{init: {"theme": "base", "fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "themeVariables": {"fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "fontSize": "14px", "primaryColor": "#F1F3F9", "primaryBorderColor": "#263FA9", "primaryTextColor": "#060606", "secondaryColor": "#E0E3F2", "tertiaryColor": "#FEFEFE", "lineColor": "#060606", "textColor": "#060606", "mainBkg": "#F1F3F9", "nodeBorder": "#263FA9", "clusterBkg": "#FEFEFE", "clusterBorder": "#C4C4C4", "edgeLabelBackground": "#FEFEFE", "actorBkg": "#F1F3F9", "actorBorder": "#263FA9", "actorTextColor": "#060606", "actorLineColor": "#9E9E9E", "signalColor": "#060606", "signalTextColor": "#060606", "labelBoxBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "labelBoxBorderColor": "#263FA9", "noteBkgColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteBorderColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteTextColor": "#060606", "sectionBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "altSectionBkgColor": "#FEFEFE", "taskBkgColor": "#263FA9", "taskBorderColor": "#263FA9", "taskTextColor": "#FEFEFE", "gridColor": "#E0E0E0"}, "flowchart": {"padding": 16, "nodeSpacing": 48, "rankSpacing": 48, "curve": "linear"}, "sequence": {"boxMargin": 16, "actorMargin": 48, "noteMargin": 16, "messageMargin": 32, "mirrorActors": false}, "state": {"padding": 16}, "gantt": {"barHeight": 24, "barGap": 8, "fontSize": 14, "sectionFontSize": 14}}}%%
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Starting: boat new / boat fork
  Starting --> Running: ready
  Running --> Stopping: boat stop / auto-stop
  Stopping --> Stopped: disk saved
  Stopping --> Running: boat resume (same machine)
  Stopped --> Starting: boat resume
  Stopped --> Starting: boat fork (new sandbox)
  Running --> Error: machine lost
  Error --> Starting: boat resume
  Running --> Deleted: boat delete
  Stopped --> Deleted: boat delete
  Error --> Deleted: boat delete
  Deleted --> [*]

  Starting: Starting (API provisioning, provisioned, cloning)
  Running: Running (API ready, idle, running)
  Stopping: Stopping (API archiving)
  Stopped: Stopped (API archived)
  Error: Error (API error)
  Deleted: Deleted (gone from lists)
```

| State | API state names | CLI and dashboard show | Billed | Disk |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Starting | `provisioning`, `provisioned`, `cloning` | `provisioning`, `starting`, `cloning` | From `provisioned` | Restoring |
| Running | `ready`, `idle`, `running` | same | Yes | On the machine, saved each minute |
| Stopping | `archiving` | `stopping` | No | Last save in progress |
| Stopped | `archived` | `stopped` | No | Saved for at least 14 days, then eligible for deletion |
| Error | `error` | `error` | No | Held for 3 days |
| Deleted | none | none | No | Erased |

The API calls a stopped sandbox `archived`. It is the same state. Nothing is moved or deleted.

`idle` and `running` differ only for the [integrated agent](/integrated-agents): `running` means a prompt runs now. Commands work in both.

What works at `ready`, and what comes a few seconds later, is in [Readiness and resume speed](/readiness).

## Words

| Word | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **Sandbox** | One Linux virtual machine that you create, with its own disk, IP address and id (`bx_...`). |
| **Machine** | The hardware under a sandbox. A resume or a fork puts the sandbox on a new machine. |
| **Size** | The CPU, memory and disk of a sandbox: `small`, `default` (the medium size), `large`, `xlarge`. Read [Machines](/machines). |
| **Snapshot** | A saved copy of the disk. boat takes one every minute and one at each stop. Only the newest one is used. Read [Snapshots](/snapshots). |
| **Saved snapshot** | A snapshot that you save under a name. It has no scheduled expiry; unpaid extras can be deleted. Start new sandboxes from it with `boat new --from <name>`. Read [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates). |
| **Template** | Not a separate object. "Use a saved snapshot as a template" means: start many sandboxes from one saved snapshot. |
| **Stop** | Save the disk, then remove the machine. A resume within 10 minutes usually gets the same machine back, with memory and running programs. After that, they are gone. There is no pause. A stopped sandbox costs nothing, and boat keeps its disk for at least 14 days. Read [Stop a sandbox](/snapshots/stop). |
| **Auto-stop** | A timer that stops the sandbox. The default is 1 hour after the create or the last resume. Read [Auto-stop](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop). |
| **Always on** | A sandbox with auto-stop turned off. It runs until you stop it. |
| **Resume** | Start a stopped sandbox again, from its newest snapshot. Same id. Within 10 minutes of the stop, usually the same machine. After that, a new machine and a new IP address. |
| **Fork** | Make a new sandbox that copies the newest snapshot of another sandbox. The source does not change. |
| **Restore** | Get older files back. Resume and fork cannot use an older snapshot. Read [Restore an older snapshot](/snapshots/resume-and-fork#restore-an-older-snapshot-roll-back). |
| **Recover** | Restart the machine of a sandbox that does not answer. The disk is not touched. Read [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting#a-sandbox-does-not-answer). |
| **Delete** | Erase a sandbox and its snapshots for good. You cannot get it back. Read [Delete a sandbox](/data-retention/delete). |
| **Ready** | The sandbox runs commands now. Read [Readiness](/readiness). |
| **Hydrated** | All file content has arrived after a resume or fork. Files are readable before that. |
| **Environment** | Settings that a sandbox starts with: variables, secret files, repositories and logins. Read [Environments](/environments). |
| **Setup script** | Commands that run when a sandbox starts. Read [Setup scripts](/setup). |
| **Public URL** | An HTTPS address for one port of a sandbox. Read [Public URLs](/hosting). |
| **Share code** | A secret code (`bsh_...`) that lets another account start a sandbox from your saved snapshot. |
| **Organization** | A team account. Members share sandboxes, a plan, a wallet and seats. Read [Organizations](/organizations). |
| **Active wallet** | The account that pays for a new sandbox: you, or an organization. Read [Active wallet](/organizations/active-wallet). |
| **Wallet balance** | Dollars on an account or organization. It pays overage, never the plan. Read [Wallet](/billing#wallet). |
| **Seat** | One paid member place in an organization. Each seat adds the plan price and the included time. It adds the full limits on the \$2000 plan, 20% of them below. |

## Words at other providers

Other providers use some of the same words for other things. This table gives the closest boat word.

| boat | E2B | Daytona | Modal |
| - | - | - | - |
| Sandbox | Sandbox | Sandbox | Sandbox |
| Stop (disk kept, memory kept only for a resume within 10 minutes) | Pause in filesystem mode. A default pause always keeps memory, a boat stop keeps it only for 10 minutes | Stop | No match. Save a filesystem snapshot, then terminate |
| Resume | Resume (connect) | Start | Create a sandbox from the saved image |
| Delete | Kill | Delete | Terminate |
| Saved snapshot | Template | Snapshot | Filesystem snapshot (an image) |
| Fork | No direct match. Create from a template or snapshot | No direct match | Create from a filesystem snapshot |
| Auto-stop | Timeout | Auto-stop interval | Timeout |
| Stopped state | Paused | Stopped. boat has no separate archive step: a stopped sandbox is already in storage | No match |

Two differences cause most surprises:

* A boat **snapshot** is automatic and per sandbox. A Daytona snapshot is closer to a boat **saved snapshot**.
* A boat **stop** keeps memory only for a resume within 10 minutes, and only usually. After that, programs that you started by hand do not come back. Enabled systemd services and Docker containers start again. Read [What a snapshot saves](/snapshots/whats-saved).


# Data retention and deletion
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/data-retention

How long boat keeps each kind of data, stop versus delete, zero data retention, and the records that stay after a deletion.

This page is part of [Security and isolation](/security).

## How long boat keeps data

| Data | boat keeps it |
| - | - |
| Newest snapshot of a running sandbox | While it runs |
| Newest snapshot of a stopped sandbox | At least 14 days after the stop. Then it becomes eligible for automated retention cleanup. Once deleted, resume and fork fail with `409 snapshot_data_expired` ([details](/snapshots/stop#keep-a-stopped-sandbox-longer-than-14-days)) |
| Older snapshots of a sandbox | A short time, usually less than a day. Resume and fork never use them |
| Saved snapshot | No scheduled expiry. You can remove it. Saved snapshots above your plan's included count can be deleted 7 days after your wallet is empty ([details](/snapshots/templates#when-your-wallet-is-empty)) |
| Deleted sandbox or snapshot | Gone from lists at once. boat erases the stored data in the background ([details](/data-retention/delete)) |
| Command history: `boat exec` and API commands, with output | 7 days |
| Output of every other process | 72 hours |
| Closed account | 30 days, then boat purges it ([details](/data-retention/close-account)) |
| With zero data retention | boat deletes a sandbox's data when it stops ([details](/data-retention/zero-data-retention)) |
| With snapshots off | Nothing. A stop erases the sandbox ([details](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#snapshots-off)) |

An empty wallet stops your sandboxes after the included time is used. It does not delete them. Read [Why did my sandbox stop?](/troubleshooting#why-did-my-sandbox-stop).

The retention cleanup runs automatically when enabled. It currently reports eligible stopped sandboxes without deleting them in production. The 14-day rule does not yet trigger deletion there. Other deletion requests, such as `boat delete`, still run.

## Stop is not delete

A stop keeps the disk. A delete erases it.

| Action | Can you resume the sandbox? | What happens to data? |
| - | - | - |
| **[Stop](/snapshots/stop)** | Yes, for at least 14 days | The newest snapshot becomes eligible for automated cleanup after day 14. The job is currently report-only in production. Once deleted, resume and fork fail with `409 snapshot_data_expired`. To keep it longer, save a saved snapshot before day 14: `boat snapshot <id> <name>`. |
| **[Delete](/data-retention/delete)** | No | boat erases the sandbox content, its unshared snapshots and its machine data. You cannot undo it. |
| **[Zero data retention (ZDR)](/data-retention/zero-data-retention)** | No, after a stop | boat deletes the data of every sandbox when it stops. |
| **[Snapshots off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#snapshots-off)** | No | boat never saves the sandbox. A stop erases it. |
| **[Monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#monitoring-off)** | Yes | boat keeps no command or process output, no process list and no CPU/RAM samples. |

The API reports a stopped sandbox as `archived`. This is the same stop. It is not a deletion.

## Command history

The [command history](/long-running-tasks/command-history) of a sandbox is account data.

* A delete erases the history with the rest of the sandbox.
* With ZDR, a stop queues the history for deletion with the rest of the sandbox.
* With ZDR, boat does not save the output that a process wrote after the last 30-second read.

## All surfaces

Every task on these pages works on all four surfaces.

| | CLI | API | SDKs | Dashboard |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Delete a sandbox | `boat delete <id>` | `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` | `deleteSandbox` | [Sandboxes](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=sandboxes) `⋯` → **Delete permanently…** |
| Delete a snapshot | `boat snapshot delete <id>` | `DELETE /snapshots/{snapshotId}` | `deleteSnapshot` | [Snapshots](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=snapshots) |
| Delete all snapshots of a sandbox | `boat snapshot delete --all <id>` | `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots` | `deleteSandboxSnapshots` | [Snapshots](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=snapshots) → Select all |
| Delete a saved snapshot | `boat snapshot rm <name>` | `DELETE /saved-snapshots/{name}` | `deleteSavedSnapshot` | [Snapshots](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=snapshots) |
| Poll an operation | `boat deletion status <id>` | `GET /deletion-operations/{id}` | `getDeletionOperation` | shown inline while deleting |
| Read ZDR | `boat data-retention status` | `GET /account/data-retention` | `getDataRetention` | [Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) |
| Enable ZDR | `boat data-retention enable` | `PATCH /account/data-retention` | `updateDataRetention` | [Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) |

> [!WARNING]
>
> You cannot cancel a deletion operation. If you disable ZDR, only future stops change. Operations that boat already accepted continue.

## Records kept after content deletion

boat keeps only the records that it needs for security, abuse prevention, compliance and billing. These records are:

* The history of which machine ran each sandbox, and when.
* Network attribution, such as assigned IP and MAC records.
* Security audit events.
* Billing and usage records.

These records show who controlled the infrastructure and when. They do not keep your sandbox files, prompts, messages, secrets or generated artifacts.

For a privacy request, use [Support](/support).

## Learn more

> [card] [Delete a sandbox or snapshot](/data-retention/delete)
>
> Delete a sandbox or snapshots, follow the operation, and how saved snapshots are deleted.

> [card] [Zero data retention](/data-retention/zero-data-retention)
>
> Read and enable ZDR. What changes when it is on.

> [card] [Snapshots off and monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off)
>
> Keep no snapshots, or keep no monitoring data, for one sandbox or the whole account.

> [card] [Close your account and GDPR erasure](/data-retention/close-account)
>
> Close your account, reopen it in 30 days, or erase it for good.

# Close your account and GDPR erasure
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/data-retention/close-account

Close your account, reopen it within 30 days, or erase it for good for a GDPR request (right to erasure).

Closing removes the whole account, not one sandbox. To delete one sandbox, read [Delete a sandbox or snapshot](/data-retention/delete).

You can close the account only on the [Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) tab. It needs a dashboard sign-in session. boat refuses the request from an API key and from the CLI.

## What closing does

Closing does all of these at once:

* It cancels your subscription **immediately**, not at the end of the period. You lose the remaining included time and the money in your wallet. If you close just after a renewal, you lose that renewal.
* It stops every running sandbox. Each stop saves the disk first.
* It revokes every API key and every other session. The session that you closed from stays active, so you can still read your invoices.
* It sends you a confirmation email with the date when boat purges your data.

## The 30-day window

| Time after closing | State of the account |
| - | - |
| Up to **30 days** | Closed but you can get it back. **Reopen** on the same tab brings it back, except the subscription. |
| After 30 days | boat purges the sandbox data permanently. If you reopen, you get a working but empty account. |

## Permanent erasure (GDPR)

> [!WARNING]
>
> The same screen also offers permanent erasure, for GDPR requests. It does not wait 30 days. It erases the data and your identity when the sandboxes finish stopping. You **cannot cancel or reopen** it. Use ordinary closing, unless you need erasure.

boat keeps a small set of records after erasure, for security, abuse prevention and billing. Read [Records kept after content deletion](/data-retention#records-kept-after-content-deletion).

For any other privacy request, use [Support](/support).


# Delete a sandbox or snapshot
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/data-retention/delete

Delete a sandbox, its snapshots or a saved snapshot for good, follow the deletion until the data is erased, and what a delete keeps.

A delete is permanent. You cannot resume, fork or get back a deleted sandbox. There is no list of deleted sandboxes.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **If you want to use the data later, stop the sandbox. Do not delete it.** A stopped sandbox costs nothing and keeps its disk for at least 14 days. Save a saved snapshot before day 14 to keep it longer. Read [Stop a sandbox](/snapshots/stop).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd            # keeps the data; `boat resume` brings it back
boat delete bx_f7k2q9hd          # erases the sandbox AND its snapshots, for good
```

## Delete a sandbox

A delete of a running sandbox stops it at once. It takes no last snapshot. Billing for the sandbox ends at the delete.

Every sandbox or snapshot delete needs the header `X-Ascii-Confirm-Delete`. Its value must be exactly the target id. If it is not, boat refuses the request with `409` and deletes nothing. The header keeps its old name. The CLI and the dashboard set it for you.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat delete bx_f7k2q9hd          # asks first, then follows the operation to completion
boat delete bx_f7k2q9hd --yes    # no prompt, for scripts
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Ascii-Confirm-Delete: $BOAT_ID"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const accepted = await sandbox.deleteSandbox({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  xAsciiConfirmDelete: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
});
console.log(accepted.operation.id, accepted.operation.status);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
accepted = sandbox.delete_sandbox(
    x_ascii_confirm_delete="bx_f7k2q9hd",
    sandbox_id="bx_f7k2q9hd",
)
print(accepted.operation.id, accepted.operation.status)
```

`$BOAT_API_BASE` is `https://boat.dev/api/v1`.

In the dashboard, open [Sandboxes](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=sandboxes). Open the `⋯` menu on the row of the sandbox and choose **Delete permanently…**.

## How a delete works

1. You send a delete request.
2. boat returns `202 Accepted` with an operation.
3. The sandbox or snapshot disappears from lists, resumes and forks at once.
4. boat erases the stored data in the background, when nothing reads it any more.
5. You poll the operation until its status is `completed`.

boat never refuses a delete because the data is still in use.

The `stage` of the operation tells you where the deletion is.

| `stage` | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `removing` | boat erases the stored data now. |
| `waiting_for_uploads` | boat erases the data at `expectedBy`, when the last upload link for it expires. This is at most six hours after the last upload. |
| `retrying` | A short fault occurred. boat tries again by itself. |
| `completed` | boat erased every snapshot of it. A newer snapshot, a fork or a saved snapshot made from it keeps the data it reads. That data goes when you delete those too. |

> [!WARNING]
>
> You cannot cancel a deletion operation.

## Poll the operation

A delete returns an operation id (`bdop_…`). Poll it until `status` is `completed`.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat deletion status bdop_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/deletion-operations/$OPERATION_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const current = await sandbox.getDeletionOperation({ operationId: accepted.operation.id });
console.log(current.operation.status);   // pending | processing | blocked | completed
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
current = sandbox.get_deletion_operation(accepted.operation.id)
print(current.operation.status)
```

`boat delete` already polls for you. It prints the operation when it finishes. Use `boat deletion status` to check later on an operation that you started elsewhere.

## Delete one snapshot

| Request | What it deletes | Confirmation header |
| - | - | - |
| `DELETE /snapshots/{snapshotId}` | One automatic snapshot | The snapshot id |
| `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots` | Every automatic snapshot of one sandbox. The sandbox stays. A stopped sandbox with no snapshot has nothing to resume from. | The sandbox id |
| `DELETE /saved-snapshots/{name}` | One saved snapshot, by name | None |

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat snapshot delete <snapshotId>               # one automatic snapshot
boat snapshot delete --all bx_f7k2q9hd          # every automatic snapshot of a sandbox
boat snapshot delete --all bx_f7k2q9hd --yes    # same, no prompt, for scripts
boat snapshot rm web-stack                      # a saved snapshot, by name
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/snapshots/$SNAPSHOT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Ascii-Confirm-Delete: $SNAPSHOT_ID"

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/snapshots" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Ascii-Confirm-Delete: $BOAT_ID"

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/saved-snapshots/web-stack" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.deleteSnapshot({
  snapshotId: "<snapshotId>",
  xAsciiConfirmDelete: "<snapshotId>",
});

await sandbox.deleteSandboxSnapshots({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  xAsciiConfirmDelete: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
});

await sandbox.deleteSavedSnapshot({ name: "web-stack" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.delete_snapshot(
    snapshot_id="<snapshotId>",
    x_ascii_confirm_delete="<snapshotId>",
)

sandbox.delete_sandbox_snapshots(
    sandbox_id="bx_f7k2q9hd",
    x_ascii_confirm_delete="bx_f7k2q9hd",
)

sandbox.delete_saved_snapshot("web-stack")
```

You can also delete snapshots on the [Snapshots](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=snapshots) tab of the dashboard.

Deletion and retention responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`.

## What a delete keeps

Sandboxes can share snapshot data. A fork, a resume and a deploy from a saved snapshot read the same data as their source. So a delete erases only the data that nothing else uses. boat keeps:

* The data that a fork of this sandbox still needs.
* Your **saved snapshots** from this sandbox. They exist to outlive it. To remove one, run `boat snapshot rm <name>`.

boat frees the storage when no sandbox and no saved snapshot uses it.

When you remove a saved snapshot, it becomes unavailable at once. boat erases its data **six hours** later at the earliest. Upload links for snapshots stay valid for six hours. This delay stops an upload that already started from making the data again after the delete.

If you enable [zero data retention](/data-retention/zero-data-retention), boat removes your saved snapshots and queues their data for deletion. You cannot save a saved snapshot while ZDR is on.


# Snapshots off and monitoring off
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off

Keep no snapshots of a sandbox, or keep no monitoring data, for one sandbox or for the whole account.

| Setting | What boat does not keep | Can you resume the sandbox? |
| - | - | - |
| [Snapshots off](#snapshots-off) | Any copy of the sandbox outside its machine | No. A stop erases it. |
| [Monitoring off](#monitoring-off) | Command and process output, the process list, CPU/RAM samples | Yes |

## Snapshots off

boat never captures a sandbox with snapshots off.

* Nothing of the sandbox is stored outside its machine.
* No background work runs on it.
* A stop erases it.
* You cannot resume it, fork it or save it as a saved snapshot.
* If its machine fails, there is no backup.
* If you create it from a saved snapshot or another sandbox, its snapshot list shows the snapshots of that source with `origin: "template"`. They are copies of the data of the source. boat did not capture them from this sandbox.

### Turn snapshots off for the whole account

Do one of these:

* On the [Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) tab, under **Data & privacy**, turn on **Snapshots off**.
* Send `PATCH /account/data-retention` with `{"snapshotsOff": true}`. This needs a browser sign-in session. An API key gets `403 session_required`.

Every sandbox that you create or fork after this has snapshots off, from any surface. Existing sandboxes keep their setting.

The setting covers the sandboxes that you create, also in an organization. It does not cover sandboxes of other members.

### Turn snapshots off for one sandbox

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --no-snapshots
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"snapshots":false}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.create({ snapshots: false });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_request import CreateSandboxRequest

sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(snapshots=False))
```

## Monitoring off

boat keeps no monitoring data for a sandbox with monitoring off.

| Not kept | Still works |
| - | - |
| [Command history](/long-running-tasks/command-history) and the output of every process | Live output of a running command (attach, read from an offset) |
| The process list | Abuse checks on the machine |
| CPU, RAM, disk and IO samples, and their graphs and [OpenTelemetry](/opentelemetry) metrics | Lifecycle events and webhooks |

* The sandbox runs no process tracer.
* Disk-full alerts need CPU/RAM samples. They are not available for this sandbox.
* The cause shown for a lost sandbox needs CPU/RAM samples. It is not available for this sandbox.
* Its history, processes and metrics calls return `409 monitoring_off`.

### Turn monitoring off for the whole account

Do one of these:

* On the [Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) tab, under **Data & privacy**, turn on **Monitoring off**.
* Send `PATCH /account/data-retention` with `{"monitoringOff": true}`. This needs a browser sign-in session. An API key gets `403 session_required`.

Every sandbox that you create or fork after this has monitoring off. Existing sandboxes keep their setting. The setting covers the sandboxes that you create, also in an organization.

While this setting is on, boat refuses a request with `monitoring: true`. The error is `409 monitoring_off_for_account`.

A fork of a sandbox with monitoring off also has monitoring off. To change this, send `monitoring: true` in the fork request.

### Turn monitoring off for one sandbox

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --no-monitoring
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"monitoring":false}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.create({ monitoring: false });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_request import CreateSandboxRequest

sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(monitoring=False))
```

The sandbox shows `"monitoring": false`.


# Zero data retention
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/data-retention/zero-data-retention

Read and enable zero data retention (ZDR): boat deletes the data of each sandbox when it stops. How it works in an organization.

With zero data retention (ZDR), boat deletes the data of each sandbox when it stops. You cannot resume or fork a sandbox after it stops.

ZDR is a setting of your own account. In an organization, each member turns it on for the sandboxes that they create. Read [Organizations](#organizations).

## Read the setting

You can read the setting from anywhere. An API key works.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat data-retention status
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/account/data-retention" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const policy = await sandbox.getDataRetention();
console.log(policy.enabled);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
policy = sandbox.get_data_retention()
print(policy.enabled)
```

`$BOAT_API_BASE` is `https://boat.dev/api/v1`. `GET /me` also returns the setting, in the `zeroDataRetention` fields.

## Enable zero data retention

> [!WARNING]
>
> To **change** the setting, you need a browser sign-in session. An API key does not work. Run `boat login` without a key first, or use the dashboard. An SDK client that uses `BOAT_API_KEY` gets `403 session_required`. This is on purpose. Enabling ZDR deletes the data of every stopped sandbox, so a leaked API key must never reach it.

1. Sign in with a browser session. Run `boat login` without a key, or open the dashboard.
2. Send the exact phrase `delete archived sandbox data` as the confirmation. "Archived" is the API name of a stopped sandbox.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat data-retention enable          # prompts for the confirmation phrase
boat data-retention enable --yes    # skip the prompt
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PATCH "$BOAT_API_BASE/account/data-retention" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_SESSION_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"enabled":true,"confirmation":"delete archived sandbox data"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
// Requires a browser session token, not an API key.
await sandbox.updateDataRetention({
  enabled: true,
  confirmation: "delete archived sandbox data",
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.data_retention_update_request import DataRetentionUpdateRequest

# Requires a browser session token, not an API key.
sandbox.update_data_retention(DataRetentionUpdateRequest(
    enabled=True,
    confirmation="delete archived sandbox data",
))
```

In the dashboard, the toggle is under **Data & privacy** on the [Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account) tab.

## What happens when ZDR is on

* boat queues the data of your stopped sandboxes for deletion.
* Each sandbox deletes its data when it stops. This includes auto-stop and a stop for an empty wallet.
* boat removes your saved snapshots and queues their data for deletion. You cannot save a new saved snapshot.
* Accepted deletions continue in the background until boat checks that they are complete.

> [!WARNING]
>
> You cannot cancel a deletion operation. If you disable ZDR, only future stops change. Operations that boat already accepted continue.

ZDR still snapshots a sandbox while it runs. boat uses these snapshots to rebuild a sandbox after a machine fails. To keep nothing at all, turn [snapshots off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#snapshots-off).

## Organizations

| Question | Answer |
| - | - |
| Who turns ZDR on? | Each person, for their own account. An organization has no ZDR setting of its own |
| Which sandboxes does it cover? | Every sandbox that you create, also the ones that an organization pays for |
| Does it cover sandboxes of other members? | No. Each member turns it on for their own sandboxes |
| Does it need a role? | No. Any member can turn it on for their own account |

To cover a whole team, ask each member to turn ZDR on. Check each account with `boat data-retention status`.

The same rule applies to [snapshots off and monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off).


# Desktop streaming
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/desktop-streaming

Open the Linux desktop of a sandbox in your browser, watch an agent use it, embed it in your app, or record it.

Each sandbox has a Linux desktop that you open in your browser. Use it for these tasks:

* Look at a running app.
* Use Chrome.
* Debug Electron apps.
* Control GUI tools that are hard to use over SSH.

The agents of the sandbox drive the same screen with the built-in [`computer` tools](/integrated-agents/computer-use). You can watch a prompt do GUI work live.

## Open the desktop

Run this command on your computer. It opens a desktop URL that is already signed in. Integrations get the same URL through the SDK or the API (`BOAT_API_BASE=https://boat.dev/api/v1`). Open the URL within 10 minutes. Read [Embed the desktop and secure its URL](/desktop-streaming/urls-and-security).

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat desktop bx_f7k2q9hd
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/desktop?theme=light" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const desktop = await sandbox.desktop({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd", theme: "light" });
console.log(desktop.desktopUrl);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
desktop = sandbox.desktop("bx_f7k2q9hd", theme="light")
print(desktop.desktop_url)
```

You can also open the desktop from the [Sandboxes](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=sandboxes) tab of the dashboard while the sandbox runs.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The desktop works only while the sandbox runs. Resume a stopped sandbox first. If the sandbox is still starting, the API returns `desktop_not_ready`. Retry a few seconds later.

## Ways to view the sandbox

| View | What you see | Command |
| - | - | - |
| Desktop (default) | The full desktop over Moonlight (WebRTC), 1920x1080 at 60 fps | `boat desktop <id>` |
| Browser | Only Chrome, 1920x1080 at 60 fps | `boat browser <id>` |

## Learn more

> [card] [Browser-only view](/desktop-streaming/browser-only)
>
> Show only Chrome. Use more than one Chrome profile.

> [card] [Drive and record the desktop](/desktop-streaming/drive-and-record)
>
> Let an agent use the screen. Record the screen to an MP4.

> [card] [Desktop background](/desktop-streaming/background)
>
> Put your own PNG on the desktop.

> [card] [Embed the desktop and secure its URL](/desktop-streaming/urls-and-security)
>
> What a desktop URL looks like, how long it works, how to embed it, and how to keep it safe.

## Related

* [Computer use for the sandbox's agents](/integrated-agents/computer-use)
* [SSH](/ssh-access)
* [Public URLs](/hosting)
* [Machines](/machines)


# Desktop background
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/desktop-streaming/background

Put your own PNG image on the sandbox desktop.

## Set your own background

1. Put a PNG file at `~/.config/boat/wallpaper.png` on the sandbox.
2. The desktop shows it at once.

The image stays after a stop, a resume and a fork. To go back to the default background, delete the file.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat scp ./wallpaper.png bx_f7k2q9hd:/home/user/.config/boat/wallpaper.png
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"curl -fsSL -o ~/.config/boat/wallpaper.png https://example.com/wallpaper.png"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.command({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  command: "curl -fsSL -o ~/.config/boat/wallpaper.png https://example.com/wallpaper.png",
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.command_request import CommandRequest

sandbox.command("bx_f7k2q9hd", CommandRequest(
    command="curl -fsSL -o ~/.config/boat/wallpaper.png https://example.com/wallpaper.png",
))
```

## Image limits

| Limit | Value |
| - | - |
| Format | PNG |
| File size | 16 MiB or less |
| Width or height | 8192 pixels or less |
| Total pixels | 16,777,216 or less (for example 4096x4096) |

The image fills the screen and keeps its aspect ratio. If the file is not a valid PNG, the desktop keeps the default background.


# Browser-only view
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/desktop-streaming/browser-only

Stream only Chrome from a sandbox, without the desktop, and choose which Chrome profile to open.

Use the browser-only view when a person must see and control Chrome, but not the sandbox desktop.

## Open the browser view

* In the dashboard, open the sandbox menu and select **Browser**.
* In the CLI, run one of these commands:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat browser bx_f7k2q9hd
boat browser bx_f7k2q9hd --profile /data/chrome-profile
```

* In the API, call `POST /sandboxes/{id}/browser`. The response has `browserUrl`.
* The URL has the same 10-minute rule as a desktop URL. Read [Embed the desktop and secure its URL](/desktop-streaming/urls-and-security#how-long-a-desktop-url-works).

## Use a Chrome profile

Add `--profile <absolute path on the sandbox>` to stream a specific Chrome user data directory. One sandbox can then hold several signed-in profiles. You choose which one to open.

| Rule | Detail |
| - | - |
| Creation | boat creates the directory for you. |
| Location | Outside system directories and outside `/home/user`. |
| Snapshots | The directory goes with the snapshots and forks of the sandbox. |
| Old sandboxes | Sandboxes created before this feature return `chrome_profile_unsupported`. |

## How the browser view works

The browser view is a separate browser surface on the same running sandbox. It does not create another sandbox. It never falls back to the desktop.

| Topic | Behavior |
| - | - |
| Stream quality | 1920x1080 at 60 fps, the same as the default desktop. |
| Chrome | Chrome keeps its tabs and its address bar. |
| Close controls | boat hides the window-close controls on purpose. |
| Minimize | Chrome's minimize cannot leave the stream on a blank desktop. |
| Last tab | When you close the last tab, Chrome opens a new tab. The stream stays up. |
| Run `boat browser` again | The live stream stays up. The command prints a new URL. |
| Second viewer tab | Two browser viewer tabs cannot share the stream. The new tab takes the stream from the first tab. |
| Desktop at the same time | The desktop and the browser view can run together. |
| Viewer controls | Mute, reconnect and fullscreen, the same as the desktop stream. |

A browser URL cannot attach to the desktop stream. The browser view has no clipboard routes.

> [!WARNING]
>
> The browser-only view limits the stream to Chrome. It does not show controls to close Chrome. It is not a security boundary against code that already runs inside the sandbox. A boat user who can run any code, or who has root, can read or change the browser process and its data. Keep the returned URL secret.


# Drive and record the desktop
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/desktop-streaming/drive-and-record

Let the agents of a sandbox use its desktop, mix shell commands with prompts, and record the screen to an MP4.

## Drive the desktop with a prompt

The coding agents of the sandbox drive the same screen that you stream. Each harness on a sandbox has built-in `computer` tools. These tools take screenshots, click, type, scroll and start apps. You only send a prompt:

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd "Open example.com in Chrome and tell me the page title"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/prompt" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Open example.com in Chrome and tell me the page title"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.prompt({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  prompt: "Open example.com in Chrome and tell me the page title",
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.prompt_request import PromptRequest

sandbox.prompt("bx_f7k2q9hd", PromptRequest(
    prompt="Open example.com in Chrome and tell me the page title",
))
```

A prompt needs a connected AI key or subscription first. Without it, the API returns `409 provider_not_configured`. Read [Keys and subscriptions](/integrated-agents/keys).

Open a stream in one window. Watch the agent work in it.

* You install nothing.
* You register nothing.
* Each harness already has the tools.

For the full tool list, the tool names per harness and the health check, read [Computer use](/integrated-agents/computer-use).

## Mix shell commands and prompts

Shell commands also work on the same screen. You can use them together with prompts. For example, open a page yourself, then give the sandbox a visual task:

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd 'DISPLAY=:0 google-chrome-stable "https://example.com" & sleep 2; wmctrl -a Chrome'
boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd "Complete the checkout flow in the open browser window"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"DISPLAY=:0 google-chrome-stable \"https://example.com\" & sleep 2; wmctrl -a Chrome"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.command({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  command: 'DISPLAY=:0 google-chrome-stable "https://example.com" & sleep 2; wmctrl -a Chrome',
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.command("bx_f7k2q9hd", CommandRequest(
    command='DISPLAY=:0 google-chrome-stable "https://example.com" & sleep 2; wmctrl -a Chrome',
))
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> A sandbox has one screen. Each conversation on the sandbox drives that same screen. If two agents click at the same time, they interfere with each other. Give each parallel GUI task its own sandbox, or run the tasks one after the other.

## Record the screen

`ascii-record-desktop` records the live desktop to an MP4 from inside the sandbox. Use it to make a demo or to keep evidence of a GUI run.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd "ascii-record-desktop start /home/user/demo.mp4"
# ... drive the desktop ...
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd "ascii-record-desktop stop"
boat scp bx_f7k2q9hd:/home/user/demo.mp4 ./demo.mp4
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"ascii-record-desktop start /home/user/demo.mp4"}'

# ... drive the desktop ...

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"ascii-record-desktop stop"}'

curl -L -o demo.mp4 "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/artifacts?path=demo.mp4" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.command({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  command: "ascii-record-desktop start /home/user/demo.mp4",
});
// ... drive the desktop ...
await sandbox.command({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd", command: "ascii-record-desktop stop" });
const video = await sandbox.artifact({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd", path: "demo.mp4" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.command_request import CommandRequest

sandbox.command("bx_f7k2q9hd", CommandRequest(
    command="ascii-record-desktop start /home/user/demo.mp4",
))
# ... drive the desktop ...
sandbox.command("bx_f7k2q9hd", CommandRequest(command="ascii-record-desktop stop"))
video = sandbox.artifact("bx_f7k2q9hd", "demo.mp4")
```

* Stop the recording before you download the file. Until then, the MP4 is not complete.
* Run `ascii-record-desktop status` to see if a recording runs.
* The tool keeps its old name, `ascii-record-desktop`.

To share a recording without a download, serve its folder from the sandbox. Then expose the folder with a URL that needs a token:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --detach "cd ~ && python3 -m http.server 8099 --bind 0.0.0.0"
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 8099
```


# Embed the desktop and secure its URL
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/desktop-streaming/urls-and-security

What a desktop URL contains, how long it works, how to embed the stream in your app in an iframe, and how boat protects the desktop.

This page covers desktop URLs. For every URL that carries a token, read [Security and isolation](/security#urls-that-carry-a-token).

## Embed the stream in your app

**1. Ask for a URL on your server**

On each page load, your server calls the desktop endpoint with your API key. Do not put the API key in the browser.

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/desktop?theme=light" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

`BOAT_API_BASE` is `https://boat.dev/api/v1`. The response has `desktopUrl`.

**2. Hide the viewer overlay (optional)**

Add `overlay=0` to the query string, before the `#`. The side panel and the stats text then never show. The token stays in the fragment.

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
https://<sandbox-desktop-host>/stream.html?hostId=<host>&appId=<app>&theme=light&overlay=0#token=<token>
```

**3. Put the URL in an iframe**

```html theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
<iframe src="DESKTOP_URL" allow="autoplay; fullscreen; clipboard-read; clipboard-write" style="width:100%;aspect-ratio:16/9;border:0"></iframe>
```

## How long a desktop URL works

| Case | What happens |
| - | - |
| You open the URL within 10 minutes | The stream starts. |
| You open the URL after 10 minutes | The viewer cannot sign in. Ask for a new URL. |
| A stream is already open | It keeps playing after the 10 minutes. |
| The page reloads, or the viewer reconnects after 10 minutes | It needs a new URL. Ask for one on each page load. |
| The sandbox stops | The stream ends. After a resume, ask for a new URL. |

## What happens when you open the desktop

1. The CLI or the dashboard asks boat for a new signed-in desktop URL for your sandbox.
2. If the desktop stream is not ready, boat prepares it.
3. boat opens the browser viewer.

The URL opens a browser page. It looks like this:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
https://<sandbox-desktop-host>/stream.html?hostId=<host>&appId=<app>&theme=light#token=<token>
```

boat generates the host, the IDs and the token for the running sandbox.

`boat desktop` also prints a `viewerUrl`. It carries the same token, so treat it the same way.

## How the Moonlight viewer handles the token

* The viewer removes the fragment from the URL at once.
* The viewer sends the token in authenticated request headers and in the first WebSocket frame.
* The viewer never puts the token in an HTTP or WebSocket request URL.

## Security model

| Topic | Rule |
| - | - |
| How boat makes a URL | Only through the authenticated boat API. The API key needs the `desktop` action. |
| URL lifetime | Open it within 10 minutes. See the table above. |
| List and info responses | They do not cache or return a desktop URL. Call the desktop endpoint each time you open a stream. |
| Clipboard | Reads and writes work only with the credentials of the active desktop Moonlight stream. |
| Browser-only view | It has no clipboard routes. |

Anyone who has the full URL can attach to that desktop session. Treat the URL as sensitive:

* Do not paste the full URL into shared chats or logs.
* To give another person lasting access to a sandbox, use an [organization](/organizations). Do not share a desktop URL.

## After a stop, resume or fork

* When you stop a sandbox, the desktop is not available. Resume the sandbox to use it again.
* Desktop programs do not survive a resume or a fork. Open Chrome again and restart your app or dev server.
* The `computer` tools come back by themselves. boat restarts the desktop daemon behind them with the sandbox.


# Environments
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments

Set what every new sandbox starts with: GitHub repositories, environment variables, secret files, repository setup scripts and credentials.

An **environment** is the set of settings that a new sandbox gets when it starts. It holds five things:

| Item | What the sandbox gets | Page |
| - | - | - |
| Repositories | GitHub repositories cloned into `/home/user` | [Repositories](/environments/repositories) |
| Secrets | Environment variables and secret files | [Secrets, env vars and .env files](/environments/secrets) |
| Setup scripts | One script per repository, run at each start | [Setup scripts](/setup) |
| Credentials | Your GitHub token, a boat API key, agent logins | [Access and credentials](/environments/access) |
| AI credential profile | The AI keys that the sandbox's agents use | [Access and credentials](/environments/access#ai-credentials) |

Every account starts with one environment named `base`. You can add more, for example `staging` and `prod`. Each one is a full environment. Name the environment when you create, resume or fork a sandbox. Read [Manage environments](/environments/manage).

Manage environments in [Dashboard > Environment](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=environment) or with the `boat env` commands.

An organization environment is open to every member by default. An owner or admin can limit it to a list of members with `boat env access`. Read [Limit who can use an environment or profile](/organizations#limit-who-can-use-an-environment-or-profile).

> [!TIP]
>
> Not sure if you need an environment, a setup script or a saved snapshot? Read [Environment, setup script or saved snapshot?](/environments/choose).

## Safe for third parties

One switch sets the security of an environment.

| Switch | Use it for | What the sandbox gets |
| - | - | - |
| On | Sandboxes that other people use, for example your end users | Nothing of yours: no variables, no secret files, no GitHub, no credentials, no repository setup scripts |
| Off | Sandboxes that only you use | What the four section toggles allow |

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set base --safe-for-third-parties true
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> `boat onboard` sets this switch when you answer that other people use your sandboxes. Then no variable and no secret file reaches a sandbox. Run `boat env info base` to see the switch.

For all the details, read [Access and credentials](/environments/access).

## What happens when you save a change

* boat makes a new version of the environment.
* New sandboxes get the new version.
* Running sandboxes stay on their version until you upgrade them.

Read [Versions and upgrades](/environments/versions).

## Learn more

> [card] [Environment, setup script or saved snapshot?](/environments/choose)
>
> Pick the right tool for what a new sandbox needs.

> [card] [Access and credentials](/environments/access)
>
> The safe for third parties switch, the four section toggles, and how to protect an existing sandbox.

> [card] [Secrets, env vars and .env files](/environments/secrets)
>
> Environment variables, secret files, and values for one sandbox only.

> [card] [Private registries](/environments/private-registries)
>
> Log in to private npm, pip and Docker registries in every sandbox.

> [card] [Repositories](/environments/repositories)
>
> Clone GitHub repositories into each sandbox, and find where they land.

> [card] [Versions and upgrades](/environments/versions)
>
> Which version a sandbox uses, and how to move it to the latest one.

> [card] [Manage environments](/environments/manage)
>
> Have more than one environment: create, rename, delete, pick one for a sandbox, share with your organization.

## Related

* [Setup scripts](/setup)
* [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates)
* [CLI reference](/cli-reference)


# Access and credentials
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments/access

Choose what of yours a sandbox receives: GitHub access, secrets, setup scripts, boat credentials and agent logins.

This page covers the credentials a sandbox gets. For the full security picture, read [Security and isolation](/security).

## Safe for third parties

One switch sets the security of an environment.

> [card] On
>
> Use it for sandboxes that other people use, for example your own end users. **boat passes nothing of yours.** The sandbox gets no environment variables, no secret files, no GitHub access, no boat credentials, no agent logins and no repository setup scripts. This is true whatever the section toggles say. The sandbox cannot act on your account or your other sandboxes.

> [card] Off
>
> Use it for sandboxes that only you use. The four section toggles below apply. You choose exactly what goes in.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set base --safe-for-third-parties true
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"safeForThirdParties":true}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.updateEnvironment({
  environmentId: envId,
  safeForThirdParties: true,
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.update_sandbox_environment_request import UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest

sandbox.update_environment(env_id, UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(safe_for_third_parties=True))
```

`$BOAT_API_BASE` is `https://boat.dev/api/v1`. Get `$ENV_ID` from `GET /environments` or `boat env list`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> When the switch is on, the toggle fields still show `true` in `boat env list` and the API. The `effective` field shows what sandboxes really get. A secret that you add to such an environment reaches no sandbox. The API answer then carries a `warning`.

Check what a sandbox received:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env info base                      # safeForThirdParties: yes or no
boat exec <id> 'echo "[$STRIPE_KEY]"'   # [] means the variable did not arrive
```

### The `--no-env` flag

The `--no-env` flag (`noEnv` in the API) gives the same protection to one sandbox. boat keeps this flag forever.

* `boat new --no-env` works exactly like a start in an environment that is safe for third parties.
* Use the environment when more than a few sandboxes need this protection.
* The environment setting applies to every sandbox that uses it.
* The environment setting stays through forks and resumes. Your code does not have to pass a flag.

### What a normal sandbox receives

This table shows what a sandbox gets from your account when boat withholds nothing.

| Type | What boat passes in |
| - | - |
| Environment variables | Your environment's variables, your GitHub token, and your model credentials if you configured agents (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CHATGPT_ACCOUNT_ID`) |
| Credential files | Your secret files, the GitHub CLI login (`~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`), git credentials in cloned repositories, Claude and Codex logins (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, `~/.codex/auth.json`), and the in-sandbox boat CLI token (`~/.config/ascii/boat/config.json`) |
| Scripts | The setup scripts of your repositories |

Every sandbox, protected or not, also gets two neutral variables: `BOAT_ID` and `ASCII_TOKEN`. `ASCII_TOKEN` can act only on this one sandbox. A protected sandbox receives nothing else, except the values that you pass with `env`.

### What a protected home contains

A protected sandbox does not start with an empty home. boat puts these defaults in every home. They are not your data, and they hold no account credentials.

| Location | Content |
| - | - |
| `~/.claude`, `~/.claude.json` | Claude Code skills, MCP configuration and default settings |
| `~/.codex`, `~/.config/opencode` | Codex and OpenCode skills and configuration |
| Default Chrome profile | Default preferences |
| Remote desktop key | A key for this sandbox only |

The credential files in the table above do not exist in a new protected sandbox.

### Protect an existing sandbox

A snapshot of a normal sandbox can contain your secrets. To protect a sandbox made from such a snapshot, resume or fork it with `--no-env`:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat resume <id> --no-env
boat fork <id> --no-env
```

Before the sandbox becomes reachable, boat removes every owner secret that the snapshot can contain:

* The managed `~/.bashrc` blocks.
* `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`. boat also runs a `gh` logout.
* `~/.git-credentials`.
* The `~/.ssh/id_*` private keys.
* The Codex and Claude credential files.
* The in-sandbox boat CLI token.
* Every secret file that you configured.

boat keeps `authorized_keys` and `known_hosts`, so you can still reach the sandbox.

boat does not touch credentials that it did not write. These stay:

* `aws` and `gcloud` credentials.
* `.netrc` and `.npmrc`.
* Docker logins added inside the sandbox.

While the removal runs, SSH and desktop return a `sandbox_securing` error. Retry the request. This change goes one way only. The sandbox stays protected after it.

> [!WARNING]
>
> boat removes the Claude and Codex credential files even when the sandbox's own user signed in with a personal account inside the sandbox. boat cannot tell whose files they are. If they belong to the sandbox's user, back them up first and restore them after.

## The four section toggles

When *Safe for third parties* is off, four separate toggles decide what a sandbox receives. Each toggle is a section in the dashboard. Open a section to edit what is inside it.

| Section | CLI flag | What the sandbox gets | When you turn it off |
| - | - | - | - |
| GitHub repositories | `--github` | Your repositories cloned in, the GitHub token, and the repository setup scripts | `gh` and `git push` stop working. No setup script runs. |
| Secrets | `--secrets` | Your environment variables and secret files | Sandboxes drop them at their next start. boat keeps what you typed. |
| boat credentials | `--boat-credentials` | A boat API key, so the sandbox can snapshot, stop and resume itself | The sandbox cannot manage its own lifecycle |
| Agents credentials | `--agents-credentials` | The provider keys (Claude, Codex, and others) from the Agents & Proxying tab | Agents in the sandbox have no login |

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set base --github true --secrets true --boat-credentials false --agents-credentials true
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"passGithub":true,"passSecrets":true,"passSandboxCredentials":false,"passAgentsCredentials":true}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.updateEnvironment({
  environmentId: envId,
  passGithub: true,
  passSecrets: true,
  passSandboxCredentials: false,
  passAgentsCredentials: true,
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.update_environment(env_id, UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(
    pass_github=True,
    pass_secrets=True,
    pass_sandbox_credentials=False,
    pass_agents_credentials=True,
))
```

## AI credentials

Two fields decide which AI credentials the environment's sandboxes get.

| Field | CLI flag | What it does |
| - | - | - |
| `credentialProfileId` | `--credential-profile <name\|id\|default>` | The [credential profile](/ai-credentials#credential-profiles) the sandboxes get. `null` (`default` in the CLI) means the sandbox owner's default profile |
| `proxyAiCredentials` | `--proxy-ai-credentials <true\|false>` | Only with *Safe for third parties* on. The sandboxes still get AI credentials, as [proxy placeholders](/ai-credentials#the-ai-credentials-proxy). Needs the proxy on for the profile owner, else `400 ai_proxy_off` |

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set base --credential-profile work
boat env set customers --safe-for-third-parties true --proxy-ai-credentials true
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"credentialProfileId":"work"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.updateEnvironment({ environmentId: envId, credentialProfileId: "work" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.update_environment(env_id, UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(credential_profile_id="work"))
```


# Environment, setup script or saved snapshot?
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments/choose

Pick the right tool for what a new sandbox needs: settings and secrets, commands at each start, or a disk with your tools already installed.

Each tool does one job. Most setups use two or three of them together.

| You want | Use | It holds | When it applies |
| - | - | - | - |
| The same secrets, repositories and credentials in every sandbox | [Environment](/environments) | Settings only, no disk | At each start |
| Packages, tools or data already installed | [Saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates) | A full copy of a sandbox disk | When you create a sandbox with `--from` |
| Commands that must run at each start, for example `git pull` or `npm install` | [Repository setup script](/setup#repository-setup-scripts) | A script, attached to a repository in an environment | At each start: create, resume and fork |
| Commands for one sandbox only | [`--setup-file`](/setup#per-sandbox-setup-file) | A script, given at create | Once, at create |

Rules:

* Put slow installs in a saved snapshot. A setup script repeats them at every start.
* Put secrets in an environment, never in a saved snapshot. A saved snapshot keeps every file on its disk.
* boat has no custom image and no Dockerfile build. A saved snapshot does that job: install your tools in a sandbox, then save it.

## Example 1: a web app with a database URL

You want each sandbox to have your repository, its dependencies and a `DATABASE_URL`.

1. Add the repository and the variable to an environment:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat env add-repo base acme/web-app
   boat env set-var base DATABASE_URL=postgres://db.example.com/app
   ```

2. Add the repository setup script `npm install` in [Dashboard > Environment](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=environment).

3. Create sandboxes with `boat new`. Each one clones the repository, gets the variable and runs `npm install`.

## Example 2: heavy tools installed once

You need Python ML packages, a large dataset and Playwright browsers. They take 10 minutes to install.

1. Create one sandbox and install everything in it:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat new --type large
   boat ssh <id> -- bash -s < ./install-tools.sh
   ```

2. Save the disk as a saved snapshot:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat snapshot <id> ml-stack
   ```

3. Create each new sandbox from it. The tools are already there:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat new --from ml-stack
   ```

The environment still adds your secrets at each start. Read [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

## Example 3: one task file per sandbox

Each sandbox works on a different customer ticket. The setup differs per sandbox.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --from ml-stack --setup-file ./ticket-4211.sh
boat info <id>   # setupStatus: pending, running, done or failed
```

The `--setup-file` script runs once, as the user `user`. A fork does not run it again. Read [Per-sandbox setup file](/setup#per-sandbox-setup-file).


# Manage environments
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments/manage

Create, rename, upgrade and delete environments, pick the environment for a sandbox, and share environments with your organization.

You can have many environments, for example `base`, `staging` and `prod`. Each one is a full environment with its own repositories, secrets and credentials. Exactly one of them is the default. A sandbox uses the default when you do not name an environment.

## Manage environments

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env list
boat env info staging
boat env new staging
boat env rename staging prod
boat env default prod
boat env rm staging
boat env upgrade prod
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"staging"}'

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"prod","isDefault":true,"safeForThirdParties":true}'

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID/upgrade" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { environments } = await sandbox.environments();
const staging = await sandbox.createEnvironment({ name: "staging" });

await sandbox.updateEnvironment({
  environmentId: envId,
  name: "prod", isDefault: true, safeForThirdParties: true,
});

await sandbox.upgradeEnvironment({ environmentId: envId });
await sandbox.deleteEnvironment({ environmentId: envId });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_environment_request import CreateSandboxEnvironmentRequest
from boat_sdk.models.update_sandbox_environment_request import UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest

envs = sandbox.environments()
staging = sandbox.create_environment(CreateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(name="staging"))

sandbox.update_environment(env_id, UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(
    name="prod", is_default=True, safe_for_third_parties=True,
))

sandbox.upgrade_environment(env_id)
sandbox.delete_environment(env_id)
```

* A delete is a soft delete. Sandboxes pinned to its versions keep running. New sandboxes cannot use it.
* `upgradeEnvironment` accepts an optional list of sandbox ids. Use it to upgrade only those sandboxes. Without the list, boat moves every sandbox of yours that is on an older version. Read [Versions and upgrades](/environments/versions).

## Pick the environment for a sandbox

Pass the environment name when you create, resume or fork a sandbox. Without a name, boat uses your default.

* boat rejects an unknown name before it creates or changes anything. A typo costs you nothing.
* boat never creates an environment by itself.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --environment staging
boat resume bx_f7k2q9hd --environment staging
boat fork bx_f7k2q9hd --environment staging
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":3600,"environment":"staging"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.create({ ttlSeconds: 3600, environment: "staging" });
await sandbox.resume({ sandboxId, environment: "staging" });
await sandbox.fork({ sandboxId, environment: "staging" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_request import CreateSandboxRequest
from boat_sdk.models.resume_request import ResumeRequest
from boat_sdk.models.fork_request import ForkRequest

sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=3600, environment="staging"))
sandbox.resume(sandbox_id, resume_request=ResumeRequest(environment="staging"))
sandbox.fork(sandbox_id, fork_request=ForkRequest(environment="staging"))
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> `--environment` and `--env` are different flags.
>
> * `--environment staging` picks the environment that the sandbox uses.
> * `--env KEY=value` sets one variable on that one sandbox. It adds to what the environment gives.

## Organization environments

An organization has its own shared environments. Add `?org=<org id or name>` to any environment route, or `--org <org>` to any `boat env` command. Only this query parameter selects them: the `X-Boat-Org` header and the active wallet do not, so a call without `org` works on your own environments. An organization API key always works on its organization's environments.

| Role | Can do |
| - | - |
| Member | List the organization environments and use them for sandboxes, except the ones [limited to other members](/organizations#limit-who-can-use-an-environment-or-profile) |
| Owner or admin | Also create, change and delete them, and choose who can use them with `boat env access` |

A sandbox billed to the organization can name an organization environment. When you have an environment of the same name, yours wins. Name an [organization credential profile](/ai-credentials#organization-profiles) on an organization environment to give the team's sandboxes the team's AI credentials.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env list --org acme
boat env new agents --org acme
boat env set agents --org acme --credential-profile team-claude
boat --org acme new --environment agents
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments?org=acme" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID?org=acme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"credentialProfileId":"team-claude"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { environments } = await sandbox.environments({ org: "acme" });
await sandbox.updateEnvironment({ environmentId: envId, org: "acme", credentialProfileId: "team-claude" });
await sandbox.create({ org: "acme", environment: "agents" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
envs = sandbox.environments(org="acme")
sandbox.update_environment(env_id, UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(credential_profile_id="team-claude"), org="acme")
sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(org="acme", environment="agents"))
```


# Private registries
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments/private-registries

Log in to private npm, pip, uv and Docker registries in every sandbox with environment variables and secret files.

Put the registry token in the environment. Every new sandbox then installs from your private registry with no extra step.

| Registry | What to set | Path inside the sandbox |
| - | - | - |
| npm, pnpm | Variable `NPM_TOKEN` and secret file `.npmrc` | `/home/user/.npmrc` |
| pip | Secret file `.config/pip/pip.conf`, or variable `PIP_INDEX_URL` | `/home/user/.config/pip/pip.conf` |
| uv | Variable `UV_DEFAULT_INDEX`, or `UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME` and `UV_INDEX_<NAME>_PASSWORD` | Environment only |
| Docker | Secret file `.docker/config.json`, or `docker login` in a setup script | `/home/user/.docker/config.json` |

Secret file paths are relative to `/home/user`. Read [Secrets, env vars and .env files](/environments/secrets).

> [!WARNING]
>
> An environment that is [safe for third parties](/environments/access#safe-for-third-parties) gets none of these values. Check with `boat exec <id> 'echo "[$NPM_TOKEN]"'`.

## npm and pnpm

npm replaces `${NPM_TOKEN}` in `.npmrc` with the variable. So the file itself holds no secret.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set-var base NPM_TOKEN=npm_xxxxxxxx
printf '@acme:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com\n//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}\n' \
  | boat env set-file base .npmrc
```

Check it in a new sandbox:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec <id> 'npm whoami --registry https://npm.pkg.github.com'
```

## pip

Use one variable:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set-var base PIP_INDEX_URL=https://user:token@pypi.example.com/simple
```

Or use a config file:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
printf '[global]\nindex-url = https://user:token@pypi.example.com/simple\n' \
  | boat env set-file base .config/pip/pip.conf
```

## uv

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set-var base UV_DEFAULT_INDEX=https://pypi.example.com/simple
boat env set-var base UV_INDEX_ACME_USERNAME=user
boat env set-var base UV_INDEX_ACME_PASSWORD=token
```

`ACME` is the uppercase name of the index in your `pyproject.toml`.

## Docker

The user `user` runs `docker` without `sudo`. Docker reads logins from `/home/user/.docker/config.json`.

Option 1: send the config file of a machine that is already logged in. The file must hold the login itself, not a `credsStore` entry.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set-file base .docker/config.json --from ./docker-config.json
```

Option 2: log in at each start. Keep the token in a variable, and add this [repository setup script](/setup#repository-setup-scripts):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
echo "$GHCR_TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io --username acme-bot --password-stdin
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> A [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates) keeps `/home/user/.docker/config.json` like every other file. Do not save a saved snapshot from a sandbox that holds a login that others must not use.

## Related

* [Secrets, env vars and .env files](/environments/secrets)
* [Setup scripts](/setup)
* [Access and credentials](/environments/access)


# Repositories
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments/repositories

Clone private or public GitHub repositories into every new sandbox, and find where they land.

Add a repository to an environment. Each new sandbox then clones it into `/home/user/<repository name>`.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env add-repo base octocat/hello-world --branch develop
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> Repositories need a GitHub connection on your account. If you signed in with Google or an email code, do these steps:
>
