> 1. Open [Dashboard > Environment](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=environment).
> 2. Under GitHub repositories, click **Connect GitHub**.
>
> This adds GitHub to the account that you already have. You keep the same way to sign in. Nothing else in boat needs this connection. You can also skip it and use `gh` with your own token inside the sandbox.

> [!WARNING]
>
> A sandbox clones no repository and runs no setup script when one of these is true:
>
> * Its environment is [safe for third parties](/environments/access#safe-for-third-parties).
> * You created it with `--no-env`.
> * The **GitHub repositories** toggle of the environment is off.
>
> Check with `boat exec <id> 'ls /home/user'`.

## Add or remove a repository

Each repository has a base branch and an optional [setup script](/setup#repository-setup-scripts).

* boat clones the base branch as it is. The default is `main`.
* boat never creates a branch for you, also not for forks.
* A repository stays on the base branch until you, or something inside the sandbox, changes it.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env add-repo base octocat/hello-world --branch develop
boat env rm-repo base octocat/hello-world
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
# $BOAT_API_BASE is https://boat.dev/api/v1
ENV_ID=$(curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.environments[] | select(.name == "base") | .id')
REPO_ID=$(curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/repos?sync=true&q=hello-world" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.installations[0].repositories[0].databaseId')

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID/repos" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"repositoryId\":\"$REPO_ID\",\"baseBranch\":\"develop\"}"

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID/repos/$REPO_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { environments } = await sandbox.environments();
const envId = environments.find((e) => e.name === "base")!.id;
const repos = await sandbox.repos({ sync: true, q: "hello-world" });
const repo = repos.installations.flatMap((i) => i.repositories)[0];

await sandbox.addEnvironmentRepo({ environmentId: envId, repositoryId: repo.databaseId, baseBranch: "develop" });
await sandbox.deleteEnvironmentRepo({ environmentId: envId, repositoryId: repo.databaseId });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.add_environment_repo_request import AddEnvironmentRepoRequest

env_id = next(e.id for e in sandbox.environments().environments if e.name == "base")
repos = sandbox.repos(sync=True, q="hello-world")
repo = repos.installations[0].repositories[0]

sandbox.add_environment_repo(env_id, AddEnvironmentRepoRequest(repository_id=repo.database_id, base_branch="develop"))
sandbox.delete_environment_repo(env_id, repo.database_id)
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> The older `POST /repos` call (`selectRepo` in the SDKs) changes only the default environment. Use the per-environment calls above instead.

## Where repositories land

The SSH user is `user` and the work directory is `/home/user`. Each folder has the name of the repository, not the `owner/name` pair.

| GitHub repository | Path in the sandbox |
| - | - |
| `acme/web-app` | `/home/user/web-app` |
| `octocat/hello-world` | `/home/user/hello-world` |

| Number of repositories | Project directory for agent tools |
| - | - |
| One | The repository folder |
| Several | `/home/user` is the parent workspace. Each repository is a folder next to the others. |


# Secrets, env vars and .env files
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments/secrets

Give sandboxes environment variables and secret files such as .env, for all sandboxes or for one sandbox only.

boat injects two types of secret when a sandbox starts.

| Type | Inside the sandbox |
| - | - |
| Environment variables | Process env vars and shell exports, in `boat exec`, `boat ssh` and every shell |
| Secret files | Files under `/home/user`, at the relative path that you give |

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set-var base STRIPE_KEY=sk_live_123
boat new
boat exec <id> 'echo "[$STRIPE_KEY]"'   # prints [sk_live_123]
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> A sandbox gets **no** variables and **no** secret files when one of these is true:
>
> * Its environment is [safe for third parties](/environments/access#safe-for-third-parties). `boat onboard` can turn this on.
> * You created it with `--no-env`.
> * The **Secrets** toggle of the environment is off.
> * It started before you saved the secret. Run `boat env upgrade base`, or read [Versions and upgrades](/environments/versions).
>
> Run `boat env info base` to see the switch and the toggles.

Use secrets for app credentials, API keys, `.env` files, deployment tokens and [private registry logins](/environments/private-registries).

Do not put secrets in these places:

* Prompts.
* URLs.
* CLI arguments that can go into logs.
* Docker build args.
* Committed files.

## Set variables and secret files

Each call changes one item and makes a new environment version. The other items stay.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set-var base STRIPE_KEY=sk_live_123
boat env rm-var base STRIPE_KEY
boat env set-file base backend/.env --from ./local.env
cat ./local.env | boat env set-file base backend/.env
boat env rm-file base backend/.env
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
# $BOAT_API_BASE is https://boat.dev/api/v1
ENV_ID=$(curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  | jq -r '.environments[] | select(.name == "base") | .id')

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID/vars/STRIPE_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value":"sk_live_123"}'

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID/secret-files" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"path":"backend/.env","contents":"DATABASE_URL=postgres://...\n"}'

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID/vars/STRIPE_KEY" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID/secret-files?path=backend%2F.env" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { environments } = await sandbox.environments();
const envId = environments.find((e) => e.name === "base")!.id;

await sandbox.setEnvironmentVar({ environmentId: envId, key: "STRIPE_KEY", value: "sk_live_123" });
await sandbox.setEnvironmentSecretFile({
  environmentId: envId,
  path: "backend/.env",
  contents: "DATABASE_URL=postgres://...\n",
});
await sandbox.deleteEnvironmentVar({ environmentId: envId, key: "STRIPE_KEY" });
await sandbox.deleteEnvironmentSecretFile({ environmentId: envId, path: "backend/.env" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.set_environment_var_request import SetEnvironmentVarRequest
from boat_sdk.models.set_environment_secret_file_request import SetEnvironmentSecretFileRequest

env_id = next(e.id for e in sandbox.environments().environments if e.name == "base")

sandbox.set_environment_var(env_id, "STRIPE_KEY", SetEnvironmentVarRequest(value="sk_live_123"))
sandbox.set_environment_secret_file(env_id, SetEnvironmentSecretFileRequest(
    path="backend/.env",
    contents="DATABASE_URL=postgres://...\n",
))
sandbox.delete_environment_var(env_id, "STRIPE_KEY")
sandbox.delete_environment_secret_file(environment_id=env_id, path="backend/.env")
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> The older `POST /secrets` call (`updateSecrets` in the SDKs) changes only the default environment. It **replaces** all variables and secret files. Use the per-environment calls above instead.

## .env files

A secret file is the way to put a `.env` file in each sandbox. The path is relative to `/home/user`. There is no repository picker. To put a file inside a clone, start the path with the repository folder name.

This path:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
web-app/backend/.env
```

writes to:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
/home/user/web-app/backend/.env
```

boat skips absolute paths and paths that go outside `/home/user`.

## Variables for one sandbox

The variables of an environment apply to every sandbox that uses it. To give one sandbox its own values, pass `env` when you create it.

boat merges the per-sandbox values over the environment's values. If the two have the same key, the per-sandbox value wins. Per-sandbox values also reach a sandbox made with `--no-env`.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --env DATABASE_URL=postgres://... --env FEATURE_FLAG=1
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":3600,"env":{"DATABASE_URL":"postgres://...","FEATURE_FLAG":"1"}}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.create({
  ttlSeconds: 3600,
  env: { DATABASE_URL: "postgres://...", FEATURE_FLAG: "1" },
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_request import CreateSandboxRequest

sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(
    ttl_seconds=3600,
    env={"DATABASE_URL": "postgres://...", "FEATURE_FLAG": "1"},
))
```

| Rule | Limit |
| - | - |
| Key format | `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*` |
| Key length | 128 characters maximum |
| Variables per sandbox | 100 maximum |
| Total size per sandbox | 64KB maximum |
| Reserved boat-internal names (`ASCII_TOKEN`, `BOAT_ID`, and similar) | Rejected |

A fork gets the per-sandbox variables of its source sandbox. If the fork passes its own `env`, it does not get them.


# Versions and upgrades
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/environments/versions

Each saved change makes a new environment version. A sandbox moves to it only when you upgrade.

Each time you save a change to an environment, boat makes a new version.

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
you save a change  ──▶  a new version is created
                            │
                            ├──▶ every sandbox that starts from now on gets it
                            │
                            └──▶ Sandboxes already running: nothing happens
                                     │
                                     └──▶ they move only when you upgrade
```

## Which version a sandbox uses

* A sandbox takes the latest version **at the moment it starts**.
* The sandbox keeps that exact version for the rest of its life.
* A save never changes a running sandbox.
* There is no automatic upgrade, no background rollout and no scheduled window.
* A sandbox moves only when you click **Upgrade** in the dashboard or run `boat env upgrade`.

## Find the version of a sandbox

1. Run `boat info <id>`. It shows the version as `environment` and `environmentVersion`.
2. Run `boat env list`. It shows the latest version of each environment.
3. Compare the two numbers. A sandbox below the latest still runs the older configuration.

This is the usual answer to "I added that secret. Why does my sandbox not have it?" If the versions match, check the [safe for third parties](/environments/access#safe-for-third-parties) switch.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat info bx_f7k2q9hd     # env:  prod (v2)
boat env list             # prod  latest v3   -> this sandbox is one upgrade behind
```

## Upgrade

An upgrade applies the new configuration. It also removes every secret that the new version withholds.

| Sandbox state | When the upgrade applies |
| - | - |
| Live | Immediately. boat cleans and updates it. |
| Stopped | When it resumes |

> [!WARNING]
>
> You cannot undo an upgrade on the disk of that sandbox. boat deletes a withheld secret from the machine. It does not hide it. If you pin the sandbox to the older version again, a secret file that the newer version dropped does not come back.

The Versions panel lists every version and the number of sandboxes on each. Use it to find sandboxes that still run an old configuration.

To upgrade only some sandboxes, give `upgradeEnvironment` an optional list of sandbox ids (`agentIds`). Without the list, boat moves every sandbox of yours that is on an older version. For the commands, read [Manage environments](/environments/manage).


# Evals and RL environments
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/evals

Run many eval or RL episodes on boat: one saved snapshot per environment, one fresh sandbox per episode, parallel fan-out within start limits, teardown, cost. Harbor and Terminal-Bench status.

An episode is one sandbox. Prepare the environment once, save it as a saved snapshot, and start each episode from it. Delete the sandbox when the episode ends. The next episode starts from the same clean state.

```mermaid theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
%%{init: {"theme": "base", "fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "themeVariables": {"fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "fontSize": "14px", "primaryColor": "#F1F3F9", "primaryBorderColor": "#263FA9", "primaryTextColor": "#060606", "secondaryColor": "#E0E3F2", "tertiaryColor": "#FEFEFE", "lineColor": "#060606", "textColor": "#060606", "mainBkg": "#F1F3F9", "nodeBorder": "#263FA9", "clusterBkg": "#FEFEFE", "clusterBorder": "#C4C4C4", "edgeLabelBackground": "#FEFEFE", "actorBkg": "#F1F3F9", "actorBorder": "#263FA9", "actorTextColor": "#060606", "actorLineColor": "#9E9E9E", "signalColor": "#060606", "signalTextColor": "#060606", "labelBoxBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "labelBoxBorderColor": "#263FA9", "noteBkgColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteBorderColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteTextColor": "#060606", "sectionBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "altSectionBkgColor": "#FEFEFE", "taskBkgColor": "#263FA9", "taskBorderColor": "#263FA9", "taskTextColor": "#FEFEFE", "gridColor": "#E0E0E0"}, "flowchart": {"padding": 16, "nodeSpacing": 48, "rankSpacing": 48, "curve": "linear"}, "sequence": {"boxMargin": 16, "actorMargin": 48, "noteMargin": 16, "messageMargin": 32, "mirrorActors": false}, "state": {"padding": 16}, "gantt": {"barHeight": 24, "barGap": 8, "fontSize": 14, "sectionFontSize": 14}}}%%
flowchart LR
  P[Prepare one sandbox] --> S[Save saved snapshot]
  S --> E1[Episode 1: boat new --from]
  S --> E2[Episode 2: boat new --from]
  S --> E3[Episode N: boat new --from]
  E1 --> D[Score, then delete]
  E2 --> D
  E3 --> D
```

## 1. Prepare the environment

Install the task's dependencies and fixtures in one sandbox. Then save it under a name:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
id=$(boat new --json | jq -r 'select(.event == "ready") | .id')
boat exec "$id" --timeout 600 -- bash -lc 'git clone https://github.com/acme/eval-tasks && pip install -r eval-tasks/requirements.txt'
boat snapshot "$id" task-env-v1
boat delete "$id" --yes
```

* Use one saved snapshot per environment version: `task-env-v1`, `task-env-v2`. A saved snapshot does not change after you save it.
* Docker images: a saved snapshot keeps only the images that a container uses. Run `docker create --name keep-<x> <image>` for each image. See [What a snapshot saves](/snapshots/whats-saved#docker).
* 10 saved snapshots are free. Each one more costs \$0.056 a day from the wallet. See [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

## 2. Run episodes in parallel

This Python script starts one sandbox per episode from the saved snapshot, runs the episode, reads the score and deletes the sandbox. It paces the starts to the minute limit of the \$20 plan.

```python title="run_episodes.py" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os
import time
import uuid
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

from boat_sdk import ApiClient, Configuration, exec_command, wait_until_ready
from boat_sdk.api.boat_api import BoatApi
from boat_sdk.exceptions import ApiException
from boat_sdk.models import CreateSandboxRequest

STARTS_PER_MINUTE = 12      # $20 plan. See https://docs.boat.dev/limits
STARTS_PER_HOUR = 60        # $20 plan. The hour limit is the tighter one for long runs.
TEMPLATE = "task-env-v1"

config = Configuration(host="https://boat.dev/api/v1", access_token=os.environ["BOAT_API_KEY"])


def start(boat: BoatApi) -> str:
    request = CreateSandboxRequest(var_from=TEMPLATE, type="small", ttl_seconds=3600)
    key = str(uuid.uuid4())          # the same key on a retry never makes a second sandbox
    for attempt in range(6):
        try:
            return boat.create(idempotency_key=key, create_sandbox_request=request).sandbox.id
        except ApiException as exc:
            if exc.status not in (429, 503):
                raise
            time.sleep(min(60, 2 ** attempt * 5))
    raise RuntimeError("could not start a sandbox")


def episode(boat: BoatApi, n: int) -> tuple[int, int, str]:
    sandbox_id = start(boat)
    try:
        wait_until_ready(boat, sandbox_id)
        result = exec_command(boat, sandbox_id, f"python3 eval-tasks/run.py --episode {n}", timeout_seconds=600)
        out = result.actual_instance
        return n, out.exit_code, out.stdout
    finally:
        boat.delete_sandbox(sandbox_id=sandbox_id, x_ascii_confirm_delete=sandbox_id)


with ApiClient(config) as client:
    boat = BoatApi(client)
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=50) as pool:
        futures = []
        for n in range(100):
            futures.append(pool.submit(episode, boat, n))
            # pace the starts under both the minute and the hour limit
            time.sleep(max(60 / STARTS_PER_MINUTE, 3600 / STARTS_PER_HOUR))
        for future in futures:
            n, code, stdout = future.result()
            print(n, code, stdout.strip()[-200:])
```

* `exec_command` waits at most 600 seconds. For a longer episode, start it with `detached=True` and poll `command_status`. See [Python SDK](/sdks/python#run-a-long-job-or-a-server-in-the-background).
* `ttl_seconds=3600` stops a sandbox after one hour if your script crashes before the delete.
* In asyncio code, wrap each call in `asyncio.to_thread`. The SDK is synchronous.

### Fork instead of a saved snapshot

`boat fork <id>` (or `fork` in the API) also copies a sandbox. Use it to branch one episode mid-way, for example to try several actions from the same state.

* A fork copies the newest snapshot of its source. If the source keeps running, later forks get later states.
* A fork of a running sandbox uses its last background snapshot. Files written after it can be missing. Stop the source first for an exact copy.

For a fixed start state, use a saved snapshot. See [Resume and fork](/snapshots/resume-and-fork).

## Limits

| Plan | Starts per minute / hour / day | Sandboxes at once |
| - | - | - |
| \$20 | 12 / 60 / 200 | 100 |
| \$100 | 30 / 210 / 840 | 300 |
| \$500 | 65 / 420 / 1,680 | 1,000 |
| \$2000 | 90 / 600 / 2,400 | 2,000 |
| [Free trial](/free-trial) | 5 / 25 / 75 | 2 |

* On the \$20 plan, the hour limit (60) sets the pace: 100 episodes take about 100 minutes to start. On the \$100 plan (210 per hour), they take about 29 minutes. The day limit caps a long run.
* A start above the limit fails with `429 rate_limited`, names the `window`, and does not count. The API sends a `Retry-After` header.
* An organization on the \$2000 plan multiplies these numbers by its seats. Below it, each extra seat adds 20%.
* `--fail-fast` (`fail_fast=True`) answers in about 1.5 seconds when no machine is free, instead of waiting.

All limits and how to raise them: [Limits](/limits).

## Cost

boat bills each second that a sandbox runs. A deleted sandbox costs nothing.

| Run | Size | Cost |
| - | - | - |
| 100 episodes of 10 minutes | `small` (\$0.018 an hour) | about \$0.30 |
| 100 episodes of 10 minutes | `default` (\$0.036 an hour) | about \$0.60 |
| 1,000 episodes of 30 minutes | `default` | about \$18 |

Model calls are extra when an agent runs in the sandbox. See [Pricing](/pricing) and [AI credentials](/ai-credentials).

## Agents in the episode

To run Claude Code, Codex or another harness in each sandbox, send a prompt to the sandbox and wait for it. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents) and [Python SDK](/sdks/python#prompt-an-integrated-agent). To keep your model keys out of the sandboxes, use the [AI credentials proxy](/ai-credentials).

For episodes that other people or untrusted code control, create the sandboxes with `no_env=True`. They then get none of your secrets.

## AgentEnv

[AgentEnv](https://www.agentenvframework.com/) runs its environments and agents on boat with its built-in `boat` sandbox provider. See [AgentEnv](/integrations/agentenv).

## Harbor and Terminal-Bench

* [Harbor](https://docs.harborframework.com) runs on boat through the [Harbor adapter](/integrations/harbor) (`harbor run -e harbor_box_environment:BoxEnvironment`).
* **Terminal-Bench 2.0 does not run through that adapter today.** Each of its tasks names a prebuilt Docker image, and the adapter refuses tasks with a Docker image.
* To run a Terminal-Bench style task on boat now, install its dependencies in a saved snapshot (step 1) and run the task's test script with `boat exec`.

## Clean up

List what is still running, and delete what your run left:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat list --json | jq -r '.sandboxes[] | "\(.id) \(.name)"'
boat delete bx_... --yes
```


# FAQ
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/faq

Short answers to the questions customers ask most: trial and billing, limits, sizes, stop and resume, snapshots, secrets, public URLs, SSH, agents, the API, teams, errors and security.

## Getting started

> [accordion] Do I need a GitHub account?
>
> No. You can sign in with GitHub, Google, or a 6-digit code that we email to you. You need GitHub only to clone your repositories into a sandbox. You can connect it later. Read [Sign-in methods](/account#sign-in-methods).

> [accordion] I signed in with Google and my sandboxes are gone, or the CLI asks me to pay again.
>
> You are on a second account. Each sign-in method makes its own account, unless you connected it to your account first. A matching email does not link them.
>
> 1. Sign in again with the method that you used first.
> 2. Add the other method from [Dashboard > Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account).
>
> Only support can merge two accounts that already exist. [Contact us](/support) with both sign-ins.

> [accordion] How do I change the email address boat writes to?
>
> boat writes to the connection that is marked primary. Connect the address that you want, then make it primary from [Dashboard > Account](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=account). You cannot remove your primary connection or your last connection.

> [accordion] Can I use my own Dockerfile or image?
>
> No. boat has no custom image and no Dockerfile build. Install your tools in a sandbox, save it as a saved snapshot, then start each sandbox with `boat new --from <name>`. You can also run your image with Docker inside the sandbox. Read [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

> [accordion] Does the setup script run as root? Does it run again on resume?
>
> A setup file (`--setup-file`) runs one time, as `user`. Use `sudo` for root. Repository setup scripts run at every start, also at resume and fork. Read [Setup scripts](/setup).

## Pricing, trial and billing

> [accordion] Is there a free tier? Do I need a credit card?
>
> There is no free tier. Your first plan starts with a free 7-day trial, and checkout asks for a card. Until your first payment you get 25 hours of compute, 2 sandboxes at once, auto-stop of 2 hours or less, and no `large` size. Organizations get no trial. Read [Free trial](/free-trial).

> [accordion] I paid, but I still have the trial limits.
>
> The trial limits stay until the first payment. Click **Upgrade now** on [Dashboard > Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) to pay now. If an organization pays for you, run `boat org switch <org>`. Read [End the trial early](/free-trial#end-the-trial-early).

> [accordion] "This identity is not eligible for another free trial."
>
> One person gets one trial. A second account, for example from a second sign-in method, gets no new trial. Sign in with the method that you used first. Read [Who gets a trial](/free-trial#who-gets-a-trial).

> [accordion] I cancelled my trial. Can I still be charged?
>
> No. **Cancel trial** on the Billing tab ends the trial now with no charge. If you see a charge after a cancel, [contact us](/support) for a refund. Read [Cancel the trial](/free-trial#cancel-the-trial).

> [accordion] How do I cancel, change my card or get an invoice?
>
> Run `boat billing portal` for the card and invoices. Cancel the plan with **Cancel plan** on [Dashboard > Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing). Read [Card, invoices and plan changes](/billing/plan-changes).

> [accordion] I forgot to cancel and was charged. Can I get a refund?
>
> boat does not refund unused time in general. Email support with the invoice number. Read [Refunds](/billing/plan-changes#refunds).

> [accordion] Why did a plan change move my billing date?
>
> A plan change starts a new billing month that day. Stripe credits the unused part of the old plan and charges the new price minus that credit. Read [Upgrade or downgrade](/billing/plan-changes#upgrade-or-downgrade).

> [accordion] Is there a fee per start?
>
> Not inside your included starts. Above them, a start costs \$0.03 to \$0.07. Read [Extra starts](/limits#extra-starts).

> [accordion] Am I billed when a sandbox is stopped?
>
> No machine time. Two charges continue while sandboxes are stopped:
>
> * Saved snapshots above your plan's included count: \$0.056 a day each, from the wallet.
> * The [AI credentials proxy](/ai-credentials#pricing), while it is on: \$1 a day, from the wallet.
>
> A stopped sandbox keeps its disk for free for at least 14 days. After that, automated retention cleanup can delete it once enabled. The job currently reports candidates without deleting them in production. Save a saved snapshot before day 14 to keep the disk longer. Read [Keep a stopped sandbox longer than 14 days](/snapshots/stop#keep-a-stopped-sandbox-longer-than-14-days).

> [accordion] What do snapshots, IP addresses and network traffic cost?
>
> Nothing extra. Automatic snapshots, a public IPv6 address, outbound IPv4 and egress are included. Only saved snapshots above your plan's included count cost money. Read [Included at no cost](/pricing#included-at-no-cost).

> [accordion] Is boat cheaper than providers that bill only active CPU?
>
> boat bills a flat price per size per hour. For a typical sandbox, boat costs less. A sandbox that is almost always idle can cost less elsewhere, so stop idle sandboxes. Read [Pricing](/pricing).

> [accordion] Does unused time or money expire?
>
> Included plan time resets every billing period. Money in the wallet never expires.

> [accordion] Where did credit packs and auto-refill go?
>
> One dollar wallet replaces them. Add any amount with **Pay** or `boat wallet pay 50`, or turn on auto top-up. Payments of \$200 or more get a bonus. Old balances moved to the wallet in dollars. Read [Wallet](/billing#wallet).

> [accordion] Can I add money for an organization?
>
> Yes, if you are the owner. Run `boat --org <org> wallet pay 50`, or click **Pay** on the organization's Billing tab. Money in a personal wallet stays personal. Read [Plan, wallet and running out](/billing).

> [accordion] How much has one sandbox cost me? Can I bill my own customers?
>
> The dashboard shows it in the **Cost** column of the Sandboxes page and in **Cost by sandbox this month** on the Billing page. From code, run `boat usage <id>`, call `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/usage`, or list every sandbox with `GET /sandboxes?include=cost`. You get the machine time and list-price cost, while the sandbox runs or after it stops. Read [Per-sandbox usage](/billing#per-sandbox-usage).

> [accordion] Can I set a spend cap?
>
> A personal account has no dollar cap. Leave auto top-up off, and your spend stops at your plan and your wallet. An organization owner can cap each member. Read [Control your spend](/billing#control-your-spend).

> [accordion] My card failed. What happens to my sandboxes?
>
> Update the card with `boat billing portal`, then pay the open invoice. For an organization, select it and use **Manage billing** on the Billing tab. Read [Running out](/billing#running-out).

## Limits

> [accordion] What counts as a start, and what are the limits?
>
> Create, fork and resume each count as one start. A resume that takes back the kept machine of the sandbox does not count. Your plan sets starts per minute, per hour and per day.
>
> | Plan | Starts per minute / hour / day | Sandboxes at once |
> | - | - | - |
> | \$20 | 12 / 60 / 200 | 100 |
> | \$100 | 30 / 210 / 840 | 300 |
> | \$500 | 65 / 420 / 1,680 | 1,000 |
> | \$2000 | 90 / 600 / 2,400 | 2,000 |
> | [Free trial](/free-trial) | 5 / 25 / 75 | 2 |
>
> Read [Limits and errors](/limits).

> [accordion] When does the daily start limit reset?
>
> Nothing resets at midnight. The windows roll: a start stops counting 24 hours after it happened. Run `boat limits` to see what is left. Read [Limits and errors](/limits).

> [accordion] Are limits per API key, per account or per organization?
>
> Per wallet: your personal account, or the organization that pays. API keys have no limits of their own. An organization shares one pool, sized by its plan and seats. Read [Shared limits](/organizations/seats-and-limits#shared-limits).

> [accordion] How do I get more starts or more sandboxes at once?
>
> Move to a bigger plan. Below the \$2000 plan, one more organization seat adds only 20% of the plan limits. On the \$2000 plan, each seat adds the full limits. For short peaks, keep money in the wallet: starts above a limit cost \$0.03 to \$0.07 each, up to 6 times the hour and day limits and 3 times the minute limit. boat raises limits only on custom plans above \$2000 a month. [Contact us](/support) for a custom plan. Read [Raise a limit](/limits#raise-a-limit).

> [accordion] Do API calls such as exec and file writes have a rate limit?
>
> Yes: 10,000 requests in 60 seconds from one IP address, on all endpoints. An open stream counts once. The `RateLimit` header on every answer shows what is left. Above it, boat answers `429` with `retryAfter` in the body. Read [Limits and errors](/limits).

> [accordion] How long can one command run?
>
> A command that waits for its result has a default timeout of 30 s. In the CLI, `boat exec <id> --timeout 0 -- <command>` waits with no limit and prints the output live. Through the API the maximum is 600 s: for longer work, run it detached. Read [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands).

## Sizes and machines

> [accordion] Do sandboxes have GPUs?
>
> No. No size has a GPU. For GPU work, use a GPU provider and keep boat for the agent and the code. Read [Sandbox sizes](/machines).

> [accordion] Which size is medium?
>
> `default` is the medium size: 4 vCPU, 8 GB of RAM, \$0.036 an hour. The sizes are `small`, `default`, `large` and `xlarge`. Read [Pricing](/pricing).

> [accordion] How do I get xlarge? Is there a bigger or custom size?
>
> Subscribe to the \$100 plan or higher, then pass `--type xlarge`. You do not have to ask us. There is no size above `xlarge` and no custom size. Read [Sandbox sizes](/machines).

> [accordion] Can I resize a sandbox?
>
> Yes. Stop the sandbox, then resume it with `--type`. A larger size always works. A smaller size fails if the sandbox holds more data than the smaller disk takes. Read [Change size](/machines/change-size).
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
> boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd
> until [ "$(boat info bx_f7k2q9hd --json | jq -r .sandbox.state)" = "stopped" ]; do sleep 2; done
> boat resume bx_f7k2q9hd --type large
> ```

> [accordion] Why do benchmark results differ between sandboxes?
>
> Sandboxes run on physical hosts dedicated to boat. They share vCPUs with other sandboxes on the same host, so a busy host can make a run slower. The fleet uses more than one CPU model. Read [Where your sandbox runs](/machines/virtualization#where-your-sandbox-runs).

> [accordion] Can I run KVM, Firecracker or the Android emulator?
>
> Yes. Every sandbox has `/dev/kvm`. Read [Virtualization](/machines/virtualization).

> [accordion] Which OS and kernel? Can I get a newer kernel?
>
> Every sandbox runs Ubuntu 24.04 LTS on Linux 6.8. boat has one image for all customers, so you cannot get another kernel. For another kernel, run your own virtual machine inside a sandbox with KVM. Read [Base image and pre-installed tools](/machines/tools).

> [accordion] Which apt mirror is fastest? apt-get is slow with the Azure mirror.
>
> Use `fr.archive.ubuntu.com`. Read [Fast apt-get](/ci#fast-apt-get-use-the-french-ubuntu-mirror) in the CI guide.

> [accordion] Is boat good for sustained heavy compute?
>
> Sandboxes have shared vCPUs. They are best for agent work that comes in bursts. `boat new --type large` gives two times the CPU and memory of `default`. For multi-hour loads at 100% CPU, dedicated compute is a better fit.

## Stop, resume and snapshots

> [accordion] Can I pause a sandbox? How long is a stopped sandbox kept?
>
> There is no pause. A stop removes the machine and keeps the disk. The API reports a stopped sandbox as `archived`.
>
> boat keeps the disk for at least 14 days after the stop. After that, automated retention cleanup can delete it once enabled. The job currently reports candidates without deleting them in production. Once deleted, resume fails with `409 snapshot_data_expired`. Save a saved snapshot before day 14 to keep the disk longer. This works on a stopped sandbox, with no resume. Read [Keep a stopped sandbox longer than 14 days](/snapshots/stop#keep-a-stopped-sandbox-longer-than-14-days).

> [accordion] Why did my sandbox stop?
>
> | Cause | Read |
> | - | - |
> | Its auto-stop time ran out (1 hour by default) | [Auto-stop](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop) |
> | Your wallet was empty for 24 hours after the included time ran out | [Running out](/billing#running-out) |
> | The free trial used its 25 hours, or it was cancelled | [Free trial](/free-trial) |
> | Snapshots failed for 3 days, so boat forced a stop | [When a stop is refused](/snapshots/stop#when-a-stop-is-refused) |
> | An organization owner capped your usage | [Per-member caps](/organizations/seats-and-limits#per-member-caps) |
>
> Your disk stays in every case. Resume the sandbox. Read [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting#why-did-my-sandbox-stop).

> [accordion] Auto-stop restarts at each resume. How do I keep a long job alive?
>
> Auto-stop counts from create or the last resume, not from activity. A running prompt moves it later. Run `boat extend <id> --hours 12` to set it to 12 hours from now, or `--no-auto-stop`. Read [Auto-stop](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop).

> [accordion] How do I get rid of a sandbox?
>
> Use `boat stop` in almost all cases. It is free, and you can resume within 14 days. To erase a sandbox and its snapshots for good, run `boat delete <id>`. Read [Delete a sandbox or snapshot](/data-retention/delete).

> [accordion] Why is my stop refused, or why does a sandbox keep running after a stop?
>
> A stop takes a last snapshot first. If that snapshot fails, boat refuses the stop and keeps the sandbox running, so you do not lose work. You do not pay for that time. `boat stop --force` stops from the last good snapshot and loses later writes. Read [When a stop is refused](/snapshots/stop#when-a-stop-is-refused).

> [accordion] How do I know that a stop is done?
>
> `boat stop` returns at `stopping`. Poll until the state is `stopped`. Read [Wait for the stop in a script](/snapshots/stop#wait-for-the-stop-in-a-script).

> [accordion] Can I save app state just before a stop?
>
> Yes. Put a command in `~/.boat/pre-stop`. boat runs it before the last snapshot of every stop and auto-stop. A saved snapshot save does not run it. Read [Save app state before a stop](/snapshots/stop#save-app-state-before-a-stop).

> [accordion] How fast are resume and fork? When can I run commands?
>
> A few seconds, whatever the sandbox holds. Files stream in the background, and a read waits for its own file. Wait for state `ready` or `idle` before you run commands. Services and Docker start a few seconds after `ready`. Read [Readiness and resume speed](/readiness).

> [accordion] My app takes long to answer after a resume. Can its files load first?
>
> Yes. boat records which files open first and fetches them first next time. Resume, start your app, wait for `hydrated: true`, then save or stop. Leave rebuild output out with `.boatignore`. Read [Make the first start faster](/readiness#make-the-first-start-faster).

> [accordion] Do processes and Docker containers survive stop and resume? Is there a memory snapshot?
>
> A resume within 10 minutes of the stop usually gets the same machine back, with memory and every program still running. Do not count on it. After 10 minutes, a resume starts a new machine from the snapshot. A snapshot saves the disk, not memory. Programs that you started by hand do not come back. Enabled systemd services and Docker containers start again by themselves. Every tagged Docker image comes back. The Docker build cache does not come back. Read [A restore is like a reboot](/snapshots/whats-saved#a-restore-is-like-a-reboot).

> [accordion] What does a snapshot save? Why did \~/.cache or a folder disappear?
>
> A snapshot saves every home folder under `/home`, folders that you create at `/`, and your changes in `/etc`, `/usr`, `/opt`, `/root`, `/srv` and `/var`. It does not save `/tmp` or `~/.cache`. It keeps two folders of `~/.cache`: Playwright browsers (`ms-playwright`) and the Deno cache (`deno`). Read [What a snapshot saves](/snapshots/whats-saved).

> [accordion] Why did my hostname change after a resume?
>
> A snapshot does not save the hostname, the IP address or the SSH host keys. To keep a hostname, set it from an enabled systemd service. Read [Keep a hostname](/snapshots/whats-saved#keep-a-hostname).

> [accordion] Saved snapshot, fork or automatic snapshot: which one do I use as a template?
>
> Use a saved snapshot: `boat snapshot <id> <name>`, then `boat new --from <name>`. New sandboxes never change it, and it stays after you delete the source. A fork copies the newest automatic snapshot of one sandbox. Read [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

> [accordion] Is there a limit on saved snapshots? Why are they charged every day?
>
> There is no maximum. Your plan includes 10 for every \$20 of plan per seat, and never fewer than 10. Each one more costs \$0.056 a day, taken each day from the wallet. Saved snapshots have no scheduled expiry. Unpaid extras can be deleted after 7 days. Read [Saved snapshot pricing](/snapshots/templates#saved-snapshot-pricing).

> [accordion] When does a saved snapshot save capture the disk?
>
> The call returns at once with status `saving`, and the capture runs after that. A write right after the call can land in the save. Wait until `getSavedSnapshot` shows `ready` before you write again. Read [Save a saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates#save-a-saved-snapshot).

> [accordion] Can I start from a fixed version of a saved snapshot?
>
> A name always deploys its newest save. To keep a version, save it under a new name, for example `web-stack-v3`, and never save that name again. Read [Update a saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates#update-a-saved-snapshot).

> [accordion] Can another account use my saved snapshot?
>
> Yes. Run `boat snapshot share <name>` and give the `bsh_...` code. The other account runs `boat new --from bsh_...`. boat removes your logins, keys, secret files and repository clones first. Read [Share a saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates#share-a-saved-snapshot-with-another-account).

> [accordion] Can I go back to an older snapshot?
>
> Resume and fork always use the newest snapshot. To keep a state that you can go back to, save a saved snapshot. Read [Restore an older snapshot](/snapshots/resume-and-fork#restore-an-older-snapshot-roll-back).

> [accordion] How do I download a snapshot or a saved snapshot?
>
> Run `boat snapshot pull <snapshotId> -o ./restore`. The sandbox can be stopped. For a saved snapshot, use its `snapshotId`. Read [Download a snapshot](/snapshots/download-and-delete).

> [accordion] Can I turn snapshots off?
>
> Yes. Run `boat new --no-snapshots`, or send `"snapshots": false`. A stop then erases the sandbox, and you cannot resume it. Read [Snapshots and monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off).

## Environments and secrets

> [accordion] What goes in an environment, and what goes in a saved snapshot?
>
> A saved snapshot holds the disk: packages and builds. An environment holds the settings: variables, secret files, repositories and logins. What you put in a Dockerfile goes in a saved snapshot. What you put in a `.env` file goes in an environment. Read [Saved snapshots and environments](/snapshots/templates#saved-snapshots-and-environments).

> [accordion] Can I set secrets per repository, or for my whole company?
>
> Secrets belong to an environment, not to a repository. Make one environment per project. An organization environment is shared by all members. Read [Environments](/environments).

> [accordion] How do I give one sandbox or one fork its own secret?
>
> Pass per-sandbox variables: `boat fork <id> -e KEY=VALUE`, or `env` in the API body. They replace the variables that the fork gets from its source. Read [Variables for one sandbox](/environments/secrets#variables-for-one-sandbox).

> [accordion] Can I pass variables to one command only?
>
> No. The command API has no `env` field. Put `export KEY=value;` in front of the command, or set per-sandbox variables at create. Read [Variables for one sandbox](/environments/secrets#variables-for-one-sandbox).

> [accordion] Does a deploy from my saved snapshot get my logins?
>
> A deploy gets its environment from `--environment`, not from the source sandbox. It does get the per-sandbox variables of the source. Do not put a secret in `--env` on a sandbox that you save as a saved snapshot. Read [Saved snapshots and environments](/snapshots/templates#saved-snapshots-and-environments).

> [accordion] Can I keep real API keys out of the sandbox?
>
> Yes. Turn on the AI credentials proxy. The sandbox gets placeholder keys, and boat adds the real key to each request. Read [AI credentials](/ai-credentials#the-ai-credentials-proxy).

## Networking and public URLs

> [accordion] Is EU latency a problem from the US or Latin America?
>
> Round trips take about 100 to 200 ms. Agent work runs for minutes, so you do not notice this in practice. For production traffic from end users, publish builds to a CDN or a regional host. Read [Sandbox per user](/platform-guide).

> [accordion] Does a sandbox have a public IPv4 address?
>
> Every sandbox has a public IPv6 address and outbound IPv4. Some sandboxes have no IPv4 address of their own. SSH and [public URLs](/hosting) work over IPv4 anyway. The IP address changes at each resume, so use a public URL.

> [accordion] How do I make a URL without a token?
>
> Run `boat host <id> 3000 --public`, or send `"public": true` to `POST /sandboxes/{id}/host`. Anyone with the URL can open it. Read [Expose a port](/hosting/host-cli).

> [accordion] My protected URL works in a tab but is blank in my iframe.
>
> In an iframe on another site, browsers can block the access cookie of a protected URL. Host the port with `--public` to embed it, or put your own server in front. Read [Show a protected URL in an iframe](/hosting#show-a-protected-url-in-an-iframe).

> [accordion] My app on localhost gives 502 on its public URL.
>
> Host the port with `--localhost` (`"localhost": true` in the API). Or start the app on `0.0.0.0`. Read [Services that listen on localhost](/hosting/how-it-works#services-that-listen-on-localhost).

> [accordion] Does the URL stay after a stop? Can I use my own domain?
>
> After a resume, the URL and token stay the same. Start your app again. boat does not support custom domains. Put your own proxy or CDN in front of the public URL. Read [Public URLs](/hosting).

> [accordion] I use a firewall. What must stay open?
>
> Keep inbound TCP 8911 and the WireGuard tunnel open. boat runs commands and snapshots through them. Port 22 is SSH. A rule that blocks them marks the sandbox `degraded`. Read [What boat needs](/hosting/firewall#what-boat-needs).

> [accordion] Can I block outbound internet?
>
> boat has no API setting for network rules. Add firewall rules in the sandbox, and run untrusted code as a separate Linux user. Snapshots do not keep firewall rules. Read [Block outbound internet](/hosting/firewall#block-outbound-internet-for-untrusted-code).

## SSH and editors

> [accordion] Why does the SSH host key change after every resume?
>
> Each resume and fork runs on a new machine with a new host key. `boat ssh` and `boat scp` get the new key from the API for you. Other clients must read it again after each resume. Read [SSH](/ssh-access).

> [accordion] How do I connect VS Code or Cursor?
>
> Use the SSH remote of your editor. Read [Editors](/ssh-access/editors).

> [accordion] How do I move large files?
>
> Use a signed upload or download URL, or `boat scp`. Read [Large files](/ssh-access#large-files).

## Desktop and browser

> [accordion] Can I change the desktop background or hide the stats overlay?
>
> Yes. Put a PNG at `~/.config/boat/wallpaper.png`. It stays after stop, resume and fork. To hide the stats, add `overlay=0` to the stream URL, before the `#`. Read [Background](/desktop-streaming/background) and [Embed the stream](/desktop-streaming/urls-and-security#embed-the-stream-in-your-app).

> [accordion] Can I embed the desktop in my app?
>
> Yes. Read [Embed the stream in your app](/desktop-streaming/urls-and-security#embed-the-stream-in-your-app).

## Agents in sandboxes

> [accordion] Which coding agents are built in?
>
> Seven: `codex`, `claude-code`, `pi`, `opencode`, `prime-agent`, `kimi` and `mistral`. You can install and run any other CLI agent yourself. Read [Harnesses and models](/integrated-agents/harnesses-and-models).

> [accordion] A prompt fails with 409 provider_not_configured.
>
> Connect an AI key or subscription first. Read [Keys and subscriptions](/integrated-agents/keys).

> [accordion] Codex or Claude says there is no credential, but I connected one.
>
> The environment has **Safe for third parties** on, so boat holds back all AI credentials. Turn it off for your own sandboxes. For end users, keep it on and use the AI credentials proxy. Read [Keys and subscriptions](/integrated-agents/keys).

> [accordion] The agent in my sandbox gets 403 api_key_action_forbidden when it creates sandboxes.
>
> The key that boat puts in a sandbox works on that sandbox only. Give the agent a `ci` key as a secret: `boat api-key create fleet --preset ci --ttl 7d`. Read [In-sandbox API key](/api-keys/scopes#in-sandbox-api-key).

> [accordion] Can I remove the built-in agents or pin their versions?
>
> Yes. Delete the agents that you do not want: the deletion stays after resume and fork. To pin a version, install your own copy. Your copy is used. Read [Deleted files stay deleted](/snapshots/whats-saved#deleted-files-stay-deleted).

> [accordion] Can I use several Claude or ChatGPT accounts?
>
> Yes. Credential profiles hold several sign-ins and keys per provider. You can switch between them. Read [Credential profiles](/ai-credentials#credential-profiles).

> [accordion] One sandbox per user, per project, or per session?
>
> [Sandbox per user](/platform-guide) compares the three patterns and their costs.

> [accordion] Can I reuse one sandbox for many of my end users?
>
> Give each user their own sandbox. boat does not clean a sandbox between your users, and containers inside one sandbox are not isolated by boat. Start each sandbox from a saved snapshot instead. Read [One sandbox per end user](/security#one-sandbox-per-end-user).

> [accordion] How long should I leave a user's sandbox running before stopping it?
>
> boat has no idle timer. Run your own countdown, and call `boat stop` a few seconds to about two minutes after the agent finishes. Resume takes seconds, but each resume counts as a start. Read [Sandbox per user](/platform-guide).

> [accordion] How do I handle launch spikes?
>
> 1. Prepare one sandbox and save it as a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates).
> 2. Start each user's sandbox from it with `boat new --from <name>`.
> 3. Make sure that your start limits cover the peak.
>
> A sandbox from a saved snapshot gets the full disk in seconds, so you never pay for the same install again.

## API, SDK and CLI

> [accordion] Which API key preset can create sandboxes?
>
> `ci` creates, uses and deletes sandboxes. `full-sandbox` uses existing sandboxes only. `admin` can do everything. An older `ci` key lacks resume: create a new one. Read [Presets](/api-keys/scopes#presets).

> [accordion] Are API keys tied to my account or to an organization?
>
> A key acts as you. An organization key, made with that organization selected in the dashboard, always bills that organization and sees nothing else. An account key bills your active wallet, or the organization named with `X-Boat-Org: <org>`. Read [API keys](/api-keys).

> [accordion] How long do keys last? How do I test a key?
>
> Keys last 90 days by default and 365 days at most. A key created with `--ttl never` (or "Never" in the dashboard) works until you revoke it. Test a key with `GET /me`. Read [API keys](/api-keys).

> [accordion] A create timed out. How do I avoid a second sandbox?
>
> Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on every create and fork. A retry with the same key returns the same sandbox and spends no start. Read [Retry rules](/limits#retry-rules).

> [accordion] My delete call does nothing.
>
> Every delete needs the header `X-Ascii-Confirm-Delete` with the exact target id. Without it, boat answers `409` and deletes nothing. In the TypeScript SDK, pass `xAsciiConfirmDelete`. Read [Delete a sandbox or snapshot](/data-retention/delete).

> [accordion] My command never returns because it starts a background process.
>
> The call waits while a process keeps the output open. Run the command detached: `boat exec <id> --detach "<command>"`, or `"detached": true`. Read [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands).

> [accordion] How do I follow, read or kill a detached command?
>
> Read only new output with offsets, attach with `boat exec <id> --attach <pid>`, and stop it with `boat exec <id> --kill <pid>`. Read [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands).

> [accordion] A command returns sandbox_restoring or 502 right after a resume.
>
> `sandbox_restoring` means that the command did not run. Retry after 1 to 3 seconds. A 502 without that code can mean that the command ran, so check its effect first. Read [API overview](/api/v1).

> [accordion] Can parallel agents each clean up only their own sandbox?
>
> Pass the sandbox id to every command. Without an id, the CLI uses the current sandbox of that shell. Set an auto-stop on each sandbox so that lost ones stop by themselves. Read [CLI reference](/cli-reference).

> [accordion] Can I get events or metrics instead of polling?
>
> Yes. Webhooks send 6 events: ready, error, archived (stopped), hydrated, degraded and recovered. OpenTelemetry export sends metrics and events to your collector. Read [Webhooks](/webhooks) and [OpenTelemetry](/opentelemetry).

## Teams

> [accordion] How do I move my personal plan into an organization?
>
> Do not cancel the personal plan by hand: its sandboxes stop with it. The owner runs `boat --org <org> org migrate`. Read [Move a personal plan](/organizations/move-personal-plan).

> [accordion] The dashboard uses my team, but the API gives trial limits or subscription_required.
>
> The API billed your personal account. Run `boat org switch <org>` one time, or send `X-Boat-Org: <org>` on each call. `GET /limits` shows the wallet that a create bills. Read [Active wallet](/organizations/active-wallet).

> [accordion] A teammate cannot see my sandbox.
>
> Members see the sandboxes that the organization pays for. Personal sandboxes stay hidden. Read [A teammate cannot see or use my sandbox](/organizations/active-wallet#a-teammate-cannot-see-or-use-my-sandbox).

> [accordion] Does each seat need a real person? Do email aliases add seats?
>
> No person is needed. Set the seat count on the Billing tab. A seat counts accounts, not emails, so aliases accepted by the same account add no seat. On the \$2000 plan each seat adds the full plan limits; below it, 20%. Read [Seats](/organizations/seats-and-limits#seats).

> [accordion] An invite fails with "could not add the paid seat".
>
> Accepting an invite with no empty seat charges the organization card for one seat. The card failed, so the invite stays unused. Fix the card with **Manage billing** on the organization's Billing tab. Read [Seats](/organizations/seats-and-limits#seats).

> [accordion] How do I move a plan from an organization back to personal?
>
> There is no one-step move. Run `boat org switch personal`, then `boat billing plan 20`. Read [Move a plan between personal and organization](/billing/plan-changes#move-a-plan-between-personal-and-organization).

## Reliability and errors

> [accordion] My sandbox does not answer, or it is in error.
>
> After a kernel crash, the sandbox restarts by itself in about 15 seconds. If it still does not answer, run `boat stop --force <id>`, then `boat resume <id>`. You lose what was written after the last snapshot. If you cannot lose that work, [contact us](/support) within 3 days. Read [Troubleshooting](/troubleshooting#a-sandbox-does-not-answer).

> [accordion] A command was killed with exit code 137.
>
> The command ran out of memory. Linux killed it, and the sandbox kept running. The result shows `oomKilled: true`. Use less memory or a bigger size. Read [Exit code 137](/troubleshooting#a-command-was-killed-exit-code-137-out-of-memory).

> [accordion] I got an out-of-disk email. What do I do?
>
> boat emails you at 85% and at 95% disk use. At 95%, snapshots fail. Free space with `docker system prune` and `sudo apt-get clean`, or resume with a bigger size. Read [Out-of-disk emails](/troubleshooting#out-of-disk-emails).

> [accordion] My sandbox shows degraded.
>
> boat cannot reach the sandbox through the paths that it needs, often because of a firewall rule. boat does not stop it. Remove the rule, and boat sends `sandbox.recovered`. Read [What happens to a blocked sandbox](/hosting/firewall#what-happens-to-a-blocked-sandbox).

> [accordion] The first outbound connection right after ready fails.
>
> boat has no separate network signal. Retry a failed first connection. Read [Readiness and resume speed](/readiness).

> [accordion] Where do I see incidents?
>
> Platform status is on [status.ascii.dev](https://status.ascii.dev). Send sandbox ids to [support](/support) when a sandbox misbehaves. Read [Compliance and uptime](/compliance).

## Security, data and compliance

> [accordion] Which region do sandboxes run in? Where is my data stored?
>
> Sandboxes run in the EU: Germany, Finland and France. You cannot pick a region. Snapshot copies can be stored outside the EU. Read [Data location](/compliance#data-location).

> [accordion] Do you have compliance certifications or an SLA?
>
> SOC 2 is in progress. Sandboxes have a measured uptime of 99.95%. Platform status is on [status.ascii.dev](https://status.ascii.dev). Read [Compliance and uptime](/compliance).

> [accordion] Can one sandbox see another? Are containers inside a sandbox isolated?
>
> Each sandbox is its own virtual machine. Sandboxes share no disk and no processes. The isolation boundary is the sandbox, not a container inside it. Read [Isolation between sandboxes](/security#isolation-between-sandboxes).

> [accordion] Which boat credentials are inside my sandbox?
>
> `ASCII_TOKEN` hosts ports of its own sandbox only. The in-sandbox API key works on its own sandbox only. **Safe for third parties** removes the key and all your secrets. Read [boat credentials inside a sandbox](/security#boat-credentials-inside-a-sandbox).

> [accordion] Do snapshots contain my secrets?
>
> A snapshot saves the disk as it is. Secrets that you write into files, including container settings, are in it. Keep keys out with the AI credentials proxy, or turn snapshots off for throwaway sandboxes. Read [Snapshots and monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off).

> [accordion] My delete stays blocked. Must I send it again?
>
> No. `waiting_for_uploads` erases at `expectedBy`. `retrying` tries again by itself. A delete never waits for a fork or a saved snapshot: it completes, and they keep the data they read. Poll with `boat deletion status <id>`. Read [How a delete works](/data-retention/delete#how-a-delete-works).

> [accordion] How do I report a security issue?
>
> Write to support with "security" in the subject. Read [Report a security issue](/compliance#report-a-security-issue).


# Free trial
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/free-trial

The 7-day free trial: a card is required, 25 hours of compute, 2 sandboxes at once, 2-hour auto-stop, no large sizes. How it ends, how to cancel it, and how to lift the limits.

Your first plan starts with a free 7-day trial. Checkout asks for a card. **There is no free tier without a card.**

| Rule | Trial | After the first payment |
| - | - | - |
| Length | 7 days, then Stripe charges the plan | - |
| Card | Required at checkout | - |
| Compute | 25 hours in total, all sandboxes together | The plan's [included time](/pricing#plans) |
| Sandboxes at once | 2 | The plan's limit, 100 or more |
| Starts (create, fork, resume) | 5 per minute, 25 per hour, 75 per day | 12 / 60 / 200 or more |
| Auto-stop | Required, 2 hours maximum | Up to 30 days, or off |
| Sizes | `small` and `default` | All sizes. `xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher. |
| Saved snapshots | You cannot save new ones. The ones you have stay free. | 10 for every \$20 of plan per seat, never fewer than 10 |

* Stop, resume and fork do not reset the 25 hours.
* The 25 hours count VM time. The [AI credentials proxy](/ai-credentials#pricing) is not VM time: the wallet pays it, \$1 for each day it is on.
* During the trial, the wallet pays only the AI credentials proxy. You can add money only while the proxy is on, when your sandboxes used it in the last 7 days, or when the wallet is in debt.
* `GET /limits` shows the allowance in `trialComputeCapSeconds` and the time used in `creditUsedSeconds`.
* A resume gives the sandbox a new auto-stop window of 2 hours or less.
* The trial limits stay until the first plan payment. A wallet top-up does not end the trial and does not lift its limits.
* A change to another plan during the trial ends the trial. Stripe charges the new plan at once.
* `boat limits` shows the trial limits and the hours that you have left.

## Who gets a trial

* A person gets one trial. An account that subscribed before restarts the plan with no trial.
* Organizations get no trial. An organization plan is paid from the first day.
* During the trial, you can own one organization. End the trial to own up to 5.
* boat can refuse a trial to an identity that looks like a repeat sign-up. The error is `trial_blocked`. If this is wrong, [contact support](/support).

## End the trial early

Pay now to lift every trial limit at once:

1. Open [Dashboard > Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing).
2. Click **Upgrade now**.

Stripe charges the plan price at once. The 7-day period then ends, and the first month starts that day.

Are you a member of an organization that pays? Then switch to it with `boat org switch <org>`. Its sandboxes do not use your trial limits.

## Cancel the trial

| How | What happens | Charge |
| - | - | - |
| **Cancel trial** on [Dashboard > Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) | The trial ends now. boat stops your running sandboxes. Their disks stay. | None |
| Cancel in the Stripe portal (`boat billing portal`) | The trial runs until its end date, then ends. | None |

After a cancel, **Upgrade now** no longer works. To keep using boat, subscribe again from the Billing tab. You get no second trial.

## Errors you can get during the trial

| Status | Code | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - | - |
| `400` | `trial_auto_stop_required` | No auto-stop, or an auto-stop above 2 hours | Set `--ttl 7200` or less, or end the trial. |
| `403` | `trial_machine_class_not_allowed` | You asked for `large` | Use `default`, or end the trial. |
| `403` | `trial_saved_snapshots_not_allowed` | You saved a snapshot | End the trial. |
| `400` | `trial_one_organization` | You created a second organization | End the trial. |
| `429` | `limit_reached` | 2 sandboxes already run | Stop one, or end the trial. |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | 5 starts in the last minute, 25 in the last hour, or 75 in the last day | Wait, or end the trial. |
| `429` | `trial_compute_limit_reached` | You used the 25 hours | End the trial. |

For every limit and error after the trial, read [Limits and errors](/limits).


# Public URLs
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/hosting

Expose a port of a sandbox on a stable public HTTPS URL, protect it with a token, rename its subdomain, or open a raw TCP or UDP port.

Run a service in your sandbox. boat gives it a stable public HTTPS URL.

## Quick path

The API examples use `BOAT_API_BASE=https://boat.dev/api/v1`.

**1. Start your app in the background**

Start the app as a detached process on an explicit port. A normal command stops after 30 seconds, and a dev server never ends.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --cwd my-repo --detach "npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000","cwd":"my-repo","detached":true}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.command({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  command: "npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000",
  cwd: "my-repo",
  detached: true,
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.command_request import CommandRequest

sandbox.command("bx_f7k2q9hd", CommandRequest(
    command="npm run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0 --port 3000",
    cwd="my-repo",
    detached=True,
))
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> An app on `0.0.0.0` needs no flag. An app on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `::1` needs `--localhost` in the next step (`"localhost": true` in the API). See [Services that listen on localhost](/hosting/how-it-works#services-that-listen-on-localhost).

**2. Host the port**

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 3000 --title "App preview"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/host" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"port":3000,"title":"App preview"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const hosted = await sandbox.hostPort({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd", port: 3000, title: "App preview" });
console.log(hosted.url);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.host_port_request import HostPortRequest

hosted = sandbox.host_port("bx_f7k2q9hd", HostPortRequest(port=3000, title="App preview"))
print(hosted.url)
```

Inside the sandbox, `host 3000` does the same thing.

**3. Open the URL**

The call returns the URL. A new URL is protected by default and includes a `_token` query parameter:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
https://<sandbox-subdomain>-3000.on.boat.dev?_token=<access-token>
```

Open it in a browser. To get a URL without a token, add `--public` (`"public": true` in the API).

## Who can open a protected URL

* Anyone who has the full URL with `_token` can open it.
* boat does not ask for a boat sign-in. boat does not check the organization.
* Treat the full URL like a password.

The `_token` URL answers with a redirect that sets a cookie. A browser follows it. For `curl`, keep the cookie:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -L -c cookies.txt -b cookies.txt "https://<sandbox-subdomain>-3000.on.boat.dev?_token=<access-token>"
```

An API client can send the token as a cookie header instead:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -H "Cookie: _port_auth=<access-token>" "https://<sandbox-subdomain>-3000.on.boat.dev/api/health"
```

### Show a protected URL in an iframe

In an iframe on another site, the `_port_auth` cookie is a third-party cookie. Browsers can block it, and the frame then stays blank. The same URL works in its own tab.

* To embed a preview, host the port with `--public`.
* Or put your own server in front of the URL. Your server sends `Cookie: _port_auth=<access-token>` to boat.

### Replace a leaked token

boat has no rotate command. Do these two calls one after the other:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 3000 --public   # removes the old token
boat host bx_f7k2q9hd 3000            # makes a new token and prints the new URL
```

* The old `_token` URL stops working.
* Between the two calls, the URL is open without a token. Stop the app first if this is a problem.
* `host hide` does not change the token. A later `host` brings back the same token.

## Facts

| Fact | Value |
| - | - |
| URL format | `https://<sandbox-subdomain>-<port>.on.boat.dev` |
| Ports per sandbox | Up to 50 |
| Default access | Protected, with `_token` |
| Address your app listens on | `0.0.0.0`, or `localhost` with `--localhost` |
| Host from your computer | `boat host <sandbox-id> <port>`, or `POST /sandboxes/{id}/host` |
| Host from inside the sandbox | `host <port>` |
| After a stop and resume | The URL stays the same. Start your app again. |
| Ports that boat uses | 22, 6080, 8090, 8911, 47984 to 48010. Do not run your app on them. |
| Custom domain | Not supported. See [Custom domain](#custom-domain). |
| Raw TCP or UDP | Through the sandbox IP address. See [Raw TCP or UDP ports](#raw-tcp-or-udp-ports). |

## Choose the subdomain

Every sandbox has one subdomain. All its public URLs use it. To change it, update the sandbox:

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PATCH "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"subdomain":"acme-staging"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.update({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd", subdomain: "acme-staging" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.update_sandbox_request import UpdateSandboxRequest

sandbox.update("bx_f7k2q9hd", UpdateSandboxRequest(subdomain="acme-staging"))
```

* The CLI has no flag for this.
* Use 3 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens.
* The name cannot end with `-desktop` or with `-<number>`.
* `409 subdomain_taken` means another sandbox uses the name.
* The sandbox must be running or fully stopped. Else the API returns `sandbox_busy`.
* Each hosted port moves to the new name, for example `acme-staging-3000.on.boat.dev`.
* The old URLs stop working. The `_token` values stay the same.

## Custom domain

boat does not support custom domains.

* A CNAME record to an `on.boat.dev` name does not work. boat routes and issues TLS certificates only for `on.boat.dev` names.
* An A record to the sandbox IP address breaks at the next resume, because the IP address changes.

To show the app on your own domain, run your own reverse proxy or CDN in front of the public URL. The proxy must send the `on.boat.dev` host name to boat.

## Raw TCP or UDP ports

The public URL carries HTTPS and WebSockets only. For another protocol, open the port in the sandbox firewall and connect to the sandbox IP address.

**1. Open the port**

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd "sudo ufw allow 27015/udp"
```

Use `27015/tcp` for TCP.

**2. Get the address**

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat info bx_f7k2q9hd
```

Connect to `ip` on your port.

* The IP address changes at each resume. Get it again after a resume.
* Snapshots do not keep firewall rules. Open the port again after each resume and fork.
* `boat host <id> <port> --public` also opens that TCP port on the IP address. boat opens it again after a resume.
* Some sandboxes have no public IPv4 address. Then `boat info` shows `sshEndpoint`, and `ip` is an IPv6 address. Only clients with IPv6 can reach a raw port there.

## Learn more

> [card] [Expose a port: host commands](/hosting/host-cli)
>
> `boat host`, `host`, `host list`, `host url` and `host hide`, with all options.

> [card] [How public URLs work](/hosting/how-it-works)
>
> How boat routes a request to your sandbox.

> [card] [Firewall rules](/hosting/firewall)
>
> Add firewall rules and block outbound traffic without breaking boat.

> [card] [Forward a port to your computer](/ssh-access#forward-a-port)
>
> Reach a sandbox port on your own `localhost`, with no public URL.
