| **Your account** | Agents & Proxying: the Grok subscription row (Sign in, then confirm the code on accounts.x.ai) or the xAI API key row |
| **Per sandbox, from your user** | `boat new --no-env -e XAI_API_KEY=…` |

Model ids: `grok-4.7`, `grok-4.6`, `grok-build-0.1`. When both xAI credentials are on, boat uses the subscription. boat renews the sign-in. The sandbox gets the access token only, never the renew token.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat prompt --provider opencode --model grok-4.7 "Summarize this repo"
```

## OpenCode Go and pay-as-you-go

One [OpenCode key](https://opencode.ai/console) (`oc_sk_…`) covers the [Go plan](https://opencode.ai/go) and pay-as-you-go credits. pi, OpenCode and Prime Agent use it.

| Plan | Model ids |
| - | - |
| Go (pi and OpenCode only: Go refuses Prime Agent, which does not send the session header Go requires) | `opencode-go:kimi-k3`, `opencode-go:glm-5.3`, `opencode-go:qwen3.8-max`, `opencode-go:deepseek-v4-pro`, `opencode-go:minimax-m3`, `opencode-go:mimo-v2.6-pro`, `opencode-go:grok-4.7`, `opencode-go:gpt-6-luna` |
| Pay-as-you-go | `opencode:claude-opus-5-5`, `opencode:claude-sonnet-5-5`, `opencode:gpt-6.1-sol`, `opencode:gemini-4-argon` |

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --no-env -e OPENCODE_API_KEY=oc_sk_…
boat prompt --provider pi --model opencode-go:kimi-k3 "Summarize this repo"
```


# Steer a running turn
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/integrated-agents/steering

Send a new message to an agent while it works, or interrupt it. The agent uses a steer and keeps what it was doing.

You have three options while a turn runs:

| Command | API | What happens to the running turn |
| - | - | - |
| `boat prompt` | [`POST /prompt`](/api/reference/agent/prompt-sandbox-agent) | The new prompt waits until the turn finishes |
| `boat interrupt` | [`POST /interrupt`](/api/reference/agent/interrupt-running-agent-work) | The turn stops. Files that it already changed stay. The conversation keeps its memory |
| **`boat steer`** | [`POST /steer`](/api/reference/agent/steer-a-running-turn) | The turn gets your new message. The agent uses it and keeps all it was doing |

Use `boat steer` to change the task. Use `boat interrupt` only to stop the work.

`boat steer` is the same as typing into a coding agent while it works.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat prompt "Refactor billing and run the full test suite"
boat steer "Skip the integration tests, the unit tests are enough"
boat steer --convo <id> "Also update the changelog when you are done"
```

If you omit `--convo`, `boat steer` steers the conversation that this shell prompted last. A bare `boat prompt` continues the same conversation.

```mermaid theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
%%{init: {"theme": "base", "fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "themeVariables": {"fontFamily": "IBM Plex Mono", "fontSize": "14px", "primaryColor": "#F1F3F9", "primaryBorderColor": "#263FA9", "primaryTextColor": "#060606", "secondaryColor": "#E0E3F2", "tertiaryColor": "#FEFEFE", "lineColor": "#060606", "textColor": "#060606", "mainBkg": "#F1F3F9", "nodeBorder": "#263FA9", "clusterBkg": "#FEFEFE", "clusterBorder": "#C4C4C4", "edgeLabelBackground": "#FEFEFE", "actorBkg": "#F1F3F9", "actorBorder": "#263FA9", "actorTextColor": "#060606", "actorLineColor": "#9E9E9E", "signalColor": "#060606", "signalTextColor": "#060606", "labelBoxBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "labelBoxBorderColor": "#263FA9", "noteBkgColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteBorderColor": "#E0E3F2", "noteTextColor": "#060606", "sectionBkgColor": "#F1F3F9", "altSectionBkgColor": "#FEFEFE", "taskBkgColor": "#263FA9", "taskBorderColor": "#263FA9", "taskTextColor": "#FEFEFE", "gridColor": "#E0E0E0"}, "flowchart": {"padding": 16, "nodeSpacing": 48, "rankSpacing": 48, "curve": "linear"}, "sequence": {"boxMargin": 16, "actorMargin": 48, "noteMargin": 16, "messageMargin": 32, "mirrorActors": false}, "state": {"padding": 16}, "gantt": {"barHeight": 24, "barGap": 8, "fontSize": 14, "sectionFontSize": 14}}}%%
sequenceDiagram
  participant You
  participant Turn as The running turn
  You->>Turn: boat prompt "refactor billing, run the tests"
  Note over Turn: working, tests running
  You->>Turn: boat steer "skip the integration tests"
  Note over Turn: still the same turn, now with your instruction
  Turn-->>You: finishes the whole thing
```

## How each harness gets the message

Four of the seven harnesses accept a message during a turn natively. Nothing stops.

OpenCode, Kimi Code and Mistral Vibe have no such feature. Their protocol has "prompt" and "cancel", and nothing between them. For these harnesses, boat uses a fallback automatically.

| Harness | Delivery | Turn interrupted? |
| - | - | - |
| Claude Code | Native. The message goes into the turn when the harness takes it in. If it does not, boat runs it right after, as its own turn on the same session. | No |
| Codex | Native. `turn/steer` adds your message to the turn in progress. | No |
| pi | Native. The message goes in at the next model call of the turn. This is usually right after the tool in progress finishes. | No |
| Prime Agent | Native. Same as pi. | No |
| OpenCode | Fallback. boat stops the turn. It then starts a new turn at once on the **same** conversation, with "Continue what you were doing" plus your instruction. | Yes, and it continues by itself |
| Kimi Code | Fallback. Same as OpenCode. | Yes, and it continues by itself |
| Mistral Vibe | Fallback. Same as OpenCode. | Yes, and it continues by itself |

## boat makes sure the agent acts on a steer

A harness can accept a message and then do nothing with it. So boat does not trust the harness. boat does these things:

* Where the harness has its own steering queue, boat watches it.
* boat waits for that queue to empty before it marks the turn finished.
* Where boat cannot see the delivery, it runs your instruction as its own turn when the turn ends.

So when `boat steer` returns and the turn later reports `finished`, the agent did the instruction. It did not only receive it.

## Steer modes

The API response and the event both carry `native`. The event also carries the exact `mode`. It is one of `native`, `native-continued`, `fallback`, or `late`.

**`native-continued`** is the honest middle case. The harness accepted the message, but its turn ended without acting on it. So boat ran it at once as its own turn on the same session. Nothing was interrupted and nothing was forgotten. The instruction only runs one turn boundary later.

The `fallback` path also keeps the harness session and all its memory. So nothing is forgotten. The cost is the one tool call that was in progress. The agent can redo a small part of the work it had just started.

## A steer in the event stream

A steer is its own event in the stream. It is never a queued prompt:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat events --convo <id>
```

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
you [prompt]: Refactor billing and run the full test suite
you [steer]: Skip the integration tests, the unit tests are enough
...
```

## Steer with no running turn

If the conversation has no turn in progress, boat refuses the steer with `no_running_turn` (409). This is on purpose. You asked to change a running turn. A new queued turn would be a surprise. To start a new turn, use `boat prompt`.


# AgentEnv
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/integrations/agentenv

Run AgentEnv RL environments and agents on boat sandboxes with the built-in boat sandbox provider: install, config, a first run, sizes and what the provider refuses.

[AgentEnv](https://www.agentenvframework.com/) is an open-source framework from engineers at Scale AI. You use it to build RL environments, and to run and grade agents inside them.

AgentEnv has a built-in `boat` sandbox provider. With it, each environment and each agent runs in its own boat sandbox: an Ubuntu VM with Docker inside.

```
agent-env run ──> boat provider ──> one boat sandbox per env, one per agent
```

## Set it up

You need Python 3.11.4 or later and a boat account. For the trial, see [Free trial](/free-trial).

**1. Get a boat API key**

Create a key on the [API keys](/api-keys) tab of the dashboard, or run `boat api-key create agentenv --preset ci`. Keep it in an environment variable:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
export BOAT_API_KEY=boat_...
```

**2. Install AgentEnv with the boat extra**

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
pip install 'agentenv-framework[boat]'
```

**3. Configure the provider**

Add the key reference to your AgentEnv config. Use `env:` or `secret:`, never the key itself:

```toml title=".agentenv/config.toml" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
[sandbox.providers.boat.config]
api_key = "env:BOAT_API_KEY"
```

**4. Check your setup**

Run the built-in hello task on boat. It needs no model:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
agent-env run hello --sandbox boat
```

## Use boat for your runs

Make boat the default for environments, agents or both:

```toml title=".agentenv/config.toml" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
[sandbox]
default = "boat"        # envs and deploy_sandbox steps
agent_default = "boat"  # agents
```

To choose boat for one run only, pass a flag:

| Command | Flag |
| - | - |
| `agent-env run` | `--sandbox boat` |
| `agent-env task run` | `--env-sandbox boat`, `--agent-sandbox boat` |

A comma-separated value, for example `"boat,local"`, tries the next provider when one fails to create a sandbox.

## What happens on boat

| AgentEnv step | What happens on boat |
| - | - |
| Create an env or agent | Creates a sandbox of the smallest size that fits the request, and waits until it is ready. |
| Exposed ports | boat hosts each port on a public HTTPS URL. |
| Run ends | AgentEnv deletes the sandbox. |
| Run crashes or is cancelled | The provider finds the sandbox by its label and deletes it. |
| Nothing deletes it | boat stops the sandbox at the AgentEnv timeout, 2 hours by default. |

Each sandbox is a [no-env sandbox](/environments#safe-for-third-parties). It gets none of your secrets, credentials or private repositories, and it cannot act on your account or on other sandboxes. Snapshots are off, so a stopped sandbox keeps no disk.

### Sizes

AgentEnv asks for CPU, memory and disk. The provider picks the smallest boat size that covers all three:

| Size | vCPU | Memory | Disk |
| - | - | - | - |
| `small` | 2 | 4 GiB | 51 GB |
| `default` | 4 | 8 GiB | 51 GB |
| `large` | 8 | 16 GiB | 111 GB |
| `xlarge` | 16 | 32 GiB | 251 GB |

A request bigger than `xlarge` fails. See [Machines](/machines).

### Labels

Every sandbox carries the label `agentenv.managed=true`. AgentEnv attribution (for example `[sandbox.attribution]` in its config) becomes `agentenv.attr.*` labels. Use them to find a run's sandboxes and to join [sandbox usage](/api/reference/sandboxes/get-sandbox-usage) to your runs.

## Limits

When boat refuses a create because a [start limit](/limits) is full, the provider waits and tries again. It makes up to 6 attempts. Keep the number of envs and agents that start at the same time under your limits.

## Not available

The provider refuses these with an error. It never creates a sandbox that is less isolated than you asked for.

* An `image` override. Every sandbox boots the standard boat image. See [Base image and tools](/machines/tools).
* A `network_policy` that restricts egress. boat has no egress allowlist yet.

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `api_key` | none (required) | boat API key, as `env:NAME` or `secret:NAME`. |
| `api_url` | `https://boat.dev/api/v1` | API base URL. |

## Resources

> [card] [AgentEnv sandboxes](https://www.agentenvframework.com/docs/sandboxes#boat)
>
> The boat provider in the AgentEnv docs.

> [card] [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/scaleapi/agentenv-framework)
>
> The AgentEnv framework and its providers.

> [card] [Evals and RL environments](/evals)
>
> Run many eval episodes on boat: saved snapshots, forks, limits and cost.

> [card] [API keys](/api-keys)
>
> Create the key that the provider needs.


# Eve adapter
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/integrations/eve

Run Eve agents in boat sandboxes with the @asciidev/eve-box backend: setup, a complete example, options, and safe sandboxes for other people.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The package keeps its old name, `@asciidev/eve-box`, and its function `asciiBox()`. Version 0.1.6 calls the old Box API, which sends a `Sunset` date of 31 October 2026. Without `apiKey`, it reads `BOX_API_KEY`. See [Migrating from Box](/migrating-from-box).

[Eve](https://www.npmjs.com/package/eve) is a TypeScript framework for coding agents. Eve runs each agent in a sandbox: a filesystem and a shell where the agent reads files, writes files and runs commands. Eve lets you choose where that sandbox runs.

boat is a cloud sandbox: a full Linux machine that you create over an API.

`@asciidev/eve-box` connects Eve to boat. It is an Eve **sandbox backend**. It sends the Eve filesystem and process operations to the boat API. Your Eve agents then run on boat sandboxes, not on your laptop.

> [!NOTE]
>
> You need only two things for this guide: Node.js 18+ and a boat API key. You do not need to know Eve or boat before you start.

## How it fits together

| Part | Job |
| - | - |
| **Eve** | Holds your agent logic. Calls a sandbox for filesystem and shell work. |
| **`@asciidev/eve-box`** | The adapter that you plug into Eve. |
| **boat** | The machine where the work runs. |

```
your Eve agent ──> Eve sandbox API ──> @asciidev/eve-box ──> Sandbox machine
```

## Set it up

**1. Create a boat account**

Sign in at [boat.dev](https://boat.dev) and start a plan. See [Quickstart](/quickstart) and [Free trial](/free-trial).

**2. Get a boat API key**

Create a key on the [API keys](/api-keys) tab of the dashboard, or run `boat api-key create eve --preset ci`. Keep it in an environment variable, never in source control.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
export BOAT_API_KEY=boat_...
```

**3. Install the packages**

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
npm install @asciidev/eve-box eve
```

Use a modern TypeScript config: `"module": "NodeNext"`, `"target": "ES2022"`, `"lib": ["ES2022", "DOM"]`. Set `"type": "module"` in `package.json`.

**4. Define the sandbox backend**

Set the Eve sandbox to use boat. In an Eve project, put this in your sandbox definition file:

```ts title="sandbox.ts" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { defineSandbox } from "eve/sandbox";
import { asciiBox } from "@asciidev/eve-box";

export default defineSandbox({
  backend: asciiBox({
    apiKey: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY!,
    ttlSeconds: 3600, // auto-stop the sandbox one hour after creation
  }),
});
```

The Eve agents in this project now run on boat.

## A complete example

This script runs on its own. It creates a boat sandbox session and tests the operations that Eve uses: run commands, read files and write files. Use it to check your setup before you connect the backend to a larger Eve agent.

```ts title="hello-sandbox.ts" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { asciiBox } from "@asciidev/eve-box";

async function main() {
  const backend = asciiBox({
    apiKey: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY!,
    name: "eve-hello",
    ttlSeconds: 600,
  });

  // Create a session (this provisions a sandbox and waits until it is ready).
  const handle = await backend.create({
    templateKey: null,
    sessionKey: "hello-session",
    runtimeContext: { appRoot: process.cwd() },
  });
  const session = await handle.useSessionFn({ networkPolicy: "allow-all" });

  // Write a file, run a command against it, and read the result back.
  await session.writeTextFile({ path: "notes/hello.txt", content: "hello from Boat\n" });
  const result = await session.run({ command: "cat notes/hello.txt && uname -a" });
  console.log("exit:", result.exitCode);
  console.log(result.stdout);

  // Paths resolve under /workspace, matching Eve's sandbox contract.
  console.log(session.resolvePath("notes/hello.txt")); // -> /workspace/notes/hello.txt
}

main().catch((error) => {
  console.error(error);
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
BOAT_API_KEY=boat_... npx tsx hello-sandbox.ts
```

The output shows the file contents, the `uname` output of the machine, and exit code `0`.

## What the backend maps

| Eve operation | boat behaviour |
| - | - |
| `run` | Runs a bounded command in the sandbox work directory. |
| `spawn` | Starts a background process. Gives streamed `stdout`/`stderr`, `wait()` and `kill()`. |
| `readTextFile` / `writeTextFile` | Reads and writes files under the sandbox work directory. |
| `readBinaryFile` / `writeBinaryFile` | The same, with base64 transfer for binary content. |
| `removePath` | Removes files and directories in the workspace. |
| `resolvePath` | Resolves relative paths from `/workspace`. |
| create / resume | Creates a new sandbox, or connects again to one from the saved Eve session state. |

## Configuration

`asciiBox(options)` accepts these options:

| Option | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `apiKey` | `process.env.BOX_API_KEY` | boat API key (`boat_...`). The examples pass `process.env.BOAT_API_KEY`. |
| `baseUrl` | the old Box API | API base URL. |
| `name` | `eve-<sessionKey>` | Name, or `(input) => string`, for the sandboxes that Eve creates. |
| `ttlSeconds` | `3600` | Auto-stop TTL in seconds. `null` turns off auto-stop. |
| `noEnv` | `false` | Keeps your account secrets and credentials out of sandboxes. Read [Agents that other people use](#running-agents-for-other-people). |
| `env` | none | Environment variables for each sandbox that Eve creates. Read [Agents that other people use](#running-agents-for-other-people). |
| `pollMs` | `500` | How often `spawn()` streams and `wait()` poll. |
| `commandTimeoutMs` | none | Timeout for blocking `run()` commands. |
| `networkPolicy` | none | Initial network policy. Read [Network policies](#network-policies). |

## Running agents for other people

> [!WARNING]
>
> By default, a sandbox gets **your** boat account. This includes your secrets, secret files, repositories cloned with your GitHub credentials, and your SSH identity. This is fine for your own agents. If other people can control the agent, set `noEnv: true`. Then they cannot read your secrets or act as you.

With `noEnv: true`, the sandbox starts without your account credentials. It cannot act on your account or other sandboxes. This does not restrict network access. You then give it only what it needs:

* Secrets: through `env`.
* Files and setup: through the Eve `onSession` hook.

```ts title="sandbox.ts" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { defineSandbox } from "eve/sandbox";
import { asciiBox } from "@asciidev/eve-box";

export default defineSandbox({
  backend: asciiBox({
    apiKey: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY!,
    noEnv: true,
    // Scoped secrets: the only env this sandbox gets:
    env: { MY_APP_TOKEN: process.env.MY_APP_TOKEN! },
  }),
  async onSession({ use }) {
    const sandbox = await use();
    // Seed files and run setup with the session API. These wrap Boat's file
    // and command APIs, so you don't need `boat scp` or `boat ssh`.
    await sandbox.writeTextFile({ path: "config/app.json", content: JSON.stringify({ mode: "prod" }) });
    await sandbox.run({ command: "git clone https://github.com/acme/public-repo . && npm ci" });
  },
});
```

Rules for `env`:

* `env` keys merge over your account variables. The per-sandbox value wins.
* The limit is 100 variables and 64 KB in total.
* boat rejects reserved boat-internal names.

The session API replaces the boat CLI inside Eve:

| Eve call | Same as |
| - | - |
| `writeFile` / `readFile` | [`boat scp`](/ssh-access#copy-files) |
| `run` / `spawn` | `boat exec <id> <cmd>` / `boat exec <id> --detach <cmd>` |

A no-env sandbox cannot reach your private repositories. Clone public ones, or let the user sign in inside the sandbox. Read [No-env sandboxes](/environments#safe-for-third-parties).

## Reusing a prepared environment

Setup runs when boat first creates the sandbox for each session. To start many sessions from the same prepared state:

1. Prepare one sandbox.
2. Save it as a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates): `boat snapshot <id> my-stack`.
3. Create each new sandbox from it: `boat new --from my-stack`, or `from` in the [API](/api/reference/sandboxes/create-sandbox).

A [fork](/api/reference/sandboxes/fork-sandbox) also copies a sandbox, but it follows the newest snapshot of its source. A saved snapshot does not change.

## Network policies

boat does not enforce the fine-grained Eve network policies yet.

* The backend accepts `"allow-all"`.
* For stricter policies, it throws `EveSandboxUnsupportedError`. This includes `"deny-all"`, allow-lists and subnet rules.

Thus you never get isolation that is not real. If you need policies that a firewall enforces, run that Eve agent on a backend that supports them.

## Resources

> [card] [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@asciidev/eve-box)
>
> `@asciidev/eve-box` on npm.

> [card] [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/ariana-dot-dev/eve-box)
>
> Issues, examples and the adapter source.

> [card] [boat quickstart](/quickstart)
>
> Install boat and create your first sandbox.

> [card] [boat API keys](/api-keys)
>
> Create and manage the key that this adapter needs.


# Harbor adapter
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/integrations/harbor

Run Harbor agent trials and evals on boat sandboxes with the harbor-box environment adapter. What works today, Terminal-Bench 2.0 status, and the harbor run command.

`harbor-box` runs [Harbor](https://pypi.org/project/harbor/) trials in boat sandboxes instead of local Docker containers. It is a Harbor environment adapter: the class `BoxEnvironment` in the module `harbor_box_environment`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Terminal-Bench 2.0 does not run on boat through this adapter today.** Every Terminal-Bench 2.0 task names a prebuilt Docker image (`docker_image`), and `harbor-box` 0.1.2 refuses tasks with a Docker image. Use the adapter for your own tasks that run on the standard boat sandbox. For other ways to run evals on boat, see [Evals and RL environments](/evals).

> [!NOTE]
>
> The package keeps its old name, `harbor-box`. Version 0.1.2 reads the key from `BOX_API_KEY` and calls the old Box API. That API sends a `Sunset` date of 31 October 2026. See [Migrating from Box](/migrating-from-box).

## Set it up

You need Python 3.12 or later and a boat account. For the trial, see [Free trial](/free-trial).

1. Create an API key on the [API keys](/api-keys) tab of the dashboard, or run `boat api-key create harbor --preset ci`.

2. Install the adapter. It also installs Harbor (`harbor>=0.14.0`), `httpx` and `tenacity`:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   pip install harbor-box
   ```

3. Give the key to the adapter. It reads `BOX_API_KEY`:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   export BOX_API_KEY=boat_...
   ```

## Run a Harbor job on boat

Pass the adapter as the environment of `harbor run`. `-e` takes a custom environment as `module:Class`:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
harbor run -p path/to/task -a claude-code -m anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 \
  -e harbor_box_environment:BoxEnvironment -n 4
```

| Flag | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `-p` | A local task or dataset directory |
| `-a`, `-m` | The Harbor agent and its model |
| `-e` | The environment: here the boat adapter |
| `-n` | Trials that run at the same time. Each trial is one sandbox, so keep `-n` under your [start limits](/limits) |

> [!WARNING]
>
> At the end of a trial, `harbor-box` 0.1.2 fails to delete its sandbox (the delete call has no confirmation header). The sandbox keeps running until its auto-stop, 24 hours by default. After each job, run `boat list` and delete the trial sandboxes with `boat delete <id> --yes`.

## Check your setup

This script creates one sandbox through the adapter, writes a file, runs a command and stops the sandbox. boat tested it with `harbor-box` 0.1.2 and Harbor 0.24.

```python title="hello_sandbox.py" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import asyncio
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

from harbor.models.task.config import EnvironmentConfig
from harbor.models.trial.paths import TrialPaths
from harbor_box_environment import BoxEnvironment


async def main() -> None:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as raw:
        tmp = Path(raw)
        # Harbor needs an environment directory. Boat reads only the WORKDIR of the Dockerfile.
        env_dir = tmp / "environment"
        env_dir.mkdir()
        (env_dir / "Dockerfile").write_text("FROM ubuntu:24.04\nWORKDIR /workspace\n")
        trial_paths = TrialPaths(tmp / "trial")
        trial_paths.mkdir()

        env = BoxEnvironment(
            environment_dir=env_dir,
            environment_name="harbor-hello",
            session_id="hello-session",
            trial_paths=trial_paths,
            task_env_config=EnvironmentConfig(workdir="/workspace"),
            ttl_seconds=600,  # auto-stop 10 minutes after creation
        )

        await env.start(force_build=False)  # creates a sandbox and waits until it is ready
        try:
            await env.upload_file(__file__, "/workspace/hello_sandbox.py")
            result = await env.exec("echo 'hello from Boat' > notes.txt && cat notes.txt && uname -a")
            print("exit:", result.return_code)
            print(result.stdout)
        finally:
            await env.stop(delete=False)  # stop; delete=True fails in 0.1.2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
BOX_API_KEY=boat_... python hello_sandbox.py
```

The output shows `hello from Boat`, the `uname` line of the sandbox and `exit: 0`.

## What the adapter maps

| Harbor operation | What happens on boat |
| - | - |
| `start` | Creates a sandbox and waits until it is ready. |
| `stop` | Stops the sandbox. boat keeps its disk in a snapshot for 14 days. |
| `exec` | Runs a command in the sandbox. Optional: `cwd`, `env`, `user` and timeout. |
| `upload_file`, `download_file` | Copies files to and from the sandbox. Binary files go as base64. |
| `upload_dir`, `download_dir` | Copies directory trees. |
| `ensure_dirs` | Creates the work and mount directories. |
| `is_file`, `is_dir` | Checks paths in the sandbox. |

## Configuration

`BoxEnvironment(...)` takes the standard Harbor arguments (`environment_dir`, `environment_name`, `session_id`, `trial_paths`, `task_env_config`) and these options:

| Option | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `api_key` | `BOX_API_KEY` | boat API key (`boat_...`). `harbor run` also needs `BOX_API_KEY` set. |
| `base_url` | the old Box API | API base URL. |
| `ttl_seconds` | `86400` (24 hours) | Auto-stop timer. `None` turns auto-stop off. |
| `no_env` | `True` | Creates [no-env sandboxes](#isolation). Set `False` to use your environment. |
| `request_timeout_seconds` | `60` | HTTP timeout for each request. |

## What the adapter does with your task

boat does not build Docker images. Each trial starts on the standard boat sandbox (Ubuntu with common toolchains). See [Base image and tools](/machines/tools).

| Task input | What the adapter does |
| - | - |
| Files in the environment directory | Uploads them to the working directory at start. |
| `Dockerfile` | Reads only the `WORKDIR` of the last stage. It does not run `RUN` or `COPY`. Install dependencies with a command (`await env.exec(...)`) or from your agent. |
| `docker_image` in `task.toml` | Refuses the task. |
| Environment variables | Sends them to the sandbox. |

To start many trials from one prepared state, prepare one sandbox, save a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates), and create each trial sandbox from it. See [Evals and RL environments](/evals).

## Isolation

The adapter creates **no-env** sandboxes by default. A trial gets none of your secrets, credentials or private repositories, and it cannot act on your account or on other sandboxes. To use your [environment](/environments), pass `no_env=False`.

## Not available

The adapter refuses these task settings with an error:

* A prebuilt Docker image (`docker_image`), Docker image builds and Compose.
* Network policies: no network, or allow-lists.
* GPUs, TPUs and Windows.

The adapter writes files as the sandbox user, not as root. A task that writes outside the work directory (for example `/solution` or `/tests`) fails.

## Resources

> [card] [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/harbor-box/)
>
> `harbor-box` on PyPI.

> [card] [Harbor: run a job](https://docs.harborframework.com/jobs/run-a-job)
>
> The `harbor run` flags.

> [card] [Evals and RL environments](/evals)
>
> Run many eval episodes on boat: saved snapshots, forks, limits and cost.

> [card] [API keys](/api-keys)
>
> Create the key that the adapter needs.


# Limits and errors
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/limits

Every boat limit per plan: sandboxes at once, included starts, extra starts, and command and output caps. The error codes, how to retry, and how to raise a limit.

A start is free up to your included number. Above it, a start costs money. Above the maximum, it fails. Create, fork and resume each count as one start. A resume that takes back the kept machine of the sandbox does not count.

## Limits per plan

| Plan | Sandboxes at once | Included starts per minute / hour / day | Maximum starts per day |
| - | - | - | - |
| [Free trial](/free-trial) | 2 | 5 / 25 / 75 | 75 |
| \$20 | 100 | 12 / 60 / 200 | 1,200 |
| \$100 | 300 | 30 / 210 / 840 | 5,040 |
| \$500 | 1,000 | 65 / 420 / 1,680 | 10,080 |
| \$2000 | 2,000 | 90 / 600 / 2,400 | 14,400 |

* boat counts starts over the last 60 seconds, 60 minutes and 24 hours. There is no reset date.
* A stopped sandbox does not count against "at once".
* For organizations, read [Seats, limits and caps](/organizations/seats-and-limits).
* To see what you have left, run `boat limits`.

## Extra starts

A start above your included number is an extra start. It needs a first payment.

| Start | Price | Per day on the \$20 plan |
| - | - | - |
| Included | Free | 1 to 200 |
| Up to 1.5 times included | \$0.03 | 201 to 300 |
| Up to 2 times | \$0.05 | 301 to 400 |
| Up to 6 times | \$0.07 | 401 to 1,200 |
| Above 6 times | Fails | 1,201 and up |

* The prices apply per minute, hour and day. A start pays the highest of the three.
* The maximum per minute is 3 times, not 6.

You choose what an extra start does. Set it in the dashboard (**Billing**, **Extra starts**) or with the CLI:

| Choice | Command | What happens |
| - | - | - |
| Pay from the wallet (default) | `boat billing extra-starts wallet` | Your wallet pays. With an empty wallet, the start fails. |
| Fail | `boat billing extra-starts fail` | The start fails, even with money in your wallet. |
| Wallet, then invoice | `boat billing extra-starts invoice` | Your wallet pays. With an empty wallet, [your invoice](#extra-starts-on-your-invoice) pays. |

**boat never queues a start.** A failed start does not run later. Send a new call after `nextStartAt`. Only [`runs-on: boat` jobs](/ci#what-happens-at-a-limit) can wait.

### Extra starts on your invoice

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat billing extra-starts on
boat billing extra-starts off
```

* `on` is the same as `invoice`. `off` turns the invoice off, and your wallet pays again. `off` does not change `fail`.
* It is off by default. A trial, a past-due account, or a plan set to end cannot use it.
* The cap per seat per month is \$80 on the \$20 plan, \$400 on the \$100 plan, and \$1,500 above.
* If your plan ends first, your wallet pays what is left and can go negative.
* In a script, add `--yes` to accept the terms.

### In the API

`GET /limits` returns:

| Field | Means |
| - | - |
| `nextStartDollars` | Price of the next start. `null` when it would fail. |
| `startLimitsWithWallet` | The maximums. `null` when extra starts are not available now, or are set to fail. |
| `keepGoing.mode` | What an extra start does: `fail`, `wallet` or `invoice`. |
| `overagePrices.startBrackets` | The price table. |
| `startWindowFull` | Only while a limit is full: `window`, `limit`, `freesAt`, `paidBy` (`wallet`, `invoice` or `null`), `message` (the text the CLI prints) and `help` (the same text in parts). |
| `planNudge` | Only when the next plan fits your last 30 days better. `text` has the sum. boat can send it by email once a billing period. Turn that off in [Alerts](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=alerts). |

## Other limits

| Limit | Value |
| - | - |
| Auto-stop | Default 1 hour. Maximum 30 days, or off. Trial: 2 hours maximum. |
| Sizes | `xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher. The trial has no `large` or `xlarge`. `boat limits` shows the sizes that you can create now. In the API: `machineTypes` in `GET /limits`. |
| Disk of a stopped sandbox | Kept for at least 14 days after the stop, then eligible for automated retention cleanup. The job currently reports candidates without deleting them in production. |
| Saved snapshots | 10 included for every \$20 of plan per seat, never fewer than 10, per account or organization. Each one more costs \$0.056 a day from the wallet. No maximum or scheduled expiry. Unpaid extras can be deleted after 7 days. |
| Command that waits for its result | API: default timeout 30 s, maximum 600 s. For longer work, run it detached. No maximum with `boat exec --timeout 0` (CLI) or `run_command` / `runCommand` (SDK). |
| Output of a waiting command | 8 MiB per stream |
| Command output kept per account | 10 MiB compressed per hour (about 50 MiB of text) |
| Output of other processes | 64 KiB/s per process, plus 10 MiB compressed per hour per account |
| Prompt attachments | 12 files, 25 MB per file, 64 MB in total |
| Webhooks | 10 per account |
| API keys | Lifetime 90 days by default, 365 days maximum, or never expires (`--ttl never`) |
| API requests | 10,000 per 60 seconds from one IP address |

For the command limits, read [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands) and [Command history and logs](/long-running-tasks/command-history).

## Errors and what to do

| Status | Code | Cause | What to do |
| - | - | - | - |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | A start limit is full. The start did not run and does not queue. The body has `window` (`minute`, `hour` or `day`), `limit`, `cause` (`trial`, `plan`, `cap` or `ceiling`), `nextStartAt` and `retryAfterSeconds`. | Pick an option in `message`, or send a new call after `nextStartAt`. At cause `ceiling`, only a bigger plan or more seats help. |
| `429` | `limit_reached` | The plan's "at once" limit is full. | Stop a sandbox, or raise the plan. |
| `429` | `member_limit_reached` | The organization owner capped how many sandboxes you run at once. | Stop one, or ask the owner to raise your cap. |
| `429` | `trial_compute_limit_reached` | The trial used its 25 hours. | [End the trial](/free-trial#end-the-trial-early). |
| `429` | `IP_RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (in `code`) | More than 10,000 API requests in 60 seconds from one IP address. An open stream counts once, when it opens. | Wait the `retryAfter` seconds in the body. Watch the `RateLimit` header to slow down before this. |
| `402` | `billing_required` | The included time is used and the wallet is empty, or the account or organization has no plan. | Open the `billingUrl` in the body. Add money to the wallet, or start a plan. |
| `402` | `team_member_cap_reached` | You used your per-member usage cap in the organization. | Ask the owner to raise it. It resets with the billing month. |
| `403` | `trial_machine_class_not_allowed` | `large` during the trial. | Use `default`, or end the trial. |
| `413` | `file_too_large` | A file read is above 5 MiB. | Get a download link with `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/download-url`. |
| `400` | `invalid_query` | A list call got a query parameter that it does not know. | Remove the parameter. |
| `400` | `trial_auto_stop_required` | No auto-stop, or more than 2 hours, during the trial. | Set an auto-stop of 2 hours or less. |
| `409` | `snapshot_data_expired` | boat deleted the data after the sandbox had been stopped for at least 14 days. | You cannot resume it. Next time, save a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/stop#keep-a-stopped-sandbox-longer-than-14-days) before day 14. |
| `503` | `no_ready_machine` | You asked to [fail fast](/machines/fail-fast) and no machine is ready. Nothing started or counted. | Retry after `retryAfterSeconds` (5). |
| `503` | `service_unavailable` | Your box could not start. Running sandboxes are not affected. | Retry after `retryAfterSeconds` (120). |

### Retry rules

* Every `429` sends a `Retry-After` header: the wait in seconds. The body also has the wait: `retryAfterSeconds` on `rate_limited`, `retryAfter` on an IP limit. A `503` has `retryAfterSeconds`.
* Every API answer carries your IP limit in two headers ([IETF RateLimit fields](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers/)). `r` is the number of requests you have left. `t` is the seconds until the window resets:

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
RateLimit-Policy: "ip";q=10000;w=60
RateLimit: "ip";r=9412;t=60
```

* Create, resume and fork answers also carry your start limits, one policy per window: `starts-minute` (`w=60`), `starts-hour` (`w=3600`) and `starts-day` (`w=86400`). `RateLimit` reports the start window with the fewest starts left: `"<policy>";r=<starts left>;t=<seconds>`. An account with no start limit gets no start policies.
* A start that fails with `rate_limited` does not count as a start.
* Send an `Idempotency-Key` header on create and fork. A retry with the same key never makes a second sandbox or spends a second start.
* The CLI does not retry. It prints the limit message and exits with an error.

## Raise a limit

| You need | Do this |
| - | - |
| More starts or more sandboxes at once | Move to a bigger plan: `boat billing plan 100`, or [Dashboard > Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing). The change applies at once. |
| More of everything, for a team | Move to a bigger plan first. On the \$2000 plan, buy seats on an [organization](/organizations/seats-and-limits): each seat adds the full limits and included time. |
| More time, same limits | Add money to the wallet (`boat wallet pay 50`) or turn on [auto top-up](/billing#auto-top-up). |
| More starts for a short time | Use [extra starts](#extra-starts). |
| More than the \$2000 plan gives | boat raises limits only on custom plans above \$2000 a month. [Contact us](/support) for a custom plan. |
| Trial limits gone | Pay the first plan. Read [Free trial](/free-trial). |


# Keep a sandbox running
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/long-running-tasks

Keep a sandbox running longer or 24/7, run long commands in the background, restart processes after resume or fork, and read past command output.

A sandbox stops by itself 1 hour after it starts or resumes. This is the default auto-stop timer. For work that runs longer, use the tools on these pages.

## What you can do

| You want | Use | Command |
| - | - | - |
| A sandbox that runs until you stop it | [Turn off auto-stop](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop#turn-off-auto-stop) | `boat extend <id> --no-auto-stop` |
| More time, with a deadline | [Extend with a deadline](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop#extend-with-a-deadline) | `boat extend <id> --hours 12` |
| An agent prompt that runs past the deadline | Nothing. While a prompt runs, boat moves the deadline forward by one auto-stop period | `boat prompt <id> "…"` |
| A command that runs longer than the 30-second default timeout, or a server | [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands) | `boat exec <id> --detach "<command>"` |
| The output of a past command, also on a stopped sandbox | [Command history and logs](/long-running-tasks/command-history) | `boat history <id>` |
| The processes in a sandbox | [List processes](/long-running-tasks/command-history#list-processes) | `boat ps <id>` |
| A process that comes back after stop, resume and fork | [Always-on services](/long-running-tasks/always-on-services) | `sudo systemctl enable --now <service>` |

> [!NOTE]
>
> On the free trial, you cannot turn off auto-stop, and auto-stop cannot be more than 2 hours. boat refuses the call with `trial_auto_stop_required`. Everything else on these pages works on the trial. Read [Free trial](/free-trial).

## What comes back after a resume

| Process | After a resume or fork |
| - | - |
| A systemd service that you enabled | Starts again by itself. |
| A process that you started by hand | Does not come back. Start it again. |
| A detached background command | Does not come back. |

## Learn more

> [card] [Auto-stop and keep alive](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop)
>
> Turn off auto-stop, read the deadline, and extend a sandbox.

> [card] [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands)
>
> Start a long command, read its output, attach to it, and stop it.

> [card] [Command history and logs](/long-running-tasks/command-history)
>
> Read the output of past commands and processes. List the processes.

> [card] [Always-on services, 24/7](/long-running-tasks/always-on-services)
>
> Make a process come back after stop, resume and fork.

# Always-on services, 24/7
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/long-running-tasks/always-on-services

Run a server, bot or worker 24/7: make a process come back by itself after stop, resume and fork with a systemd service.

To run a process 24/7, do two things:

1. [Turn off auto-stop](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop#turn-off-auto-stop): `boat extend <id> --no-auto-stop`.
2. Run the process as an enabled systemd service, as shown below. It then comes back after any stop, resume or fork.

## What comes back after a resume or fork

`boat stop` makes a snapshot of the file system. `boat resume` restores that file system. `boat fork` makes a new sandbox from the latest snapshot. A resume takes a few seconds, for any amount of data in the sandbox.

For what a snapshot saves, restore behavior, retention, and how to look at or download a snapshot, see [Snapshots](/snapshots).

A stop and resume is the same as a server reboot:

| Process | After a resume |
| - | - |
| A systemd service that you enabled | Starts again by itself. |
| A process that you started by hand: a dev server, a background job, a tunnel, a browser session | Does not come back. Start it again, or make it a systemd service. |

## Run an always-on service

To make a process come back after stop, resume and fork with no action from you, run it as an enabled systemd service. The unit file is under `/etc`, which is in the snapshot. Thus a resumed or forked sandbox starts the service by itself.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/my-app.service >/dev/null <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=My app
After=network.target

[Service]
User=user
WorkingDirectory=/home/user/my-app
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npm run start
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now my-app
```

* `Restart=always` also starts the process again if it crashes.
* To check the service, run `systemctl status my-app`.
* To read its logs, run `journalctl -u my-app`.

Run these commands inside the sandbox. Use `boat ssh`, the [command endpoint](/api/reference/agent/execute-sandbox-command), or the `command` method of the SDKs.

If the service serves HTTP, expose it with `host <port>`. After a resume, `host` on the same port gives the same URL and token. Thus links that you gave out continue to work. See [Public URLs](/hosting).

## Resume or fork

To continue earlier work, resume the sandbox. To branch earlier work, fork it. Both use the latest snapshot.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat resume bx_f7k2q9hd
boat fork bx_f7k2q9hd
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/resume" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/fork" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.resume({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd" });
const forked = await sandbox.fork({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.resume("bx_f7k2q9hd")
forked = sandbox.fork("bx_f7k2q9hd")
```

## Repeatable setup

If you do not use a systemd service, start your work again after each resume or fork. Make the setup and start commands idempotent.

* Run a short setup command normally. It must end within its timeout: 30 seconds by default, 600 at most.
* Run a dev server or any process that does not end as a **detached** command. A normal command is killed at its timeout.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ssh "$sandbox_id" -- bash -s < ./setup.sh
boat exec "$sandbox_id" --cwd my-app --detach "npm run dev"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"bash ./setup.sh","cwd":"my-app","timeoutSeconds":600}'

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"npm run dev","cwd":"my-app","detached":true}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.command({ sandboxId, command: "bash ./setup.sh", cwd: "my-app", timeoutSeconds: 600 });
await sandbox.command({ sandboxId, command: "npm run dev", cwd: "my-app", detached: true });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="bash ./setup.sh", cwd="my-app", timeout_seconds=600))
sandbox.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="npm run dev", cwd="my-app", detached=True))
```

For command timeouts and retries, see [Background commands](/long-running-tasks/background-commands#timeouts-and-retries).


# Auto-stop and keep alive
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/long-running-tasks/auto-stop

Keep a sandbox alive: turn off auto-stop, read the auto-stop deadline, and extend a sandbox. A running agent prompt moves the deadline.

## Keep a sandbox alive

Every sandbox has an auto-stop timer.

* The default is 1 hour. The maximum is 30 days, or no auto-stop at all.
* The timer counts from creation or from the last resume, not from your last activity.
* A sandbox with a 1 hour TTL stops one hour after it starts, even in the middle of your own commands.
* **A running agent prompt is the exception.** When the deadline comes while a prompt runs or waits, boat moves the deadline to one TTL later. It does this again until no prompt is active.

| You want | Command |
| - | - |
| No auto-stop | `boat extend <id> --no-auto-stop` |
| Stop 12 hours from now | `boat extend <id> --hours 12` |
| See the deadline | `boat info <id>` |

> [!NOTE]
>
> On the free trial, you cannot turn off auto-stop, and the TTL cannot be more than 2 hours. boat refuses the call with `trial_auto_stop_required`. Read [Free trial](/free-trial).

## Turn off auto-stop

Use this when the sandbox must run until you stop it yourself. Examples are demos, browser sessions, long setup jobs and unattended workflows. A stop interrupts this work, and you must then start the processes again.

Turn off auto-stop when you create the sandbox. For a sandbox that exists, set its TTL to `null`.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --no-auto-stop
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --no-auto-stop
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":null}'

curl -sS -X PATCH "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":null}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const created = await sandbox.create({ ttlSeconds: null });

await sandbox.update({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  ttlSeconds: null,
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
created = sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=None))

sandbox.update("bx_f7k2q9hd", UpdateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=None))
```

You can also select **No auto-stop** in the dashboard.

### TTL on resume and fork

`resume` and `fork` also accept `ttlSeconds`. Thus a sandbox that comes back does not need a second call to set its lifetime.

| Call | When you do not give `ttlSeconds` |
| - | - |
| Resume | The sandbox keeps its current setting. |
| Fork | The new sandbox gets 1 hour. It does not copy the setting of the source sandbox. |

Thus a fork of a sandbox with auto-stop off does not silently make a second sandbox that never stops. See [Snapshots](/snapshots).

## Read the auto-stop deadline

Each resume sets the deadline again. The new deadline is the resume time plus the TTL of the sandbox.

If you schedule long jobs, do these steps:

1. Read the deadline after each resume.
2. Before a job that runs past the deadline, extend the sandbox.

`archiveAfter` is the deadline. It is `null` when auto-stop is off. `ttlSeconds` is the TTL as you last set it.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat info bx_f7k2q9hd          # shows the deadline and the time left
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" | jq -r .sandbox.archiveAfter
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const info = await sandbox.get({ sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd" });
console.log(info.sandbox.archiveAfter);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
info = sandbox.get("bx_f7k2q9hd")
print(info.sandbox.archive_after)
```

At the deadline, the sandbox stops the same as with `boat stop`. The stop starts within about 5 seconds of the deadline. boat cuts off the jobs that run. See [what a stop does to running work](/snapshots/stop#what-a-stop-does).

There is one exception. While a prompt to the agent of the sandbox runs, boat moves the deadline forward by one TTL. Your own jobs do not move the deadline. Examples are `boat exec` commands and services. Read `archiveAfter` again each time. Do not keep the first value.

The API reports a stopped sandbox as `archived`.

## Extend with a deadline

`boat extend` sets a new TTL. The new deadline is **now plus the TTL**, not the start time plus the TTL. The sandbox also keeps this TTL for later resumes.

* `boat extend <id> --hours 12`: the sandbox stops 12 hours from now.
* `--hours` and `--ttl` set the remaining time. They do not add to it.
* `PATCH /sandboxes/{id}` with `ttlSeconds` does the same.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --hours 12
boat info bx_f7k2q9hd          # archiveAfter is now 12 hours from now
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --ttl 2592000
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PATCH "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":43200}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.update({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  ttlSeconds: 12 * 60 * 60,
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.update("bx_f7k2q9hd", UpdateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=12 * 60 * 60))
```

* `2592000` seconds is 30 days.
* 30 days is the maximum numeric TTL that the boat API accepts.
* boat caps larger values to 30 days.


# Background commands
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/long-running-tasks/background-commands

Run a long command or a server in the background with --detach, read its output, attach to it, and stop it.

A synchronous command stops at its `timeoutSeconds` limit. The default is 30 seconds. The maximum is 600 seconds (10 minutes). For a longer job or a server that does not end, start the command detached, then poll for its result. Examples are builds, installs, data processing and dev servers.

A long job that you want to wait for needs no polling:

* CLI: `boat exec <id> --timeout 0 -- <command>` runs it detached, prints its output live until it ends, and exits with its exit code.
* SDK: `run_command` ([Python](/sdks/python#run-a-command-with-no-time-limit)) and `runCommand` ([TypeScript](/sdks/typescript#run-a-command-with-no-time-limit)) do the same and yield the output.
* API: start the command with `detached: true`, then [attach](#attach-to-a-background-process) to it.

This replaces the `nohup ... &` pattern for simple cases. You do not keep an SSH session open. You do not write a unit file.

The flow is: start, then poll, then collect.

## Start a command and read its status

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
pid="$(boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --detach "npm run build" | jq -r .processId)"
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --status "$pid"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command":"npm run build","detached":true}'
# {"type":"command.started","processId":1234,"pid":1234,"logPath":"/home/user/.ascii/processes/1234.log",...}

curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/commands/1234" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"command.status","running":false,"exitCode":0,"stdout":"...","stderr":"...",...}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const started = await sandbox.command({
  sandboxId,
  command: "npm run build", detached: true,
});

const status = await sandbox.commandStatus({ sandboxId, processId: started.processId });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.command_request import CommandRequest

started = sandbox.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="npm run build", detached=True))

status = sandbox.command_status(sandbox_id, started.process_id)
```

* The command continues on the sandbox after the start call returns.
* boat appends stdout and stderr to `~/.ascii/processes/<pid>.log` on the sandbox. The folder keeps an older internal name.
* The status call gives `running`, the `exitCode` when the command ends, and the last part of each log.

## Read only new output

1. Give `stdoutOffset` and `stderrOffset` to the status call. Start at 0.
2. The answer holds only the output written after those byte offsets.
3. The answer also holds `stdoutNextOffset` and `stderrNextOffset`. Use them in the next call.
4. When `more` is `true`, call again immediately.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
# The CLI follows for you: see Attach below.
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --attach "$pid"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/commands/1234?stdoutOffset=0&stderrOffset=0" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"command.status","running":true,"stdout":"compiling...\n","stdoutNextOffset":13,"stderrNextOffset":0,"more":false,...}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
let stdoutOffset = 0, stderrOffset = 0;
for (;;) {
  const r: any = await sandbox.commandStatus({ sandboxId, processId: started.processId, stdoutOffset, stderrOffset });
  process.stdout.write(r.stdout);
  process.stderr.write(r.stderr);
  stdoutOffset = r.stdoutNextOffset;
  stderrOffset = r.stderrNextOffset;
  if (!r.running && !r.more) break;
  if (!r.more) await new Promise((ok) => setTimeout(ok, 1000));
}
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import sys, time

out_offset = err_offset = 0
while True:
    r = sandbox.command_status(sandbox_id, started.process_id, stdout_offset=out_offset, stderr_offset=err_offset)
    sys.stdout.write(r.stdout)
    sys.stderr.write(r.stderr)
    out_offset, err_offset = r.stdout_next_offset, r.stderr_next_offset
    if not r.running and not r.more:
        break
    if not r.more:
        time.sleep(1)
```

## Attach to a background process

Attach opens one stream. The stream sends the output while the command writes it, until the command ends. Use attach instead of polling.

The API allows 10,000 requests in 60 seconds per IP address. A stream counts once, when it opens, however long it stays open. Polling each of many processes every second reaches the limit. One open stream per process does not.

Each line of the stream is one JSON object:

| Line | When |
| - | - |
| `attached` | First. |
| `stdout` / `stderr` | Each chunk of output, with its `nextOffset`. |
| `heartbeat` | After 15 seconds with no output. |
| `reconnect` | After 10 minutes. The stream ends. The line holds `stdoutOffset` and `stderrOffset`. |
| `exit` | Last. It holds the exit code. |

After a `reconnect` line, open the stream again with those offsets. You get no gap and no repeat, for as long as the command runs. The CLI reconnects for you.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --attach "$pid"
# prints the output from its start, then exits with the command's exit code
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sSN "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/commands/1234/stream?stdoutOffset=0&stderrOffset=0" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"attached","processId":1234,"stdoutOffset":0,"stderrOffset":0}
# {"type":"stdout","data":"compiling...\n","nextOffset":13}
# {"type":"exit","status":"exited","exitCode":0,"signal":null,"stdoutOffset":13,"stderrOffset":0}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
let offsets = { stdout: 0, stderr: 0 };
for (let done = false; !done; ) {
  const res = await fetch(`${BOAT_API_BASE}/sandboxes/${sandboxId}/commands/${pid}/stream?stdoutOffset=${offsets.stdout}&stderrOffset=${offsets.stderr}`,
    { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${BOAT_API_KEY}` } });
  const lines = res.body!.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream());
  let buf = "";
  for await (const chunk of lines) {
    buf += chunk;
    let i;
    while ((i = buf.indexOf("\n")) >= 0) {
      const f = JSON.parse(buf.slice(0, i));
      buf = buf.slice(i + 1);
      if (f.type === "stdout" || f.type === "stderr") { process[f.type].write(f.data); offsets[f.type] = f.nextOffset; }
      if (f.type === "reconnect") offsets = { stdout: f.stdoutOffset, stderr: f.stderrOffset };
      if (f.type === "exit" || f.type === "error") done = true;
    }
  }
}
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import json, sys, requests

offsets = {"stdout": 0, "stderr": 0}
done = False
while not done:
    url = f"{BOAT_API_BASE}/sandboxes/{sandbox_id}/commands/{pid}/stream"
    params = {"stdoutOffset": offsets["stdout"], "stderrOffset": offsets["stderr"]}
    with requests.get(url, params=params, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {BOAT_API_KEY}"}, stream=True) as r:
        for line in r.iter_lines():
            if not line:
                continue
            f = json.loads(line)
            if f["type"] in ("stdout", "stderr"):
                getattr(sys, f["type"]).write(f["data"])
                offsets[f["type"]] = f["nextOffset"]
            elif f["type"] == "reconnect":
                offsets = {"stdout": f["stdoutOffset"], "stderr": f["stderrOffset"]}
            elif f["type"] in ("exit", "error"):
                done = True
```

Polling and attach both read the sandbox live. Thus the sandbox must run.

* A sandbox on an older agent answers `409 agent_outdated` until its next agent upgrade.
* To read output after the sandbox stops, use the [command history](/long-running-tasks/command-history).

## Stop a background command

Stop the command by its process id. This also stops every process that the command started.

1. boat sends `SIGTERM` to the whole process group.
2. After 5 seconds, boat sends `SIGKILL` to the processes that remain.
3. The response holds the [history record](/long-running-tasks/command-history) of the command, with status `killed` and its last output.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --kill "$pid"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/commands/1234" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"command.stopped","processId":1234,"running":false,"signaled":true,"command":{"commandId":"cmd_...","status":"killed",...}}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.stopCommand({ sandboxId, processId: started.processId });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.stop_command(sandbox_id, started.process_id)
```

## When the agent restarts

The process runs under the systemd user manager of the sandbox user. Thus a restart of the agent of the sandbox does not interrupt it. A platform upgrade is an example of such a restart.

The agent keeps a record of each process on disk. After a restart the status still shows the command, its directory and whether it runs:

* A process that ends before the restart keeps its `exitCode`.
* A process that runs during the restart shows `exited` with `exitCode` `null` when it ends.
* A process started by an agent older than the record shows `lost`, and `running` is a best-effort check.

Detached processes do not continue after a stop, resume or fork. For a process that must come back by itself, run it as an [always-on service](/long-running-tasks/always-on-services).

## Timeouts and retries

Synchronous commands accept `timeoutSeconds` from 1 to 600. The default is 30. boat refuses values outside that range with a 400 `invalid_timeout` error.

boat never retries a command call automatically. A command is not idempotent. After a timeout (`retryable: false`) or a network failure during the call, the command can already run on the sandbox. You decide what to do next.


# Command history and logs
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/long-running-tasks/command-history

Read the logs and output of past commands and processes in a sandbox, also when the sandbox is stopped, and list the processes.

boat keeps the output of the processes in a sandbox. You can read it while the sandbox is stopped. A sandbox created with [monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#monitoring-off) has no history.

In the dashboard, open the **⋯** menu of a sandbox and select **History**. A background command that runs shows its output live. You can stop it there.

## What boat keeps

| Source | Mode | Kept for |
| - | - | - |
| A command you run through `boat exec` or the commands endpoint | `sync`, `stream` or `detached` | 7 days |
| Any other process that writes output: an `ssh` session, a systemd service, a docker container, a process that an agent starts | `process` | 72 hours |

A detached command that still runs keeps its record. Its output older than 7 days is deleted.

The start answer of each command holds the `commandId` of its record.

| Kept | Details |
| - | - |
| The command | Its text (first 64 KiB), working directory, mode, process id |
| The result | `status` (`running`, `exited`, `timed_out`, `failed`, `killed`, `lost`), exit code, signal, start and end time |
| The output | stdout and stderr, compressed. A waiting command keeps up to 8 MiB per stream, the same as its answer. A streamed command adds output every 2 seconds. A detached command adds output every 30 seconds, and one more time when the sandbox stops. |

## Read the history

1. List the history.
2. Read the output of one command.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd
# cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw  exit 0      detached  2026-10-09 14:02:11  npm run build
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw            # stdout
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw --stderr
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw --follow   # until it ends
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd --mode commands              # only what you ran
boat history bx_f7k2q9hd --mode process               # only the other processes
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/command-history?limit=20&mode=commands" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"command.list","commands":[{"commandId":"cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw","status":"exited","exitCode":0,...}],"nextCursor":null}

curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/command-history/cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw/logs?stream=stdout&offset=0" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"command.logs","offset":0,"nextOffset":1830,"size":1830,"data":"...","done":true}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { commands } = await sandbox.commandHistory({ sandboxId, limit: 20, mode: "commands" });

let offset = 0;
for (;;) {
  const page = await sandbox.commandLogs({ sandboxId, commandId: commands[0].commandId, stream: "stdout", offset });
  process.stdout.write(page.data);
  offset = page.nextOffset;
  if (page.done) break;
  if (!page.data) await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000)); // still running
}
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import sys, time

page = sandbox.command_history(sandbox_id, limit=20, mode="commands")
command_id = page.commands[0].command_id

offset = 0
while True:
    logs = sandbox.command_logs(sandbox_id, command_id, stream="stdout", offset=offset)
    sys.stdout.write(logs.data)
    offset = logs.next_offset
    if logs.done:
        break
    if not logs.data:
        time.sleep(2)  # still running
```

* Each read gives at most 1 MiB.
* Read again from `nextOffset` until `done` is `true`.
* To get the exact bytes of binary output, pass `encoding=base64`.

> [!NOTE]
>
> An account keeps at most 10 MiB of compressed command output per hour. This is about 50 MiB of plain text. boat drops the output past that, and the command shows `outputTruncated: true`.

## Every process in the sandbox

boat records what each process writes to its terminal, to a pipe, or to a socket such as the journal. You do not change your programs for this. Each process is one `process` record, with its command line, its process id and its exit code.

| Rule | Details |
| - | - |
| Rate | Up to 64 KiB/s per process, with bursts up to 1 MiB. Output past that is dropped and the record shows `outputTruncated: true`. |
| Account cap | 10 MiB of compressed process output per hour, separate from the command cap. Output past that is dropped and the record shows `outputTruncated: true`. |
| Not recorded | Writes to regular files and to `/dev/null`, binary output, and the services that boat itself runs in the sandbox. |
| Delay | New output appears within about 30 seconds. Output still on the sandbox when it stops is saved before the stop. |

boat records a command that you run through `boat exec` one time, as a command. Its child processes do not show again as `process` records.

> [!TIP]
>
> A busy sandbox has many short processes, such as shell prompts and login scripts. To see only what you ran, use `--mode commands` (`mode=commands` in the API). To see only the other processes, use `--mode process`.

## Retention and deletion

The history is account data, the same as your sandbox files.

* When you delete the sandbox, boat deletes its history.
* With [zero data retention](/data-retention/zero-data-retention#enable-zero-data-retention), a stop queues the history for deletion with the rest of the sandbox.

## List processes

List every process in a sandbox, the busiest first.

A stopped sandbox answers with the last sample that boat kept, and `live: false`. boat takes the 12 busiest processes every 30 seconds and keeps them for 7 days.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ps bx_f7k2q9hd
#     PID    CPU%     MEM MB  USER        HISTORY           COMMAND
#    2210    98.0      812.4  user        cmd_k3v9x2mq7tbw  node build.js
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/$BOAT_ID/processes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"process.list","live":true,"total":64,"processes":[{"pid":2210,"user":"user","cpuPercent":98,"memoryMB":812.4,"command":"node build.js",...}]}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { live, processes } = await sandbox.processes({ sandboxId });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
listing = sandbox.processes(sandbox_id)
```

On a running sandbox, each process with a history record shows its `commandId` in the HISTORY column. To read its output, run `boat history <sandbox> <commandId>`.


# Sandbox sizes: CPU, memory, disk
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/machines

The four sandbox sizes with their vCPU, RAM, disk and price per hour, how to pick one, and what every sandbox can do: root, Docker, systemd, no GPU.

Pick a size with `--type` when you create a sandbox. Without `--type`, you get `default` (the medium size).

| Size | Per hour | CPU | RAM | Disk |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| `small` | **\$0.018** | 2 vCPU | 4 GB | 51 GB |
| `default` | **\$0.036** | 4 vCPU | 8 GB | 51 GB |
| `large` | **\$0.072** | 8 vCPU | 16 GB | 111 GB |
| `xlarge` \* | **\$0.200** | 16 vCPU | 32 GB | 251 GB |

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --type large
```

* `large` needs your first payment. The [free trial](/free-trial) cannot use it.
* \* `xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher. You do not need to contact us. Normal compute rates and account limits apply.
* These four sizes are the only sizes. boat has no custom size and no size above `xlarge`.
* "Disk" is the maximum size of your own files. The operating system and the pre-installed tools are not in it. Run `df -h /` in a sandbox to see the live figure.
* All sizes are x86_64. No size has a GPU.
* For sandboxes at once and start limits per plan, see [Limits and errors](/limits).
* The dashboard Sandboxes page shows the size of each sandbox in the **Type** column. Filter by size with **Type**. The API returns it as `type`.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new
boat new --type small
boat new --type large
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "https://boat.dev/api/v1/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type":"large","ttlSeconds":3600}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const created = await sandbox.create({ type: "large", ttlSeconds: 3600 });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_request import CreateSandboxRequest

created = sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(type="large", ttl_seconds=3600))
```

Stop, resume and fork keep the size. A fork gets the size of its source sandbox. To change the size, stop the sandbox, then resume it with `--type`. Read [Change size](/machines/change-size).

## What every sandbox has

Each sandbox is a full Linux virtual machine with its own kernel.

| | |
| - | - |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Linux 6.8, x86_64. Read [Base image and pre-installed tools](/machines/tools). |
| Root and sudo | The user is `user`. Passwordless `sudo` gives full root. |
| Services | Real `systemd`: services, timers, `journalctl` |
| Containers | Docker with BuildKit and Compose, on the sandbox's own kernel. `user` runs `docker` without `sudo`. |
| Network | Public IPv4 or IPv6 plus outbound internet. Expose ports with a [public URL](/hosting). |
| GPU | None. Graphics run on the CPU. The [desktop](/desktop-streaming) and headless Chrome work. |
| Nested virtualization | `/dev/kvm` on every sandbox. Read [Virtualization](/machines/virtualization). |

## Learn more

> [card] [Base image and pre-installed tools](/machines/tools)
>
> Languages, coding agents, Docker and utilities, with their versions.

> [card] [Change size](/machines/change-size)
>
> Stop the sandbox, then resume it with a bigger or smaller size.

> [card] [Virtualization](/machines/virtualization)
>
> Run KVM, Firecracker or the Android emulator in a sandbox.

> [card] [Fail fast when no machine is free](/machines/fail-fast)
>
> Get an answer in about 1.5 seconds when no machine of your size is ready.
