# Change size
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/machines/change-size

Move a sandbox to a bigger or smaller size: stop it, then resume it with --type. Or fork it to a new size.

A running sandbox cannot change size. Stop it first, then resume it with the new size.

1. Stop the sandbox:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat stop bx_23456789
   ```

2. Wait until `boat info bx_23456789` shows the state `stopped`. The API reports a stopped sandbox as `archived`.

3. Resume it with the new size:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat resume bx_23456789 --type large
   ```

A resume with `--type` on a running sandbox fails with `409 sandbox_running_stop_first`. Nothing changes.

To get a copy at a new size and keep the source running, fork it:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat fork bx_23456789 --type small
```

| Command | What changes |
| - | - |
| `resume --type` | The stopped sandbox itself gets the new size. |
| `fork --type` | The copy gets the new size. The source sandbox does not change. |

Resume and fork already restore a snapshot onto a new machine. So a size change costs nothing more than the resume or fork itself.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat stop   bx_23456789
until [ "$(boat info bx_23456789 --json | jq -r .sandbox.state)" = "stopped" ]; do sleep 2; done
boat resume bx_23456789 --type large
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST https://boat.dev/api/v1/sandboxes/bx_23456789/stop \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# poll GET /sandboxes/bx_23456789 until state is "archived", then:
curl -sS -X POST https://boat.dev/api/v1/sandboxes/bx_23456789/resume \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type":"large"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.stop({ sandboxId: "bx_23456789" });
// poll sandbox.get({ sandboxId }) until state is "archived", then:
await sandbox.resume({ sandboxId: "bx_23456789", type: "large" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.resume_request import ResumeRequest

sandbox.stop("bx_23456789")
# poll sandbox.get("bx_23456789") until state is "archived", then:
sandbox.resume("bx_23456789", resume_request=ResumeRequest(type="large"))
```

## Grow and shrink

* A move to a bigger size always works.
* `large` needs your first payment. `xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher.
* A move to a smaller size fails with `type_too_small` when the sandbox holds more data than the smaller size can take.
* After a refused move, the sandbox stays exactly as it was. You do not lose the sandbox.
* To shrink past that limit, delete data. Then let the sandbox make a new snapshot, and try again.

## Cost

A bigger size costs more per hour. The price per hour in [Sandbox sizes](/machines) is the full price.


# Fail fast when no machine is free
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/machines/fail-fast

Get an answer in about 1.5 seconds when no machine of your size is ready, and fall back right away. About machine availability, not setup failures.

> [!NOTE]
>
> This page is about machine availability. To stop when your setup script fails, read [Fail when setup fails](/setup#fail-when-setup-fails).

These four calls put the sandbox on a machine that is already running and waiting:

* Create a sandbox.
* Deploy from a saved snapshot.
* Fork.
* Resume.

They usually get a machine in less than one second. A burst can use all the ready machines of one size. Then the next calls wait while boat builds new machines.

## Use fail fast

If you prefer to fall back to something else instead of waiting, pass `failFast` to any of these calls. The call then answers in about 1.5 seconds with one of two results:

| Result | What it means |
| - | - |
| `202` | The usual answer. The sandbox is on a machine that was ready. |
| `503` `no_ready_machine` | Nothing started. See below. |

When you get `503` `no_ready_machine`:

* boat does not create a sandbox or a fork. A resumed sandbox stays stopped.
* You pay nothing.
* The attempt does not count against your [start limits](/limits).
* Retry, or fall back, immediately.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --fail-fast --type large
boat new --fail-fast --from ci-runner
boat fork --fail-fast bx_23456789
boat resume --fail-fast bx_23456789
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "https://boat.dev/api/v1/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"failFast":true,"from":"ci-runner"}'
# same field on POST /sandboxes/{id}/fork and /sandboxes/{id}/resume
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
try {
  const created = await sandbox.create({ failFast: true, from: "ci-runner" });
  // also: sandbox.fork({ sandboxId, failFast: true }), sandbox.resume({ sandboxId, failFast: true })
} catch (error) {
  // 503 no_ready_machine: nothing was started; fall back or retry.
}
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.exceptions import ApiException
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_request import CreateSandboxRequest

try:
    created = sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(fail_fast=True, var_from="ci-runner"))
except ApiException as error:
    # 503 no_ready_machine: nothing was started; fall back or retry.
    pass
```


# Base image and pre-installed tools
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/machines/tools

The OS image of every sandbox and the versions of its languages, Docker, coding agents and utilities. Root access and how to install more.

Every sandbox starts from the same base image: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, Linux 6.8, x86_64. The tools below are ready when you first connect.

## Root and sudo

* You work as the user `user`, in `/home/user`.
* Passwordless `sudo` gives full root. Install more with `sudo apt-get install -y <package>`.
* To keep what you install for new sandboxes, save a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates). Read [Environment, setup script or saved snapshot?](/environments/choose).

Versions measured on a new sandbox on 2026-10-13. Run `<tool> --version` in your sandbox for the live value.

| `pnpm` | 10.34.5 | |

| `kotlin` / `kotlinc` | 2.1.0 | |

## Docker

| Tool | Version |
| - | - |
| `docker` | Docker 29.7.0 with BuildKit |
| `docker compose` | Compose 5.3.1 |

* `user` runs `docker` without `sudo`.
* Docker can start a few seconds after the sandbox is `ready`. Wait for it in scripts: `until docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done`.
* The layer cache is per machine. Read [Docker builds across resume and fork](/snapshots/whats-saved#docker-builds).

## Coding agents

boat updates these to their latest release when it prepares each machine. Run `<tool> --version` for the exact version.

| Tool | Description |
| - | - |
| `claude` | Claude Code CLI |
| `codex` | OpenAI Codex CLI |
| `pi` | Pi coding agent ([pi.dev](https://pi.dev)) |
| `opencode` | OpenCode terminal coding agent |
| `hermes` | Hermes Agent by Nous Research. Browser tools are not pre-installed: `hermes` offers to add them. |
| `openclaw` | OpenClaw CLI. The gateway does not start by itself: run `openclaw gateway`. |
| `agent` / `cursor-agent` | Cursor CLI agent |
| `prime-agent` | Prime Intellect's Prime Agent |
| `kimi` | Kimi Code CLI by Moonshot AI |
| `vibe` | Mistral Vibe by Mistral AI (`--provider mistral`) |
| `host` | Expose localhost services to the internet |
| `lux` | Desktop and browser automation with demo recording |
| `boat` | boat CLI inside the sandbox |

* These tools are installed system-wide, in `/usr/local` and `/opt`.
* They take no space in your snapshots. They come back after a stop and resume.
* Each harness signs in with its own `login` command.
* `boat prompt` and the Agents & Proxying tab drive seven of them. Read [Harnesses and models](/integrated-agents/harnesses-and-models).
* You can install your own copy, for example with `npm i -g` or the vendor installer into `~/.local/bin`. Your copy hides the pre-installed one. Your snapshots keep it as usual.

| Tool | Version |

| `gh` | 2.97.0 |

| Tool | Version |

| Setting | Value | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| `LANG` and `LC_ALL` | `en_US.UTF-8` | `sort` orders lines differently from a `C.UTF-8` machine. To match one, set `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` in your job. |
| `git` | 2.43 | If your CI actions need a newer version, install it. |


# Virtualization: KVM, Firecracker, Android
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/machines/virtualization

Nested virtualization in a sandbox: every sandbox has /dev/kvm, so QEMU/KVM, Firecracker and the Android emulator run at full speed.

Every sandbox has nested virtualization. `/dev/kvm` is there, so QEMU/KVM, Firecracker and the Android emulator run at full speed. You do not need a flag or a permission.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec <id> 'test -e /dev/kvm && echo "KVM available"'
```

## Where your sandbox runs

Every sandbox runs as a full virtual machine on a physical host dedicated to boat. The fleet includes AMD Ryzen 7 9700X and Ryzen 9 9950X hosts. Sandboxes on the same host share CPU time. A sandbox's vCPUs are not dedicated physical cores. CPU virtualization extensions are passed through, and each sandbox has its own kernel.

## Run the Android emulator

This script runs a headless Android emulator. Use `default` or bigger: the emulator needs about 3 GB of RAM. We tested it on a `large` sandbox.

* The install takes about one minute.
* Android 14 then boots in 20 to 30 seconds.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sudo apt-get install -y openjdk-17-jre-headless
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-17-openjdk-amd64 ANDROID_HOME=$HOME/android
mkdir -p $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools && cd /tmp
curl -fsSLo clt.zip https://dl.google.com/android/repository/commandlinetools-linux-11076708_latest.zip
unzip -q clt.zip -d $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools && mv $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/cmdline-tools $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest
SDK=$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin
yes | $SDK/sdkmanager --licenses >/dev/null
$SDK/sdkmanager "platform-tools" "emulator" "system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64"
echo no | $SDK/avdmanager create avd -n phone -k "system-images;android-34;google_apis;x86_64" -d pixel_6
if [ ! -e /dev/kvm ]; then
  echo "No KVM on this sandbox: the Android emulator cannot start here." >&2
else
  $ANDROID_HOME/emulator/emulator -avd phone -no-window -no-audio -gpu swiftshader_indirect &
  $ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools/adb wait-for-device
fi
```

To take a screenshot, run `adb exec-out screencap -p > screen.png`.


# Migrating from Box
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/migrating-from-box

Box is now boat, and a box is now a sandbox. Old Box API paths, keys, CLI, SDK packages and hosted URLs still work. What to change and how to know you are done.

Box became **boat** on September 15, 2026. The product, the account, the machines and the data stay the same. Two words replace the word "box":

| Word | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **boat** | The product: the site, the CLI, the API, your account and your plan. |
| **sandbox** | What you create in boat. It was a "box" before. Paths, keys, events and error codes say `sandbox`. |

Your existing Box endpoints, CLI integrations, SDK packages, environment variables and hosted URLs still work. boat has not decided the retirement policy yet. The Sunset header is a migration warning only. It is not a shutdown that boat has implemented. It is also not a promise of permanent support.

## Timeline

| Date | What happens |
| - | - |
| **2026-09-15** | boat ships. Box surfaces keep working. They now answer with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers. The `box` CLI prints a reminder at each run. |
| **2026-10-31** | The Sunset date that boat shows now. boat has not decided if or when legacy endpoints, binaries, packages or hosted URLs retire. The rename adds no shutdown on a date. |

## The rename in one table

| | Box (legacy compatibility) | boat |
| - | - | - |
| Dashboard | `box.ascii.dev/box/dashboard` | [`boat.dev/dashboard`](https://boat.dev/dashboard) |
| Docs | `docs.ascii.dev/box/<page>` | `docs.boat.dev/<page>` (every old URL redirects) |
| API base | `https://ascii.dev/api/box/v1` | `https://boat.dev/api/v1` |
| Resource paths | `/boxes/{boxId}` | `/sandboxes/{sandboxId}` |
| JSON keys | 14 keys, every one listed in [Every renamed name](/migrating-from-box/renamed-names#json-keys) | the same 14 with `sandbox` in place of `box` |
| Envelope `type` | 13 values, [all listed](/migrating-from-box/renamed-names#envelope-type-values) | `sandbox.` in place of `box.` |
| Error codes | 17 codes, [all listed](/migrating-from-box/renamed-names#error-code-values) | `sandbox_` in place of `box_` |
| Webhook events | 6 events: `box.ready`, `box.error`, `box.archived`, `box.hydrated`, `box.degraded`, `box.recovered` | `sandbox.` in place of `box.` |
| API keys | `box_...` | `boat_...` (keys you already have stay valid) |
| Org header | `X-Box-Org` | `X-Boat-Org` |
| CLI | `box`, `box-dev` | `boat`, `boat-dev` |
| CLI env vars | 20 variables, [all listed](/migrating-from-box/renamed-names#cli-environment-variables) | `BOAT_` in place of `BOX_` |
| CLI config | `~/.config/ascii/box/config.json` | `~/.config/ascii/boat/config.json` |
| Snapshot ignore file | `.boxignore` | `.boatignore` |
| Hosted URLs | `https://<label>.on.ascii.dev` | `https://<label>.on.boat.dev` (same route, same token, both answer) |
| Inside a sandbox | `box` CLI, `BOX_ID`, `BOX_CURRENT_ID` | `boat` CLI, `BOAT_ID`, `BOAT_CURRENT_ID` (both spellings exported) |
| Python SDK | `ascii-box-sdk` / `ascii_box_sdk` | `boat-sdk` / `boat_sdk` |
| TypeScript SDK | `@asciidev/box-sdk` | `@boatdev/sdk` |
| Other languages | `ascii_box_sdk`, `github.com/ascii-dev/box-go-sdk` | No boat package yet. Generate a client from [`/openapi/boat-v1.yaml`](/openapi/boat-v1.yaml). |
| Integrations | `harbor-box`, `@asciidev/eve-box` | Same packages. They still call the Box API. See [Harbor](/integrations/harbor) and [Eve](/integrations/eve). |

These items do not change:

* IDs (`bx_...`) and snapshot IDs.
* The `X-Ascii-*` headers (`X-Ascii-Confirm-Delete` and the webhook headers) and `Idempotency-Key`. They are the current names.
* `sandboxId` on API keys. It already said sandbox.
* All of your data.

## Am I done?

Check each item:

* Your API client logs show no `Sunset` header.
* Your scripts do not call a `box` binary. The reminder line no longer shows.
* `pip show ascii-box-sdk` and `npm ls @asciidev/box-sdk` return nothing.
* `GET /api/v1/webhooks` lists webhooks with `sandbox.*` events.
* Your published links say `on.boat.dev`.

## Retirement policy

boat currently keeps these legacy items:

* The legacy API routes.
* The binary and environment aliases.
* The hosted addresses.

The October 31 header does not cause a `410 Gone`. It does not disable installed clients. It does not remove DNS. boat must still make an explicit policy decision on the scope and time of a future retirement. This guide does not promise a shutdown on that date. It also does not promise permanent support.

Questions: see [Support](/support).

## Learn more

> [card] [Migration steps](/migrating-from-box/steps)
>
> What to change in the CLI, the SDKs, raw HTTP, webhooks, hosted URLs and inside a sandbox.

> [card] [Every renamed name](/migrating-from-box/renamed-names)
>

# Every renamed name
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/migrating-from-box/renamed-names

This is the full list, read from the API specifications and the CLI source. It is not a sample. A name that is not in these tables did not change.

# Migration steps
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/migrating-from-box/steps

What to change to move from Box to boat: the CLI, the SDKs, raw HTTP, webhooks, hosted URLs and the inside of a sandbox.

Do the steps that apply to you. For the full list of renamed names, read [Every renamed name](/migrating-from-box/renamed-names).

## 1. CLI

Install the `boat` CLI:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -fsSL https://boat.dev/install | sh      # macOS, Linux
irm https://boat.dev/install.ps1 | iex        # Windows
```

You stay signed in. `boat` reads the config that `box` wrote. Then do these steps:

1. In scripts and CI, replace `box` with `boat`. Subcommands do not change: `boat new`, `boat list`, `boat ssh`.
2. Rename `BOX_*` variables to `BOAT_*`. Now, if a `BOAT_*` variable is not set, boat uses its `BOX_*` twin. It then prints a one-line notice on stderr.
3. Rename `.boxignore` files to `.boatignore`. boat reads both files now. If a directory has both, `.boatignore` wins.
4. Change `boat api-key create --box bx_1` to `--sandbox bx_1`.

The final compatibility release of `box` prints a migration reminder. Use `boat` to get later updates. No date check disables legacy binaries.

## 2. SDKs

Replace the package:

```bash Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
pip uninstall ascii-box-sdk
pip install boat-sdk
```

```bash TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
npm uninstall @asciidev/box-sdk
npm install @boatdev/sdk
```

Then change your code:

| What | Box | boat |
| - | - | - |
| Import | `ascii_box_sdk`, `@asciidev/box-sdk` | `boat_sdk`, `@boatdev/sdk` |
| Base URL | `https://ascii.dev/api/box/v1` | `https://boat.dev/api/v1` |
| Client class (keeps the product name) | `BoxApi` (`ascii_box_sdk.api.box_api`) | `BoatApi` (`boat_sdk.api.boat_api`) |
| Request and response types (say sandbox) | `CreateBoxRequest`, `Box`, `boxId`, `.box`, `.boxes`, `deleteBox` | `CreateSandboxRequest`, `Sandbox`, `sandboxId`, `.sandbox`, `.sandboxes`, `deleteSandbox` |

The helpers keep their names:

| SDK | Helpers |
| - | - |
| Python | `wait_until_ready`, `wait_until_idle`, `wait_for_desktop`, `wait_for_prompt`, `wait_for_prompt_done`, `stream_events`, `stream_prompt`, `stop_and_remove`, `read_text`, `write_text`, `exec_command`, `stream_command` |
| TypeScript | `waitUntilReady`, `waitUntilIdle`, `waitForDesktop`, `waitForPrompt`, `waitForPromptDone`, `streamEvents`, `streamPrompt`, `stopAndRemove`, `readText`, `writeText`, `execCommand`, `streamCommand` |

In Python, pass the request body by keyword: `boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(...))`. See [Python SDK](/sdks/python).

To change the types and keys, do a whole-word search and replace:

| Find | Replace with |
| - | - |
| `box` | `sandbox` |
| `Box` | `Sandbox` |
| `boxes` | `sandboxes` |
| `Boxes` | `Sandboxes` |

Then make two changes by hand: the package import, and `BoxApi` to `BoatApi`.

## 3. Raw HTTP

```diff theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
- POST https://ascii.dev/api/box/v1/boxes
+ POST https://boat.dev/api/v1/sandboxes
- Authorization: Bearer box_...      (still accepted)
+ Authorization: Bearer boat_...     (what new keys look like)
```

Responses use the new words: `sandbox` / `sandboxes` / `sandboxId`, `type: "sandbox.created"`, `code: "sandbox_not_found"`. Request bodies also use the new keys, for example `passSandboxCredentials` and `sourceSandboxId`.

A request to `/api/box/*` answers in box words now. It has these headers:

```http theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
Deprecation: @1789430400
Sunset: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 00:00:00 GMT
Link: <https://docs.boat.dev/migrating-from-box>; rel="deprecation"
```

If your client logs response headers, search the logs for `Sunset`. Each match is a call that you did not move yet.

## 4. Webhooks

Webhooks that you created before the rename still send `box.*` events with payloads that say `box`. Signatures, headers and retries do not change.

To move a webhook:

1. Create it again through the boat API, or with `boat webhook create`.
2. Delete the old webhook.

The new webhook sends `sandbox.*` events and `X-Ascii-Event: sandbox.ready`. There are 6 events: `ready`, `error`, `archived` (stopped), `hydrated`, `degraded` and `recovered`.

## 5. Hosted URLs

Each hosted route answers on two addresses, with the same `_token`:

* `https://<label>.on.ascii.dev`
* `https://<label>.on.boat.dev`

Update the links that you published or embedded to the `on.boat.dev` form. boat has not decided the retirement policy for the `on.ascii.dev` form.

## 6. Inside a sandbox

* The `boat` CLI is on the PATH of each sandbox. `box` still points to it.
* boat exports `BOAT_ID`, `BOAT_CURRENT_ID` and `BOAT_CLI_*` next to their `BOX_*` twins.
* Agent skills use the `boat` skill. boat removes a `box` skill directory at the next start.


# OpenTelemetry
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/opentelemetry

Send sandbox and account metrics, and sandbox lifecycle events, to Datadog, Grafana Cloud, Honeycomb, or any OTLP collector. No traces, no agent or AI token data.

boat pushes your account's telemetry to one OTLP/HTTP endpoint that you choose. You do not install an agent in your sandboxes.

| Signal | Path | When |
| - | - | - |
| Sandbox and account metrics | `<endpoint>/v1/metrics` | Every 60 seconds |
| Sandbox lifecycle events, as OTLP log records | `<endpoint>/v1/logs` | When each event occurs |

boat does not send these:

| Not sent | Where to read it instead |
| - | - |
| Traces and spans | None. boat sends no traces. |
| Agent prompts, responses and tool calls | [Agent events](/integrated-agents/conversations#stream-events) |
| AI token usage | [`boat ai usage`](/ai-credentials#usage), for proxied sandboxes |
| The output of commands and processes | [Command history and logs](/long-running-tasks/command-history) |

To export telemetry from your own app in a sandbox, run your own OpenTelemetry SDK or collector in the sandbox.

| | CLI | API | SDKs |
| - | - | - | - |
| Set or replace | `boat telemetry set <endpoint> -H key=value` | `PUT /telemetry` | `setTelemetry` |
| Read status | `boat telemetry` | `GET /telemetry` | `getTelemetry` |
| Remove | `boat telemetry unset` | `DELETE /telemetry` | `deleteTelemetry` |

An account has one endpoint. The headers hold your vendor credentials. So the API needs a key with `account.admin`.

## Set the endpoint

Use the **Webhooks & OTel** tab in the dashboard. You can also use the CLI, the API or an SDK.

1. Give the base URL of the collector. boat adds `/v1/metrics` and `/v1/logs`.
2. Give the headers that your vendor needs. Read [Vendor settings](#vendor-settings).

If you paste a URL that ends in `/v1/metrics`, boat removes that part.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat telemetry set https://otlp.datadoghq.com -H dd-api-key=$DD_API_KEY
# https://otlp.datadoghq.com
#   headers      dd-api-key
#   last export  -
# Saved. Test export accepted.
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/telemetry" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"endpoint":"https://otlp.datadoghq.com","headers":{"dd-api-key":"'"$DD_API_KEY"'"}}'
# {"type":"telemetry.updated","telemetry":{"endpoint":"https://otlp.datadoghq.com","headers":["dd-api-key"],...},"test":{"ok":true,"status":202,"message":null}}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const saved = await sandbox.setTelemetry({
  endpoint: "https://otlp.datadoghq.com",
  headers: { "dd-api-key": process.env.DD_API_KEY! },
});
console.log(saved.test.ok, saved.test.status);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os
from boat_sdk.models.telemetry_set_request import TelemetrySetRequest

saved = sandbox.set_telemetry(TelemetrySetRequest(
    endpoint="https://otlp.datadoghq.com",
    headers={"dd-api-key": os.environ["DD_API_KEY"]},
))
print(saved.test.ok, saved.test.status)
```

When you save, boat sends one empty metrics export immediately. boat returns the answer of the collector in `test`. So you see a wrong key or endpoint before you wait for data. The first metrics arrive within 60 seconds.

> [!NOTE]
>
> * The endpoint must use HTTPS on port 443 or 4318.
> * The endpoint must resolve only to public addresses.
> * boat encrypts the header values at rest and never returns them.
> * You can set up to 20 headers.

### Vendor settings

| Vendor | Endpoint | Headers |
| - | - | - |
| Datadog | `https://otlp.datadoghq.com` (use the OTLP host of your Datadog site) | `dd-api-key=<API key>` |
| Grafana Cloud | The OTLP endpoint on your stack's OpenTelemetry card, for example `https://otlp-gateway-prod-eu-west-2.grafana.net/otlp` | `Authorization=Basic <base64 of instanceId:token>` |
| Honeycomb | `https://api.honeycomb.io` (EU: `https://api.eu1.honeycomb.io`) | `x-honeycomb-team=<API key>`, `x-honeycomb-dataset=boat` |
| Your own OpenTelemetry Collector | `https://otel.example.com` (port 443 or 4318) | The auth header that your collector checks |

For Grafana Cloud, make the header value like this:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
echo -n "$GRAFANA_INSTANCE_ID:$GRAFANA_TOKEN" | base64
```

### Your own collector and Prometheus

1. Run the OpenTelemetry Collector with an OTLP/HTTP receiver behind TLS.
2. Export to Prometheus with remote write, or expose a scrape endpoint:

```yaml otelcol.yaml theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318
exporters:
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
  debug: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    metrics: { receivers: [otlp], exporters: [prometheus] }
    logs: { receivers: [otlp], exporters: [debug] }
```

Prometheus turns `boat.sandbox.cpu.utilization` into `boat_sandbox_cpu_utilization`, with `boat_sandbox_id` and `boat_sandbox_name` labels.

## Metrics

* All metrics are gauges.
* Every point has `boat.sandbox.id` and `boat.sandbox.name`. So each sandbox is its own series in every vendor.
* A sandbox with [monitoring off](/data-retention/snapshots-and-monitoring-off#monitoring-off) sends no sandbox metrics. boat still sends its lifecycle events.

| Metric | Unit | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `boat.sandbox.cpu.utilization` | `1` | Share of CPU time busy, 0 to 1 |
| `boat.sandbox.memory.utilization` | `1` | Share of memory in use, 0 to 1 |
| `boat.sandbox.memory.usage` | `By` | Memory in use |
| `boat.sandbox.filesystem.utilization` | `1` | Share of the disk in use, 0 to 1 |
| `boat.sandbox.filesystem.usage` | `By` | Disk space in use |
| `boat.sandbox.io.pressure` | `1` | Share of time stalled on disk I/O, 0 to 1 |
| `boat.account.sandboxes.active` | `{sandbox}` | Sandboxes running now |
| `boat.account.sandboxes.limit` | `{sandbox}` | Sandboxes your plan lets run at once. Not sent on unlimited plans. |
| `boat.account.credit.balance` | `s` | Machine time left on the account. Not sent on unlimited plans. |

Each sandbox is one resource:

| Resource attribute | Value |
| - | - |
| `service.name` | `boat` |
| `service.instance.id`, `boat.sandbox.id` | The sandbox id |
| `boat.sandbox.name` | The sandbox name |
| `boat.sandbox.size` | The machine size |
| `boat.sandbox.memory.size`, `boat.sandbox.disk.size` | Total memory and disk, in bytes |
| `boat.account.id` | Your account id |

A sandbox sends points only while it runs. Each export holds the samples taken since the previous one.

## Events

Each [lifecycle event](/webhooks#events) is one OTLP log record. boat puts the event name in two places: the event name field of the record, and the `event.name` attribute.

| Event name | Severity |
| - | - |
| `sandbox.ready` | `INFO` |
| `sandbox.hydrated` | `INFO` |
| `sandbox.error` | `ERROR` |
| `sandbox.archived` | `INFO` |
| `sandbox.degraded` | `WARN` |
| `sandbox.recovered` | `INFO` |

Each record has these attributes:

| Attribute | Value |
| - | - |
| `boat.sandbox.id`, `boat.sandbox.name` | The sandbox |
| `boat.sandbox.state`, `boat.sandbox.previous_state` | The new and the old state, when the event has them |
| `boat.sandbox.reason` | Why, for `sandbox.degraded` and `sandbox.recovered` |
| `boat.event.id` | The same id as the webhook event. Use it to remove duplicates. |

## Delivery and errors

| Collector answer | What boat does |
| - | - |
| `2xx` | Done. A partial-success answer shows its message in `lastError`. |
| `429`, `502`, `503`, `504`, or no answer | Sends the same data again later. boat waits for `Retry-After` when the collector sends it. |
| Any other `4xx` or `5xx` | Drops that data and shows the error in `lastError`. Fix the key or the endpoint. boat sends the next window as usual. |

* boat sends metrics in time order.
* After an outage, boat sends at most the last 10 minutes of metrics.
* boat retries an event like a [webhook delivery](/webhooks#delivery-and-retries), up to 8 attempts.

To read the status, run:

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat telemetry
# https://otlp.datadoghq.com
#   headers      dd-api-key
#   last export  2026-10-09T12:00:10.000Z
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/telemetry" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# {"type":"telemetry.info","telemetry":{"endpoint":"...","headers":["dd-api-key"],"lastExportAt":"...","lastError":null,...}}
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { telemetry } = await sandbox.getTelemetry();
console.log(telemetry?.lastExportAt, telemetry?.lastError);
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
status = sandbox.get_telemetry()
print(status.telemetry.last_export_at if status.telemetry else None)
```

## Remove the endpoint

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat telemetry unset
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/telemetry" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.deleteTelemetry();
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.delete_telemetry()
```

boat stops the export. boat deletes the queued data immediately.

## Related

* [Webhooks](/webhooks): the same lifecycle events, signed, to your own HTTPS endpoint.
* [Command history and logs](/long-running-tasks/command-history): the output of the processes in a sandbox.


# Teams and organizations
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/organizations

One shared plan and wallet for a team: members and invites, seat price, which wallet a sandbox bills, shared sandboxes, per-member caps, and moving a plan between personal and organization.

To work as a team on boat, create an **organization**. It has one plan, one wallet, and members who run sandboxes on it.

* The organization pays the plan price once per seat. A 5-seat organization on the \$20 plan pays \$100 a month.
* Each seat adds the plan's included time. It adds the full limits on the \$2000 plan, and 20% of them below. Read [Seats, limits and caps](/organizations/seats-and-limits).
* Organizations get no free trial.
* The API and the CLI also call an organization `org`, and some fields call it `team` (`teamId`, `team_…` ids). All three name the same thing.

| What | Who sees or uses it |
| - | - |
| Sandboxes the organization pays for | Every member sees them all. |
| Shared sandboxes | Every member can use them. A sandbox is shared when it holds no personal logins and its creator did not make it private. |
| Snapshots and personal environments | Only the person who made them. |
| Organization environments and credential profiles | Every member uses them, unless an owner or admin [limits who can use them](#limit-who-can-use-an-environment-or-profile). Owners change them. See [Shared sandboxes](/organizations/shared-sandboxes#shared-environments-and-ai-credentials). |

For everyone who can reach a sandbox, in and out of the team, read [Security and isolation](/security#who-can-reach-a-sandbox).

## Members and invites

The owner invites people by email.

1. The person opens the link in the email.
2. The person signs in with any sign-in method.
3. The organization shows in their `boat org list` and in the **Viewing** dropdown of the dashboard.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat org create acme                 # you become its owner
boat org switch acme
boat org invite dana@example.com     # owner only
boat org members                     # members and pending invites
boat org transfer dana               # make dana the owner; you become a member
```

To remove a member, change roles or set per-member caps, use the [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=org) tab of the dashboard. When a member leaves, the sandboxes that they created go back to their personal billing.

## Rename an organization

Only the owner can rename the organization.

1. Open the [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=org) tab and select the organization in the sidebar.
2. Select **Rename**, type the new name, and select **Save**.
3. Read the warning and select **Rename** to confirm.

The id (`team_…`) does not change. After the rename, `--org`, `?org=` and `X-Boat-Org` accept the new name only. Update the scripts that use the old name, or use the id.

New invoices show the new name when the billing name is still the organization name. A billing name that you entered at checkout does not change. Invoices that already exist keep their name.

## Limit who can use an environment or profile

By default, every member can use each organization environment and each organization credential profile. An owner or admin can limit an environment to a list of members. An owner can do the same for a profile.

| Setting | Who can use it |
| - | - |
| Everyone (default) | Every member of the organization |
| Only listed members | Owners, admins and the listed members |

A member who is not on the list:

* Does not see the environment or the profile in lists.
* Cannot create, resume or fork a sandbox in the environment. boat returns `403 environment_forbidden`.
* Cannot pick the profile. When an environment that they can use names the profile, their sandboxes get their own default profile.

Other rules:

* An API key acts as the person who created it. It never reaches more than that person can. The environment scope of a key limits it more.
* A change to the list does not change sandboxes that are already running.
* Teammates already cannot use a sandbox that holds another person's secrets. Read [Shared sandboxes](/organizations/shared-sandboxes).

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env access agents --org acme                          # show the list
boat env access agents --org acme --only a@x.com,b@y.com   # only these members
boat env access agents --org acme --add c@z.com
boat env access agents --org acme --remove a@x.com
boat env access agents --org acme --everyone               # back to every member
boat ai profile access team-claude --only a@x.com          # same flags for a profile
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID?org=acme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"access":{"restricted":true,"members":["a@x.com","b@y.com"]}}'

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles/$PROFILE_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"access":{"restricted":false,"members":[]}}'
```

* `members` takes member ids or the emails of active members. It replaces the full list.
* The environment and the profile objects return `access: { restricted, members }`, with member ids.
* A bad list returns `400 invalid_access`.

On the dashboard, open the environment page or the AI credentials page. The **Who can use this environment** or **Who can use this profile** panel has two choices: **Everyone in \<org>** or **Only the people ticked below**.

## Where to do what

| | CLI | API | SDKs | Dashboard |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| See your organizations | `boat org list` | `GET /orgs` | `listOrganizations` | **Viewing** dropdown |
| Set the active wallet | `boat org switch <org>` | `PATCH /orgs/active` | `setActiveOrganization` | sidebar **CLI and API keys bill … Change** |
| Bill one sandbox elsewhere | `boat --org acme new` | `org` on `POST /sandboxes`, or `X-Boat-Org` | `org` on `create` | select the organization in the sidebar |
| Create, transfer, delete | `boat org create` / `transfer` / `delete` | account API \* | not available | [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=org) |
| Rename (owner) | not available | `PATCH /orgs/{org}` with `name` | `updateOrganization` | [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=org), **Rename** |
| Members and invites | `boat org members` / `boat org invite` | account API \* | not available | [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=org) |
| Remove members, caps | not available | account API \* | not available | [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=org) |
| Seats | not available | account API \* | not available | [Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) viewing the org |
| See, share and unshare team sandboxes | `boat list` / `boat share` / `boat unshare` | `GET /sandboxes` / `POST /sandboxes/{id}/share` / `POST /sandboxes/{id}/unshare` | `sandboxes` / `share` / `unshare` | [Sandboxes](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=sandboxes), row menu |
| Start new sandboxes shared or private | `boat org default-visibility` | `PATCH /orgs/{org}` | `updateOrganization` | [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=team) |
| Org plan, wallet, auto top-up | `boat --org acme billing …` / `boat --org acme wallet …` | account API \* | not available | [Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) viewing the org |

\* The account API is the one that the dashboard uses. Its base is `https://boat.dev/api/boat`, not `$BOAT_API_BASE`. Organization routes are under `/teams/{org}/…` and billing routes under `/billing/…` with `teamId` in the body. These routes are not in the [v1 API reference](/api/v1) and can change.

The plan, the wallet and running out work the same on an organization as on a personal account. Read [Plan, wallet and running out](/billing).

## Learn more

> [card] [Which wallet a sandbox bills](/organizations/active-wallet)
>
> Set the active wallet, or bill one sandbox to another wallet.

> [card] [Shared sandboxes](/organizations/shared-sandboxes)
>
> What each member can do with a sandbox. Share a sandbox or make it private.

> [card] [Seats, limits and caps](/organizations/seats-and-limits)
>
> Buy seats, share start and concurrency limits, and cap each member.

> [card] [Move a personal plan in](/organizations/move-personal-plan)
>
> Move your personal sandboxes and plan to the organization.

> [card] [Card, invoices and plan changes](/billing/plan-changes)
>
> Cancel, downgrade, refunds, and move an organization plan back to personal.


# Which wallet a sandbox bills
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/organizations/active-wallet

Who pays for a sandbox: your personal account or an organization. Switch the active organization, or bill one sandbox to an organization without switching.

The **wallet** of a sandbox is the account that pays for it: your personal account or an organization.

Each wallet has its own plan and its own dollar balance for overage. Read [Plan, wallet and running out](/billing).

Every account has one **active wallet**. It is your personal account until you change it.

* A new sandbox bills the wallet that the request names.
* A request that names no wallet bills the active wallet.
* The active wallet is one setting on the account. The CLI and account API keys use it.
* The dashboard does not use it. The dashboard bills the organization selected in the sidebar.
* An organization API key always bills its own organization.
* `GET /limits` reads the wallet that a create would bill.
* boat fixes the wallet of a sandbox when it creates the sandbox.

## Name an organization

| Value | Means |
| - | - |
| The id (`team_…`) | That organization. |
| The name, as `GET /orgs` / `boat org list` show it | That organization. Case does not matter. |
| `personal` | Your own account. |

You need the id only when two organizations have the same name. Then a name gives `409 ambiguous_org`.

## Set or override the wallet

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat org                     # the wallet in effect right now
boat org list                # organizations you belong to, ids and names
boat org switch acme         # active wallet = acme, for the CLI and account API keys
boat org switch personal     # back to your own account
boat --org acme new          # bill one create to acme without switching
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/orgs" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# -> orgs: [{ id, name, type, role, active }, ...]

curl -sS -X PATCH "$BOAT_API_BASE/orgs/active" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "org": "acme" }'                  # or the team_… id, or "personal"

# one call elsewhere: header, query, or body
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" -H "X-Boat-Org: acme" ...
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/limits?org=acme" ...
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" -d '{ "org": "acme" }' ...
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { orgs } = await boat.listOrganizations();          // ids, names, active
await boat.setActiveOrganization({ org: "acme" });
await boat.create({ org: "acme" }); // one sandbox elsewhere
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.active_org_update_request import ActiveOrgUpdateRequest
from boat_sdk.models.create_sandbox_request import CreateSandboxRequest

orgs = boat.list_organizations().orgs                     # ids, names, active
boat.set_active_organization(ActiveOrgUpdateRequest(org="acme"))
boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(org="acme"))  # one sandbox elsewhere
```

## In the dashboard

| Control | What it does |
| - | - |
| **Organization** select in the sidebar | Picks the organization of every page: the sandboxes, snapshots, keys and billing shown, and the wallet of the sandboxes and keys you create. The browser remembers it. |
| Sidebar, **CLI and API keys bill … Change** | Sets the active wallet: the default of the CLI and account API keys. Picking an organization in the select above never changes it. |

Webhooks, Alerts and Account settings belong to your account. They are the same in every organization. The page header says so.

## A teammate cannot see or use my sandbox

| Cause | Fix |
| - | - |
| The sandbox bills your personal account. Teammates see only sandboxes that the organization pays for. | Move all your personal sandboxes and your plan: `boat --org acme org migrate` (organization owner only). Or create a new sandbox for the team: `boat --org acme new`. |
| The teammate looks at their personal scope. | The teammate runs `boat org switch acme`, or picks the organization in the sidebar. |
| The teammate sees it as `view` only. The sandbox is private. | Run `boat share <id>`. If it holds your logins and runs, stop and resume it after. Read [Shared sandboxes](/organizations/shared-sandboxes). |

boat fixes the wallet of a sandbox when it creates it. A fork keeps the wallet of its source.


# Move a personal plan in
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/organizations/move-personal-plan

Move the sandboxes and plan you paid for personally to your organization, without stopping them. The unused share of the month is refunded.

Did you pay personally before the organization existed? Then do not cancel the personal plan by hand. The sandboxes that bill your personal account would stop with it. Move the plan instead.

When you move:

* Every sandbox billed to your personal account bills the organization from that moment.
* Your personal plan ends the same day.
* boat refunds the unused share of the month to your card.
* The money in your personal wallet stays on your personal account.
* Only the owner of the organization can move a plan in.
* The organization must have its own plan first.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat --org acme billing plan 20 --move-personal   # first org plan, move included once it is paid
boat --org acme org migrate                       # org already on a plan
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
# Account API: not under $BOAT_API_BASE and not in the v1 API reference
curl -sS -X POST "https://boat.dev/api/boat/billing/move-to-org" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"teamId": "team_..."}'
```

The dashboard offers the same move in two places:

* The Billing tab of the organization.
* The cancel-plan dialog of your personal plan.

To move from an organization back to a personal plan, read [Card, invoices and plan changes](/billing/plan-changes#move-a-plan-between-personal-and-organization).


# Seats, limits and caps
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/organizations/seats-and-limits

Seat price (one plan price per seat), what a seat adds, buying seats, the shared start and concurrency limits, the shared wallet, and per-member caps.

## Seats

**One seat costs the plan price.** A 5-seat organization on the \$20 plan pays \$100 a month.

Each seat adds the plan's included time. So a 5-seat organization on the \$20 plan also gets \$100 of included time each month.

Seats add limits (sandboxes at once and starts) as follows:

| Plan | What one more seat adds to the limits |
| - | - |
| \$2000 | The full plan limits |
| \$20, \$100, \$500 | 20% of the plan limits. The total never goes above the limits of the next plan. |

To get higher limits, move to a bigger plan first. A bigger plan always gives more limits than the same money in seats. Organizations that had more than one seat on 28 October 2026 keep the full limits for those seats.

An organization pays for the larger of two numbers:

* Its members.
* The seats that the owner bought.

You do not need one person or one email for each seat. To pay for more seats than people, set the seat count. Use the [Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) tab with the organization selected, or call the account API. This route is not under `$BOAT_API_BASE` and is not in the v1 API reference:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -X PUT https://boat.dev/api/boat/teams/acme/seats \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"seats": 5}'
```

| Change | Result |
| - | - |
| Raise the count | The organization card pays the prorated difference at once. If the card fails, the seat count does not change. |
| A member joins | The member takes an empty seat at no extra cost. |
| A member joins and no seat is empty | Accepting the invite adds a seat. The organization card pays for it at once. If the card fails, the accept fails with "could not add the paid seat" and the invite stays unused. |
| Lower the count | You get credit on the next invoice, not a card refund. You cannot go below the number of members. |

* A seat counts accounts, not email addresses. Invites to email aliases such as `name+1@example.com`, accepted by the same account, add no seat. To get more seats, set the seat count.
* To add members, the organization needs an active plan.

## Shared limits

The included time, start-rate and concurrency numbers of the plan are **one shared pool for the whole organization**. The seats set the size of the pool, as in [Seats](#seats). For every limit, read [Limits and errors](/limits).

Example: 5 seats of \$20 against the \$100 plan, for the same \$100 a month:

| Limit | 5 seats of \$20 | \$100 plan, 1 seat |
| - | - | - |
| Included time per month | \$100 (2,777 h of `default`) | \$100 |
| Concurrent sandboxes | 180 | 300 |
| Starts per minute | 21 | 30 |
| Starts per hour | 108 | 210 |
| Starts per day | 360 | 840 |

* If one member uses all of the hourly start budget, boat refuses every other member's `new`, `fork` and `resume` billed to the organization. This lasts until the window rolls.
* Personal sandboxes use the member's own personal limits.
* The seat limits apply only while the organization's plan is active. Without a plan, money in the wallet still runs sandboxes, at the limits of a single seat.
* [Extra starts](/limits#extra-starts) use these shared limits as their included numbers.

## Per-member caps

One shared plan and one shared wallet mean one member can spend all of it. So the owner can cap each member on the [Organization](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=org) tab. Both caps are unlimited by default. These caps are the only spend caps in boat. A personal account has none: read [Control your spend](/billing#control-your-spend).

| Cap | Limits |
| - | - |
| Usage cap | That member's organization-billed machine time per billing window |
| Concurrent sandboxes | How many organization-billed sandboxes that member can run at once |

* The owner and admins set caps. Only the owner sets the owner's caps.
* Caps apply only to organization-billed sandboxes.
* A sandbox counts against the caps of its **creator**. This is also true when a teammate resumes it.

| Over the cap | `new`, `fork` and `resume` answer |
| - | - |
| Usage cap | `402 team_member_cap_reached` |
| Concurrent-sandbox cap | `429 member_limit_reached` |

In both cases, boat snapshots and stops the member's organization sandboxes within about a minute. Nothing is lost. The sandboxes can resume again when the owner raises the cap or the billing window renews.


# Shared sandboxes
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/organizations/shared-sandboxes

Every member sees the sandboxes the organization pays for. What each member can do with them, how to share a sandbox or make it private, and the default for new sandboxes.

For everyone who can reach a sandbox, in and out of the team, read [Security and isolation](/security#who-can-reach-a-sandbox).

In the scope of an organization, `boat list`, `GET /sandboxes` and the dashboard show two sets of sandboxes:

* Your own sandboxes.
* **Every sandbox the organization pays for**, whoever created it.

Each sandbox shows who created it (`createdBy`), whether it is `shared` or `private` (`visibility`), and what you can do with it (`access`).

## Shared or private

| `visibility` | When | Teammates |
| - | - | - |
| `shared` | It holds none of its creator's personal logins, and its creator did not make it private | Use it |
| `private` | It holds its creator's personal logins, or its creator made it private | See it. Stop it, unless its creator made it private |

| `access` | Who | What you can do |
| - | - | - |
| `owner` | You created it | Everything |
| `use` | A teammate's `shared` sandbox | Open it, SSH, run commands, read and write files, prompt its agent, open ports, resume and stop it |
| `view` | A teammate's `private` sandbox | See it and its usage. Stop it, unless its creator made it private |

## Make a sandbox private or shared

The creator runs `unshare` or `share`. A sandbox that holds none of the creator's logins changes at once, both ways. Nothing on the sandbox changes.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat unshare bx_4tr8wz3c     # only you can use it; teammates still see it
boat share bx_4tr8wz3c       # every member can use it again
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_4tr8wz3c/unshare" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# -> { sandbox: { ..., visibility: "private" } }
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await boat.unshare({ sandboxId: "bx_4tr8wz3c" }); // creator only
await boat.share({ sandboxId: "bx_4tr8wz3c" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat.unshare(sandbox_id="bx_4tr8wz3c")  # creator only
boat.share(sandbox_id="bx_4tr8wz3c")
```

* `unshare` removes teammates' SSH keys from the running sandbox. A terminal a teammate already has open stays open until it closes.
* Teammates never read history recorded while the sandbox was private.
* In the dashboard, pick **Make private** or **Share with org** in the row menu.

## New sandboxes: shared or private by default

New sandboxes of an organization start `shared`. Owners and admins can make them start `private`. Existing sandboxes keep their setting.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat org default-visibility             # shows the current value
boat org default-visibility private     # new sandboxes start private
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X PATCH "$BOAT_API_BASE/orgs/acme" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"newSandboxesPrivate":true}'
```

In the dashboard, the setting is on the **Organization** page.

The default applies to sandboxes created, deployed from a saved snapshot, forked, or moved in with `boat org migrate`. A fork of a private sandbox is private.

## Why a sandbox with your logins is private

A sandbox can get these from its creator, when its environment passes them:

* GitHub token.
* Claude and Codex logins.
* Environment secrets.

Anyone with a shell in that sandbox could act as that person. So a teammate gets a shell only when none of these are on the sandbox.

A sandbox created with `--no-env` is `shared` from the start, unless the organization default is `private`. So is a sandbox created on an environment that passes nothing: marked [safe for third parties](/environments/access#safe-for-third-parties) without the AI credentials proxy, or with every section turned off. Such a sandbox never receives personal logins later: an environment upgrade skips it, and a resume or fork onto an environment that passes logins returns `409 environment_passes_logins`. Pick this setup for agents that the whole team runs. Give these agents the team's own model keys with `--env`. Do not give them the logins of one person.

## Share a sandbox that holds your logins

The creator of the sandbox runs `share`. Then:

* boat never sends the creator's GitHub token, model logins, secret files or the sandbox's own CLI key to it again. The sandbox becomes `noEnv`.
* boat deletes these from its disk when the sandbox next starts.
* Files and installs stay.
* You cannot undo the removal of the logins. You can still make the sandbox private again with `unshare`.

A sandbox that runs when you share it still has your logins in the memory of its programs. It stays `view` for your team until you stop it and resume it. The response then shows `restartRequired: true`.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat org switch acme               # the org's scope: boat list shows its sandboxes too
boat list
# bx_7k2m9qpd  running  2h 10m  research-agent  [org: acme]  by alex  view only: holds alex's logins
# bx_4tr8wz3c  running  -       support-agent   [org: acme]  by alex
boat stop bx_7k2m9qpd              # alex, the creator
boat share bx_7k2m9qpd
boat resume bx_7k2m9qpd            # comes back without alex's logins: every member can use it
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "X-Boat-Org: acme"
# -> sandboxes: [{ id, name, state, createdBy, access, visibility, holdsCreatorLogins, team, ... }]

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_7k2m9qpd/share" -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
# -> { sandbox: { ... }, restartRequired: true }  when it was running: stop + resume it
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { sandboxes } = await boat.sandboxes({ org: "acme" });
for (const s of sandboxes) console.log(s.name, s.createdBy, s.access);
await boat.share({ sandboxId: "bx_7k2m9qpd" }); // creator only
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
page = boat.sandboxes(org="acme")
for s in page.sandboxes:
    print(s.name, s.created_by, s.access)
boat.share(sandbox_id="bx_7k2m9qpd")  # creator only
```

## In the dashboard

| Row label | Means |
| - | - |
| **by alex** | A teammate, alex, created this sandbox. |
| **view only** | alex's sandbox is private: it holds alex's logins, or alex made it private. |
| **private** | Your own sandbox that your teammates see as **view only**. To share it, pick **Share with org** in the row menu. "Private" does not mean billed to your personal account. |
| **shared** | Your own sandbox that every member can use. To stop that, pick **Make private** in the row menu. |

A sandbox that bills your personal account does not show to your teammates at all. Read [A teammate cannot see or use my sandbox](/organizations/active-wallet#a-teammate-cannot-see-or-use-my-sandbox).

## Errors

| Error | When |
| - | - |
| `403 sandbox_private` | A teammate tries to use a `view` sandbox. The error says whose logins the sandbox holds, or who made it private. |
| `403 owner_only` | A teammate tries an action that stays with the creator. |

These actions stay with the creator:

* Fork.
* Delete.
* Change its settings: name, subdomain, auto-stop.
* Any stop that deletes data: `--force`, or any stop of a sandbox with snapshots off. The organization owner can also do this.
* Any stop of a sandbox that its creator made private (`unshare`, or the `private` default). Owners and admins of the organization can also do this. So with `boat org default-visibility private`, each member stops only their own sandboxes.

## Shared environments and AI credentials

Give the team's sandboxes the team's own model keys, not a person's logins. Members use these unless an owner [limits them to a list of members](/organizations#limit-who-can-use-an-environment-or-profile).

| | Members | Owners |
| - | - | - |
| [Organization environments](/environments/manage#organization-environments) (`?org=` on environment routes, `boat env --org`) | Read and use | Owners and admins change them |
| [Organization credential profiles](/ai-credentials#organization-profiles) | Use | Create and change |
| [AI credentials proxy](/ai-credentials#the-ai-credentials-proxy) switch of the organization | See | Turn on or off |

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat --org acme ai profile new team-claude
echo "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" | boat ai profile set-key team-claude anthropic-api-key
boat --org acme ai proxy on
boat env new agents --org acme
boat env set agents --org acme --credential-profile team-claude
boat --org acme new --environment agents
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/credential-profiles" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"team-claude","org":"acme"}'

curl -sS -X PUT "$BOAT_API_BASE/environments/$ENV_ID?org=acme" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"credentialProfileId":"team-claude"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await boat.createCredentialProfile({ name: "team-claude", org: "acme" });
await boat.updateEnvironment({ environmentId: envId, org: "acme", credentialProfileId: "team-claude" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.create_credential_profile_request import CreateCredentialProfileRequest
from boat_sdk.models.update_sandbox_environment_request import UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest

boat.create_credential_profile(CreateCredentialProfileRequest(name="team-claude", org="acme"))
boat.update_environment(env_id, UpdateSandboxEnvironmentRequest(credential_profile_id="team-claude"), org="acme")
```

A sandbox billed to the organization can name an organization environment. When the creator has an environment of the same name, the creator's own environment wins.


# Sandbox per user: build a platform
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/platform-guide

Give each of your users a sandbox: run their agents, previews, and workspaces on boat. Architectures, costs, and provisioning patterns.

This guide is for builders of products like Lovable, Devin, or agent platforms. In these products, your product makes a sandbox for each of your own users.

The [Terms of Service](https://boat.dev/terms#tos-8) allow this, and you do not need our approval. You are responsible for what your users do in their sandboxes.

Such a platform needs:

* Persistent files and context for each user or project.
* An agent that works inside the workspace and can debug anything. Each sandbox has seven coding agents. See [Integrated agents](/integrated-agents).
* A private preview URL of what the user builds.
* A controlled sandbox cost for each user.

In all cases, you run your own backend and database. You control boat through the [API](/api/v1) or the [SDKs](/sdks/overview).

## The two rules

1. **Always create user sandboxes with `--no-env`** (`noEnv: true`). A no-env sandbox gets none of the secrets or credentials of your account. It cannot act on your account or on other sandboxes. Give the sandbox what it needs explicitly with `--env`. See [No-env sandboxes](/environments#safe-for-third-parties).
2. **Tag each sandbox** with per-sandbox environment variables. Your backend then knows which sandbox is which.

> [!TIP]
>
> You do not have to remember `--no-env` on every call. Mark an environment as safe for third parties once, and use it for your user sandboxes. Every sandbox that uses it then gets the same protection. The protection stays after forks and resumes, and your backend does not pass a flag.
>
> ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
> boat env new users
> boat env set users --safe-for-third-parties true
> boat new --environment users --env TENANT_ID=acme
> ```
>
> See [Environments](/environments).

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new --no-env --no-auto-stop --env TENANT_ID=acme
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"ttlSeconds":null,"noEnv":true,"env":{"TENANT_ID":"acme"}}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.create({ ttlSeconds: null, noEnv: true, env: { TENANT_ID: "acme" } });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
sandbox.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=None, no_env=True, env={"TENANT_ID": "acme"}))
```

Wait for the sandbox to reach `ready` or `idle` before you run commands in it. boat enforces this:

| When you send a command | boat answers |
| - | - |
| While the sandbox provisions | A retryable 409 `sandbox_starting` error |
| Earlier in provisioning | 409 `machine_not_running` |

Do not race the start. A command sent too early also runs before boat applies your `env`.

## Choose a pattern

| Pattern | Isolation | Cost | Use it when |
| - | - | - | - |
| [1. One always-on sandbox per project](/platform-guide/patterns#pattern-1-one-always-on-sandbox-per-project) | Full | About \$26/month per project on `default` | The project has real traffic, or the user pays enough to cover it. |
| [2. One always-on sandbox per user](/platform-guide/patterns#pattern-2-one-always-on-sandbox-per-user) | Projects of one user share a machine | About \$26/month per user | A user has up to 5 to 10 fullstack projects. |
| [3. Stop and resume around usage](/platform-guide/patterns#pattern-3-stop-and-resume-around-usage) | Full | \$1 to \$5 per month for a typical user | Most platforms end up here. |

## Learn more

> [card] [Sandbox-per-user patterns](/platform-guide/patterns)
>
> Three ways to run sandboxes for your users, with costs, delete and refused stops.

> [card] [Agents in your product](/platform-guide/agents)
>
> Use the integrated agents, or bring your own harness with a daemon.

> [card] [Templates and sizing](/platform-guide/templates-and-sizing)
>
> Use a saved snapshot as a template for each user. Plan concurrency and start limits.
