# Readiness and resume speed
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/readiness

What ready means, what already works at ready, what comes a few seconds later (Docker, services, system files), and how to wait for each in a script.

A sandbox is **ready** when the API reports its state as `ready`, `idle` or `running`. From then on, commands, SSH and prompts work at once.

`boat new`, `boat fork` and `boat resume` return when the sandbox is ready and a first command works. In a script, you can run your next command right after them.

## Ready, in one table

| State (API) | CLI and dashboard show | Commands | Billed |
| - | - | - | - |
| `provisioning` | `provisioning` | Wait (see below) | No |
| `provisioned` | `starting` | Wait (see below) | Yes |
| `cloning` | `cloning` | Wait (see below) | Yes |
| `ready`, `idle`, `running` | same | **Run at once** | Yes |
| `archiving` | `stopping` | Refused | No |
| `archived` | `stopped` | Refused | No |
| `error` | `error` | Refused | No |

> [!NOTE]
>
> The CLI and the dashboard show `provisioned` as `starting`. At `provisioned`, the machine is up, but boat still applies your environment, secrets and repositories.

A command that you send while the sandbox starts does not fail. The API holds it for up to 60 seconds and runs it when the sandbox is ready. After 60 seconds, it answers `409 sandbox_starting`. Send it again.

A command sent to a stopped sandbox, or to one in `error`, fails with `409 sandbox_not_ready`. Resume the sandbox first.

## What works at ready

| Part | At `ready` |
| - | - |
| Commands, SSH, prompts | Work |
| Environment variables and secret files | Set |
| Files in `/home/user` | All visible. Content downloads in the background. A read of a file waits for that file only |
| Repositories of the environment | Cloned |
| Public URLs | Normally open. A port can answer a moment later |
| The IP address | New. It changes at every resume and fork |

## What comes a few seconds after ready

On a resume, a fork or a deploy from a saved snapshot, boat restores in the background. These parts come after `ready`:

| Part | When | How to wait for it |
| - | - | - |
| Your changes in `/usr`, `/etc`, `/opt`, `/var`, `/srv`, `/root` | Visible at `ready`, like `/home/user`. A read of a file waits for that file only. The content is on the local disk a few seconds later. Files that a program opened before then keep working | Nothing to do. To wait for all of it, wait for Docker or your service, below |
| Docker and your containers | A few seconds after `ready`. The containers you had come back, and the ones that ran start again. Boat does not run `docker compose up`, build images or wait for health checks | `docker info` answers |
| Docker images | Loaded in the background after `ready`. They usually appear in `docker images` about 2 seconds later. No docker command waits for them. An image you build, pull or tag before they load stays yours | Nothing to do |
| Systemd services that you enabled | After the system files | `systemctl is-active <service>` |
| Repository setup scripts | They start at `ready`, at every start | Wait for what the script makes, for example a file or a port. Read [Setup scripts](/setup) |
| Per-sandbox setup script (`--setup-file`) | It starts after `ready`, one time | `setupStatus` in `boat info` is `done` or `failed` |
| The rest of the file content | In the background | `hydrated` is `true`, or the `sandbox.hydrated` webhook |

A new sandbox, made with `boat new` and no `--from`, restores nothing. Docker and services start with the machine.

Some users see the first outbound connection fail in the first second after `ready`. Retry a failed first connection.

## Wait in a script

The common case needs no wait. Run your command after `boat new` or `boat resume`:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
ID=$(boat new --json | jq -r 'select(.event == "ready") | .id')
boat exec "$ID" "cd my-repo && npm test"
```

Wait for Docker:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec "$ID" --timeout 120 "until docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done"
```

Wait for a systemd service:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec "$ID" --timeout 120 "until systemctl is-active --quiet my-app; do sleep 1; done"
```

Wait until every file is downloaded:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
until [ "$(boat info "$ID" --json | jq -r .sandbox.hydrated)" = "true" ]; do sleep 2; done
```

With the API, poll `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` and read `sandbox.state` and `sandbox.hydrated`. Or subscribe to the `sandbox.ready` and `sandbox.hydrated` [webhooks](/webhooks).

Wait for a stop:

`boat stop` returns at `stopping`. Poll `boat info` until the state is `stopped`. Read [Wait for the stop in a script](/snapshots/stop#wait-for-the-stop-in-a-script).

## How fast a sandbox comes back

A resume, a fork or a deploy is ready in **a few seconds, whatever the size of the disk**. You see all your files at once. boat downloads their content in the background.

| What | What happens |
| - | - |
| Every resume, fork and deploy | It runs on a new machine. boat downloads your files again in the background, even if the sandbox had all its files before the stop. `hydrated` is `false` until the download ends. |
| During the download | `GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}` returns `hydration`: the step, `entriesDone` of `entriesTotal` (files, folders and links) and a `percent`. Use `hydrated` as the end signal, not `percent`. |
| A file that is not downloaded yet | When you open or read it, boat gets that file first. Then you get the right bytes. |
| End of the download | `hydrated` becomes `true`, `hydratedAt` is set, and the `sandbox.hydrated` webhook fires. Docker volumes move to the local disk at this point. |
| Files of the base image | They are already on every machine. boat downloads only the files that differ from the image. |
| Paths in `.boatignore` | boat does not save them, so it does not download them. Read [Leave files out](/snapshots/whats-saved#leave-files-out-with-boatignore). |
| A resume during `stopping` | boat takes back the same machine. Nothing is downloaded. |

A restore does not need space for a second copy of your disk. boat removes each downloaded part when it has used it. The [restore limits of each machine](/machines) count the size of your files, not the smaller download size.

Permissions, owners, times and extended attributes come back with your files and folders. Two of them come back later:

* **Extended attributes of a file** come back when the content of that file arrives. Folders have theirs from the start.
* **Folder modification times** come back when the download ends. Each new file in a folder changes the time of that folder, so boat sets the time last.

Inode numbers and change times (`ctime`) are new on the new machine. Git keeps them in its index, so boat updates the Git index of each repository under `/home/user` (up to 4 folders deep) when the sandbox starts. Your first `git status` or `git switch` then does not read every file again. boat also downloads each `.git` folder first. If a Git command already runs, boat leaves that repository alone.

The time to a working app depends on what your app reads first. Large first reads, Docker images and services that start late add seconds. The next section makes the first start faster.

## Make the first start faster

When a sandbox starts from a snapshot, it records which files open first. It keeps this list in `~/.ascii/playbook.json`. At the next start, boat downloads these files first. Your app then works before the rest of the disk arrives. `ready` does not wait for these files.

The list is a normal file. It goes into the snapshot, so forks and deploys get it too.

**A saved snapshot learns from its deploys.** Each sandbox that you create `from` a saved snapshot of your account or org records the files it opens while it starts. When its download ends, boat keeps that list with the saved snapshot. The next sandboxes that you create from the same name download these files first. You do nothing for this: the list follows what your sandboxes really open, and it stays when you save the name again. Sandboxes that another account creates with a share code use the list, but they do not change it.

To give a brand-new saved snapshot a list before its first deploy, record it yourself. The list is recorded **only while a sandbox starts from a snapshot**. Do these steps in this order:

**1. Start the sandbox from a snapshot**

Resume a stopped sandbox, or deploy one from the saved snapshot that you want to update. A new, empty sandbox has nothing to record.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat resume bx_f7k2q9hd
```

**2. Start your app at once**

Run your normal start command at once, while files still download. boat records each file that your app opens, in order. boat does not record files that open after the download ends.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --detach "cd my-repo && npm run dev"
```

**3. Wait for the download to end, then save**

boat writes the list when the download ends. Save after that. If you save too early, the saved snapshot does not have this run.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
until [ "$(boat info bx_f7k2q9hd --json | jq -r .sandbox.hydrated)" = "true" ]; do sleep 2; done
boat snapshot bx_f7k2q9hd web-stack
```

Each run adds to the list. It does not replace it. The newest run counts most. Each time you repeat these steps, the saved snapshot starts a little faster. The list holds the first 20,000 paths.


# Run a coding agent on your repo
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/recipes/agent-on-repo

Step by step: connect GitHub and an AI key, clone your repository into a sandbox, and let Claude Code or Codex work on it.

You get a sandbox with your repository cloned in it, and an agent that works on it. It takes five steps.

## Before you start

* The `boat` CLI is installed and signed in. Read [Quickstart](/quickstart).
* Your account has GitHub connected. If you signed in with Google or an email code, open [Dashboard > Environment](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=environment) and click **Connect GitHub**.

## 1. Connect an AI key or subscription

Open [Agents & Proxying](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=agents). Sign in to Claude (Pro or Max) or ChatGPT, or paste an API key. Do this one time.

Without this step, the first prompt fails with `409 provider_not_configured`. For all options, read [Keys and subscriptions](/integrated-agents/keys).

## 2. Add the repository to your environment

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env add-repo base acme/web-app --branch main
```

`base` is your default environment. Every new sandbox on it clones `acme/web-app` into `/home/user/web-app`. Private repositories work.

## 3. Let the environment pass your GitHub access and AI keys

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env set base --safe-for-third-parties false --github true --agents-credentials true
```

* `--github true` lets the sandbox clone and push with your GitHub access.
* `--agents-credentials true` gives the agents the keys from step 1.
* **Safe for third parties** withholds all your secrets: variables, secret files, GitHub access and AI credentials. Turn it on only for sandboxes that other people use.

## 4. Start a sandbox

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new
```

The command prints the sandbox id, for example `bx_f7k2q9hd`. Check that the repository is there:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd 'ls /home/user/web-app && git -C /home/user/web-app status'
```

The repository setup script, if you set one, runs at each start. Setup scripts are set on the dashboard only. Read [Setup scripts](/setup).

## 5. Give the agent a task

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd --provider claude "Fix the failing tests, then commit on a new branch fix/tests and push it"
```

* The command prints what the agent does, and exits when the turn ends.
* Use `--provider codex` for Codex. Omit `--provider` to use your default harness.
* With one repository, the agent starts inside the repository folder.
* To send more work in the same thread, run `boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd "…"` again. The agent keeps its memory.
* To change the task while it works, run `boat steer bx_f7k2q9hd "…"`. Read [Steer a running turn](/integrated-agents/steering).

## After the task

| You want | Command |
| - | - |
| Watch the work from another terminal | `boat events bx_f7k2q9hd --follow` |
| Look at the changes yourself | `boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd` |
| More time than the 1-hour auto-stop | `boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --hours 6`. A running prompt also moves the deadline by itself |
| Stop and keep the disk | `boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd`. `boat resume` brings back the files and the conversation |

## Next

* [Run many agents in parallel](/recipes/parallel-agents)
* [Customize the harness: rules, MCP, skills](/integrated-agents/customize)
* [Repositories](/environments/repositories)


# Run many agents in parallel
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/recipes/parallel-agents

Fork one prepared sandbox into N copies and give each copy its own agent task, from the CLI or Python. Stay under the start limits.

Prepare one sandbox, fork it N times, and prompt each fork. Each agent gets its own disk, processes and IP address. They do not interfere.

To run a few tasks on one sandbox instead, use [parallel conversations](/integrated-agents/conversations#parallel-conversations). They share one disk and one desktop.

## Watch the start limits

Each fork counts as one start. Above a limit, boat refuses the fork with `429 rate_limited`. The answer names the `window` that you hit.

| Plan | Starts per minute / hour / day | Sandboxes at once |
| - | - | - |
| \$20 | 12 / 60 / 200 | 100 |
| \$100 | 30 / 210 / 840 | 300 |
| \$500 | 65 / 420 / 1,680 | 1,000 |
| \$2000 | 90 / 600 / 2,400 | 2,000 |
| [Free trial](/free-trial) | 5 / 25 / 75 | 2 |

* An organization on the \$2000 plan gets these limits times its number of seats. Below it, each extra seat adds 20%.
* Pace your forks below the per-minute limit. The examples below wait 6 seconds between forks, which fits the \$20 plan.

Read [Limits and errors](/limits) for every limit and how to raise it.

## 1. Prepare the source sandbox

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat new
boat exec bx_f7k2q9hd --cwd web-app --timeout 600 "npm ci"
boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd
```

A fork copies the newest snapshot of its source. Stop the source first, so that its snapshot has your last change. A fork of a running sandbox can miss the writes of the last minute.

The source needs your AI keys. Read [Run a coding agent on your repo](/recipes/agent-on-repo) for the environment settings.

## 2. Fork N copies and prompt each one

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
source=bx_f7k2q9hd
tasks=("Fix issue 101" "Fix issue 102" "Fix issue 103" "Fix issue 104")

for task in "${tasks[@]}"; do
  id=$(boat fork "$source" --ttl 7200 --json | jq -r .id)
  echo "$id" >> forks.txt
  boat prompt "$id" "$task" > "$id.log" 2>&1 &   # runs in the background
  sleep 6                                         # stay under the start limit
done
wait                                              # every agent is done
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os, time, uuid
from boat_sdk import ApiClient, Configuration, wait_until_ready, wait_for_prompt
from boat_sdk.api.boat_api import BoatApi
from boat_sdk.exceptions import ApiException
from boat_sdk.models.fork_request import ForkRequest
from boat_sdk.models.prompt_request import PromptRequest

config = Configuration(host="https://boat.dev/api/v1", access_token=os.environ["BOAT_API_KEY"])
source = "bx_f7k2q9hd"
tasks = ["Fix issue 101", "Fix issue 102", "Fix issue 103", "Fix issue 104"]

with ApiClient(config) as client:
    sandbox = BoatApi(client)
    runs = []
    for task in tasks:
        key = str(uuid.uuid4())   # the same key on a retry never makes a second fork
        while True:
            try:
                forked = sandbox.fork(
                    sandbox_id=source,
                    fork_request=ForkRequest(ttl_seconds=7200),
                    idempotency_key=key,
                )
                break
            except ApiException as exc:
                if exc.status != 429:
                    raise
                time.sleep(10)    # start limit hit: wait, then retry with the same key
        wait_until_ready(sandbox, forked.id)
        queued = sandbox.prompt(forked.id, PromptRequest(prompt=task))
        runs.append((forked.id, queued.prompt_id))
        time.sleep(6)             # stay under the start limit

    for sandbox_id, prompt_id in runs:
        run = wait_for_prompt(sandbox, sandbox_id, prompt_id)
        print(sandbox_id, run.status)
```

* `--ttl 7200` gives each fork a 2-hour auto-stop. A fork never copies the auto-stop setting of its source. A running prompt moves the deadline by itself.
* `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry safe. Without it, a retry after a lost answer can make a second fork that you pay for.
* Prompts queue while a fork starts. You do not have to wait for `ready` before a prompt. The Python example waits only to fail early on a bad fork.

## 3. Collect the results and clean up

Each `<id>.log` file holds the work of one agent. Then read the result in each fork and stop or delete it:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
while read -r id; do
  boat exec "$id" --cwd web-app "git log --oneline -1"
done < forks.txt

boat stop bx_k3v9x2mq           # keep the disk of a fork; boat resume brings it back
boat delete bx_p8w4z7nc --yes   # erase a fork that you do not need
```

A fork that you do not stop stops by itself at its auto-stop deadline.

## Related

* [Resume and fork](/snapshots/resume-and-fork)
* [Use a saved snapshot as a template](/platform-guide/templates-and-sizing)
* [Stream events](/integrated-agents/conversations#stream-events)


# SDKs
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/sdks/overview

Use boat from Python or TypeScript: install, configure, and a complete create, run, stop example. Other languages: generate a client from the OpenAPI file.

| SDK | Package | Method names |
| - | - | - |
| [Python](/sdks/python) | `boat-sdk` on PyPI | snake_case, synchronous |
| [TypeScript / JavaScript](/sdks/typescript) | `@boatdev/sdk` on npm | camelCase, `async` |

Each SDK covers the full [HTTP API](/api/v1): sandboxes, commands, files, public URLs, snapshots, saved snapshots, environments, integrated agents, webhooks and API keys.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Used the `box` SDKs before? Read [Migrating from Box](/migrating-from-box).

## Install

```bash Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
python -m pip install boat-sdk
```

```bash TypeScript / JavaScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
npm install @boatdev/sdk
```

## Configure

1. Create an API key: `boat api-key create my-app --preset ci`, or use the [dashboard](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=api-keys). The key starts with `boat_`.
2. Store it as `BOAT_API_KEY`.
3. Give it to the `Configuration` object. The base URL is `https://boat.dev/api/v1`.

## Create, run a command, stop

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os

from boat_sdk import ApiClient, Configuration, wait_until_ready
from boat_sdk.api.boat_api import BoatApi
from boat_sdk.models import CommandRequest, CreateSandboxRequest

config = Configuration(host="https://boat.dev/api/v1", access_token=os.environ["BOAT_API_KEY"])

with ApiClient(config) as client:
    boat = BoatApi(client)
    sandbox_id = boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=1800)).sandbox.id
    try:
        wait_until_ready(boat, sandbox_id)
        out = boat.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="echo hi")).actual_instance
        print(out.exit_code, out.stdout)
    finally:
        boat.stop(sandbox_id)
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { BoatApi, Configuration, waitUntilReady } from "@boatdev/sdk";
import type { CommandResponse } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const boat = new BoatApi(new Configuration({
  basePath: "https://boat.dev/api/v1",
  accessToken: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY!,
}));

const sandboxId = (await boat.create({ ttlSeconds: 1800 })).sandbox.id;
try {
  await waitUntilReady(boat, sandboxId);
  const out = (await boat.command({ sandboxId, command: "echo hi" })) as CommandResponse;
  console.log(out.exitCode, out.stdout);
} finally {
  await boat.stop({ sandboxId });
}
```

Next: stream output, commands with no time limit, one job with its cost, folder copies, files, public URLs, forks and prompts are on the [Python](/sdks/python) and [TypeScript](/sdks/typescript) pages.

## Other languages

boat publishes SDKs for Python and TypeScript only. For another language, generate a client from the OpenAPI file with [OpenAPI Generator](https://openapi-generator.tech):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate \
  -i https://docs.boat.dev/openapi/boat-v1.yaml -g go -o ./boat-go
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Keep these values secret: API keys, environment secrets, SSH keys, and the desktop, VNC and signed file URLs that boat returns. Do not log them without redaction.


# Python SDK
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/sdks/python

Install boat-sdk, create a sandbox, run a command and read stdout and the exit code, stream output, run background jobs, move files, prompt agents. Every method, by group.

Install the package. It needs Python 3.9 or later:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
python -m pip install boat-sdk
```

On Windows, `python` can open the Microsoft Store. Use `py -m pip install boat-sdk` there.

## Create, run a command, stop

This script creates a sandbox, runs a command, prints the output and the exit code, and stops the sandbox. Set `BOAT_API_KEY` first. See [API keys](/api-keys).

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os

from boat_sdk import ApiClient, Configuration, wait_until_ready
from boat_sdk.api.boat_api import BoatApi
from boat_sdk.models import CommandRequest, CreateSandboxRequest

config = Configuration(
    host="https://boat.dev/api/v1",
    access_token=os.environ["BOAT_API_KEY"],
)

with ApiClient(config) as client:
    boat = BoatApi(client)
    created = boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=1800))
    sandbox_id = created.sandbox.id
    try:
        wait_until_ready(boat, sandbox_id)
        result = boat.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="echo hi && uname -a"))
        out = result.actual_instance
        print(out.exit_code)
        print(out.stdout)
    finally:
        boat.stop(sandbox_id)
```

Three rules make this work:

* Pass the request body by keyword: `create(create_sandbox_request=...)`. The first positional argument of `create` is the idempotency key.
* `command()` returns a wrapper. Read the result from `.actual_instance`. It is a `CommandResponse` for a normal command, and a `CommandStartedResponse` for `detached=True`.
* `wait_until_ready` is a module function. It is not a method of `boat`.

To delete the sandbox and its snapshots instead of a stop, call `boat.delete_sandbox(sandbox_id=sandbox_id, x_ascii_confirm_delete=sandbox_id)`.

## Configure

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import os

from boat_sdk import ApiClient, Configuration
from boat_sdk.api.boat_api import BoatApi

config = Configuration(
    host=os.getenv("BOAT_API_BASE", "https://boat.dev/api/v1"),
    access_token=os.environ["BOAT_API_KEY"],   # boat_...
)

with ApiClient(config) as client:
    boat = BoatApi(client)
```

* Call every API method on `boat`. Method names are snake_case.
* Request models are in `boat_sdk.models`. Import them from there:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models import (
    CommandRequest, CreateSandboxRequest, FileUrlRequest, ForkRequest, HostPortRequest,
    SavedSnapshotSaveRequest, PromptRequest, ResumeRequest, SteerRequest, StopRequest,
    UpdateSandboxRequest,
)
```

* Helper functions are in `boat_sdk`: `wait_until_ready`, `wait_until_idle`, `wait_for_desktop`, `wait_for_prompt`, `wait_for_prompt_done`, `stream_events`, `stream_prompt`, `stop_and_remove`, `read_text`, `write_text`, `exec_command`, `stream_command`, `run_command`, `follow_command`. Each takes `boat` as its first argument.

### asyncio

The client is synchronous. In asyncio code, run each call in a thread with `asyncio.to_thread`:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import asyncio

from boat_sdk import exec_command

async def run(boat, sandbox_id: str, command: str):
    result = await asyncio.to_thread(exec_command, boat, sandbox_id, command)
    return result.actual_instance

async def run_many(boat, sandbox_ids: list[str]):
    return await asyncio.gather(*(run(boat, sid, "pytest -q") for sid in sandbox_ids))
```

## Run commands

A synchronous command times out after 30 seconds by default. Set `timeout_seconds` up to 600. For a longer command, use [`run_command`](#run-a-command-with-no-time-limit). A command sent while the sandbox starts waits up to 60 seconds.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk import exec_command
from boat_sdk.models import CommandRequest

result = boat.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="npm test", cwd="my-repo", timeout_seconds=600))
out = result.actual_instance
print(out.exit_code, out.timed_out)
print(out.stdout, out.stderr)

# Same call. It also resends a command that the sandbox refused while it restored its disk.
out = exec_command(boat, sandbox_id, "python3 -c 'print(6*7)'").actual_instance
```

### Stream the output

`stream_command` yields the output as the command writes it. Each frame is a dict.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk import stream_command

for frame in stream_command(boat, sandbox_id, "npm test", cwd="my-repo", timeout_seconds=600):
    if frame["type"] in ("stdout", "stderr"):
        print(frame["data"], end="")
    elif frame["type"] == "exit":
        print("exit code:", frame["exitCode"])
    elif frame["type"] == "error":
        print("error:", frame["message"])
```

### Run a command with no time limit

`run_command` has no 600-second limit. It starts the command in the background, then yields its output until the command ends. It reconnects by itself, with no gap and no repeat.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk import run_command

for frame in run_command(boat, sandbox_id, "npm run test:e2e", cwd="my-repo"):
    if frame["type"] in ("stdout", "stderr"):
        print(frame["data"], end="")
    elif frame["type"] == "exit":
        print("exit code:", frame["exitCode"])
    elif frame["type"] == "error":
        print("error:", frame["message"])
```

* The first frame is `{"type": "started", "processId": ...}`.
* A loop that stops early leaves the command running. Stop it with `boat.stop_command(sandbox_id, process_id)`.
* `follow_command(boat, sandbox_id, process_id)` follows a command that you started with `detached=True`.

### Run a server in the background

A detached command returns at once with a process id. It keeps running after the call. Use it for servers, and to poll a job yourself.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import time

from boat_sdk.models import CommandRequest

started = boat.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="npm run build", detached=True))
process_id = started.actual_instance.process_id

while True:
    status = boat.command_status(sandbox_id, process_id)
    if not status.running:
        break
    time.sleep(2)
print(status.status, status.exit_code)
print(status.stdout)
```

* `attach_command(sandbox_id, process_id)` streams the output of a detached command.
* `stop_command(sandbox_id, process_id)` stops it and every process that it started.
* `command_history(sandbox_id)` and `command_logs(sandbox_id, command_id)` read past commands, also while the sandbox is stopped. See [Command history](/long-running-tasks/command-history).

## Files

Small text files:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk import read_text, write_text

write_text(boat, sandbox_id, "notes/result.txt", "done\n")
print(read_text(boat, sandbox_id, "notes/result.txt"))
```

Paths are relative to `/home/user`. `read_file` and `write_file` also accept `encoding="base64"` for binary content.

For a file of any size, get a signed URL. Then send the bytes with any HTTP client:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import urllib.request

from boat_sdk.models import FileUrlRequest

up = boat.create_upload_url(sandbox_id, FileUrlRequest(path="data/input.csv"))
with open("input.csv", "rb") as f:
    urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(up.url, data=f.read(), method=up.method))

down = boat.create_download_url(sandbox_id, FileUrlRequest(path="data/input.csv"))
with urllib.request.urlopen(down.url) as resp:
    data = resp.read()
```

The URLs expire. Treat them as secrets.

### Copy a local folder in

Pack the folder, upload it, unpack it on the sandbox. In a git checkout, send the files that git tracks and the new files that `.gitignore` does not exclude. `node_modules` and build output stay out.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import io
import os
import subprocess
import tarfile
import urllib.request

from boat_sdk import exec_command
from boat_sdk.models import FileUrlRequest

def push(boat, sandbox_id: str, folder: str, remote: str = "repo"):
    listed = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
        cwd=folder, capture_output=True, check=True,
    ).stdout.decode().split("\0")
    packed = io.BytesIO()
    with tarfile.open(fileobj=packed, mode="w:gz") as tar:
        for name in listed:
            path = os.path.join(folder, name)
            # Skip a file that git tracks but that you deleted, and a submodule (a directory entry).
            if name and os.path.lexists(path) and (os.path.islink(path) or not os.path.isdir(path)):
                tar.add(path, arcname=name, recursive=False)
    up = boat.create_upload_url(sandbox_id, FileUrlRequest(path="push.tgz"))
    urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(up.url, data=packed.getvalue(), method=up.method))
    command = f"mkdir -p {remote} && tar xzf push.tgz -C {remote} && rm push.tgz"
    exec_command(boat, sandbox_id, command, timeout_seconds=600)
```

The archive keeps the exec bit and keeps links as links. It skips submodules. `boat push <id> <dir>` in the CLI also copies submodules.

## Run one job and delete the sandbox

Create a sandbox, copy the code in, run one command, read the cost, delete the sandbox. This is what `boat run` does in the CLI.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk import run_command, wait_until_ready
from boat_sdk.models import CreateSandboxRequest

created = boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(var_from="ci-base", type="large", ttl_seconds=3600))
sandbox_id = created.sandbox.id
code = None
try:
    wait_until_ready(boat, sandbox_id)
    push(boat, sandbox_id, ".")
    for frame in run_command(boat, sandbox_id, "npm ci && npm test", cwd="repo"):
        if frame["type"] in ("stdout", "stderr"):
            print(frame["data"], end="")
        elif frame["type"] == "exit":
            code = frame["exitCode"]
    usage = boat.usage(sandbox_id)
    print(f"exit {code} · {usage.seconds}s · {usage.sandbox_type} · ${usage.dollars:.4f}")
finally:
    boat.delete_sandbox(sandbox_id=sandbox_id, x_ascii_confirm_delete=sandbox_id)
raise SystemExit(code if isinstance(code, int) else 1)
```

* The script exits with the exit code of the command, so a failed test fails the CI job.
* `ttl_seconds` stops the sandbox if your script dies before the delete. Set it above your longest job.
* `usage()` gives the machine time and the cost of one sandbox. It also works after a stop.

## Public URL for a port

Start the server detached, then expose its port:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models import CommandRequest, HostPortRequest

boat.command(sandbox_id, CommandRequest(command="python3 -m http.server 8000", detached=True))
hosted = boat.host_port(sandbox_id, HostPortRequest(port=8000, public=True))
print(hosted.url)   # https://<sandbox>-8000.on.boat.dev
```

Without `public=True`, the URL is private and carries a `_token`. See [Public URLs](/hosting).

## Machine size

Pass `type`: `small`, `default` (the medium size), `large` or `xlarge`. `xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher. The [free trial](/free-trial) allows only `small` and `default`.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
created = boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(type="large", ttl_seconds=3600))
info = boat.get(created.sandbox.id)
print(info.sandbox.type, info.sandbox.vcpu, info.sandbox.memory_gb)
```

A fork gets the size of its source. To change the size of a sandbox, stop it, then resume it with `ResumeRequest(type=...)`. See [Sandbox sizes](/machines) and [Pricing](/pricing).

To know which types your account can create now, read `limits()`. A blocked type carries the reason:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
for t in boat.limits().machine_types:
    print(t.type, "ok" if t.available else t.reason)
```

## Per-sandbox environment variables

Pass `env`. The values come on top of the [environment](/environments) of the sandbox. A per-sandbox value wins over a variable with the same name. The maximum is 100 variables and 64 KB in total.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
created = boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(
    ttl_seconds=3600,
    env={"DATABASE_URL": "postgres://user:pass@host:5432/app", "FEATURE_FLAG": "1"},
))
```

A fork gets the `env` of its source, unless you give the fork its own `env`.

## No-env sandboxes

For a sandbox that you give to your own users, set `no_env=True`. boat then gives it none of your secrets: model keys, GitHub token, environment variables, secret files and SSH identity. SSH, desktop, snapshots, public URLs and forks still work. A fork of a no-env sandbox is always no-env.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
created = boat.create(create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(ttl_seconds=1800, no_env=True))
boat.resume(sandbox_id, ResumeRequest(no_env=True))
forked = boat.fork(sandbox_id, fork_request=ForkRequest(no_env=True))
```

## Saved snapshots and forks

Save a sandbox under a name. Then start new sandboxes from it. Use a saved snapshot as a template for many sandboxes:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import time
import uuid

from boat_sdk.models import CreateSandboxRequest, ForkRequest, SavedSnapshotSaveRequest

boat.save_saved_snapshot(SavedSnapshotSaveRequest(sandbox_id=sandbox_id, name="web-stack"))
while boat.get_saved_snapshot("web-stack").snapshot.status not in ("ready", "failed"):
    time.sleep(5)

created = boat.create(
    idempotency_key=str(uuid.uuid4()),
    create_sandbox_request=CreateSandboxRequest(var_from="web-stack", ttl_seconds=900),
)
```

* The Python field for `from` is `var_from`, because `from` is a Python keyword.
* Send `idempotency_key` to make a create or a fork safe to retry. See [Idempotent sandbox creation](/api/v1#idempotent-sandbox-creation).

A fork copies the newest snapshot of a sandbox into a new sandbox:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
forked = boat.fork(sandbox_id, fork_request=ForkRequest(ttl_seconds=900))
fork_id = forked.sandbox.id
```

A fork of a running sandbox uses its last background snapshot. Files written after that snapshot can be missing. See [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates) and [Resume and fork](/snapshots/resume-and-fork).

## Prompt an integrated agent

Connect a key or a subscription on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying) first. Without it, `prompt` raises `ApiException` with status 409 and code `provider_not_configured`.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk import wait_for_prompt
from boat_sdk.models import PromptRequest, SteerRequest

queued = boat.prompt(sandbox_id, PromptRequest(provider="codex", prompt="Run the tests and fix the failures."))
# Add an instruction to the running turn without stopping it:
boat.steer(sandbox_id, SteerRequest(message="Skip the integration tests."))

run = wait_for_prompt(boat, sandbox_id, queued.prompt_id)
print(run.status)

events = boat.events(sandbox_id, limit=50, type="prompt,response")
for event in events.events:
    print(event.type, event.conversation_id)
```

* `provider` is one of 7 harnesses: `codex`, `claude-code` (alias `claude`), `pi`, `opencode`, `prime-agent` (alias `prime`), `kimi` and `mistral`. Omit it to use the default from the dashboard.
* A sandbox runs [many conversations in parallel](/integrated-agents). Pass `new=True` for a new one, or `conversation_id` to continue one.
* To know when a prompt is done, use `wait_for_prompt`. Do not guess from the sandbox state.
* `interrupt(sandbox_id)` discards the running turn. `steer` keeps it running.

### Stream the agent's work

`stream_prompt` queues a prompt and yields its events. `stream_events` follows all the events of a sandbox.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk import stream_prompt
from boat_sdk.models import PromptRequest

for event in stream_prompt(boat, sandbox_id, PromptRequest(provider="codex", prompt="Run pwd and ls.")):
    if event.type != "response":
        continue
    data = event.data
    content = data.get("content") if isinstance(data, dict) else getattr(data, "content", "")
    if content:
        print(content, end="")
```

## Browse a stopped sandbox

Snapshot reads do not need the machine. They work while the sandbox is stopped:

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
latest = boat.get_latest_sandbox_snapshot(sandbox_id)
tree = boat.get_snapshot_tree(latest.snapshot.id)
data = boat.get_snapshot_file(latest.snapshot.id, path="projects/app/.env")
```

## Errors

Methods raise `ApiException` for a non-2xx response. Log the status and the body. Redact API keys, secrets, SSH keys and desktop URLs.

```python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import json

from boat_sdk.exceptions import ApiException

try:
    boat.get("bx_missing")
except ApiException as exc:
    print(exc.status)
    print(json.loads(exc.body)["code"])
```

The codes and the retry rules are on [API overview](/api/v1#error-model) and [Limits](/limits).

## Methods

Pass path parameters by position or keyword. Pass request bodies and optional parameters by keyword. The list comes from the [OpenAPI file](/openapi/boat-v1.yaml).

### Sandboxes

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `sandboxes(org=None, x_boat_org=None, limit=None, cursor=None, sort=None, state=None)` | `GET /sandboxes` | List sandboxes |
| `create(idempotency_key=None, org=None, x_boat_org=None, create_sandbox_request=None)` | `POST /sandboxes` | Create sandbox |
| `get(sandbox_id)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` | Get sandbox |
| `update(sandbox_id, update_sandbox_request)` | `PATCH /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` | Update sandbox |
| `delete_sandbox(x_ascii_confirm_delete, sandbox_id)` | `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` | Delete sandbox |
| `stop(sandbox_id, stop_request=None)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stop` | Stop sandbox |
| `share(sandbox_id)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/share` | Share sandbox with the organization |
| `recover(sandbox_id)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/recover` | Deprecated. Recover a sandbox that stopped responding |
| `resume(sandbox_id, resume_request=None)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/resume` | Resume sandbox |
| `fork(sandbox_id, idempotency_key=None, fork_request=None)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/fork` | Fork sandbox |
| `get_stop(sandbox_id, stop_id)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stops/{stopId}` | Get a stop |
| `usage(sandbox_id, since=None, until=None)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/usage` | Get sandbox usage |

### Commands

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `command(sandbox_id, command_request)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands` | Run a command |
| `command_status(sandbox_id, process_id, tail_bytes=None, stdout_offset=None, stderr_offset=None)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}` | Get command status |
| `stop_command(sandbox_id, process_id)` | `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}` | Stop a detached command |
| `attach_command(sandbox_id, process_id, stdout_offset=None, stderr_offset=None)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}/stream` | Attach to a detached command |
| `command_history(sandbox_id, mode=None, q=None, limit=None, cursor=None)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/command-history` | List the command and process history |
| `get_command(sandbox_id, command_id)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/command-history/{commandId}` | Get one command from the history |
| `command_logs(sandbox_id, command_id, stream=None, offset=None, limit=None, encoding=None)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/command-history/{commandId}/logs` | Read command logs |
| `processes(sandbox_id)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/processes` | List the processes in a sandbox |

### Files and access

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `read_file(sandbox_id, path, encoding=None)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files` | Read a file |
| `write_file(sandbox_id, file_write_request)` | `PUT /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files` | Write a file |
| `create_download_url(sandbox_id, file_url_request)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/download-url` | Get a download URL for a sandbox file |
| `create_upload_url(sandbox_id, file_url_request)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/upload-url` | Get an upload URL for a sandbox file |
| `artifact(sandbox_id, path)` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/artifacts` | Download a file |
| `desktop(sandbox_id, vnc=None, theme=None, desktop_request=None)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/desktop` | Get the desktop URL |
| `host_port(sandbox_id, host_port_request)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/host` | Expose a port on a public URL |
| `ssh_key(sandbox_id, ssh_key_request)` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/sshkey` | Add an SSH key |

### Integrated agents

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |

### Account, organizations and API keys

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `me()` | `GET /me` | Get current user |
| `list_organizations()` | `GET /orgs` | List organizations |
| `set_active_organization(active_org_update_request)` | `PATCH /orgs/active` | Set the active organization |
| `limits(org=None, x_boat_org=None, team_id=None)` | `GET /limits` | Get account limits |
| `api_keys()` | `GET /api-keys` | List API keys |
| `create_scoped_api_key(create_scoped_api_key_request)` | `POST /api-keys/scoped` | Create a scoped API key |
| `revoke_api_key(api_key_id)` | `DELETE /api-keys/{apiKeyId}` | Revoke an API key |
| `rotate_api_key(api_key_id)` | `POST /api-keys/{apiKeyId}/rotate` | Rotate an API key |
| `api_key_usage(api_key_id)` | `GET /api-keys/{apiKeyId}/usage` | Get API key usage |

### Webhooks and OpenTelemetry

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `list_webhooks()` | `GET /webhooks` | List webhooks |
| `create_webhook(webhook_create_request)` | `POST /webhooks` | Create webhook |
| `get_webhook(webhook_id)` | `GET /webhooks/{webhookId}` | Get webhook |
| `update_webhook(webhook_id, webhook_update_request)` | `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}` | Update webhook |
| `delete_webhook(webhook_id)` | `DELETE /webhooks/{webhookId}` | Delete webhook |
| `rotate_webhook_signing_secret(webhook_id)` | `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/rotate` | Rotate webhook signing secret |
| `get_telemetry()` | `GET /telemetry` | Get OpenTelemetry export |
| `set_telemetry(telemetry_set_request)` | `PUT /telemetry` | Set OpenTelemetry export |
| `delete_telemetry()` | `DELETE /telemetry` | Remove OpenTelemetry export |
| `get_ci_overview(account=, repo=, state=, limit=)` | `GET /ci` | Get CI overview |
| `connect_ci_github(ci_connect_request)` | `POST /ci/connect` | Connect GitHub for CI |
| `get_ci_job(job_id)` | `GET /ci/jobs/{jobId}` | Get CI job |
| `get_ci_job_log(job_id)` | `GET /ci/jobs/{jobId}/logs` | Get CI job log |

### Data retention

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `get_data_retention()` | `GET /account/data-retention` | Get account data-retention policy |
| `update_data_retention(data_retention_update_request)` | `PATCH /account/data-retention` | Update account data-retention policy |
| `get_deletion_operation(operation_id)` | `GET /deletion-operations/{operationId}` | Get deletion operation |


# TypeScript SDK
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/sdks/typescript

Install @boatdev/sdk, create a sandbox, run a command and read stdout and the exit code, stream output, run background jobs, move files, prompt agents. Every method, by group.

Install the package. It needs Node 18 or later (for `fetch`):

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
npm install @boatdev/sdk
```

## Create, run a command, stop

This script creates a sandbox, runs a command, prints the output and the exit code, and stops the sandbox. Set `BOAT_API_KEY` first. See [API keys](/api-keys).

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { BoatApi, Configuration, waitUntilReady } from "@boatdev/sdk";
import type { CommandResponse } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const boat = new BoatApi(new Configuration({
  basePath: "https://boat.dev/api/v1",
  accessToken: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY!,
}));

const created = await boat.create({ ttlSeconds: 1800 });
const sandboxId = created.sandbox.id;
try {
  await waitUntilReady(boat, sandboxId);
  const result = (await boat.command({ sandboxId, command: "echo hi && uname -a" })) as CommandResponse;
  console.log(result.exitCode);
  console.log(result.stdout);
} finally {
  await boat.stop({ sandboxId });
}
```

* `command()` returns `CommandResponse | CommandStartedResponse`. A normal command gives a `CommandResponse`. A command with `detached: true` gives a `CommandStartedResponse`.
* To delete the sandbox and its snapshots instead of a stop, call `boat.deleteSandbox({ sandboxId, xAsciiConfirmDelete: sandboxId })`.

## Configure

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { BoatApi, Configuration } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const boat = new BoatApi(new Configuration({
  basePath: process.env.BOAT_API_BASE ?? "https://boat.dev/api/v1",
  accessToken: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY!,   // boat_...
}));
```

* Call every API method on `boat` with one object. Method names are camelCase.
* Put the fields of a request body directly in that object, next to the path and query parameters: `boat.fork({ sandboxId, type: "small" })`. The wrapped form also works: `boat.fork({ sandboxId, forkRequest: { type: "small" } })`. The flat form needs 1.1.0 or later.
* Helper functions take `boat` as their first argument: `waitUntilReady`, `waitUntilIdle`, `waitForDesktop`, `waitForPrompt`, `waitForPromptDone`, `streamEvents`, `streamPrompt`, `stopAndRemove`, `readText`, `writeText`, `execCommand`, `streamCommand`, `runCommand`, `followCommand`.

Use these compiler options for the ESM examples, and set `"type": "module"` in `package.json`:

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "lib": ["ES2022", "DOM"],
    "types": ["node"],
    "strict": true
  }
}
```

In CommonJS, use `require`:

```js theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const { BoatApi, Configuration } = require("@boatdev/sdk");

const boat = new BoatApi(new Configuration({
  basePath: "https://boat.dev/api/v1",
  accessToken: process.env.BOAT_API_KEY,
}));
```

## Run commands

A synchronous command times out after 30 seconds by default. Set `timeoutSeconds` up to 600. For a longer command, use [`runCommand`](#run-a-command-with-no-time-limit). A command sent while the sandbox starts waits up to 60 seconds.

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { execCommand } from "@boatdev/sdk";
import type { CommandResponse } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const result = (await boat.command({
  sandboxId,
  command: "npm test",
  cwd: "my-repo",
  timeoutSeconds: 600,
})) as CommandResponse;
console.log(result.exitCode, result.timedOut, result.stdout, result.stderr);

// Same call. It also resends a command that the sandbox refused while it restored its disk.
const again = (await execCommand(boat, sandboxId, "node -v")) as CommandResponse;
```

### Stream the output

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { streamCommand } from "@boatdev/sdk";

for await (const frame of streamCommand(boat, sandboxId, "npm test", { cwd: "my-repo", timeoutSeconds: 600 })) {
  if (frame.type === "stdout" || frame.type === "stderr") process.stdout.write(String(frame.data));
  if (frame.type === "exit") console.log("exit code:", frame.exitCode);
  if (frame.type === "error") console.error(frame.message);
}
```

Pass `signal` (an `AbortSignal`) in the options to stop reading early.

### Run a command with no time limit

`runCommand` has no 600-second limit. It starts the command in the background, then yields its output until the command ends. It reconnects by itself, with no gap and no repeat.

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { runCommand } from "@boatdev/sdk";

for await (const frame of runCommand(boat, sandboxId, "npm run test:e2e", { cwd: "my-repo" })) {
  if (frame.type === "stdout" || frame.type === "stderr") process.stdout.write(String(frame.data));
  if (frame.type === "exit") console.log("exit code:", frame.exitCode);
  if (frame.type === "error") console.error(frame.message);
}
```

* The first frame is `{ type: "started", processId }`.
* A loop that stops early leaves the command running. Stop it with `boat.stopCommand({ sandboxId, processId })`.
* `followCommand(boat, sandboxId, processId)` follows a command that you started with `detached: true`.

### Run a server in the background

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import type { CommandStartedResponse } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const started = (await boat.command({ sandboxId, command: "npm run build", detached: true })) as CommandStartedResponse;

let status = await boat.commandStatus({ sandboxId, processId: started.processId });
while (status.running) {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 2000));
  status = await boat.commandStatus({ sandboxId, processId: started.processId });
}
console.log(status.status, status.exitCode, status.stdout);
```

* `attachCommand({ sandboxId, processId })` streams the output of a detached command.
* `stopCommand({ sandboxId, processId })` stops it and every process that it started.
* `commandHistory` and `commandLogs` read past commands, also while the sandbox is stopped. See [Command history](/long-running-tasks/command-history).

## Files

Small text files:

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { readText, writeText } from "@boatdev/sdk";

await writeText(boat, sandboxId, "notes/result.txt", "done\n");
console.log(await readText(boat, sandboxId, "notes/result.txt"));
```

Paths are relative to `/home/user`. `readFile` and `writeFile` also accept `encoding: "base64"`.

For a file of any size, get a signed URL. Then send the bytes with `fetch`:

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const up = await boat.createUploadUrl({ sandboxId, path: "data/input.csv" });
await fetch(up.url, { method: up.method, body: await readFile("input.csv") });

const down = await boat.createDownloadUrl({ sandboxId, path: "data/input.csv" });
const bytes = await (await fetch(down.url)).arrayBuffer();
```

The URLs expire. Treat them as secrets.

### Copy a local folder in

Pack the folder, upload it, unpack it on the sandbox. In a git checkout, send the files that git tracks and the new files that `.gitignore` does not exclude. `node_modules` and build output stay out. This uses the `git` and `tar` commands of your machine:

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { lstatSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { execCommand } from "@boatdev/sdk";
import type { BoatApi } from "@boatdev/sdk";

// Skip a file that git tracks but that you deleted, and a submodule (a directory entry).
function isFileOrLink(path: string): boolean {
  try { return !lstatSync(path).isDirectory(); } catch { return false; }
}

async function push(boat: BoatApi, sandboxId: string, folder: string, remote = "repo") {
  const listed = execFileSync("git", ["ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"], { cwd: folder })
    .toString().split("\0").filter((name) => name && isFileOrLink(join(folder, name)));
  const packed = execFileSync("tar", ["--null", "--no-recursion", "-czf", "-", "-T", "-"], {
    cwd: folder, input: listed.join("\0"), maxBuffer: 4 * 1024 ** 3,
  });
  const up = await boat.createUploadUrl({ sandboxId, path: "push.tgz" });
  await fetch(up.url, { method: up.method, body: packed });
  await execCommand(boat, sandboxId, `mkdir -p ${remote} && tar xzf push.tgz -C ${remote} && rm push.tgz`, undefined, 600);
}
```

The archive keeps the exec bit and keeps links as links. It skips submodules. `boat push <id> <dir>` in the CLI also copies submodules.

## Run one job and delete the sandbox

Create a sandbox, copy the code in, run one command, read the cost, delete the sandbox. This is what `boat run` does in the CLI.

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { runCommand, waitUntilReady } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const created = await boat.create({ from: "ci-base", type: "large", ttlSeconds: 3600 });
const sandboxId = created.sandbox.id;
let code: unknown;
try {
  await waitUntilReady(boat, sandboxId);
  await push(boat, sandboxId, ".");
  for await (const frame of runCommand(boat, sandboxId, "npm ci && npm test", { cwd: "repo" })) {
    if (frame.type === "stdout" || frame.type === "stderr") process.stdout.write(String(frame.data));
    if (frame.type === "exit") code = frame.exitCode;
  }
  const usage = await boat.usage({ sandboxId });
  console.log(`exit ${code} · ${usage.seconds}s · ${usage.sandboxType} · $${usage.dollars.toFixed(4)}`);
} finally {
  await boat.deleteSandbox({ sandboxId, xAsciiConfirmDelete: sandboxId });
}
process.exitCode = typeof code === "number" ? code : 1;
```

* The script exits with the exit code of the command, so a failed test fails the CI job.
* `ttlSeconds` stops the sandbox if your script dies before the delete. Set it above your longest job.
* `usage()` gives the machine time and the cost of one sandbox. It also works after a stop.

## Public URL for a port

The TypeScript field for `public` is `_public`, because `public` is a reserved word:

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await boat.command({ sandboxId, command: "python3 -m http.server 8000", detached: true });
const hosted = await boat.hostPort({ sandboxId, port: 8000, _public: true });
console.log(hosted.url);   // https://<sandbox>-8000.on.boat.dev
```

Without `_public: true`, the URL is private and carries a `_token`. See [Public URLs](/hosting).

## Machine size

Pass `type`: `small`, `default` (the medium size), `large` or `xlarge`. `xlarge` needs the \$100 plan or higher. The [free trial](/free-trial) allows only `small` and `default`.

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const created = await boat.create({ type: "large", ttlSeconds: 3600 });
const info = await boat.get({ sandboxId: created.sandbox.id });
console.log(info.sandbox.type, info.sandbox.vcpu, info.sandbox.memoryGB);
```

A fork gets the size of its source. To change the size of a sandbox, stop it, then `resume({ sandboxId, type: "large" })`. See [Sandbox sizes](/machines).

To know which types your account can create now, read `limits()`. A blocked type carries the reason:

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
for (const t of (await boat.limits({})).machineTypes ?? []) {
  console.log(t.type, t.available ? "ok" : t.reason);
}
```

## Per-sandbox environment variables

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const created = await boat.create({
  ttlSeconds: 3600,
  env: { DATABASE_URL: "postgres://user:pass@host:5432/app", FEATURE_FLAG: "1" },
});
```

The values come on top of the [environment](/environments) of the sandbox. A per-sandbox value wins. The maximum is 100 variables and 64 KB in total. A fork gets the `env` of its source, unless you give the fork its own `env`.

## No-env sandboxes

For a sandbox that you give to your own users, set `noEnv: true`. boat then gives it none of your secrets: model keys, GitHub token, environment variables, secret files and SSH identity. SSH, desktop, snapshots, public URLs and forks still work. A fork of a no-env sandbox is always no-env.

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const created = await boat.create({ ttlSeconds: 1800, noEnv: true });
await boat.resume({ sandboxId, noEnv: true });
const forked = await boat.fork({ sandboxId, noEnv: true });
```

## Saved snapshots and forks

Save a sandbox under a name. Then start new sandboxes from it:

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";

await boat.saveSavedSnapshot({ sandboxId, name: "web-stack" });
let snap = (await boat.getSavedSnapshot({ name: "web-stack" })).snapshot;
while (snap.status !== "ready" && snap.status !== "failed") {
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 5000));
  snap = (await boat.getSavedSnapshot({ name: "web-stack" })).snapshot;
}

const fromTemplate = await boat.create({ idempotencyKey: randomUUID(), from: "web-stack", ttlSeconds: 900 });
const forked = await boat.fork({ sandboxId, idempotencyKey: randomUUID(), ttlSeconds: 900 });
console.log(fromTemplate.sandbox.id, forked.sandbox?.id);
```

* `idempotencyKey` makes a create or a fork safe to retry. See [Idempotent sandbox creation](/api/v1#idempotent-sandbox-creation).
* A fork of a running sandbox uses its last background snapshot. Files written after it can be missing.

## Prompt an integrated agent

Connect a key or a subscription on the dashboard (Agents & Proxying) first. Without it, `prompt` rejects with status 409 and code `provider_not_configured`.

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { waitForPrompt } from "@boatdev/sdk";

const queued = await boat.prompt({ sandboxId, provider: "codex", prompt: "Run the tests and fix the failures." });
// Add an instruction to the running turn without stopping it:
await boat.steer({ sandboxId, message: "Skip the integration tests." });

const run = await waitForPrompt(boat, sandboxId, queued.promptId);
console.log(run.status);

const events = await boat.events({ sandboxId, limit: 50, type: "prompt,response" });
for (const event of events.events) console.log(event.type);
```

* `provider` is one of 7 harnesses: `codex`, `claude-code` (alias `claude`), `pi`, `opencode`, `prime-agent` (alias `prime`), `kimi` and `mistral`. Omit it to use the default from the dashboard.
* A sandbox runs [many conversations in parallel](/integrated-agents). Pass `new: true` for a new one, or `conversationId` to continue one.
* `interrupt({ sandboxId, conversation })` discards the running turn. `steer` keeps it running.

### Stream the agent's work

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { streamPrompt } from "@boatdev/sdk";

for await (const event of streamPrompt(boat, sandboxId, { provider: "codex", prompt: "Run pwd and ls." })) {
  if (event.type !== "response") continue;
  const data = (event as any).data;
  if (data?.tools?.length) console.log("tools", data.tools);
  if (data?.content) process.stdout.write(data.content);
}
```

For all events of a sandbox, use `streamEvents(boat, sandboxId, { type: "prompt,response", signal })`. Stop it with an `AbortController`.

## Browse a stopped sandbox

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const latest = await boat.getLatestSandboxSnapshot({ sandboxId });
const tree = await boat.getSnapshotTree({ snapshotId: latest.snapshot!.id });
const blob = await boat.getSnapshotFile({ snapshotId: latest.snapshot!.id, path: "projects/app/.env" });
```

## Errors

A non-2xx response rejects with a `ResponseError`. Read the status and parse the JSON body. Redact API keys, secrets, SSH keys and desktop URLs.

```ts theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { ResponseError } from "@boatdev/sdk";

try {
  await boat.get({ sandboxId: "bx_missing" });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof ResponseError) {
    console.error(error.response.status);
    console.error((await error.response.json()).code);
  }
}
```

The codes and the retry rules are on [API overview](/api/v1#error-model) and [Limits](/limits).

## Methods

Each method takes one object. `...body` means the fields of the request body. The list comes from the [OpenAPI file](/openapi/boat-v1.yaml).

### Sandboxes

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `sandboxes({ org, xBoatOrg, limit, cursor, sort, state })` | `GET /sandboxes` | List sandboxes |
| `create({ idempotencyKey, org, xBoatOrg, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes` | Create sandbox |
| `get({ sandboxId })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` | Get sandbox |
| `update({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `PATCH /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` | Update sandbox |
| `deleteSandbox({ sandboxId, xAsciiConfirmDelete })` | `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}` | Delete sandbox |
| `stop({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stop` | Stop sandbox |
| `share({ sandboxId })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/share` | Share sandbox with the organization |
| `recover({ sandboxId })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/recover` | Deprecated. Recover a sandbox that stopped responding |
| `resume({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/resume` | Resume sandbox |
| `fork({ sandboxId, idempotencyKey, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/fork` | Fork sandbox |
| `getStop({ sandboxId, stopId })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/stops/{stopId}` | Get a stop |
| `usage({ sandboxId, since, until })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/usage` | Get sandbox usage |

### Commands

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `command({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands` | Run a command |
| `commandStatus({ sandboxId, processId, tailBytes, stdoutOffset, stderrOffset })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}` | Get command status |
| `stopCommand({ sandboxId, processId })` | `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}` | Stop a detached command |
| `attachCommand({ sandboxId, processId, stdoutOffset, stderrOffset })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands/{processId}/stream` | Attach to a detached command |
| `commandHistory({ sandboxId, mode, q, limit, cursor })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/command-history` | List the command and process history |
| `getCommand({ sandboxId, commandId })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/command-history/{commandId}` | Get one command from the history |
| `commandLogs({ sandboxId, commandId, stream, offset, limit, encoding })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/command-history/{commandId}/logs` | Read command logs |
| `processes({ sandboxId })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/processes` | List the processes in a sandbox |

### Files and access

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `readFile({ sandboxId, path, encoding })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files` | Read a file |
| `writeFile({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `PUT /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files` | Write a file |
| `createDownloadUrl({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/download-url` | Get a download URL for a sandbox file |
| `createUploadUrl({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/files/upload-url` | Get an upload URL for a sandbox file |
| `artifact({ sandboxId, path })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/artifacts` | Download a file |
| `desktop({ sandboxId, vnc, theme, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/desktop` | Get the desktop URL |
| `hostPort({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/host` | Expose a port on a public URL |
| `sshKey({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/sshkey` | Add an SSH key |

### Integrated agents

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `prompt({ sandboxId, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/prompt` | Prompt the agent |
| `events({ sandboxId, limit, cursor, sort, type, conversation })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/events` | List sandbox events |
| `conversations({ sandboxId })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/conversations` | List conversations |
| `promptRunStatus({ sandboxId, promptId })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/prompts/{promptId}` | Get prompt run status |
| `steer({ sandboxId, conversation, ...body })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/steer` | Steer a running turn (API) |
| `interrupt({ sandboxId, conversation })` | `POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/interrupt` | Interrupt running work |

### Snapshots

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `listSnapshots({ limit, cursor, sort })` | `GET /snapshots` | List snapshots |
| `listSandboxSnapshots({ sandboxId, limit, cursor, sort })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots` | List snapshots of a sandbox |
| `deleteSandboxSnapshots({ sandboxId, xAsciiConfirmDelete })` | `DELETE /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots` | Delete all snapshots of a sandbox |
| `getLatestSandboxSnapshot({ sandboxId })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/snapshots/latest` | Get the latest snapshot of a sandbox |
| `deleteSnapshot({ snapshotId, xAsciiConfirmDelete })` | `DELETE /snapshots/{snapshotId}` | Delete snapshot |
| `getSnapshotTree({ snapshotId })` | `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/tree` | Get snapshot file tree |
| `getSnapshotFile({ snapshotId, path })` | `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/files` | Download a file or folder from a snapshot |
| `getSnapshotDownload({ snapshotId })` | `GET /snapshots/{snapshotId}/download` | Get snapshot download |

### Saved snapshots

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `listSavedSnapshots()` | `GET /saved-snapshots` | List saved snapshots |
| `saveSavedSnapshot({ ...body })` | `POST /saved-snapshots` | Save a saved snapshot |
| `getSavedSnapshot({ name })` | `GET /saved-snapshots/{name}` | Get a saved snapshot |
| `deleteSavedSnapshot({ name })` | `DELETE /saved-snapshots/{name}` | Delete a saved snapshot |
| `listSnapshotShares({ name })` | `GET /saved-snapshots/{name}/shares` | List share codes of a saved snapshot |
| `createSnapshotShare({ name })` | `POST /saved-snapshots/{name}/shares` | Share a saved snapshot |
| `revokeSnapshotShare({ name, shareId })` | `DELETE /saved-snapshots/{name}/shares/{shareId}` | Revoke a share code |

### Environments and repositories

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |
| `repos({ sync, limit, cursor, sort, q, selected })` | `GET /repos` | List GitHub repositories |
| `selectRepo({ ...body })` | `POST /repos` | Select a repository |
| `secrets()` | `GET /secrets` | Get account secrets (legacy) |
| `updateSecrets({ ...body })` | `POST /secrets` | Update account secrets (legacy) |
| `environments({ org })` | `GET /environments` | List environments |
| `createEnvironment({ org, ...body })` | `POST /environments` | Create an environment |
| `updateEnvironment({ environmentId, org, ...body })` | `PUT /environments/{environmentId}` | Update an environment |
| `deleteEnvironment({ environmentId, org })` | `DELETE /environments/{environmentId}` | Delete an environment |
| `upgradeEnvironment({ environmentId, org, ...body })` | `POST /environments/{environmentId}/upgrade` | Upgrade sandboxes to the latest environment version |
| `setEnvironmentVar({ environmentId, key, org, ...body })` | `PUT /environments/{environmentId}/vars/{key}` | Set one environment variable |
| `deleteEnvironmentVar({ environmentId, key, org })` | `DELETE /environments/{environmentId}/vars/{key}` | Remove one environment variable |
| `setEnvironmentSecretFile({ environmentId, org, ...body })` | `PUT /environments/{environmentId}/secret-files` | Write one secret file |
| `deleteEnvironmentSecretFile({ environmentId, org, path })` | `DELETE /environments/{environmentId}/secret-files` | Remove one secret file |
| `addEnvironmentRepo({ environmentId, org, ...body })` | `POST /environments/{environmentId}/repos` | Add a repository to an environment |
| `deleteEnvironmentRepo({ environmentId, repositoryId, org })` | `DELETE /environments/{environmentId}/repos/{repositoryId}` | Remove a repository from an environment |

### AI credentials

| Method | Endpoint | Does |
| - | - | - |

| `setCredentialProfileKey({ profile, credential, ...body })` | `PUT /credential-profiles/{profile}/keys/{credential}` | Set a credential profile API key |
| `deleteCredentialProfileKey({ profile, credential })` | `DELETE /credential-profiles/{profile}/keys/{credential}` | Remove a credential profile credential |
| `listCredentialAccounts({ profile, credential })` | `GET /credential-profiles/{profile}/accounts/{credential}` | List the accounts of a credential |

| `switchCredentialAccount({ profile, credential, account })` | `PUT /credential-profiles/{profile}/accounts/{credential}/{account}/active` | Switch a credential to another account |

| `getAiProxy({ org, xBoatOrg })` | `GET /ai-proxy` | Get AI credentials proxy |
| `updateAiProxy({ org, xBoatOrg, ...body })` | `PUT /ai-proxy` | Turn the AI credentials proxy on or off |
| `getAiUsage({ days, profile, org, xBoatOrg })` | `GET /ai-usage` | Get AI usage |
| `getSandboxAiUsage({ sandboxId, days })` | `GET /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/ai-usage` | Get sandbox AI usage |

# Security and isolation
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/security

How boat isolates sandboxes, who can reach a sandbox, which credentials it holds, network rules, URLs with tokens, team access, data retention, compliance and uptime. Each topic links to its detail page.

This page is the map of boat security. Each section is short and links to the page that has the details.

| Question | Short answer | Details |
| - | - | - |
| Can one sandbox see another? | No. Each sandbox is its own virtual machine. | [Isolation](#isolation-between-sandboxes) |
| Who can open my sandbox? | You. Members of your organization, for sandboxes it pays for. People you share it with. | [Who can reach a sandbox](#who-can-reach-a-sandbox) |
| Which of my secrets are inside? | What your environment gives. None with **Safe for third parties**. | [Credentials](#boat-credentials-inside-a-sandbox) |
| Can it reach the internet? | Outbound yes. Inbound only SSH and the ports you publish. | [Network](#network) |
| Who can open a public URL? | Anyone with the full URL. | [URLs that carry a token](#urls-that-carry-a-token) |
| How long is my data kept? Can I erase it? | At least 14 days after a stop. Delete erases it. | [Data](#data) |
| SOC 2? Uptime? | SOC 2 in progress. 99.95% measured sandbox uptime. Platform status on [status.ascii.dev](https://status.ascii.dev). | [Compliance and uptime](/compliance) |

## Give sandboxes to end users

To give an end user a sandbox, do these three things:

1. Start the sandbox in an environment with **Safe for third parties** on, or with `boat new --no-env`. No secret of yours goes in.
2. Give the user an API key limited to that one sandbox, if they need the API.
3. Treat every URL with a token as a password.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat env new customers
boat env set customers --safe-for-third-parties true
boat new --environment customers --json
boat api-key create tenant-42 --preset full-sandbox --sandbox bx_123 --ttl 30d
```

## Isolation between sandboxes

* Each sandbox is its own virtual machine, with its own kernel, disk and IP address.
* Sandboxes share no disk and no processes. They reach each other only over the network.
* The `user` account has passwordless `sudo`. Anyone with a shell in a sandbox is root in that sandbox.
* So treat everything inside a sandbox as readable and changeable by its user. This includes files, environment variables and the browser profile.
* The security boundary is between sandboxes and between accounts. Inside a sandbox, use normal Linux tools (users, file permissions, firewall rules) as on any server.

### One sandbox per end user

Give each end user their own sandbox. Containers inside one sandbox share its kernel, so boat does not isolate them from each other. boat also does not clean a sandbox between your users.

* To start fast, save a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates) and start each user's sandbox with `boat new --from <name>`.
* If you must reuse one sandbox for many users, assume each user looks for traces of the user before. Run each job as a new Linux user, delete its files after the job, and keep no keys in the sandbox.

## Who can reach a sandbox

| Who | What they can do | Details |
| - | - | - |
| You, the creator | Everything | |
| Members of your organization | See every sandbox the organization pays for. Use it if it is shared: it holds no personal logins and its creator did not make it private. | [Shared sandboxes](/organizations/shared-sandboxes) |
| People you share a sandbox with | What the share allows | [Shared sandboxes](/organizations/shared-sandboxes) |
| An API key | What its scopes allow. A key limited with `--sandbox` reaches one sandbox only. | [Scopes](/api-keys/scopes) |
| An SSH key you added | A shell as `user` | [SSH access](/ssh-access) |
| Anyone with a URL that carries a token | That one port or desktop | [URLs that carry a token](#urls-that-carry-a-token) |

Snapshots and personal environments stay private to the person who made them. Read [Teams and organizations](/organizations).

## boat credentials inside a sandbox

| Credential | Where | What it can do | Safe for third parties / `--no-env` |
| - | - | - | - |
| `ASCII_TOKEN` | Environment variable, `~/.bashrc` | Host ports of its own sandbox. Nothing else. | Stays |
| In-sandbox API key | `~/.config/ascii/boat/config.json` | Read, stop, exec, files, SSH, desktop, host and snapshots, on its own sandbox only. Read [Scopes](/api-keys/scopes#in-sandbox-api-key). | Removed |
| Your environment variables and secret files | Environment, files you configured | Whatever the secret allows | Removed |
| GitHub token, `gh` login, git credentials | `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`, `~/.git-credentials` | Your repositories | Removed |
| AI logins and keys | `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/` and others | Your AI provider accounts | Removed, or replaced by [proxy placeholders](/ai-credentials#the-ai-credentials-proxy) |

`ASCII_TOKEN` lets the user publish any port of their sandbox on a public URL under that sandbox's subdomain. It cannot reach your account or other sandboxes.

For the full list of what a protected sandbox does not receive, read [Access and credentials](/environments/access#what-a-normal-sandbox-receives).

### Check a sandbox

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat exec bx_123 'echo "[$STRIPE_KEY]"; ls ~/.config/ascii/boat/config.json ~/.git-credentials 2>&1'
```

A protected sandbox prints `[]` and `No such file or directory` for each file.

### Sandboxes made from your own snapshots

A snapshot of a normal sandbox can contain your secrets. Resume or fork it with `--no-env` before an end user gets it. boat removes the owner secrets before the sandbox becomes reachable. Read [Protect an existing sandbox](/environments/access#protect-an-existing-sandbox).

## API keys for end users

| Need | Use |
| - | - |
| The user works in one sandbox | `--preset full-sandbox --sandbox <id>` |
| The user only reads | `--preset read-only --sandbox <id>` |
| Your backend creates sandboxes | `--preset ci`. Keep this key on your server. |

* A key limited with `--sandbox` cannot see or touch other sandboxes. It cannot list keys or read billing.
* `full-sandbox` cannot create, resume, fork or delete. Your backend does that.
* Use a short `--ttl`. Revoke the key when the user leaves.
* Never give an end user an `admin` key or a key with `account.admin`. These can create more keys.

Read [Scopes](/api-keys/scopes).

## Network

| Direction | Default | How to change it |
| - | - | - |
| Inbound | Refused, except SSH and the ports that boat uses | `host <port>` for a public URL. `ufw allow` for a raw port. Read [Public URLs](/hosting#raw-tcp-or-udp-ports). |
| Outbound | Open to the internet | Firewall rules inside the sandbox. Read [Block outbound internet](/hosting/firewall#block-outbound-internet-for-untrusted-code). |

* boat has no API setting for network rules.
* The user is root, so the user can remove rules that you add as root. To keep a rule, run the untrusted code as a separate account without `sudo`.
* Snapshots do not keep firewall rules. Apply them again after each resume and fork.

## URLs that carry a token

| URL | Who can open it | How long |
| - | - | - |
| Protected public URL (`?_token=`) | Anyone with the full URL. No boat sign-in. | Until you replace the token. Read [Replace a leaked token](/hosting#replace-a-leaked-token). |
| Public URL with `--public` | Anyone | Until `host hide` |
| Desktop URL (Moonlight) | Anyone with the full URL | Open within 10 minutes. Read [Embed the desktop](/desktop-streaming/urls-and-security#how-long-a-desktop-url-works). |
| VNC desktop URL | Anyone with the full URL | Until the port becomes public |
| Signed file upload or download URL | Anyone with the URL | 15 minutes, up to 1 hour. Read [Large files](/ssh-access#large-files). |
