To stop auto-stop for a long job:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --hours 12     # sets the auto-stop to 12 hours from now
boat extend bx_f7k2q9hd --no-auto-stop # runs until you stop it
```

Read [Auto-stop](/long-running-tasks/auto-stop). To never stop for an empty wallet, turn on **Auto top-up** on the [Billing](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing) tab, or run `boat wallet auto-top-up 50`.

## A sandbox does not answer

If commands and SSH hang, boat marks the sandbox as not answering. boat sends you an email. **Billing pauses while it does not answer.** The disk stays on the machine.

Do these steps in this order:

1. Wait a few minutes. After a kernel crash, the machine restarts by itself in about 15 seconds. The disk is not touched. A sandbox that answers again reconnects by itself, with all its data.
2. If it still does not answer, run `boat stop --force <id>`, then `boat resume <id>`. The sandbox comes back from its last good snapshot. **You lose what was written after that snapshot.** `snapshotCompletedAt` in `boat info` shows its time.
3. If the sandbox never completed a snapshot, do not stop it. [Contact us](/support). We get the disk back by hand.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat stop --force bx_f7k2q9hd
boat resume bx_f7k2q9hd
```

After 3 days without an answer, boat stops the sandbox. It falls back to its last snapshot. boat sends a reminder one day before.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `boat recover` and `POST /sandboxes/{id}/recover` are deprecated. boat removes them soon. Use the steps above.

## A sandbox is in error

`error` means that boat lost contact with the machine, or that a start failed. `boat info` shows the reason in `error`.

| Question | Answer |
| - | - |
| Am I billed? | No. Billing stops while the sandbox is in `error` |
| Is my data safe? | boat keeps the machine and its disk for 3 days. Everything up to the last snapshot is safe in any case |
| Does boat fix it by itself? | Sometimes. If the last snapshot is newer than the failure, boat rebuilds the sandbox on a new machine from that snapshot and sends you an email |
| Can I run commands? | No. Commands fail with `409 sandbox_not_ready` |

Do these steps in this order:

1. Read the reason: `boat info <id>`. Check your email from boat.
2. If it is still in `error`, run `boat resume <id>`. You lose what was written after `snapshotCompletedAt`.
3. If you cannot lose that work, do not resume. [Contact us](/support) within 3 days.

After 3 days, boat stops the sandbox. It falls back to its last snapshot.

To stop an errored sandbox without a resume, run `boat stop <id>`. To erase it, read [Delete a sandbox](/data-retention/delete).

## A command was killed: exit code 137 (out of memory)

Your programs can use all the RAM of the size except 512 MiB. boat keeps that part for its own services. Above that limit, Linux kills the process that uses the most memory. The sandbox stays up.

* The killed command ends with `exitCode` 137, and the command result shows `oomKilled: true`.
* Other processes and the sandbox keep running.
* Use less memory, or move to a bigger size. Read [Change size](/machines/change-size).

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat stop bx_f7k2q9hd
until [ "$(boat info bx_f7k2q9hd --json | jq -r .sandbox.state)" = "stopped" ]; do sleep 2; done
boat resume bx_f7k2q9hd --type large
```

## Out-of-disk emails

boat reads the disk use of each running sandbox and emails you:

| Disk use | Email |
| - | - |
| 85% | A warning. Free space before the disk fills. |
| 95% | "Out of disk". Snapshots fail, so your newest work is not saved. A stop also fails. |

You get at most one email per level per day for each sandbox. When space gets low, boat deletes caches that it can download again: the apt cache, journal logs and pulled Docker images that no container uses. boat never deletes your own files.

To free space:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd
docker system prune      # unused Docker data
sudo apt-get clean       # apt download cache
```

If the sandbox needs more disk, stop it and resume it with a bigger `--type`. If you cannot get in, [contact us](/support). Do not resume from an old snapshot if you need the unsaved work.

## A stop does not finish

A stop saves the disk first. If the save fails, boat refuses the stop, keeps the sandbox running and does not bill you while it waits. Read [When a stop is refused](/snapshots/stop#when-a-stop-is-refused).

`boat stop` returns at `stopping`. A short `stopping` is normal. To wait for `stopped`, read [Wait for the stop in a script](/snapshots/stop#wait-for-the-stop-in-a-script).

## Error messages

### `409 snapshot_data_expired`

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
This sandbox's data was deleted after it was stopped for at least 14 days. Save a saved snapshot to keep data: boat snapshot <id> <name>.
```

boat deleted this sandbox's data after it had been stopped for at least 14 days. Resume, fork and a saved snapshot save of this sandbox fail. You cannot get the data back. The sandbox stays in your list until you delete it.

Next time, save a saved snapshot before day 14. Read [Keep a stopped sandbox longer than 14 days](/snapshots/stop#keep-a-stopped-sandbox-longer-than-14-days).

### `409 sandbox_starting`

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
Sandbox is still starting (current state: provisioned); environment and secrets are not applied yet. Retry when the sandbox is ready.
```

The API held your command for 60 seconds, and the sandbox was still starting. Send the command again. Read [Readiness and resume speed](/readiness).

### `409 sandbox_not_ready`

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
Sandbox bx_abc12345 is in error: <reason>. Run `boat resume bx_abc12345`, then retry.
```

The sandbox is in `error` or another state that cannot run commands. Run `boat resume <id>`. For `error`, read [A sandbox is in error](#a-sandbox-is-in-error).

### `409 machine_not_running`

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
Sandbox bx_abc12345 is stopped. Run `boat resume bx_abc12345`, then retry.
```

The sandbox has no machine now. Usually its TTL ran out or someone stopped it. Run the `boat resume` command from the message. The body also carries `state`, and `retryable` is `true` only while the sandbox is still starting.

### `409 sandbox_stopping`

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
Sandbox is still stopping and would resume on its live machine, which cannot switch size.
```

A resume during `stopping` keeps the same machine. It cannot change the size, the environment, the provider or the host. The stop finishes in a few seconds. The answer carries a `Retry-After` header and the running stop operation. Wait that many seconds, or wait for `stopped`. Then run the same resume again.

### `429 rate_limited`

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
You used all 200 sandbox starts included in the last 24 hours.
Your running sandboxes keep running. New ones can start again at 14:32 UTC.

Need more now? Pick one:
  1. Pay per extra start, from $0.03 each, on your next invoice, up to $80 a month.
     boat billing extra-starts on
  2. Move to the $100 plan, 840 starts included a day.
     boat billing plan 100
  3. Add seats to your team, each seat adds 20% more starts, up to the next plan.
     https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=billing
```

Nothing is broken. Create, fork and resume each count as one start. Run one of the commands, or wait until that time. Read [Limits and errors](/limits).

### `429 trial_compute_limit_reached`

```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
Trial Sandbox compute is limited to 25 hours total. Stopping, forking, or resuming does not reset that allowance.
```

The free trial used its 25 hours. The first payment removes this limit. Read [Free trial](/free-trial).

### `503 no_ready_machine`

You sent `failFast` and no machine of that size was free. Nothing was created or billed. Retry, or fall back to another size. Read [Fail fast when no machine is free](/machines/fail-fast).

### `402 credit_required`

You keep your plan's included saved snapshots or more, and you saved one more with an empty wallet. Add money with `boat wallet pay 20`, or remove a saved snapshot. Read [Saved snapshot pricing](/snapshots/templates#saved-snapshot-pricing).

## Still stuck

[Contact us](/support). Send the sandbox id and the output of `boat info <id>`.


# Webhooks
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/webhooks

Receive signed notifications when a sandbox becomes ready, finishes restoring, fails, stops, degrades or recovers.

A webhook sends sandbox lifecycle events to your HTTPS endpoint. One webhook gets the events of all the sandboxes in your account.

Use webhooks to:

* Start work when a sandbox is usable.
* Respond when a sandbox fails to start.
* Continue an automation after a sandbox stops.

boat sends 6 events: `sandbox.ready`, `sandbox.hydrated`, `sandbox.error`, `sandbox.archived` (stopped), `sandbox.degraded` and `sandbox.recovered`. Read [Events](#events).

| | CLI | API | SDKs | Dashboard |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| Register | `boat webhook create` | `POST /webhooks` | `createWebhook` | [Webhooks & OTel](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=webhooks) |
| List / read | `boat webhook list` | `GET /webhooks`, `GET /webhooks/{id}` | `listWebhooks`, `getWebhook` | [Webhooks & OTel](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=webhooks) |
| Edit in place | not available | `PATCH /webhooks/{id}` | `updateWebhook` | not available |
| Rotate secret | `boat webhook rotate` | `POST /webhooks/{id}/rotate` | `rotateWebhookSigningSecret` | [Webhooks & OTel](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=webhooks) |
| Remove | `boat webhook remove` | `DELETE /webhooks/{id}` | `deleteWebhook` | [Webhooks & OTel](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=webhooks) |
| Delivery history | not available | not available | not available | [Webhooks & OTel](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=webhooks) → Deliveries |

## Register an endpoint

The examples use `BOAT_API_BASE=https://boat.dev/api/v1`. The API key needs the `account.admin` action.

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat webhook create https://example.com/hooks/sandbox \
  --name production \
  --event ready \
  --event error \
  --event archived
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/webhooks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "production",
    "url": "https://example.com/hooks/sandbox",
    "events": ["sandbox.ready", "sandbox.error", "sandbox.archived"]
  }'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
const created = await sandbox.createWebhook({
  name: "production",
  url: "https://example.com/hooks/sandbox",
  events: new Set(["sandbox.ready", "sandbox.error", "sandbox.archived"]),
});
console.log(created.webhook.id, created.secret);   // secret is shown once
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.webhook_create_request import WebhookCreateRequest

created = sandbox.create_webhook(WebhookCreateRequest(
    name="production",
    url="https://example.com/hooks/sandbox",
    events=["sandbox.ready", "sandbox.error", "sandbox.archived"],
))
print(created.webhook.id, created.secret)   # secret is shown once
```

How to name events:

| Surface | Event names | If you give no event |
| - | - | - |
| CLI `--event` | `ready`, `error`, `archived`, `hydrated`, `degraded` or `recovered`. The `sandbox.` prefix is optional. | You get all six events. |
| API and SDKs | The full name, for example `sandbox.ready`. | The call fails. You must give at least one event. |

The call returns a signing secret that starts with `whsec_`. **You see this secret only once.** Store it in your secret manager.

> [!NOTE]
>
> The endpoint must use HTTPS on port 443. Its address must resolve only to public IP addresses. boat does not follow redirects. An account can register up to 10 endpoint URLs.

## Manage endpoints

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat webhook list
boat webhook rotate <id>   # replaces the signing secret
boat webhook remove <id>
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/webhooks" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS "$BOAT_API_BASE/webhooks/$WEBHOOK_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X PATCH "$BOAT_API_BASE/webhooks/$WEBHOOK_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"events":["sandbox.error"]}'

curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/webhooks/$WEBHOOK_ID/rotate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"

curl -sS -X DELETE "$BOAT_API_BASE/webhooks/$WEBHOOK_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY"
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.listWebhooks();
await sandbox.getWebhook({ webhookId: "wh_0123456789abcdef01234567" });

await sandbox.updateWebhook({
  webhookId: "wh_0123456789abcdef01234567",
  events: new Set(["sandbox.error"]),
});

const rotated = await sandbox.rotateWebhookSigningSecret({ webhookId: "wh_0123456789abcdef01234567" });
console.log(rotated.secret);

await sandbox.deleteWebhook({ webhookId: "wh_0123456789abcdef01234567" });
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.webhook_update_request import WebhookUpdateRequest

sandbox.list_webhooks()
sandbox.get_webhook("wh_0123456789abcdef01234567")

sandbox.update_webhook(
    "wh_0123456789abcdef01234567",
    WebhookUpdateRequest(events=["sandbox.error"]),
)

rotated = sandbox.rotate_webhook_signing_secret("wh_0123456789abcdef01234567")
print(rotated.secret)

sandbox.delete_webhook("wh_0123456789abcdef01234567")
```

The [Webhooks & OTel](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=webhooks) tab of the dashboard does the same tasks. Only the dashboard shows the delivery history.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Only the API and SDKs can change the name, URL or events of an endpoint in place (`PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}`). The CLI and the dashboard cannot edit an endpoint. Delete it and create it again. This gives you a new signing secret.

When you rotate the secret, accept the old secret and the new secret for a short time. A delivery attempt that already started can still carry the old signature.

When you delete an endpoint, boat removes its queued deliveries. A delivery attempt that already started can still arrive.

## Events

| Event | boat sends it when |
| - | - |
| `sandbox.ready` | A sandbox becomes usable (`ready`, `idle` or `running`) after it was not usable. This includes recovery from an error. boat can run commands now. Your own services and Docker containers can need more seconds to start. |
| `sandbox.hydrated` | A restored sandbox finishes materializing. See [After a restore](#after-a-restore). |
| `sandbox.error` | A sandbox enters `error`. |
| `sandbox.archived` | A sandbox is stopped. The API reports a stopped sandbox as `archived`. |
| `sandbox.degraded` | The machine is alive, but boat cannot fully reach it. boat sends this about a minute after the machine stops answering. The sandbox keeps running. boat does not stop it. `data.reason` gives the cause. |
| `sandbox.recovered` | A degraded sandbox is fully reachable again. This happens on the same machine, or on a new machine after a resume or an automatic recovery. |

boat creates `sandbox.ready`, `sandbox.error` and `sandbox.archived` in the same database transaction as the state change.

### After a restore

`sandbox.hydrated` arrives after `sandbox.ready`. It can arrive at the same moment, or minutes later.

1. The sandbox becomes `ready`. boat sends `sandbox.ready`.
2. The Docker containers of the sandbox start as soon as their images load.
3. The background disk copy finishes. The Docker volumes move onto the real disk.
4. Each running container's volume mounts move onto the real disk in place. The containers pause for about 0.1 s. They do not restart.
5. boat sends `sandbox.hydrated`.

To poll instead, read `hydrated` and `hydratedAt` on `GET /sandboxes/{id}`.

### Degraded sandboxes

A degraded sandbox shows `"health": "degraded"` and a `healthReason` on `GET /sandboxes/{id}`. The most common cause is a firewall rule inside the sandbox that blocks the boat tunnel. See [Firewall rules](/hosting/firewall).

## Payload

```json theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
{
  "id": "evt_2af97cd17a8248bb8fe37653a235bc91",
  "type": "sandbox.ready",
  "createdAt": "2026-08-11T12:00:00.000Z",
  "data": {
    "sandbox": {
      "id": "bx_23456789",
      "name": "Production worker"
    },
    "previousState": "cloning",
    "state": "ready"
  }
}
```

* `data.sandbox.id` is the public sandbox ID.
* Use the top-level event `id` as an idempotency key.

The fields in `data` change with the event:

| Event | `previousState` | `state` | `reason` |
| - | - | - | - |
| `sandbox.ready`, `sandbox.error`, `sandbox.archived` | yes | yes | no |
| `sandbox.hydrated` | no | no | no |
| `sandbox.degraded`, `sandbox.recovered` | no | yes | yes |

## Verify signatures

Each request has these headers. The header names keep the old `Ascii` prefix.

| Header | Value |
| - | - |
| `X-Ascii-Event` | Event type |
| `X-Ascii-Delivery` | Stable event ID |
| `X-Ascii-Timestamp` | Unix timestamp for this attempt |
| `X-Ascii-Signature` | `v1=` followed by a hex HMAC-SHA256 signature |
| `X-Ascii-Attempt` | Attempt number, starting at 1 |

To verify a request:

1. Compute the expected signature over the exact raw request body:

   ```text theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   HMAC_SHA256(secret, delivery_id + "." + timestamp + "." + raw_body)
   ```

2. Compare the signatures in constant time.

3. Reject old timestamps.

4. Deduplicate on the delivery ID.

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

function verifyWebhook(rawBody: Buffer, headers: Headers, secret: string) {
  const id = headers.get("x-ascii-delivery") ?? "";
  const timestamp = headers.get("x-ascii-timestamp") ?? "";
  const supplied = (headers.get("x-ascii-signature") ?? "").replace(/^v1=/, "");
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(`${id}.${timestamp}.`)
    .update(rawBody)
    .digest("hex");

  const issuedAt = Number(timestamp);
  if (!Number.isFinite(issuedAt) || Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - issuedAt) > 300) return false;
  if (!/^[a-f0-9]{64}$/i.test(supplied)) return false;
  return timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(supplied, "hex"), Buffer.from(expected, "hex"));
}
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
import hmac, re, time
from hashlib import sha256

def verify_webhook(raw_body: bytes, headers, secret: str) -> bool:
    delivery = headers.get("x-ascii-delivery", "")
    timestamp = headers.get("x-ascii-timestamp", "")
    supplied = headers.get("x-ascii-signature", "").removeprefix("v1=")

    try:
        if abs(time.time() - float(timestamp)) > 300:
            return False
    except ValueError:
        return False
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[a-fA-F0-9]{64}", supplied):
        return False

    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode(),
        f"{delivery}.{timestamp}.".encode() + raw_body,
        sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(supplied.lower(), expected)
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> Verify the raw bytes before you parse the JSON. If you serialize the body again, the signature changes.

## Delivery and retries

| Your endpoint | What boat does |
| - | - |
| Returns a `2xx` | Marks the event as delivered. |
| Returns another status, fails to connect, or takes more than 5 seconds | Retries with exponential backoff, up to 8 attempts. |

* Delivery is **at least once**. The same event ID can arrive more than once.
* Events can arrive out of order. Use the ID, creation time and state of each event. Do not rely on the request order.
* Return a `2xx` quickly. Move slow work to your own queue.
* boat keeps completed and exhausted delivery records for 30 days.

## Inspect deliveries

1. Open [Webhooks & OTel](https://boat.dev/dashboard?tab=webhooks) in the boat dashboard.
2. Expand **Deliveries** next to an endpoint.

The log of recent deliveries shows:

* The event that boat sent.
* The exact payload.
* The boat ID and the event ID.
* The number of attempts.
* The HTTP result, or a connection diagnostic.
* The time of the next retry, if there is one.


# Windows apps
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/windows-apps

Run Windows-only desktop software in a sandbox with Wine, let an agent drive it, and reuse the set-up sandbox as a saved snapshot.

A sandbox runs Windows programs on its Linux desktop through [Wine](https://www.winehq.org).

* The programs open as normal windows on the [desktop stream](/desktop-streaming). You can watch them.
* The agents of the sandbox can click, type and read them with the built-in [`computer` tools](/integrated-agents/computer-use).
* You install once. Then you save the sandbox as a [saved snapshot](/snapshots/templates) and start new sandboxes from it.

## Main task

1. [Install Wine](/windows-apps/install-wine) in the sandbox. It takes about 5 minutes.
2. [Install and start the app](/windows-apps/run-apps). Every GUI command needs `DISPLAY=:0`. Check the [tested apps](/windows-apps/tested-apps) first.
3. [Give a prompt to an agent](/windows-apps/agents-and-forks#let-an-agent-drive-it) that uses the app.
4. [Save a saved snapshot and start a sandbox from it](/windows-apps/agents-and-forks#set-up-once-start-many-times) for each task.

If something fails, read [Windows apps troubleshooting](/windows-apps/troubleshooting).

## Learn more

> [card] [Tested apps](/windows-apps/tested-apps)
>
> The apps that run, the extra steps they need, and the apps that do not run.

> [card] [Install Wine](/windows-apps/install-wine)
>
> The install script, and what each part of it does.

> [card] [Run an app](/windows-apps/run-apps)
>
> Install and start an app. Recipes for Steam, Paint.NET, Sysinternals and Direct3D games.

> [card] [Agents and forks](/windows-apps/agents-and-forks)
>
> Let an agent drive the app. Set up once, then start many sandboxes from a saved snapshot.

> [card] [Windows apps troubleshooting](/windows-apps/troubleshooting)
>
> Common errors and their fixes. Licence rules.

# Agents and forks
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/windows-apps/agents-and-forks

Let an agent drive a Windows app in a sandbox. Set up the sandbox once, save it as a saved snapshot, and start a new sandbox from it for each task.

## Let an agent drive it

The Windows apps open as ordinary windows on the sandbox desktop. A prompt is enough. The agent needs a connected AI key first: read [Keys](/integrated-agents/keys).

```bash CLI theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
boat prompt bx_f7k2q9hd --provider claude "Open Notepad++, write a short release note, and save it as release.txt in My Documents"
```

```bash curl theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
curl -sS -X POST "$BOAT_API_BASE/sandboxes/bx_f7k2q9hd/prompt" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BOAT_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"provider":"claude","prompt":"Open Notepad++, write a short release note, and save it as release.txt in My Documents"}'
```

```ts TypeScript theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
await sandbox.prompt({
  sandboxId: "bx_f7k2q9hd",
  provider: "claude",
  prompt: "Open Notepad++, write a short release note, and save it as release.txt in My Documents",
});
```

```python Python theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
from boat_sdk.models.prompt_request import PromptRequest

sandbox.prompt("bx_f7k2q9hd", PromptRequest(
    provider="claude",
    prompt="Open Notepad++, write a short release note, and save it as release.txt in My Documents",
))
```

For scripted steps, `xdotool` and `wmctrl` are installed. Examples:

* `wmctrl -l` lists the open windows.
* `wmctrl -a Notepad++` brings one window to the front.

To record the run, use the [desktop recorder](/desktop-streaming/drive-and-record#record-the-screen).

## Set up once, start many times

The Wine set-up is in `~/.wine` and in the system packages. A snapshot keeps both.

1. Make one sandbox with Wine and the apps that your agents need.

2. Save it as a saved snapshot:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat snapshot bx_f7k2q9hd wine-apps
   ```

3. Start a new sandbox from it for each task:

   ```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
   boat new --from wine-apps
   ```

The saved snapshot does not change when the source sandbox changes. To copy one sandbox in its current state, fork it instead: `boat fork bx_f7k2q9hd`. Read [Saved snapshots](/snapshots/templates).

In our test, a sandbox with Wine and 40 Windows apps (16 GB) gave these results:

| Action | Time | Result |
| - | - | - |
| Fork | About 2 minutes until the desktop accepts windows | Every app starts. Notepad++ keeps its unsaved text. |
| Stop | 4 seconds | |
| Resume | 20 to 32 seconds, on a different machine | Every app starts. |

The sandbox itself is ready in a few seconds. The desktop needs more time, because the 16 GB of data streams in while the desktop starts.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Running Windows programs do not survive a stop, a fork or a new sandbox. Start them again.


# Install Wine
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/windows-apps/install-wine

Install Wine and the Windows runtimes in a sandbox with one script.

Run this script one time inside the sandbox. It takes about 5 minutes.

## Run the script

1. Save the script below as `install-wine.sh` on your computer.

2. Send it to the sandbox in one of these ways:

   | Surface | How |
   | - | - |
   | CLI | `boat ssh bx_f7k2q9hd -- bash -s < install-wine.sh` |
   | API | Pass the script as the `command` of [`POST /sandboxes/{sandboxId}/commands`](/api/reference/agent/execute-sandbox-command), with `detached: true`. |
   | SDK | Pass the script to the `command` call, with `detached: true`. |

3. For the API and the SDK, poll the command status until the command finishes.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Without `detached`, a command stops after 30 seconds by default and after 600 seconds at most. Then Wine is only half installed.

```bash install-wine.sh theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
set -e
sudo dpkg --add-architecture i386
sudo mkdir -pm755 /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo wget -qO /etc/apt/keyrings/winehq-archive.key https://dl.winehq.org/wine-builds/winehq.key
sudo wget -qNP /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ https://dl.winehq.org/wine-builds/ubuntu/dists/noble/winehq-noble.sources
printf 'Package: libgd3\nPin: release o=Ubuntu\nPin-Priority: 1001\n' | sudo tee /etc/apt/preferences.d/wine-libgd3
sudo apt-get update -qq
sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq --allow-downgrades --no-install-recommends \
  winehq-staging mesa-vulkan-drivers mesa-vulkan-drivers:i386 cabextract p7zip-full
sudo wget -qO /usr/local/bin/winetricks https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Winetricks/winetricks/master/src/winetricks
sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/winetricks
export DISPLAY=:0
WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml=" wineboot -i
winetricks -q corefonts vcrun2022 dxvk d3dcompiler_47
wine --version
```

## What each part does

| Part | Why it is there |
| - | - |
| **WineHQ staging** | Ubuntu's own Wine is version 9. Steam, Paint.NET 5.2 and Direct3D games need Wine 11 or newer. |
| **The `libgd3` pin** | The sandbox has a PHP repository. Its `libgd3` exists only for 64-bit. 32-bit Wine needs the same version for both. The pin selects Ubuntu's version. As a side effect, PHP's `gd` extension is removed. |
| **`mesa-vulkan-drivers`** | A sandbox has no GPU. This software Vulkan driver lets DXVK run Direct3D 8 to 11 on the CPU. |
| **`WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml="`** | A new Wine set-up opens a "Wine Mono Installer" window and waits for a click. This setting skips that window. Apps that need .NET get Microsoft's runtime from winetricks instead. |
| **winetricks** | Installs Microsoft's free redistributables: core fonts, the Visual C++ 2015 to 2022 runtime, DXVK and the Direct3D shader compiler. |

## Next step

[Run an app](/windows-apps/run-apps).


# Run an app
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/windows-apps/run-apps

Install and start a Windows app in a sandbox. Recipes for Steam, Paint.NET, Sysinternals and Direct3D games.

Before you start, [install Wine](/windows-apps/install-wine).

## Install and start an app

1. Download the official installer or portable archive in the sandbox.
2. Install it.
3. Start it on the desktop. Every GUI command needs `DISPLAY=:0`.

This example installs the MicroDicom medical image viewer and opens a CT scan:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
export DISPLAY=:0
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/microdicom.exe https://www.microdicom.com/downloads/Software/MicroDicom-2026.4-Setup.exe
wine /tmp/microdicom.exe /S
curl -fsSL -o ~/CT_small.dcm https://github.com/pydicom/pydicom/raw/main/src/pydicom/data/test_files/CT_small.dcm
wine start /unix "$HOME/.wine/drive_c/Program Files/MicroDicom/mDicom.exe" 'Z:\home\user\CT_small.dcm'
```

On the first start, MicroDicom asks to become the default viewer. It does not open the file. To open the scan:

1. Press Escape.
2. Close MicroDicom.
3. Run the last command again.

After this, the scan opens immediately.

## Tips

* Use `wine start /unix <path>` to start a program. `start` gives the program normal Windows console handles. Without it, programs written in Python (Blender, FreeCAD) and many others crash.

* Most installers have a silent switch:

  | Installer type | Silent switch |
  | - | - |
  | NSIS | `/S` |
  | Inno Setup | `/VERYSILENT` |
  | MSI | `msiexec /i app.msi /qn` |

* To find an official download link, open the app's manifest in [winget-pkgs](https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs/tree/master/manifests). The `InstallerUrl` field is the vendor's own link.

* Windows paths map to Linux paths:

  | Windows path | Linux path |
  | - | - |
  | `C:\` | `~/.wine/drive_c` |
  | `Z:\` | The Linux root `/` |

## Steam

Steam has these needs:

* It needs the Arial font.
* It must not use Wine's DirectWrite.
* Its web view must not use a GPU.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
export DISPLAY=:0
winetricks -q arial
wine reg add 'HKCU\Software\Wine\AppDefaults\steam.exe\DllOverrides' /v dwrite /t REG_SZ /d '' /f
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/SteamSetup.exe https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/client/installer/SteamSetup.exe
wine /tmp/SteamSetup.exe /S
wine start 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steam.exe' -no-dwrite -cef-disable-gpu -cef-disable-sandbox
```

The first start updates Steam and takes about 2 minutes. Then the sign-in window opens.

## Paint.NET

Paint.NET 5.2 has a separate [build for Wine](https://github.com/paintdotnet/Paint.NET-on-Wine).

* It needs Wine 11.15 or newer. The [Wine set-up](/windows-apps/install-wine) installs this version.
* Its installer makes its own Wine set-up and needs Wine Mono. So it opens the "Wine Mono Installer" window.
* The `xdotool` loop below presses **Install** for you.

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
export DISPLAY=:0
mkdir -p ~/apps/paintnet && cd ~/apps/paintnet
curl -fsSL -o pdn.zip "$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/paintdotnet/Paint.NET-on-Wine/releases \
  | grep -o '"browser_download_url": *"[^"]*x64[^"]*\.zip"' | cut -d'"' -f4 | head -1)"
unzip -q pdn.zip
( for i in $(seq 1 120); do
    w=$(wmctrl -l | grep 'Wine Mono Installer' | awk '{print $1}')
    [ -n "$w" ] && { wmctrl -i -a $w; sleep 0.5; xdotool key Return; break; }
    sleep 2
  done ) &
./install.sh
./paintdotnet.sh &
```

* Use the `x64` file. The release also has an `arm64` file. That file does not run on a sandbox.
* The Wine build is experimental. It expires 12 weeks after its build date. When it expires, download a new one.
* Paint.NET 5.1 and older do not run.

## Sysinternals

Process Explorer and Autoruns show a licence window on the first start. Accept the licence before the start, so that an agent does not have to. Autoruns rejects the `/accepteula` flag. So set the registry value for both apps:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
export DISPLAY=:0
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/procexp.zip https://download.sysinternals.com/files/ProcessExplorer.zip
curl -fsSL -o /tmp/autoruns.zip https://download.sysinternals.com/files/Autoruns.zip
mkdir -p ~/apps/sysinternals && cd ~/apps/sysinternals
unzip -qo /tmp/procexp.zip && unzip -qo /tmp/autoruns.zip
wine reg add 'HKCU\Software\Sysinternals\Process Explorer' /v EulaAccepted /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
wine reg add 'HKCU\Software\Sysinternals\Autoruns' /v EulaAccepted /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
wine start /unix ~/apps/sysinternals/procexp64.exe
```

## Direct3D games

DXVK from the Wine set-up runs Direct3D 8, 9, 10 and 11 games on the software Vulkan driver.

| Game type | Speed |
| - | - |
| Simple 2D games and older 3D games | Playable |
| Modern 3D games | Too slow without a GPU |

Old games that change the screen resolution can leave a full-screen window over the desktop. To stop Wine from changing the resolution, run:

```bash theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"github-dark-default"}}
wine reg add 'HKCU\Software\Wine\X11 Driver' /v UseXRandR /t REG_SZ /d N /f
wine reg add 'HKCU\Software\Wine\X11 Driver' /v UseXVidMode /t REG_SZ /d N /f
```


# Tested apps
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/windows-apps/tested-apps

Windows apps that run in a boat sandbox with Wine, the extra steps they need, and the apps that do not run.

Every app below ran on a boat sandbox with the set-up from [Install Wine](/windows-apps/install-wine). The "Extra step" column gives what the app needs in addition to that set-up.

## Apps that run

| App | What it is | Extra step |
| - | - | - |
| Notepad++, HxD, WinMerge, Everything | Editors, hex, diff, file search | None |
| WinRAR, 7-Zip, WinDirStat | Archives, disk usage | None |
| HeidiSQL | Database client | None. Install a database server, for example `sudo apt-get install -y mysql-server`, if you need a local one. |
| Winamp, foobar2000, MPC-HC, IrfanView, FastStone, XnView | Media and image viewers | None |
| LTspice | Circuit simulator | None |
| FORScan | Car diagnostics | None |
| x64dbg | Debugger | None |
| Process Explorer, Autoruns | Microsoft Sysinternals | [Accept the licence first](/windows-apps/run-apps#sysinternals) |
| MicroDicom, RadiAnt | Medical image (DICOM) viewers | RadiAnt asks you to start its free trial |
| Steam | Game store client | [Steam](/windows-apps/run-apps#steam) |
| Paint.NET 5.2 | Image editor | [Paint.NET](/windows-apps/run-apps#paint-net) |
| Spelunky, Cave Story | Games | None. Direct3D runs through DXVK. |
| ImgBurn | Disc image tool | None |
| SkiFree and other 16-bit Windows 3.1 programs | Old games and tools | Run them alone. Their emulator slows every other Wine window. |

## Apps that do not run

No set-up makes these apps work.

| App | Why |
| - | - |
| CPU-Z | Opens with a driver error. It loads a Windows kernel driver, and Wine cannot load kernel drivers. |
| Paint.NET 5.1 and older | Needs a Windows system file that Wine does not have. Use 5.2. |
| CCleaner | Starts, then opens no window. |


# Windows apps troubleshooting
Source: https://docs.boat.dev/windows-apps/troubleshooting

Fix common errors when you run Windows apps with Wine in a sandbox. Licence rules.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| - | - | - |
| `apt-get` says `libgd3:i386` "is not going to be installed" | The `libgd3` from the PHP repository | Add the `libgd3` pin from [Install Wine](/windows-apps/install-wine#what-each-part-does) |
| `wineboot` never finishes | The "Wine Mono Installer" window waits for a click | `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="mscoree,mshtml=" wineboot -i` |
| `Cannot open display` | The command does not know the desktop | `export DISPLAY=:0` |
| A Python-based app exits immediately with `init_sys_streams` | No Windows console handles | Start it with `wine start /unix` |
| `unimplemented function msvcp140.dll...` | Old Visual C++ runtime | `winetricks -q vcrun2022` |
| Windows go blank and show "Not Responding" | A window was closed from Linux with `wmctrl -c` or the title bar while it held a modal dialog | Answer dialogs with keys (`xdotool key Return`). Do not close them from outside. |
| Every Wine window is slow | A 16-bit Windows 3.1 program is running. Its emulator keeps Wine busy. | Close it. Run 16-bit programs on their own. |
| A game covers the whole desktop | It changed the screen resolution | Set `UseXRandR` and `UseXVidMode` to `N`. Read [Direct3D games](/windows-apps/run-apps#direct3d-games). |

## Licences

* Install only software that you have the right to use.
* Download it from the vendor, as on these pages.
* Do not copy Windows system files into Wine. Microsoft's licence does not allow it.
* Wine does not need Windows system files for the apps on these pages.
* The winetricks components on these pages are Microsoft's free redistributables.
